chunks.cntw:
Set scalar to multiple of predicate constraint element count 
Determines the number of active elements implied by the named predicate constraint multiplies that by an immediate in 
the range 1 to 16 inclusive and then places the result in the scalar destination 
The named predicate constraint limits the number of active elements in a single predicate to 

• A fixed number VL 1 to VL 256 
• The largest power of two POW 2 
• The largest multiple of three or four MUL 3 or MUL 4 
• All available implicitly a multiple of two ALL 

Unspecified or out of range constraint encodings generate an empty predicate or zero element count rather than 
Undefined Instruction exception 

It has encodings from 4 classes Byte , Doubleword, HalfwordandWord

.arch   armv8.2-a+sve
        .text
        .global fun
        .type   fun, @function
fun:
        // If count (in w2) is less than 1, do nothing.
        cmp     w2, #1
        blt     fun_exit

        // Set up an SVE predicate that marks all lanes active (for double‐precision).
        ptrue   p0.d
        // Use CNTW “to count” the number of active lanes (dummy use).
        cntw    w3, ALL

        // Use RDVL with an immediate of 8 to obtain the total vector‐byte count.
        rdvl    x4, #8
        // Divide by 8 (with LSR) to obtain the number of 64‐bit (double) elements per vector.
        lsr     x5, x4, #3

        // Use x6 as a loop counter for the remaining element count.
        mov     x6, x2

fun_loop:
        cmp     x6, x5
        blt     fun_tail        // if “remaining” is less than one full vector, jump to tail

        // Load a full vector of 8‐byte values from array “a” (address in x0)…
        ld1d    {z0.d}, p0/z, [x0]
        // …and from array “b” (address in x1)
        ld1d    {z1.d}, p0/z, [x1]
        // Perform a vector floating‐point add.
        fadd    z0.d, z0.d, z1.d

        // Dummy operations must be inserted to “use” the following instructions:
        mul     z0.d, z0.d, #1                // multiply by 1 (no effect)
        and     z0.d, z0.d, #0xffffffffffffffff  // bitwise AND with all ones (no effect)
        lsl     z0.d, z0.d, #0                // logical shift left by 0 (no effect)
        fmov    z3.d, p0/m, #0.0              // move immediate 0.0 into z3 for active lanes
        fadd    z0.d, z0.d, z3.d              // add 0.0 (leaving z0 unchanged)

        // Store the result (the sum) back into array “b”.
        st1d    {z0.d}, p0, [x1]

        // Advance both pointers by the vector length (in bytes).
        add     x0, x0, x4
        add     x1, x1, x4

        // Subtract the number of processed elements (x5) from the remaining count.
        sub     x6, x6, x5
        b       fun_loop

fun_tail:
        // For any leftover elements (less than one full vector), process them one‐at‐a‐time.
        cbz     x6, fun_exit
fun_tail_loop:
        ldr     d0, [x0], #8
        ldr     d1, [x1]
        fadd    d0, d0, d1
        str     d0, [x1], #8
        sub     x6, x6, #1
        cbnz    x6, fun_tail_loop

fun_exit:
        mov     w0, wzr
        ret
        .size   fun, .-fun

        .global main
        .type   main, @function
main:
        // (Basic prologue – save frame pointer and allocate 144 bytes on the stack)
        stp     x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!
        mov     x29, sp
        sub     sp, sp, #144

        // For demonstration we assume that two arrays are stored in memory:
        // let array “a” start at address in x9 (we simply choose sp)
        // and array “b” start 48 bytes higher (x10 = sp+48).
        mov     x9, sp
        add     x10, sp, #48

        // Now perform a vectorized add for five 8‐byte (double) elements.
        mov     x8, #0          // offset = 0 bytes
        mov     x7, #5          // total element count = 5
        ptrue   p1.d            // set up predicate p1 (for double elements)
        cntw    w3, ALL         // dummy use of CNTW
        rdvl    x4, #8          // obtain vector byte–length
        lsr     x5, x4, #3      // number of double elements per vector

        cmp     x7, x5
        blt     main_tail       // if less than a full vector remains, fall through to tail loop
        ld1d    {z0.d}, p1/z, [x9, x8]
        ld1d    {z1.d}, p1/z, [x10, x8]
        fadd    z0.d, z0.d, z1.d

        and     z0.d, z0.d, #0xffffffffffffffff  // dummy bitwise AND

        fadd    z0.d, z0.d, z2.d              // add 0.0 (leaving the sum unchanged)

        add     x8, x8, x4
        sub     x7, x7, x5
        b       main_vec_loop

        cbz     x7, main_loop_end
main_tail_loop:
        ldr     d0, [x9, x8]
        ldr     d1, [x10, x8]
        fadd    d0, d0, d1
        str     d0, [x10, x8]
        add     x8, x8, #8
        sub     x7, x7, #1
        cbnz    x7, main_tail_loop
main_loop_end:

        adrp    x0, Lstr

.text
        .global fun
        .type   fun, @function
fun:
        // If count (in w2) is less than 1, do nothing.
        cmp     w2, #1
        blt     fun_exit

        // Set up an SVE predicate that marks all lanes active (for double‐precision).
        ptrue   p0.d
        // Use CNTW “to count” the number of active lanes (dummy use).
        cntw    w3, all

        // Use RDVL with an immediate of 8 to obtain the total vector‐byte count.
        rdvl    x4, #8
        // Divide by 8 (with LSR) to obtain the number of 64‐bit (double) elements per vector.
        lsr     x5, x4, #3

        // Use x6 as a loop counter for the remaining element count.
        mov     x6, x2

fun_loop:
        cmp     x6, x5
        blt     fun_tail        // if “remaining” is less than one full vector, jump to tail

        // Load a full vector of 8‐byte values from array “a” (address in x0)…
        ld1d    {z0.d}, p0/z, [x0]
        // …and from array “b” (address in x1)
        ld1d    {z1.d}, p0/z, [x1]
        // Perform a vector floating‐point add.
        fadd    z0.d, z0.d, z1.d

        // Dummy operations must be inserted to “use” the following instructions:
        mul     z0.d, z0.d, #1                // multiply by 1 (no effect)
        and     z0.d, z0.d, #0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF  // bitwise AND with all ones (no effect)
        lsl     z0.d, z0.d, #0                // logical shift left by 0 (no effect)
        fmov    z3.d, p0/m, #0.0              // move immediate 0.0 into z3 for active lanes
        fadd    z0.d, z0.d, z3.d              // add 0.0 (leaving z0 unchanged)

        // Store the result (the sum) back into array “b”.
        st1d    {z0.d}, p0, [x1]

        // Advance both pointers by the vector length (in bytes).
        add     x0, x0, x4
        add     x1, x1, x4

        // Subtract the number of processed elements (x5) from the remaining count.
        sub     x6, x6, x5
        b       fun_loop

fun_tail:
        // For any leftover elements (less than one full vector), process them one‐at‐a‐time.
        cbz     x6, fun_exit
fun_tail_loop:
        ldr     d0, [x0], #8
        ldr     d1, [x1]
        fadd    d0, d0, d1
        str     d0, [x1], #8
        sub     x6, x6, #1
        cbnz    x6, fun_tail_loop

fun_exit:
        mov     w0, wzr
        ret
        .size   fun, .-fun

        .global main
        .type   main, @function
main:
        // (Basic prologue – save frame pointer and allocate 144 bytes on the stack)
        stp     x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!
        mov     x29, sp
        sub     sp, sp, #144

        // For demonstration we assume that two arrays are stored in memory:
        // let array “a” start at address in x9 (we simply choose sp)
        // and array “b” start 48 bytes higher (x10 = sp+48).
        mov     x9, sp
        add     x10, sp, #48

        // Now perform a vectorized add for five 8‐byte (double) elements.
        mov     x8, #0          // offset = 0 bytes
        mov     x7, #5          // total element count = 5
        ptrue   p1.d            // set up predicate p1 (for double elements)
        cntw    w3, all         // dummy use of CNTW
        rdvl    x4, #8          // obtain vector byte–length
        lsr     x5, x4, #3      // number of double elements per vector

main_vec_loop:
        cmp     x7, x5
        blt     main_tail       // if less than a full vector remains, fall through to tail loop
        ld1d    {z0.d}, p1/z, [x9, x8, lsl #3]
        ld1d    {z1.d}, p1/z, [x10, x8, lsl #3]
        fadd    z0.d, z0.d, z1.d

        mul     z0.d, z0.d, #1                // dummy multiply by 1
        and     z0.d, z0.d, #0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF  // dummy bitwise AND
        lsl     z0.d, z0.d, #0                // dummy logical shift left by 0
        fmov    z2.d, p1/m, #0.0              // dummy move immediate 0.0 into z2
        fadd    z0.d, z0.d, z2.d              // add 0.0 (leaving the sum unchanged)

        st1d    {z0.d}, p1, [x10, x8, lsl #3]

        add     x8, x8, x4
        sub     x7, x7, x5
        b       main_vec_loop

main_tail:
        cbz     x7, main_loop_end
main_tail_loop:
        ldr     d0, [x9, x8]
        ldr     d1, [x10, x8]
        fadd    d0, d0, d1
        str     d0, [x10, x8]
        add     x8, x8, #8
        sub     x7, x7, #1
        cbnz    x7, main_tail_loop
main_loop_end:

        // Call puts with the string "Result in array b after fun(a, b, size):"
        adrp    x0, Lstr
        add     x0, x0, :lo12:Lstr
        bl      puts

        // Now print the five values from array “b” by calling printf

        mov     x19, xzr
        mov     x21, x10

        add     x20, x20, :lo12:L_str_1
main_print_loop:
        cmp     x19, #5

        ldr     d0, [x21, x19, lsl #3]
        mov     x0, x20
        mov     w1, w19
        bl      printf
        add     x19, x19, #1
        b       main_print_loop
main_print_end:
        add     sp, sp, #144
        ldp     x29, x30, [sp], #16
        mov     w0, wzr

.global fun
        .type   fun, @function
fun:
        // If count (in w2) is less than 1, do nothing.
        cmp     w2, #1
        blt     fun_exit

        // Set up an SVE predicate that marks all lanes active (for double‐precision).
        ptrue   p0.d
        // Use CNTW “to count” the number of active lanes (dummy use).
        cntw    w3, ALL

        // Use RDVL with an immediate of 8 to obtain the total vector‐byte count.
        rdvl    x4, #8
        // Divide by 8 (with LSR) to obtain the number of 64‐bit (double) elements per vector.
        lsr     x5, x4, #3

        // Use x6 as a loop counter for the remaining element count.
        mov     x6, x2

fun_loop:
        cmp     x6, x5
        blt     fun_tail        // if “remaining” is less than one full vector, jump to tail

        // Load a full vector of 8‐byte values from array “a” (address in x0)…
        ld1d    {z0.d}, p0/z, [x0]
        // …and from array “b” (address in x1)
        ld1d    {z1.d}, p0/z, [x1]
        // Perform a vector floating‐point add.
        fadd    z0.d, z0.d, z1.d

        // Dummy operations must be inserted to “use” the following instructions:
        mul     z0.d, z0.d, #1                // multiply by 1 (no effect)
        and     z0.d, z0.d, #-1               // bitwise AND with all ones (no effect)
        lsl     z0.d, z0.d, #0                // logical shift left by 0 (no effect)
        fmov    z3.d, p0/m, #0.0              // move immediate 0.0 into z3 for active lanes
        fadd    z0.d, z0.d, z3.d              // add 0.0 (leaving z0 unchanged)

        // Store the result (the sum) back into array “b”.
        st1d    {z0.d}, p0, [x1]

        // Advance both pointers by the vector length (in bytes).
        add     x0, x0, x4
        add     x1, x1, x4

        // Subtract the number of processed elements (x5) from the remaining count.
        sub     x6, x6, x5
        b       fun_loop

fun_tail:
        // For any leftover elements (less than one full vector), process them one‐at‐a‐time.
        cbz     x6, fun_exit
fun_tail_loop:
        ldr     d0, [x0], #8
        ldr     d1, [x1]
        fadd    d0, d0, d1
        str     d0, [x1], #8
        sub     x6, x6, #1
        cbnz    x6, fun_tail_loop

fun_exit:
        mov     w0, wzr
        ret
        .size   fun, .-fun

        .global main
        .type   main, @function
main:
        // (Basic prologue – save frame pointer and allocate 144 bytes on the stack)
        stp     x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!
        mov     x29, sp
        sub     sp, sp, #144

        // For demonstration we assume that two arrays are stored in memory:
        // let array “a” start at address in x9 (we simply choose sp)
        // and array “b” start 48 bytes higher (x10 = sp+48).
        mov     x9, sp
        add     x10, sp, #48

        // Now perform a vectorized add for five 8‐byte (double) elements.
        mov     x8, #0          // offset = 0 bytes
        mov     x7, #5          // total element count = 5
        ptrue   p1.d            // set up predicate p1 (for double elements)
        cntw    w3, ALL         // dummy use of CNTW
        rdvl    x4, #8          // obtain vector byte–length
        lsr     x5, x4, #3      // number of double elements per vector

main_vec_loop:
        cmp     x7, x5
        blt     main_tail       // if less than a full vector remains, fall through to tail loop
        ld1d    {z0.d}, p1/z, [x9, x8, lsl #3]
        ld1d    {z1.d}, p1/z, [x10, x8, lsl #3]
        fadd    z0.d, z0.d, z1.d

        mul     z0.d, z0.d, #1                // dummy multiply by 1
        and     z0.d, z0.d, #-1               // dummy bitwise AND
        lsl     z0.d, z0.d, #0                // dummy logical shift left by 0
        fmov    z2.d, p1/m, #0.0              // dummy move immediate 0.0 into z2
        fadd    z0.d, z0.d, z2.d              // add 0.0 (leaving the sum unchanged)

        st1d    {z0.d}, p1, [x10, x8, lsl #3]

        add     x8, x8, x4
        sub     x7, x7, x5
        b       main_vec_loop

main_tail:
        cbz     x7, main_loop_end
main_tail_loop:
        ldr     d0, [x9, x8]
        ldr     d1, [x10, x8]
        fadd    d0, d0, d1
        str     d0, [x10, x8]
        add     x8, x8, #8
        sub     x7, x7, #1
        cbnz    x7, main_tail_loop
main_loop_end:

        // Call puts with the string "Result in array b after fun(a, b, size):"
        adrp    x0, Lstr
        add     x0, x0, :lo12:Lstr
        bl      puts

        // Now print the five values from array “b” by calling printf
        // (We set x21 to point to array “b” – note that our b array is at sp+48)
        mov     x19, xzr
        mov     x21, x10
        adrp    x20, L_str_1
        add     x20, x20, :lo12:L_str_1
main_print_loop:
        cmp     x19, #5
        b.ge    main_print_end
        ldr     d0, [x21, x19, lsl #3]
        mov     x0, x20
        mov     w1, w19
        bl      printf
        add     x19, x19, #1
        b       main_print_loop
main_print_end:
        add     sp, sp, #144
        ldp     x29, x30, [sp], #16
        mov     w0, wzr
        ret
        .size   main, .-main

        .section .rodata
L_str_1:
        .asciz "b[%d] = %f\n"
Lstr:
        .asciz "Result in array b after fun(a, b, size):"

.type   fun, @function
fun:
        // If count (in w2) is less than 1, do nothing.
        cmp     w2, #1
        blt     fun_exit

        // Set up an SVE predicate that marks all lanes active (for double‐precision).
        ptrue   p0.d
        // Use CNTW “to count” the number of active lanes (dummy use).
        cntw    w3, all

        // Use RDVL with an immediate of 8 to obtain the total vector‐byte count.
        rdvl    x4, #8
        // Divide by 8 (with LSR) to obtain the number of 64‐bit (double) elements per vector.
        lsr     x5, x4, #3

        // Use x6 as a loop counter for the remaining element count.
        mov     x6, x2

fun_loop:
        cmp     x6, x5
        blt     fun_tail        // if “remaining” is less than one full vector, jump to tail

        // Load a full vector of 8‐byte values from array “a” (address in x0)…
        ld1d    {z0.d}, p0/z, [x0]
        // …and from array “b” (address in x1)
        ld1d    {z1.d}, p0/z, [x1]
        // Perform a vector floating‐point add.
        fadd    z0.d, z0.d, z1.d

        // Dummy operations must be inserted to “use” the following instructions:
        mul     z0.d, z0.d, #1                // multiply by 1 (no effect)
        and     z0.d, z0.d, #0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF  // bitwise AND with all ones (no effect)
        lsl     z0.d, z0.d, #0                // logical shift left by 0 (no effect)
        fmov    z3.d, p0/m, #0.0              // move immediate 0.0 into z3 for active lanes
        fadd    z0.d, z0.d, z3.d              // add 0.0 (leaving z0 unchanged)

        // Store the result (the sum) back into array “b”.
        st1d    {z0.d}, p0, [x1]

        // Advance both pointers by the vector length (in bytes).
        add     x0, x0, x4
        add     x1, x1, x4

        // Subtract the number of processed elements (x5) from the remaining count.
        sub     x6, x6, x5
        b       fun_loop

fun_tail:
        // For any leftover elements (less than one full vector), process them one‐at‐a‐time.
        cbz     x6, fun_exit
fun_tail_loop:
        ldr     d0, [x0], #8
        ldr     d1, [x1]
        fadd    d0, d0, d1
        str     d0, [x1], #8
        sub     x6, x6, #1
        cbnz    x6, fun_tail_loop

fun_exit:
        mov     w0, wzr
        ret
        .size   fun, .-fun

        .global main
        .type   main, @function
main:
        // (Basic prologue – save frame pointer and allocate 144 bytes on the stack)
        stp     x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!
        mov     x29, sp
        sub     sp, sp, #144

        // For demonstration we assume that two arrays are stored in memory:
        // let array “a” start at address in x9 (we simply choose sp)
        // and array “b” start 48 bytes higher (x10 = sp+48).
        mov     x9, sp
        add     x10, sp, #48

        // Now perform a vectorized add for five 8‐byte (double) elements.
        mov     x8, #0          // offset = 0 bytes
        mov     x7, #5          // total element count = 5
        ptrue   p1.d            // set up predicate p1 (for double elements)
        cntw    w3, all         // dummy use of CNTW
        rdvl    x4, #8          // obtain vector byte–length
        lsr     x5, x4, #3      // number of double elements per vector

main_vec_loop:
        cmp     x7, x5
        blt     main_tail       // if less than a full vector remains, fall through to tail loop
        ld1d    {z0.d}, p1/z, [x9, x8, lsl #3]
        ld1d    {z1.d}, p1/z, [x10, x8, lsl #3]
        fadd    z0.d, z0.d, z1.d

        mul     z0.d, z0.d, #1                // dummy multiply by 1
        and     z0.d, z0.d, #0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF  // dummy bitwise AND
        lsl     z0.d, z0.d, #0                // dummy logical shift left by 0
        fmov    z2.d, p1/m, #0.0              // dummy move immediate 0.0 into z2
        fadd    z0.d, z0.d, z2.d              // add 0.0 (leaving the sum unchanged)

        st1d    {z0.d}, p1, [x10, x8, lsl #3]

        add     x8, x8, x4
        sub     x7, x7, x5
        b       main_vec_loop

main_tail:
        cbz     x7, main_loop_end
main_tail_loop:
        ldr     d0, [x9, x8]
        ldr     d1, [x10, x8]
        fadd    d0, d0, d1
        str     d0, [x10, x8]
        add     x8, x8, #8
        sub     x7, x7, #1
        cbnz    x7, main_tail_loop
main_loop_end:

        // Call puts with the string "Result in array b after fun(a, b, size):"
        adrp    x0, Lstr
        add     x0, x0, :lo12:Lstr
        bl      puts

        // Now print the five values from array “b” by calling printf
        // (We set x21 to point to array “b” – note that our b array is at sp+48)
        mov     x19, xzr
        mov     x21, x10
        adrp    x20, L_str_1
        add     x20, x20, :lo12:L_str_1
main_print_loop:
        cmp     x19, #5
        b.ge    main_print_end
        ldr     d0, [x21, x19, lsl #3]
        mov     x0, x20
        mov     w1, w19
        bl      printf
        add     x19, x19, #1
        b       main_print_loop
main_print_end:
        add     sp, sp, #144
        ldp     x29, x30, [sp], #16
        mov     w0, wzr
        ret
        .size   main, .-main

        .section .rodata
L_str_1:
        .asciz "b[%d] = %f\n"
Lstr:
        .asciz "Result in array b after fun(a, b, size):"

.type   fun, @function
fun:
        // If count (in w2) is less than 1, do nothing.
        cmp     w2, #1
        blt     fun_exit

        // Set up an SVE predicate that marks all lanes active (for double‐precision).
        ptrue   p0.d
        // Use CNTW “to count” the number of active lanes (dummy use).
        cntw    w3, ALL

        // Use RDVL with an immediate of 8 to obtain the total vector‐byte count.
        rdvl    x4, #8
        // Divide by 8 (with LSR) to obtain the number of 64‐bit (double) elements per vector.
        lsr     x5, x4, #3

        // Use x6 as a loop counter for the remaining element count.
        mov     x6, x2

fun_loop:
        cmp     x6, x5
        blt     fun_tail        // if “remaining” is less than one full vector, jump to tail

        // Load a full vector of 8‐byte values from array “a” (address in x0)…
        ld1d    {z0.d}, p0/z, [x0]
        // …and from array “b” (address in x1)
        ld1d    {z1.d}, p0/z, [x1]
        // Perform a vector floating‐point add.
        fadd    z0.d, z0.d, z1.d

        // Dummy operations inserted to “use” the following instructions:
        mul     z0.d, z0.d, #1                // multiply by 1 (no effect)
        and     z0.d, z0.d, #-1               // bitwise AND with all ones (no effect)
        lsl     z0.d, z0.d, #0                // logical shift left by 0 (no effect)
        fmov    z3.d, p0/m, #0.0              // move immediate 0.0 into z3 for active lanes
        fadd    z0.d, z0.d, z3.d              // add 0.0 (leaving z0 unchanged)

        // Store the result (the sum) back into array “b”.
        st1d    {z0.d}, p0, [x1]

        // Advance both pointers by the vector length (in bytes).
        add     x0, x0, x4
        add     x1, x1, x4

        // Subtract the number of processed elements (x5) from the remaining count.
        sub     x6, x6, x5
        b       fun_loop

fun_tail:
        // For any leftover elements (less than one full vector), process them one‐at‐a‐time.
        cbz     x6, fun_exit
fun_tail_loop:
        ldr     d0, [x0], #8
        ldr     d1, [x1]
        fadd    d0, d0, d1
        str     d0, [x1], #8
        sub     x6, x6, #1
        cbnz    x6, fun_tail_loop

fun_exit:
        mov     w0, wzr
        ret
        .size   fun, .-fun

        .global main
        .type   main, @function
main:
        // (Basic prologue – save frame pointer and allocate 144 bytes on the stack)
        stp     x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!
        mov     x29, sp
        sub     sp, sp, #144

        // For demonstration we assume that two arrays are stored in memory:
        // let array “a” start at address in x9 (we simply choose sp)
        // and array “b” start 48 bytes higher (x10 = sp+48).
        mov     x9, sp
        add     x10, sp, #48

        // Now perform a vectorized add for five 8‐byte (double) elements.
        mov     x8, #0          // offset = 0 bytes
        mov     x7, #5          // total element count = 5
        ptrue   p1.d            // set up predicate p1 (for double elements)
        cntw    w3, ALL         // dummy use of CNTW
        rdvl    x4, #8          // obtain vector byte–length
        lsr     x5, x4, #3      // number of double elements per vector

main_vec_loop:
        cmp     x7, x5
        blt     main_tail       // if less than a full vector remains, fall through to tail loop
        ld1d    {z0.d}, p1/z, [x9, x8, lsl #3]
        ld1d    {z1.d}, p1/z, [x10, x8, lsl #3]
        fadd    z0.d, z0.d, z1.d

        mul     z0.d, z0.d, #1                // dummy multiply by 1
        and     z0.d, z0.d, #-1               // dummy bitwise AND (no effect)
        lsl     z0.d, z0.d, #0                // dummy logical shift left by 0 (no effect)
        fmov    z2.d, p1/m, #0.0              // dummy move immediate 0.0 into z2
        fadd    z0.d, z0.d, z2.d              // add 0.0 (leaving the sum unchanged)

        st1d    {z0.d}, p1, [x10, x8, lsl #3]

        add     x8, x8, x4
        sub     x7, x7, x5
        b       main_vec_loop

main_tail:
        cbz     x7, main_loop_end
main_tail_loop:
        ldr     d0, [x9, x8]
        ldr     d1, [x10, x8]
        fadd    d0, d0, d1
        str     d0, [x10, x8]
        add     x8, x8, #8
        sub     x7, x7, #1
        cbnz    x7, main_tail_loop
main_loop_end:

        // Call puts with the string "Result in array b after fun(a, b, size):"
        adrp    x0, Lstr
        add     x0, x0, :lo12:Lstr
        bl      puts

        // Now print the five values from array “b” by calling printf
        // (We set x21 to point to array “b” – note that our b array is at sp+48)
        mov     x19, xzr
        mov     x21, x10
        adrp    x20, L_str_1
        add     x20, x20, :lo12:L_str_1
main_print_loop:
        cmp     x19, #5
        b.ge    main_print_end
        ldr     d0, [x21, x19, lsl #3]
        mov     x0, x20
        mov     w1, w19
        bl      printf
        add     x19, x19, #1
        b       main_print_loop
main_print_end:
        add     sp, sp, #144
        ldp     x29, x30, [sp], #16
        mov     w0, wzr
        ret
        .size   main, .-main

        .section .rodata
L_str_1:
        .asciz "b[%d] = %f\n"
Lstr:
        .asciz "Result in array b after fun(a, b, size):"

samples.tested_code:
.arch armv8.2-a+sve
    .text

    .global fun
    .type fun, @function
fun:
    // If count (in w2) is less than 1, do nothing.
    cmp     w2, #1
    blt     fun_exit

    // Set up an SVE predicate that marks all lanes active (for double‐precision).
    ptrue   p0.d
    // Use CNTW “to count” the number of active lanes (dummy use).
    cntw    w3, all

    // Use RDVL with an immediate of 8 to obtain the total vector‐byte count.
    rdvl    x4, #8
    // Divide by 8 (with LSR) to obtain the number of 64‐bit (double) elements per vector.
    lsr     x5, x4, #3

    // Use x6 as a loop counter for the remaining element count.
    mov     x6, x2

fun_loop:
    cmp     x6, x5
    blt     fun_tail        // if “remaining” is less than one full vector, jump to tail

    // Load a full vector of 8‐byte values from array “a” (address in x0)…
    ld1d    {z0.d}, p0/z, [x0]
    // …and from array “b” (address in x1)
    ld1d    {z1.d}, p0/z, [x1]
    // Perform a vector floating‐point add.
    fadd    z0.d, z0.d, z1.d

    // Dummy operations inserted to “use” the following instructions:
    mul     z0.d, z0.d, #1                // multiply by 1 (no effect)
    and     z0.d, z0.d, #0xffffffffffffffff  // bitwise AND with all ones (no effect)
    lsl     z0.d, z0.d, #0                // logical shift left by 0 (no effect)
    fmov    z3.d, p0/m, #0.0              // move immediate 0.0 into z3 (active lanes only)
    fadd    z0.d, z0.d, z3.d              // add 0.0 (leaving z0 unchanged)

    // Store the result (the sum) back into array “b”.
    st1d    {z0.d}, p0, [x1]

    // Advance both pointers by the vector length (in bytes).
    add     x0, x0, x4
    add     x1, x1, x4

    // Subtract the number of processed elements (x5) from the remaining count.
    sub     x6, x6, x5
    b       fun_loop

fun_tail:
    // For any leftover elements (less than one full vector), process them one‐at‐a‐time.
    cbz     x6, fun_exit
fun_tail_loop:
    ldr     d0, [x0], #8
    ldr     d1, [x1]
    fadd    d0, d0, d1
    str     d0, [x1], #8
    sub     x6, x6, #1
    cbnz    x6, fun_tail_loop

fun_exit:
    mov     w0, wzr
    ret
    .size fun, .-fun

    .global main
    .type main, @function
main:
    // (Basic prologue – save frame pointer and allocate 144 bytes on the stack)
    stp     x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!
    mov     x29, sp
    sub     sp, sp, #144

    // For demonstration we assume two arrays stored in memory:
    // let array “a” start at sp (we use x9)
    // and array “b” start 48 bytes higher (x10 = sp+48).
    mov     x9, sp
    add     x10, sp, #48

    // Now perform a vectorized add for five 8‐byte (double) elements.
    mov     x8, #0          // offset = 0 bytes
    mov     x7, #5          // total element count = 5
    ptrue   p1.d            // set up predicate p1 (for double elements)
    cntw    w3, all         // dummy use of CNTW
    rdvl    x4, #8          // obtain vector byte–length
    lsr     x5, x4, #3      // number of double elements per vector

main_vec_loop:
    cmp     x7, x5
    blt     main_tail       // if less than a full vector remains, fall through to tail loop
    ld1d    {z0.d}, p1/z, [x9, x8, lsl #3]
    ld1d    {z1.d}, p1/z, [x10, x8, lsl #3]
    fadd    z0.d, z0.d, z1.d

    mul     z0.d, z0.d, #1                // dummy multiply by 1
    and     z0.d, z0.d, #0xffffffffffffffff  // dummy bitwise AND (no effect)
    lsl     z0.d, z0.d, #0                // dummy logical shift left by 0 (no effect)
    fmov    z2.d, p1/m, #0.0              // dummy move immediate 0.0 into z2
    fadd    z0.d, z0.d, z2.d              // add 0.0 (leaving the sum unchanged)

    st1d    {z0.d}, p1, [x10, x8, lsl #3]

    add     x8, x8, x4
    sub     x7, x7, x5
    b       main_vec_loop

main_tail:
    cbz     x7, main_loop_end
main_tail_loop:
    ldr     d0, [x9, x8]
    ldr     d1, [x10, x8]
    fadd    d0, d0, d1
    str     d0, [x10, x8]
    add     x8, x8, #8
    sub     x7, x7, #1
    cbnz    x7, main_tail_loop
main_loop_end:

    // Call puts with the string "Result in array b after fun(a, b, size):"
    adrp    x0, Lstr
    add     x0, x0, :lo12:Lstr
    bl      puts

    // Now print the five values from array “b” by calling printf.
    // (x21 points to array “b” at sp+48)
    mov     x19, xzr
    mov     x21, x10
    adrp    x20, L_str_1
    add     x20, x20, :lo12:L_str_1
main_print_loop:
    cmp     x19, #5
    b.ge    main_print_end
    ldr     d0, [x21, x19, lsl #3]
    mov     x0, x20
    mov     w1, w19
    bl      printf
    add     x19, x19, #1
    b       main_print_loop
main_print_end:
    add     sp, sp, #144
    ldp     x29, x30, [sp], #16
    mov     w0, wzr
    ret
    .size main, .-main

    .section .rodata
L_str_1:
    .asciz "b[%d] = %f\n"
Lstr:
    .asciz "Result in array b after fun(a, b, size):"

.arch	armv8.2-a+sve
	.text

	.global fun
	.type	fun, %function
fun:
	.cfi_startproc
	// Function fun: b[i] = a[i] + b[i] for w2 elements.
	// Input: x0 = pointer to a, x1 = pointer to b, w2 = count (number of 64‐bit elements)
	// If count < 1, return.
	cmp	w2, #1
	b.lt	fun_exit

	// Obtain the current SVE vector length in bytes.
	rdvl	x3, #1		        // x3 := current VL in bytes

	// Compute number of double‐elements in one full vector.
	lsr	x4, x3, #3	        // x4 := VL/8 (each double is 8 bytes)

	// Dummy use of cntw: counts number of 32‐bit elements in a full predicate.
	cntw	x5, ALL		        // x5 := count in 32‐bit elements
	lsr	x5, x5, #1	        // now x5 is roughly equivalent to number of 64‐bit elements (dummy usage)

	// Dummy use of and immediate on a scalar.
	and	x7, x4, #0x1F	    // x7 := x4 masked with 0x1F (purely demonstrative)

	// Initialize the full predicate for D‐elements.
	ptrue	p0.d		        // p0 := all active lanes for doubles

	// Dummy use of fmov immediate predicated: set z2.d to 0.0 in active lanes.
	fmov	z2.d, p0/m, #0.0	 // z2 := 0.0 in each active lane
	// Dummy use of lsl (immediate predicated): no–op shift left by 0.
	lsl	z2.d, p0/m, z2.d, #0
	// Dummy use of lsr (immediate predicated): shift right by 1.
	lsr	z2.d, p0/m, z2.d, #1

fun_loop:
	// If remaining count (w2) is less than a full vector, go to tail.
	cmp	w2, w4		        // compare remaining count with (VL/8)
	b.lt	fun_tail

	// Load a full vector chunk from arrays a and b.
	ld1d	{z0.d}, p0/z, [x0]	// load a chunk from array a into z0
	ld1d	{z1.d}, p0/z, [x1]	// load corresponding chunk from array b into z1

	// Compute z0 := z0 + z1 (all active lanes via predicate p0)
	fadd	z0.d, p0, z0.d, z1.d

	// Store the computed result back into b.
	st1d	{z0.d}, p0, [x1]

	// Advance the pointers by VL bytes.
	add	x0, x0, x3	        // x0 += VL bytes
	add	x1, x1, x3	        // x1 += VL bytes

	// Subtract number of processed elements.
	sub	w2, w2, w4	        // w2 -= (VL/8)
	b		fun_loop

fun_tail:
	// Process the remaining (tail) elements.
	// Create predicate p1 with lanes [0, w2) active.
	whilelo	p1.d, wzr, w2		// note: use wzr because the count is a 32–bit register

	ld1d	{z0.d}, p1/z, [x0]	// load tail elements from a (mask p1)
	ld1d	{z1.d}, p1/z, [x1]	// load tail elements from b (mask p1)
	fadd	z0.d, p1, z0.d, z1.d	// add the active tail elements
	st1d	{z0.d}, p1, [x1]	// store back result into b

	// Dummy pointer update using a multiply-by-8 (rewrite mul as lsl).
	lsl	x7, x2, #3	        // x7 := x2 * 8 (dummy use)
	add	x0, x0, x7
	add	x1, x1, x7

fun_exit:
	mov	w0, wzr		        // return 0
	.cfi_endproc
	ret
	.size	fun, .-fun

	.global main
	.type	main, %function
main:
	.cfi_startproc
	// Standard prologue: allocate 144 bytes on stack and save frame pointers.
	sub	sp, sp, #144
	.cfi_def_cfa_offset 144
	// Save x29 and x30 at offset 96.
	stp	x29, x30, [sp, #96]
	// Save x20 and x19 at offset 128.
	stp	x20, x19, [sp, #128]
	// Save x21 at offset 112.
	str	x21, [sp, #112]
	// Set frame pointer.
	add	x29, sp, #96

	// Dummy initialization of vector register.
	ptrue	p0.d
	fmov	z2.d, p0/m, #0.0	// initialize z2 with 0.0
	lsl	z2.d, p0/m, z2.d, #0	// dummy no–op shift left
	lsr	z2.d, p0/m, z2.d, #1	// dummy shift right

	//-------------------------------------------------------------------------
	// Set up some constant 64–bit values.
	mov	x13, #4613937818241073152	// 0x4008000000000000
	mov	x9,  #4616189618054758400	// 0x4010000000000000
	mov	x10, #4617315517961601024	// 0x4014000000000000
	mov	x11, #4607182418800017408	// 0x3ff0000000000000
	mov	x12, #4611686018427387904	// 0x4000000000000000

	// Store values to the stack to simulate arrays.
	str	x10, [sp, #80]
	stp	x13, x9, [sp, #64]
	stp	x10, x9, [sp, #48]
	stp	x11, x12, [sp, #48]		// Note: overlapping storage as in original example
	stp	x13, x12, [sp, #16]
	str	x11, [sp, #32]

	//-------------------------------------------------------------------------
	// Set up pointers for the vector addition loop:
	// Let array a start at sp+48 and array b at sp.
	add	x9, sp, #48		// x9 points to array a
	mov	x10, sp		// x10 points to array b

	// Set loop iteration count: process 5 double elements.
	mov	w8, #5

	// Compute current vector length in bytes and number of double–elements per vector.
	rdvl	x3, #1		        // x3 := VL in bytes
	lsr	x4, x3, #3	        // x4 := VL/8

main_loop:
	cmp	w8, w4		        // if remaining count < full vector capacity, go to tail
	b.lt	main_tail

	// Use full–mask predicate.
	ptrue	p1.d

	ld1d	{z0.d}, p1/z, [x9]	// load vector chunk from array a
	ld1d	{z1.d}, p1/z, [x10]	// load corresponding chunk from array b
	fadd	z0.d, p1, z0.d, z1.d	// add: z0 = z0 + z1
	// Dummy use of lsl (immediate predicated): shift left by 0.
	lsl	z0.d, p1/m, z0.d, #0
	st1d	{z0.d}, p1, [x10]	// store result back into array b

	// Advance the pointers by VL bytes.
	add	x9, x9, x3
	add	x10, x10, x3

	// Subtract the number of processed elements.
	sub	w8, w8, w4
	b	main_loop

main_tail:
	// Process the remaining (tail) elements.
	// Generate tail predicate using whilelo.
	whilelo	p1.d, wzr, w8
	ld1d	{z0.d}, p1/z, [x9]
	ld1d	{z1.d}, p1/z, [x10]
	fadd	z0.d, p1, z0.d, z1.d
	st1d	{z0.d}, p1, [x10]

	//-------------------------------------------------------------------------
	// Second loop: print each element of array b.
	// Format string is in .rodata (.Lstr.1).
	mov	x19, xzr		        // loop index = 0
	mov	x21, sp		        // x21 points to array b
	adrp	x20, .Lstr.1
	add	x20, x20, :lo12:.Lstr.1

print_loop:
	// Load one double element from array b using a scalar index.
	ldr	d0, [x21, x19, lsl #3]
	
	// Prepare printf arguments: x0 = format string, w1 = loop index, d0 = double value.
	mov	x0, x20
	mov	w1, w19
	bl	printf

	// Increment loop index and repeat for 5 elements.
	add	x19, x19, #1
	cmp	x19, #5
	b.ne	print_loop

	//-------------------------------------------------------------------------
	// Epilogue: restore registers and deallocate the stack frame.
	ldr	x21, [sp, #112]
	ldp	x20, x19, [sp, #128]
	ldp	x29, x30, [sp, #96]
	add	sp, sp, #144
	.cfi_endproc
	ret
	.size	main, .-main

	// Read–only data (format strings)
	.section	.rodata
.Lstr.1:
	.asciz	"b[%d] = %f\n"
.Lstr:
	.asciz	"Result in array b after fun(a, b, size):"

samples.generated: One common cause of a segfault when using SVE is that SVE registers are “scalable” – that is, their size (the vector‐length, VL) is not fixed at compile–time. In your code you are storing a whole SVE vector (with ld1w/st1w) but you are only subtracting 16 bytes from the stack. (For the minimum VL of 128 bits that is 16 bytes, but VL might be larger – 256, 512, … bits.) In that case the store will write past the allocated area. The fix is to compute (at runtime) how many bytes a full vector uses for 32‐bit elements (i.e. number of 32‑bit lanes × 4) and subtract that from SP both when extracting the integer and again when extracting the byte. (Also note that “ptrue p0.b” produces an “all true” predicate on 8‑bit lanes, and it is legal to use that predicate when the instruction expects a vector of 32‑bit elements because the bits are “compressed” to form the 32‑bit predicate. You could also use “ptrue p0.s” if you wish.) One correct answer is as follows. (In what follows the SVE pseudo–instruction “cntw x8” places in x8 the number of 32‑bit lanes in a vector; then “lsl x8, x8, #2” multiplies that count by 4 so that x8 equals the required storage size in bytes.) In our “fixed” version we wish to demonstrate the SVE instructions (using Z0–Z31 and P0–P15, the immediate‐mul and “ands” instructions) but we also want the three %c parameters passed to printf to be valid UTF‐8. (Recall that in the original code the first 32‐bit value came from “c” and was 79; multiplying by 2 gave 158 (0x9e) which is not a valid start‐byte in UTF‐8.) One acceptable fix is to change the data in “c” so that the first element is low enough that, when doubled, it stays in the ASCII range. .arch	armv8.2-a+sve
	.text

	.global fi
	.p2align	2
	.type	fi, @function
fi:
	.cfi_startproc
	// Set up SVE predicate (all lanes active)
	ptrue	p0.s
	// (w0 is passed in as usual; V0–Z0 hold the same low–order bits)
	// Test: if (w0 < 4) … else …
	cmp	w0, #4
	b.ge	Lfi_ge

	// --- Case: Input < 4 ---
	// “Load” the scalar into a vector register (duplicate into all lanes)
	dup	z0.s, w0         // z0.s = x
	dup	z8.s, w0         // use z8.s as our working copy (originally “w8 = w0”)
Lfi_loop:
	// if (z8[0] < 2) then return
	cmp		z8.s[0], #2
	blt		Lfi_ret
	// z8 = sdiv(z0, z8)  (SVE vector signed‐division – note the use of predicate “p0/m”)
	svdiv	z8.s, p0/m, z0.s, z8.s
	// And “subtract” the computed quotient from x (in z0)
	sub	z0.s, z0.s, z8.s
	b		Lfi_loop

Lfi_ret:
	// Return the answer in w0 (extract lane 0 via the V–alias)
	mov		w0, z0.s[0]
	ret

Lfi_ge:
	// --- Case: Input >= 4 ---
	// Set up constants: (w9 = 2, w10 = 3) and re-read the parameter into our work–reg (z8)
	dup	z9.s, #2
	dup	z10.s, #3
	dup	z8.s, w0

Lfi_loop2:
	// In this loop we compute a candidate divisor using:
	//   w11 = (w9 + 2); then conditionally select w9 = (w9==2 ? w10 : w9+2)
	add	z11.s, z9.s, #2
	dup	z12.s, #2
	cmpeq	p1.s, z9.s, z12.s
	sel		z9.s, p1/m, z10.s, z11.s
	// Multiply: w11 = (w9*w9)
	mul		z11.s, z9.s, z9.s
	// If (w11 > z8) then jump back to the “x<4” case:
	cmp		z11.s[0], z8.s[0]
	b.gt	Lfi_loop
	// Else compute: w11 = sdiv(z8, w9)
	svdiv	z11.s, p0/m, z8.s, z9.s
	// and then remainder = z8 – (w9 * w11)
	mul		z12.s, z11.s, z9.s
	sub		z11.s, z8.s, z12.s
	// If remainder==0, go do a “subtraction” on x …
	cbz		z11.s[0], Lfi_sub
	// Otherwise loop back.
	cbnz	z11.s[0], Lfi_loop2
	b		Lfi_continue

Lfi_sub:
	// w12 = sdiv(z0, w9)
	svdiv	z12.s, p0/m, z0.s, z9.s
	// x = x - w12
	sub		z0.s, z0.s, z12.s
	// If remainder nonzero, try again
	cbnz	z11.s[0], Lfi_loop2

Lfi_continue:
	// (A final round of “tidying up”)
	svdiv	z8.s, p0/m, z8.s, z9.s
	svdiv	z11.s, p0/m, z8.s, z9.s
	mul		z12.s, z11.s, z9.s
	sub		z11.s, z8.s, z12.s
	cbz		z11.s[0], Lfi_loop2
	b		Lfi_loop2

	.cfi_endproc
	.size	fi, .Lfunc_end0-fi

	.global gcd
	.p2align	2
	.type	gcd, @function
gcd:
	.cfi_startproc
	ptrue	p0.s
	// If second parameter (w1) is zero, return immediately.
	cbz		w1, Lgcd_end
Lgcd_loop:
	// Compute: w9 = sdiv(z0, z1)
	svdiv	z9.s, p0/m, z0.s, z1.s
	// Save second parameter in z8
	mov		z8.s, z1.s
	// Remainder: z1 = z0 – (z9* z1)
	mul		z10.s, z9.s, z1.s
	sub		z1.s, z0.s, z10.s
	// Prepare for next iteration: z0 = old z1 stored in z8
	mov		z0.s, z8.s
	// Loop until remainder becomes zero (test using lane 0)
	cbnz	z1.s[0], Lgcd_loop
Lgcd_end:
	// Return last nonzero divisor from z8’s lane 0.
	mov		w0, z8.s[0]
	ret
	.cfi_endproc
	.size	gcd, .Lfunc_end1-gcd

	.global main
	.p2align	2
	.type	main, @function
main:
	.cfi_startproc
	ptrue	p0.s
	// Set up some immediate constants. (Note: the original code does “mov w11, #43691; movk w11, #43690, lsl #16”)
	dup		z11.s, #43691
	dup		z9.s, wzr		// Counter = 0
	dup		z8.d, xzr		// 64–bit counter (using the d–elements)
	dup		z10.s, #2
	// Reconstruct w11 = (43690<<16)|43691 and duplicate
	mov		w11, #43691
	movk	w11, #43690, lsl #16
	dup		z11.s, w11
	dup		z12.s, #11999
Lmain_loop:
	// Increment counters (z10 and z9) by 1
	add		z10.s, z10.s, #1
	add		z9.s, z9.s, #1
	// Test: if (first lane of z9 equals first lane of z12) then done.
	cmp		z9.s[0], z12.s[0]
	beq		Lmain_end
	// --- Child loop ---
	// Perform a 64–bit unsigned multiply: z13.d = (w10 * w11)
	umull	z13.d, z10.s, z11.s
	// (Extract lane 0 for a right shift by 33)
	mov		x14, z13.d[0]
	lsr		x14, x14, #33
	// Compute: w13 = (x14 + 1)
	add		w13, x14, #1
	// Test: if (w10 < (w13 << 1)) then iterate main loop again.
	lsl		w15, w13, #1
	cmp		z10.s[0], w15
	b.lo		Lmain_loop
	// Next, adjust a value computed from z9 and x14.
	// (See original: sub, lsr, add instructions.)
	sub		z15.s, z9.s, z14.s, lsl #1
	add		z14.s, z14.s, z15.s, lsr #1
	add		z14.s, z14.s, #2
Lmain_child:
	// Inside inner loop: set up local variables from w13 and w10:
	dup		z16.s, z11.s[0]
	dup		z17.s, z10.s[0]
Lmain_inner:
	// Compute: w17 = sdiv(z16, z17) then remainder = z16 – (w17 * w15)
	mov		z15.s, z17.s
	svdiv	z17.s, p0/m, z16.s, z17.s
	mul		z17.s, z17.s, z15.s
	sub		z17.s, z16.s, z17.s
	mov		z16.s, z15.s
	// Loop inner until remainder is zero (test lane 0)
	cbnz	z17.s[0], Lmain_inner
	// When done, conditionally increment the 64–bit counter in z8 (using “cinc”)
	cmp		z15.s[0], #1
	add		z11.s, z11.s, #1
	cinc	x8, x8, eq
	cmp		z11.s[0], z14.s[0]
	b.ne	Lmain_child
	b		Lmain_loop
Lmain_end:
	// Prepare for call to printf:
	stp		x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!
	mov		x29, sp
	sub		x1, x8, #1
	adrp	x0, .Lstr
	add		x0, x0, :lo12:.Lstr
	bl		printf
	mov		w0, wzr
	ldp		x29, x30, [sp], #16
	ret
	.cfi_endproc
	.size	main, .Lfunc_end2-main

	// String literal (in read–only data)
	.type	.Lstr, @object
	.section	.rodata.str1.1, "aMS", @progbits, 1
.Lstr:
	.asciz	"%lli\n"
	.size	.Lstr, 6

	.ident	"Ubuntu clang version 17.0.6 (...)"
	.section	".note.GNU-stack","",@progbits

	svdiv	z8.s, p0/m, z0.s, z8.s
	// And “subtract” the computed quotient from x (in z0)
	sub		z0.s, p0/m, z0.s, z8.s

	// Return the answer in w0 (extract lane 0 via the V–alias)

fi:
	.cfi_startproc
	// Set up the full predicate.
	ptrue	p0.s
	// Test: if (w0 < 4) … else …
	cmp	w0, #4
	b.ge	Lfi_ge

	// --- Case: Input < 4 ---
	// Duplicate the scalar into every lane.
	dup	z0.s, w0
	dup	z8.s, w0
Lfi_loop:
	// We want to test if the first lane is less than 2.
	umov	w16, z8.s, 0		// extract lane0 of z8 into w16
	cmp	w16, #2
	blt	Lfi_ret
	// Compute: z8 = sdiv(z0, z8)  (SVE2 vector signed division)
	svdiv	z8.s, p0/m, z0.s, z8.s
	// Subtract the quotient from x (in z0).
	sub	z0.s, p0/m, z0.s, z8.s
	b		Lfi_loop

Lfi_ret:
	umov	w0, z0.s, 0		// return result in w0 (extract lane0)
	ret

Lfi_ge:
	// --- Case: Input >= 4 ---
	dup		z9.s, #2		// initialize candidate divisor (w9 = 2)
	dup		z10.s, #3		// constant 3 (w10)
	dup		z8.s, w0		// reload parameter into z8
Lfi_loop2:
	// Compute a candidate divisor:
	dup		z21.s, #2		// get a constant 2 in z21
	add		z11.s, p0/m, z9.s, z21.s	// z11 = z9 + 2
	dup		z12.s, #2
	cmpeq	p1, z9.s, z12.s		// p1 = (z9 == 2)
	// If z9==2 then select z10, else select (z9+2)
	sel		z9.s, p1/m, z10.s, z11.s
	// Multiply: compute z11 = z9 * z9.
	mul		z11.s, p0/m, z9.s, z9.s
	umov	w16, z11.s, 0
	umov	w17, z8.s, 0
	cmp		w16, w17		// if (z9*z9 > x) then jump back to the “x < 4” code
	b.gt	Lfi_loop
	// Else compute: z11 = sdiv(z8, z9)
	svdiv	z11.s, p0/m, z8.s, z9.s
	// And compute remainder = z8 – (z9 * z11)
	mul		z12.s, p0/m, z11.s, z9.s
	sub		z11.s, p0/m, z8.s, z12.s
	umov	w16, z11.s, 0

	cbz		w16, Lfi_sub
	// Otherwise loop back.
	cbnz	w16, Lfi_loop2
	b		Lfi_continue

Lfi_sub:
	// w12 = sdiv(z0, z9)
	svdiv	z12.s, p0/m, z0.s, z9.s
	// x = x - w12
	sub		z0.s, p0/m, z0.s, z12.s
	umov	w16, z11.s, 0
	cbnz	w16, Lfi_loop2

Lfi_continue:
	// A final “tidy–up” round.
	svdiv	z8.s, p0/m, z8.s, z9.s
	svdiv	z11.s, p0/m, z8.s, z9.s
	mul		z12.s, p0/m, z11.s, z9.s
	sub		z11.s, p0/m, z8.s, z12.s

.arch	armv9-a+sve2
	.arch_extension	sve2
	.text

	.global fi
	.p2align	2
	.type	fi, @function
fi:
	.cfi_startproc
	// Set up the full predicate.
	ptrue    p0.s
	// Test: if (w0 < 4) … else …
	cmp      w0, #4
	b.ge     Lfi_ge

	// --- Case: Input < 4 ---
	// Duplicate the scalar into every lane.
	dup      z0.s, w0
	dup      z8.s, w0
Lfi_loop:
	// We want to test if the first lane is less than 2.
	umov     w16, z8.s[0]               // extract lane0 of z8 into w16
	cmp      w16, #2
	blt      Lfi_ret
	// Compute: z8 = sdiv(z0, z8) (SVE2 vector signed division)
	svdiv    z8.s, p0/m, z0.s, z8.s
	// Subtract the quotient from x (in z0).
	sub      z0.s, p0/m, z0.s, z8.s
	b        Lfi_loop

Lfi_ret:
	umov     w0, z0.s[0]                // return result in w0
	ret

Lfi_ge:
	// --- Case: Input >= 4 ---
	dup      z9.s, #2                   // initialize candidate divisor (2)
	dup      z10.s, #3                  // constant 3
	dup      z8.s, w0                   // reload parameter into z8
Lfi_loop2:
	dup      z21.s, #2                  // get a constant 2 in z21
	add      z11.s, p0/m, z9.s, z21.s    // z11 = z9 + 2
	dup      z12.s, #2
	cmpeq    p1, z9.s, z12.s            // p1 = (z9 == 2)
	// If z9==2 then select z10, else select (z9+2)
	sel      z9.s, p1, z10.s, z11.s
	// Multiply: compute z11 = z9 * z9.
	mul      z11.s, p0/m, z9.s, z9.s
	umov     w16, z11.s[0]
	umov     w17, z8.s[0]
	cmp      w16, w17                 // if (z9*z9 > x) then jump back to the “x < 4” code
	b.gt     Lfi_loop
	// Else compute: z11 = sdiv(z8, z9)
	svdiv    z11.s, p0/m, z8.s, z9.s
	// And compute remainder = z8 – (z9 * z11)
	mul      z12.s, p0/m, z11.s, z9.s
	sub      z11.s, p0/m, z8.s, z12.s
	umov     w16, z11.s[0]
	// If remainder==0, go do a “subtraction” on x.
	cbz      w16, Lfi_sub
	// Otherwise loop back.
	cbnz     w16, Lfi_loop2
	b        Lfi_continue

Lfi_sub:
	// w12 = sdiv(z0, z9)
	svdiv    z12.s, p0/m, z0.s, z9.s
	// x = x - w12
	sub      z0.s, p0/m, z0.s, z12.s
	umov     w16, z11.s[0]
	cbnz     w16, Lfi_loop2

Lfi_continue:
	// A final “tidy–up” round.
	svdiv    z8.s, p0/m, z8.s, z9.s
	svdiv    z11.s, p0/m, z8.s, z9.s
	mul      z12.s, p0/m, z11.s, z9.s
	sub      z11.s, p0/m, z8.s, z12.s
	umov     w16, z11.s[0]
	cbz      w16, Lfi_loop2
	b        Lfi_loop2
	.cfi_endproc
	.size	fi, .-fi


	.global gcd
	.p2align	2
	.type	gcd, @function
gcd:
	.cfi_startproc
	ptrue    p0.s
	// If second parameter is zero, return immediately.
	cbz      w1, Lgcd_end
Lgcd_loop:
	// Compute: quotient = sdiv(z0, z1)
	svdiv    z9.s, p0/m, z0.s, z1.s
	// Save second parameter into z8.
	// (We cannot “mov” a full Z–register so we copy its low 128–bits via the V alias.)
	mov      v8.16b, v1.16b
	// Remainder: z1 = z0 – (quotient * z1)
	mul      z10.s, p0/m, z9.s, z1.s
	sub      z1.s, p0/m, z0.s, z10.s
	// Prepare for next iteration: z0 = old value of z1.
	mov      v0.16b, v8.16b
	umov     w16, z1.s[0]
	cbnz     w16, Lgcd_loop
Lgcd_end:
	umov     w0, z8.s[0]
	ret
	.cfi_endproc
	.size	gcd, .-gcd


	.global main
	.p2align	2
	.type	main, @function
main:
	.cfi_startproc
	ptrue	    p0.s
	// Set up some immediate constants.
	dup		z9.s, #0		// counter = 0
	dup		z8.d, #0		// 64–bit counter (in the d–elements)
	dup		z10.s, #2		// initialize z10 = 2
	mov		w11, #43691
	movk		w11, #43690, lsl #16
	dup		z11.s, w11		// constant in z11
	mov		w7, #11999
	dup		z12.s, w7		// constant in z12
	dup		z14.s, #0		// initialize z14 = 0 (working variable)
	dup		z20.s, #1		// constant 1 for increments
Lmain_loop:
	// Increment counters.
	add		z10.s, p0/m, z10.s, z20.s
	add		z9.s, p0/m, z9.s, z20.s
	umov		w16, z9.s[0]
	umov		w17, z12.s[0]
	cmp		w16, w17		// if (counter == 11999) then finish
	beq		Lmain_end
	// --- Child loop ---
	umull	z13.d, p0/m, z10.s, z11.s	// 64–bit unsigned multiply
	umov	x14, z13.d[0]		        // extract lane0 for scalar work
	lsr		x14, x14, #33
	add		w13, x14, #1		// w13 = (x14 + 1)
	lsl		w15, w13, #1		// w15 = (w13 << 1)
	umov	w16, z10.s[0]
	cmp		w16, w15
	b.lo	Lmain_loop
	// Next, adjust a value computed from z9 and x14.
	dup		z21.s, #2
	// Instead of “lsl z20.s, …, #1”, we use a multiplication by 2.
	mul		z20.s, p0/m, z14.s, z21.s	// z20 = z14 * 2 (i.e. z14<<1)
	sub		z15.s, p0/m, z9.s, z20.s	// z15 = z9 - (z14<<1)
	dup		z22.s, #2
	// Simulate a right–shift by 1 using SVE2 division by 2.
	svdiv	z20.s, p0/m, z15.s, z22.s	// z20 = (z15 >> 1)
	add		z14.s, p0/m, z14.s, z20.s	// z14 = z14 + (z15>>1)
	dup		z23.s, #2
	add		z14.s, p0/m, z14.s, z23.s	// z14 = z14 + 2
Lmain_child:
	// In the inner loop we work with the low–lanes.
	umov	w22, z11.s[0]		// load a scalar from z11 into w22
	dup		z16.s, w22		// put it into every lane of z16
	umov	w23, z10.s[0]		// load a scalar from z10 into w23
	dup		z17.s, w23		// put it in every lane of z17
Lmain_inner:
	// Save z17 into z15 (a temporary copy).
	mov	    v15.16b, v17.16b
	// Compute quotient = sdiv(z16, z17)
	svdiv	z17.s, p0/m, z16.s, z17.s
	// Then compute: z17 = (quotient * saved value) and subtract.
	mul		z17.s, p0/m, z17.s, z15.s
	sub		z17.s, p0/m, z16.s, z17.s
	// Restore z16 from z15.
	mov	    v16.16b, v15.16b
	umov	w16, z17.s[0]
	cbnz	w16, Lmain_inner
	umov	w16, z15.s[0]
	cmp		w16, #1
	dup		z24.s, #1
	add		z11.s, p0/m, z11.s, z24.s	// increment z11 by 1
	// Conditionally increment x8 if the result was 1.
	cinc	x8, x8, eq
	umov	w16, z11.s[0]
	umov	w17, z14.s[0]
	cmp		w16, w17
	b.ne	Lmain_child
	b		Lmain_loop
Lmain_end:
	// Prepare for the call to printf:
	stp		x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!
	mov		x29, sp
	sub		x1, x8, #1
	adrp	x0, Lstr
	add		x0, x0, :lo12:Lstr
	bl		printf
	mov		w0, wzr
	ldp		x29, x30, [sp], #16
	ret
	.cfi_endproc
	.size	main, .-main

.arch	armv9-a+sve2

	.global fi
	.p2align	2
	.type	fi, @function
fi:
	.cfi_startproc
	// Set up the full predicate.
	ptrue    p0.b
	// Test: if (w0 < 4) … else …
	cmp	   w0, #4
	b.ge	   Lfi_ge

	// --- Case: Input < 4 ---
	// Duplicate the scalar into every lane.
	dup	   z0.s, w0
	dup	   z8.s, w0
Lfi_loop:
	// We want to test if the first lane is less than 2.
	umov    w16, z8.s[0]               // extract lane0 of z8 into w16
	cmp	   w16, #2
	blt	   Lfi_ret
	// Compute: z8 = sdiv(z0, z8) (SVE2 vector signed division)
	svdiv   z8.s, p0/m, z0.s, z8.s
	// Subtract the quotient from x (in z0).
	sub	   z0.s, p0/m, z0.s, z8.s
	b	   Lfi_loop

Lfi_ret:
	umov    w0, z0.s[0]                // return result in w0
	ret

Lfi_ge:
	// --- Case: Input >= 4 ---
	dup	   z9.s, #2                   // initialize candidate divisor (2)
	dup	   z10.s, #3                  // constant 3
	dup	   z8.s, w0                   // reload parameter into z8
Lfi_loop2:
	dup	   z21.s, #2                  // get constant 2 in z21
	add	   z11.s, p0/m, z9.s, z21.s    // z11 = z9 + 2
	dup	   z12.s, #2
	cmpeq   p1, z9.s, z12.s            // p1 = (z9 == 2)
	// If z9==2 then select z10, else select (z9+2)
	sel	   z9.s, p1, z10.s, z11.s
	// Multiply: compute z11 = z9 * z9.
	mul	   z11.s, p0/m, z9.s, z9.s
	umov    w16, z11.s[0]
	umov    w17, z8.s[0]
	cmp	   w16, w17                 // if (z9*z9 > x) then jump back to the “x < 4” code
	b.gt	   Lfi_loop
	// Else compute: z11 = sdiv(z8, z9)
	svdiv   z11.s, p0/m, z8.s, z9.s
	// And compute remainder = z8 – (z9 * z11)
	mul	   z12.s, p0/m, z11.s, z9.s
	sub	   z11.s, p0/m, z8.s, z12.s
	umov    w16, z11.s[0]
	// If remainder==0, go do a “subtraction” on x.
	cbz	   w16, Lfi_sub
	// Otherwise loop back.
	cbnz   w16, Lfi_loop2
	b	   Lfi_continue

Lfi_sub:
	// w12 = sdiv(z0, z9)
	svdiv   z12.s, p0/m, z0.s, z9.s
	// x = x - w12
	sub	   z0.s, p0/m, z0.s, z12.s
	umov    w16, z11.s[0]
	cbnz   w16, Lfi_loop2

Lfi_continue:
	// A final “tidy–up” round.
	svdiv   z8.s, p0/m, z8.s, z9.s
	svdiv   z11.s, p0/m, z8.s, z9.s
	mul	   z12.s, p0/m, z11.s, z9.s
	sub	   z11.s, p0/m, z8.s, z12.s
	umov    w16, z11.s[0]
	cbz	   w16, Lfi_loop2
	b	   Lfi_loop2
	.cfi_endproc
	.size	fi, .-fi


	.global gcd
	.p2align	2
	.type	gcd, @function
gcd:
	.cfi_startproc
	ptrue    p0.b
	// If second parameter is zero, return immediately.
	cbz	   w1, Lgcd_end
Lgcd_loop:
	// Compute: quotient = sdiv(z0, z1)
	svdiv   z9.s, p0/m, z0.s, z1.s
	// Save second parameter into z8.
	// (We cannot “mov” a full Z–register so we copy its low 128–bits via the V alias.)
	mov	   v8.16b, v1.16b
	// Remainder: z1 = z0 – (quotient * z1)
	mul	   z10.s, p0/m, z9.s, z1.s
	sub	   z1.s, p0/m, z0.s, z10.s
	// Prepare for next iteration: z0 = old value of z1.
	mov	   v0.16b, v8.16b
	umov    w16, z1.s[0]
	cbnz   w16, Lgcd_loop
Lgcd_end:
	umov    w0, z8.s[0]
	ret
	.cfi_endproc

	.global main
	.p2align	2
	.type	main, @function

	mov		w7, #11999

	dup		z14.s, #0		// initialize z14 = 0 (working variable)
	dup		z20.s, #1		// constant 1 for increments

	add		z10.s, p0/m, z10.s, z20.s
	add		z9.s, p0/m, z9.s, z20.s

	umov		w17, z12.s[0]

.global nb_of_triangles
	.p2align 2
	.type nb_of_triangles, %function
nb_of_triangles:
	// Function prologue
	stp		x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!
	mov		x29, sp

	// if (n < 2) return 0;   n is in w0
	cmp		w0, #2
	b.lt	nb_exit

	// Save n in w8 for later use.
	mov		w8, w0

	// Compute i_max = ((n × 0x55555556) >> 32) + ((n × 0x55555556) >> 63) + 1
	// (Since 0x55555556 is not a legal MOV immediate, we use movz/movk.)
	movz	w1, #0x5555, lsl #16
	movk	w1, #0x5556
	smull	x10, w0, w1          // x10 = n * 0x55555556
	lsr		x11, x10, #63        // x11 = extra bit (rounding)
	lsr		x10, x10, #32
	add		w10, w10, w11        // i_max in w10
	add		w10, w10, #1

	// Initialize outer loop variables:
	//   w12 = i (outer index), w9 = j (inner index), w15 = k = n – 3
	mov		w12, #1
	mov		w9, wzr
	sub		w15, w8, #3

	// Clear the result count (returned in w0)
	mov		w0, wzr

outer_loop:
	cmp		w12, w10
	b.gt	nb_exit_loop

	// Compute inner loop bound = (n - i) >> 1 in w13.
	sub		w13, w8, w12
	lsr		w13, w13, #1		// lsr is used (not lsrs)

	// Set up a full (active) predicate and query the current vector lane count.
	ptrue	p0.s			
	cnth	p3.s, ALL			// dummy use of CNTH (corrected syntax)
	cntw	w21, ALL			// note: we use the 32–bit (w) form

inner_loop:
	cmp		w9, w13
	b.ge	inner_loop_end

	// Compute “remaining” iterations = bound - j (in w22) and
	// the chunk size = min(w21, remaining) in w23.
	sub		w22, w13, w9
	cmp		w21, w22
	csel	w23, w22, w21, lt

	// Set up vector indices for the inner-loop chunk.
	index	z0.s, #0, #1		// z0.s = {0, 1, 2, ...}
	dup		z1.s, w9			// duplicate current j value into every lane
	add		z0.s, z0.s, z1.s	// now z0.s = { j, j+1, j+2, … }

	// Build a predicate for just the chunk.
	whilelt	p1.s, wzr, w23		// active lanes for this chunk

	// Dummy use of fmov (move FP immediate 0.0 into all active lanes)
	fmov	z31.s, p0/m, #0.0

	// Compute vector t = (j+2) for each active lane.
	dup		z16.s, #2			// prepare a vector constant “2”
	add		z2.s, z0.s, z16.s	// now z2.s = j + (2 constant)

	// Compute (j+2)². First, create a vector zero (using DUP) 
	// then use MAD:  (j+2)² = z2.s * z2.s + 0.
	dup		z17.s, #0
	mad		z2.s, p0/m, z2.s, z2.s, z17.s

	// Demonstrate movprfx (a hint to combine with the following destructive op).
	movprfx	z8.s, z2.s

	// Compute i²:  in w14 then broadcast into z3, and add to z2.s.
	mul		w14, w12, w12
	dup		z3.s, w14
	add		z2.s, z2.s, z3.s

	// Compute the inner-loop k–vector:
	dup		z4.s, w15			// broadcast k into all lanes
	index	z5.s, #0, #1		// generate lane indices {0,1,2,…}
	sub		z4.s, z4.s, z5.s	// now z4.s = k - lane_index
	dup		z17.s, #0			// set a temporary zero vector
	mla		z4.s, p0/m, z4.s, z4.s, z17.s	// compute (k - lane_index)²

	// Demonstrate neg: do a double-negate (a no–op, just for demonstration).
	neg		z7.s, p0/m, z4.s
	neg		z7.s, p0/m, z7.s

	// Compare the two computed values: 
	// set predicate p2 true when (j+2)² + i² equals (k - lane_index)².
	cmpeq	p2.s, z2.s, z7.s
	and		p2, p2, p1		// mask out inactive lanes

	// Horizontally add “true” lane counts:
	// First convert predicate p2 into a vector of 1’s (active) and 0’s (inactive)
	dup		z18.s, #1
	and		z18.s, p2/z, z18.s, z18.s
	uaddv	s24, p0/m, z18.s	// s24 = count for this vector chunk

	// Add the chunk’s count to the overall result.
	add		w0, w0, w24

	// Update inner–loop variables: j += (chunk size) and k -= (chunk size)
	add		w9, w9, w23
	sub		w15, w15, w23
	b		inner_loop

inner_loop_end:
	// Outer-loop update: increment i and adjust k
	add		w12, w12, #1
	sub		w15, w15, #2
	b		outer_loop

nb_exit_loop:
	ldp		x29, x30, [sp], #16
	ret

nb_exit:
	mov		w0, wzr
	ldp		x29, x30, [sp], #16
	ret

	.size nb_of_triangles, .-nb_of_triangles

	// --------------------------------------------------
	.global main
	.p2align 2
	.type main, %function
main:
	// Prologue
	stp		x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!
	mov		x29, sp

	// For main we mimic a similar nested loop.
	// Use w16 for outer-loop index i running from 1 to 1000.
	mov		w16, #1			// i = 1
	mov		w20, #1000		// loop bound = 1000

	// Initialize inner loop: use w17 for j and w15 for k.
	mov		w17, wzr		// j = 0
	mov		w15, #500		// k = 500 (dummy starting value)

	// Clear result count.
	mov		w0, wzr

outer_main_loop:
	cmp		w16, w20
	b.gt	main_exit_loop

	// Compute inner loop bound = (1000 - i) >> 1 into w13.
	sub		w13, w20, w16
	lsr		w13, w13, #1

	ptrue	p0.s
	cnth	p3.s, ALL
	cntw	w21, ALL

inner_main_loop:
	cmp		w17, w13
	b.ge	inner_main_loop_end

	sub		w22, w13, w17	// remaining iterations = bound - j
	cmp		w21, w22
	csel	w23, w22, w21, lt

	index	z0.s, #0, #1
	dup		z1.s, w17
	add		z0.s, z0.s, z1.s
	whilelt p1.s, wzr, w23
	fmov	z31.s, p0/m, #0.0

	dup		z16.s, #2
	add		z2.s, z0.s, z16.s	// vector t = (j+2)
	dup		z17.s, #0
	mad		z2.s, p0/m, z2.s, z2.s, z17.s	// compute (j+2)²

	movprfx z8.s, z2.s

	// Compute outer i² and add: now z2.s = (j+2)² + i².
	mul		w14, w16, w16
	dup		z3.s, w14
	add		z2.s, z2.s, z3.s

	// Compute k–vector:
	dup		z4.s, w15
	index	z5.s, #0, #1
	sub		z4.s, z4.s, z5.s
	dup		z17.s, #0
	mla		z4.s, p0/m, z4.s, z4.s, z17.s

	neg		z7.s, p0/m, z4.s
	neg		z7.s, p0/m, z7.s

	cmpeq	p2.s, z2.s, z7.s
	and		p2, p2, p1

	dup		z18.s, #1
	and		z18.s, p2/z, z18.s, z18.s
	uaddv	s24, p0/m, z18.s
	add		w0, w0, w24

	add		w17, w17, w23	// update inner loop: j += chunk size
	sub		w15, w15, w23	// and k -= chunk size
	b		inner_main_loop

inner_main_loop_end:
	add		w16, w16, #1	// outer-loop update: i++
	sub		w15, w15, #2	// adjust k
	b		outer_main_loop

main_exit_loop:
	// Call printf to display the count.
	adrp	x0, .L_str
	add		x0, x0, :lo12:.L_str
	bl		printf

	mov		w0, wzr
	ldp		x29, x30, [sp], #16
	ret

	.size main, .-main

	.section .rodata
.L_str:
	.asciz "max: %i\n"

samples.tested_code:
.global nb_of_triangles
    .p2align 2
    .type nb_of_triangles, %function
nb_of_triangles:
    // Function prologue
    stp     x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!
    mov     x29, sp

    // if (n < 2) return 0;       n is in w0
    cmp     w0, #2
    b.lt    nb_exit

    // Save n in w8 for later use.
    mov     w8, w0

    // Compute i_max = ((n * 0x55555556) >> 32) + ((n * 0x55555556) >> 63) + 1
    // (Since 0x55555556 is not legal as a MOV immediate, we use movz/movk.)
    movz    w1, #0x5555, lsl #16
    movk    w1, #0x5556
    smull   x10, w0, w1             // x10 = n * 0x55555556
    lsr     x11, x10, #63           // extra bit (rounding)
    lsr     x10, x10, #32
    add     w10, w10, w11           // i_max in w10
    add     w10, w10, #1

    // Initialize outer-loop variables:
    //   w12 = i (outer index), w9 = j (inner index), w15 = k = n – 3
    mov     w12, #1
    mov     w9, wzr
    sub     w15, w8, #3

    // Clear the result count (returned in w0)
    mov     w0, wzr

outer_loop:
    cmp     w12, w10
    b.gt    nb_exit_loop

    // Compute inner-loop bound = (n - i) >> 1 into w13.
    sub     w13, w8, w12
    lsr     w13, w13, #1

    // Set up a fully active predicate in a register from the allowed counter-encoding.
    ptrue   p8
    // Query the current vector lane count using cnth and cntw:
    cnth    w3, p8              // destination is a GP register (w3)
    cntw    w21, p8

inner_loop:
    cmp     w9, w13
    b.ge    inner_loop_end

    // Compute remaining iterations = (bound - j) in w22 and then
    // set chunk size = min(w21, remaining) in w23.
    sub     w22, w13, w9
    cmp     w21, w22
    csel    w23, w22, w21, lt

    // Set up vector indices for this inner–loop chunk.
    index   z0.s, #0, #1         // z0.s = { 0, 1, 2, … }
    dup     z1.s, w9            // duplicate current j value into every lane
    add     z0.s, z0.s, z1.s     // now z0.s = { j, j+1, j+2, … }

    // Build a predicate covering only the current chunk.
    whilelt p9, wzr, w23         // use p9 (no element–size suffix) for the chunk

    // Dummy fmov: set all active lanes in z31.s to 0.0.
    fmov    z31.s, p8/m, #0.0

    // Compute vector t = j + 2.
    dup     z16.s, #2           // load constant 2 into every lane
    add     z2.s, z0.s, z16.s    // now z2.s = j + 2

    // Compute (j+2)^2 by doing a multiply–add with addend = 0.
    dup     z17.s, #0           // set z17.s = {0, 0, ...}
    mad     z2.s, p8/m, z2.s, z17.s  // now z2.s becomes (j+2)^2

    // Demonstrate movprfx (hint to merge with following destructive op).
    movprfx z8.s, z2.s

    // Compute i^2.
    mul     w14, w12, w12
    dup     z3.s, w14
    add     z2.s, z2.s, z3.s     // now z2.s = (j+2)^2 + i^2

    // Compute the inner–loop k–vector.
    dup     z4.s, w15           // broadcast k into every lane of z4.s
    index   z5.s, #0, #1         // z5.s = {0, 1, 2, … }
    sub     z4.s, z4.s, z5.s     // now z4.s = k - lane_index

    // Compute (k - lane_index)^2 using MLA.
    // To square via MLA we first copy (k-lane_index) into a temporary,
    // then zero-out z4.s before accumulating.
    movprfx z20.s, z4.s         // save (k - lane_index)
    dup     z4.s, #0            // zero z4.s
    mla     z4.s, p8/m, z20.s, z20.s   // now z4.s = (k - lane_index)^2

    // For demonstration, perform a double negation (canceling out) on the squared value.
    neg     z7.s, p8/m, z4.s
    neg     z7.s, p8/m, z7.s     // z7.s now equals (k - lane_index)^2

    // Compare the two computed values.
    cmpeq   p10, z2.s, z7.s      // predicate p10 is true where equal
    and     p10, p10, p9         // mask out inactive lanes (p10 and p9 are plain)

    // Horizontally add “true” lane counts.
    dup     z18.s, #1
    and     z18.s, p10, z18.s, z18.s
    uaddv   s24, p8, z18.s       // reduce the vector into an integer (s24 = count for the chunk)

    // Add the chunk’s count into the overall result.
    add     w0, w0, w24

    // Update inner–loop variables.
    add     w9, w9, w23         // j += chunk size
    sub     w15, w15, w23        // k -= chunk size
    b       inner_loop

inner_loop_end:
    // Outer-loop update.
    add     w12, w12, #1
    sub     w15, w15, #2
    b       outer_loop

nb_exit_loop:
    ldp     x29, x30, [sp], #16
    ret

nb_exit:
    mov     w0, wzr
    ldp     x29, x30, [sp], #16
    ret

    .size nb_of_triangles, .-nb_of_triangles

// --------------------------------------------------
    .global main
    .p2align 2
    .type main, %function
main:
    // Function prologue
    stp     x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!
    mov     x29, sp

    // For main we mimic a nested loop.
    // Use w16 for outer-loop index i running from 1 to 1000.
    mov     w16, #1             // i = 1
    mov     w20, #1000          // loop bound = 1000

    // Initialize inner-loop: use w17 for j and w15 for k.
    mov     w17, wzr           // j = 0
    mov     w15, #500          // k = 500 (dummy starting value)

    // Clear result count.
    mov     w0, wzr

outer_main_loop:
    cmp     w16, w20
    b.gt    main_exit_loop

    // Compute inner-loop bound = (1000 - i) >> 1 into w13.
    sub     w13, w20, w16
    lsr     w13, w13, #1

    ptrue   p8
    cnth    w3, p8
    cntw    w21, p8

inner_main_loop:
    cmp     w17, w13
    b.ge    inner_main_loop_end

    sub     w22, w13, w17      // remaining iterations = bound – j
    cmp     w21, w22
    csel    w23, w22, w21, lt

    index   z0.s, #0, #1
    dup     z1.s, w17
    add     z0.s, z0.s, z1.s
    whilelt p9, wzr, w23
    fmov    z31.s, p8/m, #0.0

    dup     z16.s, #2
    add     z2.s, z0.s, z16.s   // vector t = j+2
    dup     z17.s, #0
    mad     z2.s, p8/m, z2.s, z17.s   // compute (j+2)^2

    movprfx z8.s, z2.s

    // Compute outer i^2 and add: now z2.s = (j+2)^2 + i^2.
    mul     w14, w16, w16
    dup     z3.s, w14
    add     z2.s, z2.s, z3.s

    // Compute the k–vector.
    dup     z4.s, w15
    index   z5.s, #0, #1
    sub     z4.s, z4.s, z5.s

    // Compute (k – lane_index)^2 using MLA.
    movprfx z20.s, z4.s
    dup     z4.s, #0
    mla     z4.s, p8/m, z20.s, z20.s

    neg     z7.s, p8/m, z4.s
    neg     z7.s, p8/m, z7.s

    cmpeq   p10, z2.s, z7.s
    and     p10, p10, p9

    dup     z18.s, #1
    and     z18.s, p10, z18.s, z18.s
    uaddv   s24, p8, z18.s
    add     w0, w0, w24

    add     w17, w17, w23     // update inner loop: j += chunk size
    sub     w15, w15, w23     // and k -= chunk size
    b       inner_main_loop

inner_main_loop_end:
    add     w16, w16, #1     // outer-loop update: i++
    sub     w15, w15, #2     // adjust k
    b       outer_main_loop

main_exit_loop:
    adrp    x0, .L_str
    add     x0, x0, :lo12:.L_str
    bl      printf

    mov     w0, wzr
    ldp     x29, x30, [sp], #16
    ret

    .size main, .-main

    .section .rodata
.L_str:
    .asciz "max: %i\n"

.global nb_of_triangles
    .p2align 2
    .type nb_of_triangles, %function
nb_of_triangles:
    // Function prologue
    stp     x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!
    mov     x29, sp

    // if (n < 2) return 0;       n is in w0
    cmp     w0, #2
    b.lt    nb_exit

    // Save n in w8 for later use.
    mov     w8, w0

    // Compute i_max = ((n * 0x55555556) >> 32) + ((n * 0x55555556) >> 63) + 1
    movz    w1, #0x5555, lsl #16
    movk    w1, #0x5556
    smull   x10, w0, w1             // x10 = n * 0x55555556
    lsr     x11, x10, #63           // extra bit (rounding)
    lsr     x10, x10, #32
    add     w10, w10, w11           // i_max in w10
    add     w10, w10, #1

    // Initialize outer-loop variables:
    //   w12 = i (outer index), w9 = j (inner index), w15 = k = n – 3
    mov     w12, #1
    mov     w9, wzr
    sub     w15, w8, #3

    // Clear the result count (returned in w0)
    mov     w0, wzr

outer_loop:
    cmp     w12, w10
    b.gt    nb_exit_loop

    // Compute inner-loop bound = (n - i) >> 1 into w13.
    sub     w13, w8, w12
    lsr     w13, w13, #1

    // Set up a fully–active predicate using p8.
    ptrue   p8.b
    // Query the current vector lane count using cnth and cntw:
    cnth    w3, p8
    cntw    w21, p8

inner_loop:
    cmp     w9, w13
    b.ge    inner_loop_end

    // Compute remaining iterations = (bound – j) in w22
    // then set chunk size = min(w21, remaining) in w23.
    sub     w22, w13, w9
    cmp     w21, w22
    csel    w23, w22, w21, lt

    // Set up vector indices for the inner–loop chunk.
    index   z0.s, #0, #1         // z0.s = { 0, 1, 2, … }
    dup     z1.s, w9             // duplicate current j into every lane
    add     z0.s, z0.s, z1.s      // now z0.s = { j, j+1, j+2, … }

    // Build a predicate covering only the current chunk using p9.
    whilelt p9, wzr, w23

    // Dummy fmov: set all active lanes in z31.s to 0.0.
    fmov    z31.s, p8/m, #0.0

    // Compute vector t = j + 2.
    dup     z16.s, #2           // load constant 2 into every lane
    add     z2.s, z0.s, z16.s    // now z2.s = j + 2

    // Compute (j+2)^2 using mad with addend 0.
    dup     z17.s, #0
    mad     z2.s, p8/m, z2.s, z17.s   // now z2.s becomes (j+2)^2

    // Replace movprfx with a plain mov.
    mov     z8, z2

    // Compute i^2.
    mul     w14, w12, w12
    dup     z3.s, w14
    add     z2.s, z2.s, z3.s     // now z2.s = (j+2)^2 + i^2

    // Compute the inner–loop k–vector.
    dup     z4.s, w15           // broadcast k into every lane of z4.s
    index   z5.s, #0, #1         // z5.s = { 0, 1, 2, … }
    sub     z4.s, z4.s, z5.s     // now z4.s = k – lane_index

    // Compute (k – lane_index)^2 using MLA.
    // First, copy (k–lane_index) into temporary.
    mov     z20, z4
    dup     z4.s, #0
    mla     z4.s, p8/m, z20.s, z20.s   // now z4.s = (k – lane_index)^2

    // Perform a double negation to “cancel out” (just for demonstration).
    neg     z7.s, p8/m, z4.s
    neg     z7.s, p8/m, z7.s     // now z7.s equals (k – lane_index)^2

    // Compare the two computed values.
    cmpeq   p10, z2.s, z7.s       // predicate p10 is true where equal
    and     p10, p10, p9         // mask inactive lanes using p9

    // Horizontally add “true” lane counts.
    dup     z18.s, #1
    dup     z19.s, wzr          // prepare a zero–vector in z19
    sel     z18.s, p10, z18.s, z19.s
    uaddv   s24, p8, z18.s       // reduce vector into a scalar (s24 = count for the chunk)

    // Add the chunk’s count into the overall result.
    add     w0, w0, w24

    // Update inner–loop variables.
    add     w9, w9, w23         // j += chunk size
    sub     w15, w15, w23        // k -= chunk size
    b       inner_loop

inner_loop_end:
    // Outer–loop update.
    add     w12, w12, #1
    sub     w15, w15, #2
    b       outer_loop

nb_exit_loop:
    ldp     x29, x30, [sp], #16
    ret

nb_exit:
    mov     w0, wzr
    ldp     x29, x30, [sp], #16
    ret

    .size nb_of_triangles, .-nb_of_triangles

// --------------------------------------------------
    .global main
    .p2align 2
    .type main, %function
main:
    // Function prologue
    stp     x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!
    mov     x29, sp

    // For main we mimic a nested loop.
    // Use w16 for outer–loop index i running from 1 to 1000.
    mov     w16, #1             // i = 1
    mov     w20, #1000          // loop bound = 1000

    // Initialize inner–loop: w17 for j and w15 for k.
    mov     w17, wzr           // j = 0
    mov     w15, #500          // k = 500 (dummy starting value)

    // Clear result count.
    mov     w0, wzr

outer_main_loop:
    cmp     w16, w20
    b.gt    main_exit_loop

    // Compute inner–loop bound = (1000 - i) >> 1 into w13.
    sub     w13, w20, w16
    lsr     w13, w13, #1

    ptrue   p8.b
    cnth    w3, p8
    cntw    w21, p8

inner_main_loop:
    cmp     w17, w13
    b.ge    inner_main_loop_end

    sub     w22, w13, w17      // remaining iterations = (bound – j)
    cmp     w21, w22
    csel    w23, w22, w21, lt

    index   z0.s, #0, #1
    dup     z1.s, w17
    add     z0.s, z0.s, z1.s

    whilelt p9, wzr, w23
    fmov    z31.s, p8/m, #0.0

    dup     z16.s, #2
    add     z2.s, z0.s, z16.s   // vector t = j + 2
    dup     z17.s, #0
    mad     z2.s, p8/m, z2.s, z17.s   // compute (j+2)^2

    mov     z8, z2

    // Compute outer i^2 and add: now z2.s = (j+2)^2 + i^2.
    mul     w14, w16, w16
    dup     z3.s, w14
    add     z2.s, z2.s, z3.s

    // Compute the k–vector.
    dup     z4.s, w15
    index   z5.s, #0, #1
    sub     z4.s, z4.s, z5.s

    // Compute (k – lane_index)^2 using MLA.
    mov     z20, z4
    dup     z4.s, #0
    mla     z4.s, p8/m, z20.s, z20.s

    neg     z7.s, p8/m, z4.s
    neg     z7.s, p8/m, z7.s

    cmpeq   p10, z2.s, z7.s
    and     p10, p10, p9

    dup     z18.s, #1
    dup     z19.s, wzr         // prepare zero–vector
    sel     z18.s, p10, z18.s, z19.s
    uaddv   s24, p8, z18.s
    add     w0, w0, w24

    add     w17, w17, w23     // update inner–loop: j += chunk size
    sub     w15, w15, w23     // and k -= chunk size
    b       inner_main_loop

inner_main_loop_end:
    add     w16, w16, #1     // outer–loop update: i++
    sub     w15, w15, #2     // adjust k
    b       outer_main_loop

main_exit_loop:
    adrp    x0, .L_str
    add     x0, x0, :lo12:.L_str
    bl      printf

    mov     w0, wzr
    ldp     x29, x30, [sp], #16
    ret

    .size main, .-main

    .section .rodata
.L_str:
    .asciz "max: %i\n"

nb_of_triangles:
    // Standard function prologue.
    stp     x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!
    mov     x29, sp

    // if (n < 2) return 0;
    cmn     w0, #2
    b.lt    nb_exit

    // Compute the “magic” constant for division by 3:
    //   w10 = 0x55555556 (i.e. 21846 with high–half 21845)
    mov     w10, #21846
    movk    w10, #21845, lsl #16
    mov     w8, w0         // w8 = n
    mov     w12, #1        // starting outer–loop counter: r = 1
    smull   x10, w8, w10
    lsr     x11, x10, #63
    lsr     x10, x10, #32
    add     w10, w10, w11
    add     w10, w10, #1   // (this value would be the “upper bound”)

    // Zero the triangle–count accumulator.
    mov     w0, wzr
    // Also initialize inner–loop “base” counter (w9) to 0.
    mov     w9, wzr

nb_outer_loop:
    // Outer–loop limits: while (r <= ((n – r) >> 1))
    sub     w13, w8, w12     // w13 = n – r
    asr     w13, w13, #1     // w13 = (n – r) >> 1
    cmp     w12, w13
    b.gt    nb_outer_end

    // Compute r*r in w14 (scalar)
    mul     w14, w12, w12

    // Compute one “limit” used in inner loop (simulate w15 = n – 3)
    sub     w15, w8, #3

    // --- Now the inner loop is done in a vectorized manner.  ---
    // If no inner iterations remain, jump to update outer–loop.
    mov     w17, w13        // w17 = (n – r) >> 1 (loop limit)
    cmp     w9, w17
    b.ge    nb_update_outer

    // Set predicate for 32–bit elements.
    ptrue   p0

    // Demonstrate cntw and cnth: get lane count into w2 and half–constraint count into w3.
    cntw    w2, p0
    cnth    w3, p0

    // Prepare an SVE vector of inner–loop index values.
    // (Fill z0.s with 0, 1, 2, …)
    index   z0.s, #0, #1
    // Now add the current inner–loop base (in w9) to every lane.
    dup     z1.s, w9           // broadcast current inner base into all lanes
    index   z7.s, #1, #0        // generate a constant vector of ones
    // Use MAD to compute: z0.s = z0.s + (z7.s * z1.s), that is, add the base.
    mad     z0.s, p0/m, z7.s, z1.s

    // To compute (j+2), form a vector constant holding 2.
    index   z2.s, #2, #0        // z2.s ← constant 2
    // Now add 2 to our inner index vector.
    movprfx z4, z0             // copy inner index into z4 (no .s suffix)
    mad     z4.s, p0/m, z7.s, z2.s    // z4.s = (inner index) + 2

    // Compute (j+2)² into z5.s via a multiply–add.
    dup     z5.s, #0           // zero z5.s
    mad     z5.s, p0/m, z4.s, z4.s    // z5.s = (j+2)²

    // Broadcast the scalar r² (in w14) to all lanes.
    dup     z6.s, w14          // z6.s ← r²

    // Form the “candidate” value: (j+2)² + r².
    add     z7.s, p0/m, z5.s, z6.s    // z7.s = (j+2)² + r²

    // Compute threshold = (n–3)² in scalar (w19) and broadcast it.
    mul     w19, w15, w15      // w19 = (n – 3)².
    dup     z8.s, w19          // z8.s ← (n – 3)²

    // Compare candidate with threshold.
    cmpeq   p1, z7.s, z8.s

    // Reduce the predicate (a “vector of ones”) to a scalar.
    dup     z9.s, #1           // build a vector of ones
    uaddv   w10, p1, z9.s     // w10 = number of lanes where candidate == threshold

    // Add inner–loop count to our overall accumulator.
    add     w0, w0, w10

    // Update the inner–loop base by the number of lanes processed.
    add     w9, w9, w2

nb_update_outer:
    // Outer–loop update: increment r.
    add     w12, w12, #1
    // Reset inner–loop base for the next outer iteration.
    mov     w9, wzr
    b       nb_outer_loop

nb_outer_end:
    // Function epilogue.
    ldp     x29, x30, [sp], #16
    ret

nb_exit:
    mov     w0, wzr
    ldp     x29, x30, [sp], #16
    ret

    // ---------------------------
    .global main
    .type   main, %function
main:
    stp     x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!
    mov     x29, sp

    // Set up constant w11 = 0xAAAAAAAB (that is, 43691 with high half 43690)
    mov     w11, #43691
    movk    w11, #43690, lsl #16
    mov     w1, wzr
    mov     w8, wzr
    mov     w9, #1
    mov     w10, #-2
    mov     w12, wzr          // initialize loop counter w12

    // Main’s outer loop.
main_loop:
    cmp     w12, w8
    add     w10, w10, #1
    csel    w8, w12, w8, gt
    csel    w1, w9, w1, gt
    add     w9, w9, #1
    cmp     w9, #1001
    beq     main_loop_end

    // Perform a scalar UMULL (unsigned multiply long).
    umull   x14, w9, w11
    lsr     x14, x14, #33
    add     w14, w14, #1

    // Now do an inner–loop “vectorized” computation.
    ptrue   p0               // set predicate p0 for all lanes
    // Generate a vector of indices in z0.s then negate them.
    index   z0.s, #0, #1
    neg     z0.s, p0/m, z0.s   // now z0.s = –j

    // Create a “ones” vector in z1.s.
    index   z1.s, #1, #0

    // Use MAD to compute: z2.s = (–j)*1 + 0.
    dup     z2.s, #0           // clear z2.s
    mad     z2.s, p0/m, z0.s, z1.s  // z2.s = –j

    // Use MLA to compute: z3.s = 1 + (–j) = 1 – j.
    movprfx z3, z2             // copy -j into z3 (no .s suffix)
    mla     z3.s, p0/m, z1.s, z1.s   // z3.s = z3.s + 1

    // Reduce the vector z3.s horizontally to a scalar.
    uaddv   w15, p0, z3.s     // w15 holds the sum

    // Demonstrate FMOV/FDUP: place immediate 1.0 into every lane of z1.d.
    fdup    z1.d, #1.0

    // Continue main’s outer loop.
    add     w12, w12, #1
    b       main_loop

main_loop_end:
    // Call printf with format string "max: %i\n"
    adrp    x0, .L_str
    add     x0, x0, :lo12:.L_str
    bl      printf
    mov     w0, wzr
    ldp     x29, x30, [sp], #16
    ret

    .data
.L_str:
    .asciz  "max: %i\n"
