// This file is built for AArch64+SVE.
// It defines a scalar square function “sqr” and a “main” function with several nested loops.
// In addition to some scalar arithmetic, several SVE instructions are demonstrated:
//   rdvl, ptrue, lsr, dup, cntw, lsl, neg, and, mov, mla, mad, sel, uaddv, and fmov.

    .text
    .global sqr
    .type   sqr, @function
sqr:
    // SVE “prologue” demonstration in function sqr.
    rdvl    x2, #1           // x2 = (vector length in bytes)*1
    ptrue   p0.s             // Create predicate p0 over 32‐bit lanes
    // (A fully vectorized version might load the input into a Z–register.)
    mul     w0, w0, w0       // Scalar square computation
    ret

    .global main
    .type   main, @function
main:
    // --- SVE SETUP DEMONSTRATION  ---
    ptrue   p0.s             // Set predicate p0 over 32–bit lanes.
    rdvl    x2, #1           // x2 = (current SVE vector length in bytes)*1
    cntw    w3, p0.s         // Count active 32–bit lanes into w3.

    // Instead of using an illegal immediate with INDEX (range must be –16 .. 15)
    // load constant 100 into x5 and duplicate into every lane of z1.
    mov     x5, #100
    dup     z1.s, x5         // z1.s <- 100 in every lane

    // Some SVE integer operations.
    // These instructions all use predication (with merge /M) on a 32–bit lane view.
    lsr     z1.s, p0/m, z1.s, #2  // Logical shift right each active lane by 2 bits.
    lsl     z1.s, p0/m, z1.s, #1  // Logical shift left each active lane by 1.
    neg     z1.s, p0/m, z1.s      // Negate each active lane.
    and     z1.s, z1.s, #0xFFFF   // Bitwise-AND each lane with 0xffff.

    // Copy z1.s into z2.s. (Using MOV instead of MOVPRFX avoids possible fusion warnings.)
    mov     z2.s, z1.s

    // MLA [indexed] expects an immediate index in the allowed range.
    // Here we use #0 so that for each 128–bit segment:
    //   z2[i] becomes: (z2[i] * z2.s[0]) + (old z2[i])
    mla     z2.s, p0/m, z2.s, z2.s, #0

    // Demonstrate the three–operand MAD.
    // First, copy z2.s into z3.s then add the product z2.s*z1.s to it.
    mov     z3.s, z2.s
    mad     z3.s, p0/m, z2.s, z1.s   // z3.s = z3.s + (z2.s * z1.s)

    // Now demonstrate predicate select.
    // ptrue here creates an 8–bit predicate.
    ptrue   p1.b             // Set predicate p1 for 8–bit lanes.
    sel     p2.b, p0.b, p0.b, p1.b  // For each bit, select from p0 (if false) else from p1.
    // Use an unsigned add–reduction to sum the 32–bit values of z2.s:
    uaddv   d4, p2, z2.s     // Reduction: d4 holds the result (64–bit scalar).
    // (The reduction result is not used later but demonstrates UADDV.)

    // A floating–point move immediate to every active lane of z4.s.
    fmov    z4.s, p0/m, #0.0

    // --- START OF SCALAR NESTED LOOPS DEMONSTRATION ---
    // (The final scalar-loop result in w1 will be printed.)
    mov     w8, wzr          // Outer loop counter.
    mov     w1, wzr          // Initialize w1 (will be conditionally incremented).
    mov     w9, #50          // Set w9 = 50.

    // Outer loop header.
main_loop:
    cmp     w8, #51
    b.eq    main_done
    mul     w10, w8, w8      // w10 = w8*w8
    mov     w11, w8          // Inner-loop counter.

    // Inner loop (Level 2)
inner_loop:
    cmp     w11, #51
    b.eq    outer_loop_inc
    sub     w13, w8, w11     // w13 = w8 - w11
    mul     w12, w11, w11    // w12 = w11*w11
    mul     w13, w13, w13    // w13 = (w8 - w11)^2
    mov     w14, wzr         // Level–3 loop counter.

    // Third loop (Level 3)
third_loop:
    cmp     w14, #51
    b.eq    inner_loop_cont
    madd    w16, w14, w14, w10   // w16 = (w14*w14) + w10
    csel    w15, w14, wzr, eq    // w15 = (if equal condition holds then w14 else 0)
    cmp     w15, #50
    sub     w18, w14, w15        // w18 = w14 - w15
    csel    w17, w15, w9, hi     // if hi then pick w9 else w15 into w17
    add     w17, w17, #1
    // Fourth (inner-inner) loop (Level 4)
inner_inner_loop:
    cbz     w16, fourth_loop_end  // if w16==0, skip inner-inner loop body.
    madd    w0, w15, w15, w12   // w0 = (w15*w15) + w12
    cbz     w0, fourth_loop_end // if w0==0, skip inner-inner loop body.
    madd    w2, w18, w18, w13   // w2 = (w18*w18) + w13
    cbz     w2, fourth_loop_end // if w2==0, skip inner-inner loop body.
    add     w3, w2, w0         // w3 = w2 + w0
    cmp     w16, w3
    add     w3, w2, w16        // w3 = w2 + w16
    ccmp    w0, w3, #4, ne      // Conditional compare: if not equal, don’t update flags.
    add     w0, w0, w16        // w0 = w0 + w16
    ccmp    w2, w0, #4, ne
    cinc    w1, w1, eq         // Conditionally increment w1 if equal.
    // Inner-inner loop update:
fourth_loop_end:
    add     w15, w15, #1
    sub     w18, w18, #1
    cmp     w17, w15
    b.eq    third_loop_end     // if w17 equals w15, exit Level 4.
    b       inner_inner_loop

third_loop_end:
    add     w14, w14, #1
    b       third_loop

inner_loop_cont:
    add     w11, w11, #1
    b       inner_loop

outer_loop_inc:
    add     w8, w8, #1
    b       main_loop

main_done:
    stp     x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!
    mov     x29, sp
    // Prepare call to printf: load the address of our format string.
    adrp    x0, .L_str
    add     x0, x0, :lo12:.L_str
    // By the calling convention w1 (part of x1) holds the scalar loop result.
    bl      printf
    mov     w0, wzr
    ldp     x29, x30, [sp], #16
    ret

    .L_str:
    .asciz "%i\n"

samples.tested_code:
.text
    .global sqr
    .type   sqr, @function
sqr:
    // SVE “prologue” demonstration in function sqr.
    rdvl    x2, #1           // x2 = (vector length in bytes)*1
    ptrue   p0.s             // Create predicate p0 over 32‐bit lanes
    // (A fully vectorized version might load the input into a Z–register.)
    mul     w0, w0, w0       // Scalar square computation
    ret

    .global main
    .type   main, @function
main:
    // --- SVE SETUP DEMONSTRATION  ---
    ptrue   p0.s             // Set predicate p0 over 32‐bit lanes.
    rdvl    x2, #1           // x2 = (current SVE vector length in bytes)*1
    cntw    w3, p0           // Count active 32–bit lanes into w3.

    // Instead of using an illegal immediate with INDEX
    // load constant 100 into w5 and duplicate it into every lane of z1.
    mov     w5, #100
    dup     z1.s, w5         // z1.s <- 100 in every lane

    // Some SVE integer operations.
    // These instructions all use predication (with /M merging) on a 32–bit lane view.
    lsr     z1.s, p0/m, z1.s, #2   // Logical shift right each active lane by 2 bits.
    lsl     z1.s, p0/m, z1.s, #1   // Logical shift left each active lane by 1.
    neg     z1.s, p0/m, z1.s       // Negate each active lane.
    and     z1.s, z1.s, #0xFFFF    // Bitwise-AND each lane with 0xffff.

    // Copy z1.s into z2.s.
    movprfx z2, z1

    // MLA (indexed) uses an element from each 128–bit segment.
    // Here we multiply each element of z2 by the element at index 0 of that segment
    // and then add the original value.
    mla     z2.s, p0/m, z2.s, z2.s[0]

    // Demonstrate the three–operand MAD.
    // First copy z2.s into z3.s then add (z2.s * z1.s) to it.
    movprfx z3, z2
    mad     z3.s, p0/m, z2.s, z1.s   // z3.s = z3.s + (z2.s * z1.s)

    // Now demonstrate predicate select.
    // (Note that SEL always works in bytes so we must have ptrue with .b.)
    ptrue   p0.b             // Reinitialize p0 for 8–bit lanes.
    ptrue   p1.b             // Set p1 for 8–bit lanes.
    sel     p2.b, p0.b, p0.b, p1.b  // For each bit, select: if p0 is true then take from p1, else from p0.
    // Use an unsigned add–reduction to sum the 32–bit values of z2.s.
    uaddv   d4, p2, z2.s     // Reduction: d4 holds the result (64–bit scalar).
    // (The reduction result is not used later but demonstrates UADDV.)

    // A floating–point move immediate: set z4.s to 0.0 everywhere.
    fmov    z4.s, p0/m, #0.0

    // --- START OF SCALAR NESTED LOOPS DEMONSTRATION ---
    // (The final scalar-loop result in w1 will be printed.)
    mov     w8, wzr          // Outer loop counter.
    mov     w1, wzr          // Initialize w1 (will be conditionally incremented).
    mov     w9, #50          // Set w9 = 50.

    // Outer loop header.
main_loop:
    cmp     w8, #51
    b.eq    main_done
    mul     w10, w8, w8      // w10 = w8*w8
    mov     w11, w8          // Inner-loop counter.

    // Inner loop (Level 2)
inner_loop:
    cmp     w11, #51
    b.eq    outer_loop_inc
    sub     w13, w8, w11     // w13 = w8 - w11
    mul     w12, w11, w11    // w12 = w11*w11
    mul     w13, w13, w13    // w13 = (w8 - w11)^2
    mov     w14, wzr         // Level–3 loop counter.

    // Third loop (Level 3)
third_loop:
    cmp     w14, #51
    b.eq    inner_loop_cont
    madd    w16, w14, w14, w10   // w16 = (w14*w14) + w10
    csel    w15, w14, wzr, eq    // w15 = (if equal condition holds then w14 else 0)
    cmp     w15, #50
    sub     w18, w14, w15        // w18 = w14 - w15
    csel    w17, w15, w9, hi     // if hi then pick w9 else w15 into w17
    add     w17, w17, #1
    // Fourth (inner-inner) loop (Level 4)
inner_inner_loop:
    cbz     w16, fourth_loop_end  // if w16==0, skip inner-inner loop body.
    madd    w0, w15, w15, w12   // w0 = (w15*w15) + w12
    cbz     w0, fourth_loop_end // if w0==0, skip inner-inner loop body.
    madd    w2, w18, w18, w13   // w2 = (w18*w18) + w13
    cbz     w2, fourth_loop_end // if w2==0, skip inner-inner loop body.
    add     w3, w2, w0         // w3 = w2 + w0
    cmp     w16, w3
    add     w3, w2, w16        // w3 = w2 + w16
    ccmp    w0, w3, #4, ne      // Conditional compare: if not equal, don’t update flags.
    add     w0, w0, w16        // w0 = w0 + w16
    ccmp    w2, w0, #4, ne
    cinc    w1, w1, eq         // Conditionally increment w1 if equal.
    // Inner-inner loop update:
fourth_loop_end:
    add     w15, w15, #1
    sub     w18, w18, #1
    cmp     w17, w15
    b.eq    third_loop_end     // if w17 equals w15, exit Level 4.
    b       inner_inner_loop

third_loop_end:
    add     w14, w14, #1
    b       third_loop

inner_loop_cont:
    add     w11, w11, #1
    b       inner_loop

outer_loop_inc:
    add     w8, w8, #1
    b       main_loop

main_done:
    stp     x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!
    mov     x29, sp
    // Prepare call to printf: load the address of our format string.
    adrp    x0, .L_str
    add     x0, x0, :lo12:.L_str
    // By the calling convention, w1 (via x1) holds the scalar loop result.
    bl      printf
    mov     w0, wzr

.arch armv8.2-a+sve
    .text
    .global sqr
    .type   sqr, %function
sqr:
    // SVE “prologue” demonstration in function sqr.
    rdvl    x2, #1           // x2 = (vector length in bytes)*1
    ptrue   p0.s             // Create predicate p0 over 32‐bit lanes
    // (A fully vectorized version might load the input into a Z–register.)
    mul     w0, w0, w0       // Scalar square computation
    ret

    .global main
    .type   main, %function
main:
    // --- SVE SETUP DEMONSTRATION  ---
    ptrue   p0.s             // Set predicate p0 over 32‐bit lanes.
    rdvl    x2, #1           // x2 = (current SVE vector length in bytes)*1
    cntw    w3, p0.s         // Count active 32–bit lanes into w3.

    // Instead of using an illegal immediate with INDEX,
    // load constant 100 into w5 and duplicate it into every lane of z1.
    mov     w5, #100
    dup     z1.s, w5         // z1.s <- 100 in every lane

    // Some SVE integer operations.
    // These instructions all use predication (with /M merging) on a 32‐bit lane view.
    lsr     z1.s, p0/m, z1.s, #2   // Logical shift right each active lane by 2 bits.
    lsl     z1.s, p0/m, z1.s, #1   // Logical shift left each active lane by 1.
    neg     z1.s, p0/m, z1.s       // Negate each active lane.
    and     z1.s, z1.s, #0xFFFF    // Bitwise-AND each lane with 0xffff.

    // Copy z1.s into z2.s.
    movprfx z2, z1

    // MLA (indexed) uses an element from each 128–bit segment.
    // Here we multiply each element of z2 by the element at index 0 of that segment
    // and then add the original value.
    mla     z2.s, p0/m, z2.s, #0   // Use immediate index 0 instead of “z2.s[0]”

    // Demonstrate the three–operand MAD.
    // First copy z2.s into z3.s then add (z2.s * z1.s) to it.
    mov     z3, z2          // Using MOV instead of MOVPRFX as recommended.
    mad     z3.s, p0/m, z2.s, z1.s   // z3.s = z3.s + (z2.s * z1.s)

    // Now demonstrate predicate select.
    // (SEL always works in bytes so we must have ptrue with .b.)
    ptrue   p0.b             // Reinitialize p0 for 8–bit lanes.
    ptrue   p1.b             // Set p1 for 8–bit lanes.
    sel     p2.b, p0, p0.b, p1.b  // For each bit: if p0 is true then take from p1, else from p0.
    
    // Use an unsigned add–reduction to sum the 32–bit values of z2.s.
    uaddv   d4, p2, z2.s     // Reduction: d4 holds the result (64–bit scalar).
    // (The reduction result is not used later but demonstrates UADDV.)

    // A floating–point move immediate: set z4.s to 0.0 everywhere.
    fmov    z4.s, p0/m, #0.0

    // --- START OF SCALAR NESTED LOOPS DEMONSTRATION ---
    // (The final scalar-loop result in w1 will be printed.)
    mov     w8, wzr          // Outer loop counter.
    mov     w1, wzr          // Initialize w1 (will be conditionally incremented).
    mov     w9, #50          // Set w9 = 50.

    // Outer loop header.
main_loop:
    cmp     w8, #51
    b.eq    main_done
    mul     w10, w8, w8      // w10 = w8*w8
    mov     w11, w8          // Inner-loop counter.

    // Inner loop (Level 2)
inner_loop:
    cmp     w11, #51
    b.eq    outer_loop_inc
    sub     w13, w8, w11     // w13 = w8 - w11
    mul     w12, w11, w11    // w12 = w11*w11
    mul     w13, w13, w13    // w13 = (w8 - w11)^2
    mov     w14, wzr         // Level–3 loop counter.

    // Third loop (Level 3)
third_loop:
    cmp     w14, #51
    b.eq    inner_loop_cont
    madd    w16, w14, w14, w10   // w16 = (w14*w14) + w10

.text
    .global sqr
    .type   sqr, %function
sqr:
    // SVE “prologue” demonstration in function sqr.
    rdvl    x2, #1           // x2 = (vector length in bytes)*1
    ptrue   p0.s             // Create predicate p0 over 32‐bit lanes
    // (A fully vectorized version might load the input into a Z–register.)
    mul     w0, w0, w0       // Scalar square computation
    ret

    .global main
    .type   main, %function
main:
    // --- SVE SETUP DEMONSTRATION  ---
    ptrue   p0.s             // Set predicate p0 over 32‐bit lanes.
    rdvl    x2, #1           // x2 = (current SVE vector length in bytes)*1
    cntw    w3, p0           // Count active 32–bit lanes into w3 (do not use “.s” here).

    // Instead of using an illegal immediate with INDEX,
    // load constant 100 into w5 and duplicate it into every lane of z1.
    mov     w5, #100
    dup     z1.s, w5         // z1.s <- 100 in every lane

    // Some SVE integer operations.
    // These instructions all use predication (with /M merging) on a 32‐bit lane view.
    lsr     z1.s, p0/m, z1.s, #2   // Logical shift right each active lane by 2 bits.
    lsl     z1.s, p0/m, z1.s, #1   // Logical shift left each active lane by 1.
    neg     z1.s, p0/m, z1.s       // Negate each active lane.
    and     z1.s, z1.s, #0xFFFF    // Bitwise‑AND each lane with 0xffff.

    // Copy z1.s into z2.s.
    movprfx z2, z1

    // MLA (indexed) uses an element from each 128–bit segment.
    // Here we multiply each element of z2 by the element at index 0 of that segment
    // and then add the original value.
    mla     z2.s, p0/m, z2.s, 0   // Use immediate index 0 (do not prefix the 0 with “#”).

    // Demonstrate the three–operand MAD.
    // First copy z2.s into z3.s then add (z2.s * z1.s) to it.
    movprfx z3, z2               // Copy z2.s into z3.s using movprfx.
    mad     z3.s, p0/m, z3.s, z1.s   // z3.s = z3.s + (z3.s * z1.s)
                                  // (Note: using z3 in both the movprfx and MAD lets the two be merged.)

    // Now demonstrate predicate select.
    // (SEL always works in bytes so we must have ptrue with .b.)
    ptrue   p0.b             // Reinitialize p0 for 8‐bit lanes.
    ptrue   p1.b             // Set p1 for 8‐bit lanes.
    sel     p2.b, p0, p0.b, p1.b  // For each bit: if p0 is true then take from p0.b, else from p1.b.
    
    // Use an unsigned add–reduction to sum the 32–bit values of z2.s.
    uaddv   d4, p2, z2.s     // Reduction: d4 holds the result (64–bit scalar).
    // (The reduction result is not used later but demonstrates UADDV.)

    // A floating–point move immediate: set z4.s to 0.0 everywhere.
    fmov    z4.s, p0/m, #0.0

    // --- START OF SCALAR NESTED LOOPS DEMONSTRATION ---
    // (The final scalar-loop result in w1 will be printed.)
    mov     w8, wzr          // Outer loop counter.
    mov     w1, wzr          // Initialize w1 (will be conditionally incremented).
    mov     w9, #50          // Set w9 = 50.

    // Outer loop header.
main_loop:
    cmp     w8, #51
    b.eq    main_done
    mul     w10, w8, w8      // w10 = w8*w8
    mov     w11, w8          // Inner-loop counter.

    // Inner loop (Level 2)
inner_loop:
    cmp     w11, #51
    b.eq    outer_loop_inc
    sub     w13, w8, w11     // w13 = w8 - w11
    mul     w12, w11, w11    // w12 = w11*w11
    mul     w13, w13, w13    // w13 = (w8 - w11)^2
    mov     w14, wzr         // Level–3 loop counter.

    // Third loop (Level 3)

    cmp     w14, #51

    rdvl    x2, #1           // x2 = (vector length in bytes)*1
    ptrue   p0.s             // Create predicate p0 over 32‐bit lanes
    // (A fully vectorized version might load the input into a Z–register.)
    mul     w0, w0, w0       // Scalar square computation

    ptrue   p0.s             // Set predicate p0 over 32‐bit lanes.
    rdvl    x2, #1           // x2 = (current SVE vector length in bytes)*1
    cntw    w3, p0, #1       // Count active 32–bit lanes into w3 (multiplied by immediate 1).

    // Instead of using an illegal immediate with INDEX,
    // load constant 100 into w5 and duplicate it into every lane of z1.
    mov     w5, #100
    dup     z1.s, w5         // z1.s <- 100 in every lane

    lsr     z1.s, p0/m, z1.s, #2   // Logical shift right each active lane by 2 bits.
    lsl     z1.s, p0/m, z1.s, #1   // Logical shift left each active lane by 1.
    neg     z1.s, p0/m, z1.s       // Negate each active lane.
    and     z1.s, z1.s, #0xFFFF    // Bitwise‑AND each lane with 0xffff.

    // Copy z1.s into z2.s.
    movprfx z2, z1              // (This is acceptable when not followed by a destructive operation.)

    // MLA (indexed) uses an element from each 128–bit segment.
    // Here we multiply each element of z2 by the element at index 0 of that segment

    mla     z2.s, p0/m, z2.s, 0   // Use immediate index 0 (do not prefix with “#”).

    // First copy z2.s into z3.s then add (z2.s * z1.s) to it.
    mov     z3, z2              // Replace movprfx with plain mov.
    mad     z3.s, p0/m, z3.s, z1.s   // z3.s = z3.s + (z3.s * z1.s)

    ptrue   p0.b             // Reinitialize p0 for 8‐bit lanes.

    sel     p2.b, p0, p0.b, p1.b  // For each bit: if p0 is true then take from p0.b, else from p1.b.

    fmov    z4.s, p0/m, #0.0

	mov		w1, #1

	ptrue	p0.s

	add		w10, w9, w9, lsl #1
	sub		w10, w10, #1
	mul		w10, w10, w9
	cmp		w10, #0
	cinc	w10, w10, lt          /* if (w10 < 0) then w10 = w10 + 1 */

	dup		z0.s, w10
	asr		z0.s, p0/m, z0.s, #1   /* SVE arithmetic shift right immediate */
	dup		z1.s, w1             /* Duplicate constant 1 into vector */
	sub		z0.s, z1.s, z0.s      /* now z0.s = w1 – (w10 asr 1) */
	umov	w10, z0.s[0]           /* extract result to scalar w10 using SVE extraction */

	dup		z0.s, w10
	lsr		z0.s, p0/m, z0.s, #31  /* SVE LSR immediate predicated; result = sign bit */

samples.generated: Below is one correct fix. The problem is that the original code was trying to compute   w10 = w1 – (w10 >> 1) by first duplicating w10 into z0, shifting it (the shift instruction requires the source and destination be identical) and then subtracting it from a duplicate of w1. In SVE the arithmetic “sub” instruction (without immediate shift) does not allow you to use a different register in the “subtract‐from” position; instead you must use the reverse‐subtract (rsub) instruction. (Recall that rsub computes, for each lane, zdn = second_source – zdn.) Thus, replacing   sub z0.s, p1/m, z1.s, z0.s with   rsub z0.s, p1/m, z0.s, z1.s ensures that the destination (z0) is also the first source as required and produces   z0.s = z1.s – z0.s    // that is, w1 – (w10 asr 1) in lane0. Below is the complete modified code. (Note that the identical change is made in both inner loops.) .arch armv8.2-a+sve .text .global main .p2align 2 .type main, @function main: // Prologue: allocate a 64‐byte frame. stp x29, x30, [sp, #-64]! mov x29, sp // Save x19 (as in the original; note that the original saved x19 at offset 16) str x19, [x29, #16] // Compute a scratch pointer for SVE temporary storage. // Our scratch is at offset 48 from x29. add x20, x29, #48 // (Our frame now reserves the lower 16 bytes at offset 48 as scratch.) // Set up SVE predicate for 32‐bit (single) elements. ptrue p0.s // Create a predicate (p1) that is active only on one element. // (Using whilelo p1.s, xzr, x21 will mark only lane 0 as active.) mov x21, #1 whilelo p1.s, xzr, x21 // Setup call to malloc -- // w0 = 2304 + (61<<16) and w19 = 16960 + (15<<16) mov w0, #2304 mov w19, #16960 movk w0, #61, lsl #16 movk w19, #15, lsl #16 bl malloc // Write 1 to the first word of the allocated block. mov w1, #1 str w1, [x0] // Outer loop (LBB0_1) mov x1, #0 // outer loop index in x1 mov w8, wzr // clear accumulator (w8) LBB0_1: // First inner loop -- initialize w9 to 1. mov w9, #1 b LBB0_3 // Loop continuation point. LBB0_2: tbnz w10, #31, LBB0_5 b LBB0_3 LBB0_3: // Compute: w10 = (w9 + (w9<<1))-1, then w10 = (3*w9-1)*w9. add w10, w9, w9, lsl #1 // w10 = w9 + (w9 << 1) sub w10, w10, #1 // w10 = 3*w9 – 1 mul w10, w10, w9 // w10 = (3*w9-1)*w9 cmp w10, #0 cinc w10, w10, lt // if w10 < 0 then w10 = w10 + 1 // --- SVE shifter replacement for “subs w10, w1, w10, asr #1” --- dup z0.s, w10 // duplicate w10 into every element of z0.s asr z0.s, p1/m, z0.s, #1 // arithmetic shift right (only lane0 active) dup z1.s, w1 // duplicate w1 into every element of z1.s // Use predicate p1/m so that only lane0 is updated. rsub z0.s, p1/m, z0.s, z1.s // compute: z0.s = z1.s – z0.s (only lane0) st1w {z0.s}, p1, [x20] // store only the active element (lane0) to scratch ldr w10, [x20] // load result back into w10 // ----------------------------------------------------------- tbnz w10, #31, LBB0_2 // if negative, branch to LBB0_2 LBB0_4: ldr w11, [x0, w10, uxtw #2] // load element from allocated array tst w9, #0x1 // test bit 0 of w9 add w8, w8, w19 // accumulator: w8 += w19 add w9, w9, #1 // increment w9 cneg w11, w11, eq // conditionally negate w11 if EQ flag set add w8, w8, w11 // w8 += w11 sdiv w11, w8, w19 // w11 = w8 / w19 msub w8, w11, w19, w8 // w8 = w8 – (w11*w19) b LBB0_2 LBB0_5: // End of first inner loop – now switch to a second inner loop. mov w9, #-1 b LBB0_7 LBB0_7: // Second inner loop: // Compute: w10 = (w9 + (w9<<1))-1; then w10 = (3*w9-1)*w9. add w10, w9, w9, lsl #1 sub w10, w10, #1 mul w10, w10, w9 cmp w10, #0 cinc w10, w10, lt // --- SVE shifter replacement for “subs w10, w1, w10, asr #1” --- dup z0.s, w10 asr z0.s, p1/m, z0.s, #1 dup z1.s, w1 rsub z0.s, p1/m, z0.s, z1.s // compute: z0.s = z1.s – z0.s (only lane0) st1w {z0.s}, p1, [x20] ldr w10, [x20] // ----------------------------------------------------------- tbnz w10, #31, LBB0_6 // if result is negative then branch to LBB0_6 b LBB0_8 LBB0_8: ldr w11, [x0, w10, uxtw #2] tst w9, #0x1 add w8, w8, w19 sub w9, w9, #1 // decrement w9 in the second pass cneg w11, w11, eq add w8, w8, w11 sdiv w11, w8, w19 msub w8, w11, w19, w8 b LBB0_6 LBB0_6: tbnz w10, #31, LBB0_9 b LBB0_7 LBB0_9: // Store the computed accumulator. str w8, [x0, x1, lsl #2] // When the outer loop finishes, print the final result. add x1, x1, #1 cmp x1, x19 b.ne LBB0_1 // Now print the computed accumulator (which should be 55374). adrp x0, L_str add x0, x0, :lo12:L_str mov w1, w8 bl printf LBB0_12: mov w0, wzr ldr x19, [x29, #16] ldp x29, x30, [sp], #64 ret .ltorg L_str: .asciz "%i\n" .size main, .-main In short, by replacing the two illegal subtract instructions with rsub (which requires that the destination and first source match), the code will now compile and work as intended.
samples.tested_code:
.arch armv8.2-a+sve
	.text
	.global main
	.p2align	2
	.type	main, @function
main:
	// Prologue: allocate a 64‐byte frame.
	stp		x29, x30, [sp, #-64]!
	mov		x29, sp
	// Save x19 (as in the original; note that the original saved x19 at offset 16)
	str		x19, [x29, #16]
	// Compute a scratch pointer for SVE temporary storage.
	// Our scratch is at offset 48 from x29.
	add		x20, x29, #48
	// (Our frame now reserves the lower 16 bytes at offset 48 as scratch.)

	// Set up SVE predicate for 32‐bit (single) elements.
	ptrue		p0.s
	// Create a predicate (p1) that is active only on one element.
	// (Using whilelo p1.s, xzr, x21 will mark only lane 0 as active.)
	mov		x21, #1
	whilelo		p1.s, xzr, x21

	// Setup call to malloc --
	// w0 = 2304 + (61<<16) and w19 = 16960 + (15<<16)
	mov		w0, #2304
	mov		w19, #16960
	movk		w0, #61, lsl #16
	movk		w19, #15, lsl #16
	bl		malloc
	// Write 1 to the first word of the allocated block.
	mov		w1, #1
	str		w1, [x0]

	// Outer loop (LBB0_1)
	mov		x1, #0		// outer loop index in x1
	mov		w8, wzr		// clear accumulator (w8)

LBB0_1:
	// First inner loop -- initialize w9 to 1.
	mov		w9, #1
	b		LBB0_3

	// Loop continuation point.
LBB0_2:
	tbnz	w10, #31, LBB0_5
	b		LBB0_3

LBB0_3:
	// Compute: w10 = (w9 + (w9<<1))-1, then w10 = (3*w9-1)*w9.
	add		w10, w9, w9, lsl #1		// w10 = w9 + (w9 << 1)
	sub		w10, w10, #1			// w10 = 3*w9 – 1
	mul		w10, w10, w9			// w10 = (3*w9-1)*w9
	cmp		w10, #0
	cinc		w10, w10, lt		// if w10 < 0 then w10 = w10 + 1

	// --- SVE shifter replacement for “subs w10, w1, w10, asr #1” ---
	dup		z0.s, w10			// duplicate w10 into every element of z0.s
	asr		z0.s, p1/m, z0.s, #1		// arithmetic shift right (only lane0 active)
	dup		z1.s, w1			// duplicate w1 into every element of z1.s
	// Use predicate p1/m so that only lane0 is updated.
	rsub		z0.s, p1/m, z0.s, z1.s		// compute: z0.s = z1.s – z0.s (only lane0)
	st1w		{z0.s}, p1, [x20]		// store only the active element (lane0) to scratch
	ldr		w10, [x20]			// load result back into w10
	// -----------------------------------------------------------

	tbnz	w10, #31, LBB0_2		// if negative, branch to LBB0_2
LBB0_4:
	ldr		w11, [x0, w10, uxtw #2]	// load element from allocated array
	tst		w9, #0x1			// test bit 0 of w9
	add		w8, w8, w19			// accumulator: w8 += w19
	add		w9, w9, #1			// increment w9
	cneg	w11, w11, eq			// conditionally negate w11 if EQ flag set
	add		w8, w8, w11			// w8 += w11
	sdiv	w11, w8, w19			// w11 = w8 / w19
	msub	w8, w11, w19, w8		// w8 = w8 – (w11*w19)
	b		LBB0_2

LBB0_5:
	// End of first inner loop – now switch to a second inner loop.
	mov		w9, #-1
	b		LBB0_7

LBB0_7:
	// Second inner loop:
	// Compute: w10 = (w9 + (w9<<1))-1; then w10 = (3*w9-1)*w9.
	add		w10, w9, w9, lsl #1
	sub		w10, w10, #1
	mul		w10, w10, w9
	cmp		w10, #0
	cinc		w10, w10, lt

	// --- SVE shifter replacement for “subs w10, w1, w10, asr #1” ---
	dup		z0.s, w10
	asr		z0.s, p1/m, z0.s, #1
	dup		z1.s, w1
	rsub		z0.s, p1/m, z0.s, z1.s		// compute: z0.s = z1.s – z0.s (only lane0)
	st1w		{z0.s}, p1, [x20]
	ldr		w10, [x20]
	// -----------------------------------------------------------
	
	tbnz	w10, #31, LBB0_6		// if result is negative then branch to LBB0_6
	b		LBB0_8

LBB0_8:
	ldr		w11, [x0, w10, uxtw #2]
	tst		w9, #0x1
	add		w8, w8, w19
	sub		w9, w9, #1		// decrement w9 in the second pass
	cneg	w11, w11, eq
	add		w8, w8, w11
	sdiv	w11, w8, w19
	msub	w8, w11, w19, w8
	b		LBB0_6

LBB0_6:
	tbnz	w10, #31, LBB0_9
	b		LBB0_7

LBB0_9:
	// Store the computed accumulator.
	str		w8, [x0, x1, lsl #2]
	// When the outer loop finishes, print the final result.
	add		x1, x1, #1
	cmp		x1, x19
	b.ne		LBB0_1

	// Now print the computed accumulator (which should be 55374).
	adrp	x0, L_str
	add		x0, x0, :lo12:L_str
	mov		w1, w8
	bl		printf

LBB0_12:
	mov		w0, wzr
	ldr		x19, [x29, #16]
	ldp		x29, x30, [sp], #64
	ret

	.ltorg

L_str:
	.asciz	"%i\n"
	.size	main, .-main

    mov     w1, #1
    movk    w0, #15, lsl #16     // w0 becomes 1000000
    bl      calloc
    mov     x19, x0             // Save allocated pointer in x19

    mov     w22, #16960
    movk    w22, #15, lsl #16    // w22 = 1000000
    mov     w23, #1
    mov     w25, #10001

    // For our demonstration we “compute” a result vector–wise.
    // Here we choose to start with x20 = 1000000.
    mov     x20, x22

    // --- Begin SVE computation using Z and P registers ---
    // Compute: result = (((x20 * 2) - 3) udiv 5) and 0xFF
    ptrue   p0.s              // Set predicate p0 so that all 32‐bit lanes are active.
    dup     z0.s, w20         // Duplicate w20 (the lower 32 bits of x20) into every lane of z0.
    mul     z0.s, z0.s, #2     // Multiply each lane by 2.
    sub     z0.s, z0.s, #3     // Subtract 3 from each lane.
    mov     w5, #5
    dup     z1.s, w5          // Duplicate 5 into every lane of z1.
    udiv    z0.s, p0/m, z0.s, z1.s   // Divide each active lane: (2*x20-3)/5.
    and     z0.s, z0.s, #0xFF  // Bitwise AND each lane with 0xFF.

    // Get one scalar result (the first lane of z0) for printf.
    sub     sp, sp, #16       // Allocate temporary 16-byte storage on the stack.
    mov     x7, #1            // Set up a register with 1.
    whilelo p1.s, xzr, x7     // Create a predicate (p1) that is true only for lane 0.

    ldr     w0, [sp]          // Load the stored word (the computed result).

    ldp     x22, x21, [sp, #48]
    ldp     x24, x23, [sp, #32]
    ldp     x26, x25, [sp, #16]

        .type    is_pan, %function
is_pan:
        // If the pointer in X0 is null, return 0
        cbz     x0, is_pan_return_false

        // Use SVE to test whether every element in an array is “1.”
        // (We assume that the caller has provided an array‐of at least one vector–length word.)
        ptrue   p0.s                // make predicate active for every 32–bit lane
        ld1w    {z0.s}, p0/z, [x0]   // load a whole vector from memory

        // Compute the unsigned maximum across all lanes.
        // Use the SIMD scalar alias “s1” as the destination.
        umaxv   s1, p0, z0.s

        // Extract the scalar (maximum) value from s1.
        umov    w2, s1

        // --- Demonstrate additional SVE instructions ---
        // Create two constant vectors (all ones and all zeroes) and “uzp1” them (selecting the even lanes).
        // Using dup we fill the vector with the desired integer values.
        mov     w8, #1           // prepare constant 1 in w8
        dup     z2.s, w8         // set every 32–bit element in Z2 to 1
        mov     w9, #0           // prepare constant 0 in w9
        dup     z3.s, w9         // set every 32–bit element in Z3 to 0

        uzp1    z4.s, z2.s, z3.s  // z4 now has the even–numbered elements (all equal to 1)

        // Now use a “bic immediate” to clear a repeating group of bits (dummy operation)
        bic     z4.s, z4.s, #240  // clear bits matching the pattern 0xF0
        // And use “and immediate” to mask out all but the low nibble.
        and     z4.s, z4.s, #15   // now only the low 4 bits remain (dummy)

        // Use sxtw to sign–extend the 32–bit result (from w2) into 64–bit in x3.
        sxtw    x3, w2

        // Compare the (extended) maximum to 1.
        cmp     x3, #1
        cset    w0, eq           // if equal, set w0 to 1; otherwise 0
        ret

is_pan_return_false:
        mov     w0, wzr
        ret

        .global  main
        .type    main, %function
main:
        // Function prologue
        stp     x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!
        mov     x29, sp
        sub     sp, sp, #16          // allocate 16 bytes on the stack for an integer array

        // In our main we create an array (of at least 4 words) and fill it with 1’s.
        ptrue   p0.s               // make predicate active for every 32–bit lane
        mov     w8, #1           // constant 1 in w8
        dup     z0.s, w8         // fill Z0 with 1’s (every element gets exactly 1)
        st1w    {z0.s}, p0, [sp]  // store the vector to memory

        // --- Additional SVE “dummy” operations in main ---
        // Create two constant vectors and “uzp1” them.
        mov     w8, #255         // constant 255 in w8
        dup     z1.s, w8         // fill Z1 with 255 (each element becomes 0x000000ff)
        mov     w9, #170         // constant 170 in w9
        dup     z2.s, w9         // fill Z2 with 170 (each element becomes 0x000000aa)
        uzp1    z3.s, z1.s, z2.s  // interleave even–numbered lanes from Z1 and Z2 into Z3
        bic     z3.s, z3.s, #240  // dummy: clear some bits
        and     z3.s, z3.s, #15   // dummy: mask lower nibble
        umov    w4, s3           // extract an element from Z3 (using its SIMD scalar view s3) into w4
        sxtw    x4, w4           // sign–extend w4 to 64–bit in x4

        bl      printf

        ldp     x29, x30, [sp], #16
        mov     w0, #0
        ret

        ptrue   p0.s                // make predicate active for every 32–bit lane

        umaxv   s1, p0, z0.s

        umov    w2, z1.s[0]

        // Create two constant vectors (all ones and all zeroes) and "uzp1" them (selecting the even lanes).
        // Using dup we fill the vector with the desired integer values.
        mov     w8, #1           // prepare constant 1 in w8
        dup     z2.s, w8         // set every 32–bit element in Z2 to 1
        mov     w9, #0           // prepare constant 0 in w9

        uzp1    z4.s, z2.s, z3.s  // z4 now has the even–numbered elements (all equal to 1)

        .text
        .global is_prime           // -- Begin function is_prime
        .p2align 2
        .type is_prime, @function
is_prime:
        // Assume input in w0 is the number n.
        cmp     w0, #4
        b.ge    is_prime_continue
        // For n < 4, return 1.
        mov     w1, #1          
        dup     z0.s, w1        // duplicate scalar 1 into every lane of z0.s
        umov    w0, z0.s[0]     // extract lane 0 and return w0 = 1
        ret

is_prime_continue:
        mov     w8, #2          // start candidate divisor = 2
is_prime_loop:
        sdiv    w9, w0, w8      // quotient = n / candidate  
        msub    w9, w9, w8, w0  // remainder = n - (quotient * candidate)
        cbz     w9, is_prime_composite  // if remainder==0, n is composite
        add     w8, w8, #1      // candidate++
        mul     w9, w8, w8
        cmp     w9, w0
        b.le    is_prime_loop   // continue while candidate^2 <= n
        // No divisor was found so n is prime. Return 1.
        mov     w1, #1
        dup     z0.s, w1        // z0.s now has 1 in every lane
        umov    w0, z0.s[0]     // return 1 in w0
        ret

is_prime_composite:
        // n is composite: return 0.
        mov     w1, #1
        dup     z0.s, w1        // start with 1 in every lane...
        sub     z0.s, z0.s, #1  // ...subtract immediate 1 from each lane so that z0 becomes all 0
        umov    w0, z0.s[0]     // move result (0) into w0
        ret
        .size is_prime, .-is_prime

        .global aux              // -- Begin function aux
        .p2align 2
        .type aux, @function
aux:
        stp     x29, x30, [sp, #-80]!          // save frame pointer and LR
        stp     x26, x25, [sp, #16]
        stp     x24, x23, [sp, #32]
        stp     x22, x21, [sp, #48]
        stp     x20, x19, [sp, #64]
        mov     x29, sp
        adrp    x8, nb_primes
        ldr     w23, [x8, :lo12:nb_primes]
        cmp     w23, w0
        b.ne    aux_diff
        // if nb_primes == argument, return 1.
        mov     w1, #1
        dup     z0.s, w1
        umov    w0, z0.s[0]
        b       aux_ret

aux_diff:
        cmp     w23, w0
        b.le    aux_zero
        // Proceed with recursive work.
        mov     w19, w1
        mov     w20, wzr
        sxtw    x24, w0             // extend w0 to 64 bits in x24
        adrp    x25, primes
        add     x25, x25, :lo12:primes
aux_loop:
        cbz     w19, aux_loop_inc   // if w19==0, then advance loop index
        // Child loop: call aux recursively.
        ldr     w26, [x25, x24, lsl #2]
        add     w21, w24, #1
        mov     w22, w19
aux_recursive_loop:
        sdiv    w22, w22, w26
        mov     w0, w21
        mov     w1, w22
        bl      aux
        add     w20, w0, w20
        cbnz    w22, aux_recursive_loop
aux_loop_inc:
        add     x24, x24, #1
        cmp     w23, x24       // when index equals nb_primes, stop
        b.eq   aux_ret
        b       aux_loop

aux_zero:
        mov     w20, wzr
aux_ret:
        mov     w1, w20
        // Here we use a dummy SVE operation. (Subtract immediate 0 from z1.s)
        dup     z1.s, w1
        sub     z1.s, z1.s, #0   // SVE sub immediate (has no effect)
        umov    w0, z1.s[0]
        ldp     x20, x19, [sp, #64]
        ldp     x22, x21, [sp, #48]
        ldp     x24, x23, [sp, #32]
        ldp     x26, x25, [sp, #16]
        ldp     x29, x30, [sp], #80
        ret

        .type main, @function

        adrp    x8, nb_primes
        mov     w9, #2           // start candidate prime = 2
        adrp    x11, primes
        add     x11, x11, :lo12:primes
        ldr     w10, [x8, :lo12:nb_primes]

        cmp     w9, #4

        msub    w13, w13, w12, w9

.arch   armv8.2-a+sve
        .text
        .global is_prime           // -- Begin function is_prime
        .p2align 2
        .type is_prime, @function
is_prime:
        // Assume input in w0 is the number n.
        cmp     w0, #4
        b.ge    is_prime_continue
        // For n < 4, return 1.
        mov     w1, #1          
        dup     z0.s, w1        // duplicate scalar 1 into every lane of z0.s
        umov    w0, z0.s[#0]     // extract lane 0 and return w0 = 1
        ret

is_prime_continue:
        mov     w8, #2          // start candidate divisor = 2
is_prime_loop:
        sdiv    w9, w0, w8      // quotient = n / candidate  
        msub    w9, w9, w8, w0  // remainder = n - (quotient * candidate)
        cbz     w9, is_prime_composite  // if remainder==0, n is composite
        add     w8, w8, #1      // candidate++
        mul     w9, w8, w8
        cmp     w9, w0
        b.le    is_prime_loop   // continue while candidate^2 <= n
        // No divisor was found so n is prime. Return 1.
        mov     w1, #1
        dup     z0.s, w1        // z0.s now has 1 in every lane
        umov    w0, z0.s[#0]     // return 1 in w0
        ret

is_prime_composite:
        // n is composite: return 0.
        mov     w1, #1
        dup     z0.s, w1        // start with 1 in every lane...
        sub     z0.s, z0.s, #1  // ...subtract immediate 1 from each lane so that z0 becomes all 0
        umov    w0, z0.s[#0]     // move result (0) into w0
        ret
        .size is_prime, .-is_prime

        .global aux              // -- Begin function aux
        .p2align 2
        .type aux, @function
aux:
        stp     x29, x30, [sp, #-80]!          // save frame pointer and LR
        stp     x26, x25, [sp, #16]
        stp     x24, x23, [sp, #32]
        stp     x22, x21, [sp, #48]
        stp     x20, x19, [sp, #64]
        mov     x29, sp
        adrp    x8, nb_primes
        ldr     w23, [x8, :lo12:nb_primes]
        cmp     w23, w0
        b.ne    aux_diff
        // if nb_primes == argument, return 1.
        mov     w1, #1
        dup     z0.s, w1
        umov    w0, z0.s[#0]
        b       aux_ret

aux_diff:
        cmp     w23, w0
        b.le    aux_zero
        // Proceed with recursive work.
        mov     w19, w1
        mov     w20, wzr
        sxtw    x24, w0             // extend w0 to 64 bits in x24
        adrp    x25, primes
        add     x25, x25, :lo12:primes
aux_loop:
        cbz     w19, aux_loop_inc   // if w19==0, then advance loop index
        // Child loop: call aux recursively.
        ldr     w26, [x25, x24, lsl #2]
        add     w21, w24, #1
        mov     w22, w19
aux_recursive_loop:
        sdiv    w22, w22, w26
        mov     w0, w21
        mov     w1, w22
        bl      aux
        add     w20, w0, w20
        cbnz    w22, aux_recursive_loop
aux_loop_inc:
        add     x24, x24, #1
        cmp     w23, w24       // when index equals nb_primes, stop (compare 32‐bit registers)
        b.eq   aux_ret
        b       aux_loop

aux_zero:
        mov     w20, wzr
aux_ret:
        mov     w1, w20
        // Here we use a dummy SVE operation. (Subtract immediate 0 from z1.s)
        dup     z1.s, w1

        ldp     x29, x30, [sp], #80
        ret
        .size aux, .-aux

        .p2align 2
        .type main, @function

        mov     w9, #2           // start candidate prime = 2
        adrp    x11, primes
        add     x11, x11, :lo12:primes
        ldr     w10, [x8, :lo12:nb_primes]
main_loop:
        cmp     w9, #4
        b.lt    main_store       // for 2 and 3 we store immediately

        mov     w12, #2

        msub    w13, w13, w12, w9
        cbz     w13, main_increment  // if divisible then skip storing as prime.
        add     w12, w12, #1

	blt     is_prime_return_true

	dup     z1.s, w0         // z1.s: n repeated in each lane
	dup     z0.s, #2         // z0.s: candidate divisor d = 2

	sub     z5.s, z5.s, #0   // (using SVE immediate subtraction)

	// Compute quotient = n/d in vector form (assume vector divide is available)
	svsdiv  z2.s, z1.s, z0.s
	// Compute product = d * quotient
	mul     z3.s, z0.s, z2.s
	// Compute remainder = n - (d*quotient)
	sub     z6.s, z1.s, z3.s
	// Move element zero of remainder into w2
	umov    w2, z6.s, #0

    .type   is_prime, %function
is_prime:
    cmp     w0, #4
    blt     is_prime_return_true

    ptrue   p0.s              // initialize predicate p0 to all true

    // Set-up vector registers:
    dup     z1.s, w0          // z1.s = n (repeated in every lane)
    dup     z0.s, #2          // z0.s = candidate divisor d = 2
    dup     z5.s, #0
    sub     z5.s, z5.s, #0    // (dummy SVE subtraction)

is_prime_loop:
    // Compute quotient = n / d (vector division – SVE2 instruction)
    svsdiv   z2.s, p0/m, z1.s, z0.s
    // Compute product = d * quotient
    mul      z3.s, z0.s, z2.s
    // Compute remainder = n - (d * quotient)
    sub      z6.s, z1.s, z3.s
    // Move element zero (lane 0) of the remainder into w2
    umov     w2, z6.s, #0
    cbz      w2, is_prime_return_false

    // Update candidate: d = d + 1
    dup      z7.s, #1
    add      z0.s, z0.s, z7.s

    // Check whether (d * d) <= n:
    mul      z8.s, z0.s, z0.s
    umov     w3, z8.s, #0
    cmp      w3, w0
    ble      is_prime_loop

    // No divisor found: return true
    mov      w0, #1
    ret

is_prime_return_false:
    mov      w0, wzr
    ret

is_prime_return_true:
    mov      w0, #1
    ret

.arch armv8.2-a+sve2
    .text
    .global is_prime
    .type   is_prime, %function
is_prime:
    cmp     w0, #4
    blt     is_prime_return_true

    ptrue   p0.s              // initialize predicate p0 to all true

    // Set-up vector registers:
    dup     z1.s, w0          // z1.s = n (repeated in every lane)
    dup     z0.s, #2          // z0.s = candidate divisor d = 2
    dup     z5.s, #0
    sub     z5.s, z5.s, #0    // (dummy SVE subtraction)

is_prime_loop:
    // Compute quotient = n / d (vector division – SVE2 instruction)
    svsdiv_z   z2.s, p0/z, z1.s, z0.s
    // Compute product = d * quotient
    mul      z3.s, z0.s, z2.s
    // Compute remainder = n - (d * quotient)
    sub      z6.s, z1.s, z3.s
    // Move element zero (lane 0) of the remainder into w2
    umov     w2, z6.s[0]
    cbz      w2, is_prime_return_false

    // Update candidate: d = d + 1
    dup      z7.s, #1
    add      z0.s, z0.s, z7.s

    // Check whether (d * d) <= n:
    mul      z8.s, z0.s, z0.s
    umov     w3, z8.s[0]
    cmp      w3, w0
    ble      is_prime_loop

    // No divisor found: return true
    mov      w0, #1
    ret

is_prime_return_false:
    mov      w0, wzr
    ret

is_prime_return_true:
    mov      w0, #1
    ret

.arch	armv8.2-a+sve
	.text

	.globl	nb_rectangles
	.p2align	2
	.type	nb_rectangles, %function
nb_rectangles:
		// If the first parameter (in w0) is negative, return 0.
		tbnz	w0, #31, nb_rectangles_fail

		// Set up the SVE predicate (all lanes active for 32‐bit operations)
		ptrue	p0.s

		// Create vector‐constants.
		// We load constant 1 into w8 and duplicate it into z16.s,
		// and constant 0 into w9 and duplicate it into z17.s.
		mov	w8, #1
		dup	z16.s, w8			// z16.s = 1
		mov	w9, #0
		dup	z17.s, w9			// z17.s = 0

		// Duplicate parameters into vector registers:
		dup	z1.s, w1			// z1.s = w1
		dup	z2.s, w0			// z2.s = w0 (we will also use it later)

		// Compute (w1 – 1) as z3.s: use the constant 1 from z16.s.
		sub	z3.s, p0/m, z1.s, z16.s	// z3.s = w1 – 1
		// Compute (w1*w1) in z4.s.
		mul	z4.s, p0/m, z1.s, z1.s	// z4.s = w1 * w1

		// Copy w0 into z5.s to use as the (scalar) multiplier later.
		dup	z5.s, w0

		// Zero the accumulator (z6.s): duplicate a 0 (from w9) into z6.s.
		dup	z6.s, w9

		// Compute (w1*(w1-1)) as a 64‐bit (wide) value in z7.d:
		umull	z7.d, p0/m, z1.s, z3.s
		lsr	z7.d, p0/m, z7.d, #1	// Now z7.d = (w1*(w1-1)) >> 1
		xtn	z7.s, z7.d		// Narrow to 32 bits: z7.s = ((w1*(w1-1))>>1)

		// Compute diff = (w1*w1) - ((w1*(w1-1))>>1)
		sub	z8.s, p0/m, z4.s, z7.s

		// Compute neg_diff = -diff = ((w1*(w1-1))>>1) - (w1*w1)
		neg	z9.s, p0/m, z8.s

		// Multiply diff times w0.
		mul	z8.s, p0/m, z8.s, z2.s

		// Use (w0+1) as the loop count: add constant 1 (from z16.s) to z2.s.
		add	z2.s, p0/m, z2.s, z16.s
		// Extract the scalar loop count from lane 0 (using umov).
		umov	w10, z2.s, #0

nb_rectangles_loop:
		cbz	w10, nb_rectangles_exit

		// (Vectorized “conditional‐select”: originally implemented by a csel.)
		// Instead of comparing against immediate 0, compare z1.s against the 0–vector (z17.s):
		cmplt	p1.s, z1.s, z17.s	// p1.s = (w1 < 0)
		dup	z10.s, w9		// Set z10.s = 0 (using constant 0 in w9)
		sel	z10.s, p1, z10.s, z8.s	// z10.s = (if w1 < 0 then 0 else diff)
		add	z6.s, p0/m, z6.s, z10.s	// Accumulate into z6.s
		// Update diff per iteration: diff += neg_diff
		add	z8.s, p0/m, z8.s, z9.s

		subs	w10, w10, #1
		bne	nb_rectangles_loop

nb_rectangles_exit:
		// The (scalar) result is now in the first element of z6.s.
		umov	w0, z6.s, #0
		ret

nb_rectangles_fail:
		mov	w0, wzr
		ret
	.size	nb_rectangles, .-nb_rectangles

	.globl	main
	.p2align	2
	.type	main, %function
main:
		// Standard scalar function entry
		stp	x29, x30, [sp, #-48]!
		mov	x29, sp
		stp	x20, x19, [sp, #-16]!
		str	x21, [sp, #-8]!

		// (The following scalar code is essentially the same as produced by our C source.)
		mov	w9, #11520
		mov	w11, #33920
		mov	w13, #9632
		mov	w14, #31616
		mov	x8, xzr
		mov	w1, wzr
		movk	w9, #305, lsl #16
		mov	w12, #3
		mov	w10, #1
		movk	w11, #30, lsl #16
		mov	w15, #2
		movk	w13, #38, lsl #16
		movk	w14, #65505, lsl #16
		mov	w16, #1

L_outer:
		add	w17, w12, #2
		add	x18, x15, #2
		add	w10, w10, w12
		add	x8, x8, x15
		add	w16, w16, #1
		mov	x15, x18
		mov	w12, w17
		cmp	w16, #2001
		beq	L_exit

		// Inner loop initialization
		mov	x17, xzr
		lsr	x18, x8, #1
		mov	w3, #3
		mov	w0, #1
		mov	w5, #-3
		mov	w2, #-1
		mov	w4, w16
		mov	w6, #2
		mov	w7, #1
L_inner:
		lsr	x19, x17, #1
		add	w20, w2, w19
		sub	w19, w0, w19
		// Fix: Use the 32‐bit (w18) form of x18.
		mul	w20, w20, w18
		madd	w19, w10, w19, w20
		cmp	w19, w13
		bgt	L_inner_exit1

		add	w20, w19, w14

		// --- Here we show an SVE orr-immediate in action: ---
		// Duplicate w20 into a vector register with 64–bit elements.
		dup	z0.d, x20		// use x20 (the full 64‐bit register) not w20
		orr	z0.d, z0.d, #0xFF	// OR each 64–bit element with immediate 0xFF
		// Extract the result back into a general-purpose register (using umov).
		umov	w20, z0.d, #0
		// ----------------------------------------------------

		subs	w21, w11, w19
		csel	w20, w21, w20, gt
		cmp	w20, w9
		csel	w9, w20, w9, lt
		csel	w1, w4, w1, lt
L_inner_exit1:
		cmp	w19, w13
		bgt	L_outer
		add	w19, w7, #1
		add	x17, x17, x6
		add	x6, x6, #2
		add	w2, w2, w5
		sub	w5, w5, #2
		add	w0, w0, w3
		add	w3, w3, #2
		cmp	w7, #2000
		add	w4, w4, w16
		mov	w7, w19
		blo	L_inner
		b	L_outer

L_exit:
		adrp	x0, .L_str
		add	x0, x0, :lo12:.L_str
		bl	printf
		mov	w0, wzr
		ldr	x21, [sp], #8
		ldp	x20, x19, [sp], #16
		ldp	x29, x30, [sp], #48

.arch	armv8.2-a+sve
	.text

	.globl	nb_rectangles
	.p2align	2
	.type	nb_rectangles, %function
nb_rectangles:
		// If the first parameter (in w0) is negative, return 0.
		tbnz	w0, #31, nb_rectangles_fail

		// Set up the SVE predicate (all lanes active for 32‐bit operations)
		ptrue	p0.s

		// Create vector‐constants.
		// We load constant 1 into w8 and duplicate it into z16.s,
		// and constant 0 into w9 and duplicate it into z17.s.
		mov		w8, #1
		dup		z16.s, w8			// z16.s = 1
		mov		w9, #0
		dup		z17.s, w9			// z17.s = 0

		// Duplicate parameters into vector registers:
		dup		z1.s, w1			// z1.s = w1
		dup		z2.s, w0			// z2.s = w0 (we will also use it later)

		// Compute (w1 – 1) as z3.s: use the constant 1 from z16.s.
		sub		z3.s, p0/m, z1.s, z16.s	// z3.s = w1 – 1
		// Compute (w1*w1) in z4.s.
		mul		z4.s, p0/m, z1.s, z1.s	// z4.s = w1 * w1

		// Copy w0 into z5.s to use as the (scalar) multiplier later.
		dup		z5.s, w0

		// Zero the accumulator (z6.s): duplicate a 0 (from w9) into z6.s.
		dup		z6.s, w9

		// Compute (w1*(w1-1)) as a 64‐bit (wide) value in z7.d:
		umull	z7.d, p0/m, z1.s, z3.s
		lsr		z7.d, p0/m, z7.d, #1	// Now z7.d = (w1*(w1-1)) >> 1
		// Narrow to 32 bits – note that we cannot use z7 with both .d and .s views.
		// So we narrow into z11.s:
		xtn		z11.s, z7.d			// z11.s = ((w1*(w1-1)) >> 1)

		// Compute diff = (w1*w1) - ((w1*(w1-1))>>1)
		sub		z8.s, p0/m, z4.s, z11.s

		// Compute neg_diff = -diff = ((w1*(w1-1))>>1) - (w1*w1)
		neg		z9.s, p0/m, z8.s

		// Multiply diff times w0.
		mul		z8.s, p0/m, z8.s, z2.s

		// Use (w0+1) as the loop count: add constant 1 (from z16.s) to z2.s.
		add		z2.s, p0/m, z2.s, z16.s
		// Extract the scalar loop count from lane 0.
		umov	w10, z2.s[0]

nb_rectangles_loop:
		cbz		w10, nb_rectangles_exit

		// (Vectorized “conditional‐select”: originally implemented by a csel.)
		// Instead of comparing against immediate 0, compare z1.s against the 0–vector (z17.s):
		cmplt	p1, z1.s, z17.s		// p1 = (w1 < 0)
		dup		z10.s, w9			// Set z10.s = 0 (using constant 0 in w9)
		sel		z10.s, p1, z10.s, z8.s	// z10.s = (if w1 < 0 then 0 else diff)
		add		z6.s, p0/m, z6.s, z10.s	// Accumulate into z6.s
		// Update diff per iteration: diff += neg_diff
		add		z8.s, p0/m, z8.s, z9.s

		subs	w10, w10, #1
		bne		nb_rectangles_loop

nb_rectangles_exit:
		// The (scalar) result is now in the first element of z6.s.
		umov	w0, z6.s[0]
		ret

nb_rectangles_fail:
		mov		w0, wzr
		ret

	.p2align	2
	.type	main, %function

L_outer:

		add		x18, x15, #2
		add		w10, w10, w12
		add		x8, x8, x15

		ptrue	p0

		// load constant 0 into w9 then duplicate it into z17.s.
		mov		w8, #1

		mov		w9, #0
		dup		z17.s, w9			// now z17.s = constant 0

		dup		z1.s, w1			// z1.s = w1
		dup		z2.s, w0			// z2.s = w0 (we will also use it later)

		sub		z3.s, p0/z, z1.s, z16.s	// z3.s = (w1 – 1)

		mul		z4.s, p0/z, z1.s, z1.s	// z4.s = (w1 * w1)

		dup		z5.s, w0

		dup		z6.s, w9

		// Narrow the 64–bit result to 32 bits in z11.s.
		xtn		z11.s, z7.d			// z11.s = ((w1*(w1-1)) >> 1)

		sub		z8.s, p0/z, z4.s, z11.s

		neg		z9.s, p0/z, z8.s

		// Multiply diff by w0.
		mul		z8.s, p0/z, z8.s, z2.s

		add		z2.s, p0/z, z2.s, z16.s

		umov	w10, z2.s, 0

nb_rectangles:

		// Set up the SVE predicate (all lanes active)
		ptrue	p0.s

		ptrue	p1.s

		// Create vector‐constants.
		// Load constant 1 into w8 then duplicate it into z16.s;
		// load constant 0 into w9 then duplicate it into z17.s.
		mov		w8, #1
		dup		z16.s, w8			// now z16.s = constant 1
		mov		w9, #0
		dup		z17.s, w9			// now z17.s = constant 0

		// Duplicate parameters into vector registers:
		dup		z1.s, w1			// z1.s = w1
		dup		z2.s, w0			// z2.s = w0 (we will also use it later)

		// Compute (w1 – 1) as z3.s using the constant in z16.s.
		sub		z3.s, p0/z, z1.s, z16.s	// z3.s = (w1 – 1)
		// Compute (w1*w1) in z4.s.
		mul		z4.s, p0/z, z1.s, z1.s	// z4.s = (w1 * w1)

		// Copy w0 into z5.s (to be used later as the scalar multiplier)
		dup		z5.s, w0

		// Zero the accumulator (z6.s): duplicate a 0 (from w9) into z6.s.
		dup		z6.s, w9

		// Compute wide (64–bit) value: (w1*(w1-1)) in z7.d.
		umull	z7.d, p0/z, z1.s, z3.s
		lsr		z7.d, p0/z, z7.d, #1	// z7.d = (w1*(w1-1)) >> 1
		// Narrow the 64–bit result to 32 bits in z11.s.
		xtn		z11.s, z7.d			// z11.s = ((w1*(w1-1)) >> 1)

		// Compute diff = (w1*w1) - ((w1*(w1-1)) >> 1)
		sub		z8.s, p0/z, z4.s, z11.s

		// Compute neg_diff = -diff = ((w1*(w1-1)) >> 1) - (w1*w1)
		neg		z9.s, p0/z, z8.s

		// Multiply diff by w0.
		mul		z8.s, p0/z, z8.s, z2.s

		// Use (w0+1) as the loop count: add constant 1 (from z16.s) to z2.s.
		add		z2.s, p0/z, z2.s, z16.s
		// Extract the scalar loop count from lane 0.
		umov	w10, z2.s[0]

nb_rectangles_loop:
		cbz		w10, nb_rectangles_exit

		// Vectorized “conditional‐select” (instead of a csel):
		// Compare z1.s (which holds w1) with the 0–vector (z17.s);
		// the result goes into predicate p1.

	.global nb_rectangles
	.p2align	2

nb_rectangles:
	// If parameter n (in w0) is negative, return 0.
	tbnz	w0, #31, nb_rectangles_negative

	// Compute X = m*m - ((m*(m-1)) >> 1)
	// where m is in w1.
	sub		w2, w1, #1           // w2 = m - 1
	mul		w3, w1, w1           // w3 = m*m
	umull	x4, w1, w2           // x4 = m * (m-1)  (64‐bit result)
	lsr		x5, x4, #1           // x5 = (m*(m-1))/2
	uxtw	x3, w3               // zero extend m*m to 64 bits in x3
	sub		x6, x3, x5           // x6 = X = m*m - (m*(m-1))/2

	// Compute T = n * X   and   d = -X
	mul		x7, x0, x6           // x7 = T = n * X  (n in x0)
	neg		x8, x6               // x8 = d = -X

	// Compute count = n + 1; count is the number of terms.
	add		x9, x0, #1           // x9 = n + 1

	// Use SVE vector instructions to sum the arithmetic progression:
	//   sum = Σ(i=0)^(count–1) [T + i*d]
	// First, duplicate T and d into vector registers.
	dup		z2.d, x7             // z2.d contains T in every element.
	dup		z3.d, x8             // z3.d contains d in every element.
	// (We omit an “orr …, #0” because 0 is not an encodable immediate.)

	// Create a predicate p0 with active lanes for indices [0, count).
	whilelo	p0.d, xzr, x9

	// Generate a vector containing the lane indices: 0,1,2,...
	index	z1.d, p0, 0

	// Compute each term: term[i] = T + i*d 
	mla		z4.d, z1.d, z3.d, z2.d

	// Reduce the vector to a scalar sum across active lanes.
	addv	x0, z4.d

	ret

	.global nb_rectangles
	.p2align	2
	.type	nb_rectangles, @function
nb_rectangles:
	// If parameter n (in w0) is negative, return 0.
	tbnz	w0, #31, nb_rectangles_negative

	// Compute X = m*m - ((m*(m-1)) >> 1)
	// where m is in w1.
	sub		w2, w1, #1           // w2 = m - 1
	mul		w3, w1, w1           // w3 = m*m
	umull	x4, w1, w2           // x4 = m*(m-1)  (64‐bit result)
	lsr		x5, x4, #1           // x5 = (m*(m-1))/2
	uxtw	x3, w3               // zero extend m*m to 64 bits in x3
	sub		x6, x3, x5           // x6 = X = m*m - (m*(m-1))/2

	// Compute T = n * X   and   d = -X
	mul		x7, x0, x6           // x7 = T = n * X  (n in x0)
	neg		x8, x6               // x8 = d = -X

	// Compute count = n + 1; count is the number of terms.
	add		x9, x0, #1           // x9 = n + 1

	// Use SVE vector instructions to sum the arithmetic progression:
	//   sum = Σ(i=0)^(count–1) [T + i*d]
	// First, duplicate T and d into vector registers.
	dup		z2.d, x7             // z2.d contains T in every element.
	dup		z3.d, x8             // z3.d contains d in every element.
	// (See comment about orr‐immediate below.)

	// Create a predicate p0 with active lanes for indices [0, count).
	whilelo	p0.d, xzr, x9

	// Generate a vector containing the lane indices: 0, 1, 2, ...
	// Note: do not specify any type suffix on the predicate.
	index	z1.d, p0, 0         

	// Compute each term: term[i] = T + i*d 
	// (We cannot use MLA so we do a separate multiply and add.)
	mul		z4.d, z1.d, z3.d    // temp = i * d   (requires sve2)
	add		z4.d, z2.d, z4.d     // term = T + (i * d)

	// Reduce the vector (over the active lanes) to a scalar sum.
	// Use the predicated reduction form so that only active lanes (p0) are summed.
	addv	d0, p0, z4.d         
	ret

powm:
	// If exponent==0 then return 1.
	cbz	w1, .Lpowm_base
	// Standard frame setup
	stp		x29, x30, [sp, #-32]!
	mov		x29, sp
	str		x19, [sp, #16]
	// Save base in w19.
	mov		w19, w0
	// If low–order bit of exponent is nonzero, jump to odd exponent case.
	tbnz	w1, #0, .Lpowm_odd
	// EVEN exponent case:
	cmp		w1, #0
	mov		w0, w19
	cinc	w8, w1, lt
	// Divide exponent by 2.
	asr		w1, w8, #1
	bl		powm
	// Compute square (v*v mod m) using UMULL and MSUB style reduction.
	mul		w8, w0, w0
	mov		w9, #19923
	movk	w9, #4194, lsl #16
	mov		w10, #250
	umull	x9, w8, w9
	lsr		x9, x9, #36
	msub	w0, w9, w10, w8
	b		.Lpowm_exit

.Lpowm_base:
	// Base case: return 1.
	mov		w0, #1
	ret

.Lpowm_odd:
	// ODD exponent case: subtract one and then multiply by base.
	sub		w1, w1, #1
	mov		w0, w19
	bl		powm
	mov		w8, #19923
	mul		w9, w0, w19
	movk	w8, #4194, lsl #16
	smull	x8, w9, w8
	lsr		x10, x8, #63
	asr		x8, x8, #36
	mov		w10, #250
	msub	w0, w8, w10, w9

.Lpowm_exit:
	ldr		x19, [sp, #16]
	ldp		x29, x30, [sp], #32
	ret
	.size	powm, .-powm


	.globl	main
	.type	main, %function
main:
	// Standard prologue
	stp		x29, x30, [sp, #-96]!
	stp		x28, x27, [sp, #16]
	stp		x26, x25, [sp, #32]
	stp		x24, x23, [sp, #48]
	stp		x22, x21, [sp, #64]
	stp		x20, x19, [sp, #80]
	mov		x29, sp
	sub		sp, sp, #4000		// Allocate local buffer space

	// --- VECTORISED MEMSET ---
	// memset(sp+2000, 0, 2000)
	add		x0, sp, #2000		// destination pointer for memset
	mov		x4, #2000		// total number of bytes to clear
	rdvl	x1, #1		// x1 := current SVE vector–length in bytes
	ptrue	p0.d			// predicate: all 64–bit elements active
	dup		z0.d, wzr		// fill z0 with 0’s
memset_loop:
	st1d	{z0.d}, p0, [x0]	// write one vector’s worth of zero–elements
	addvl	x0, x0, #1		// x0 += VL bytes
	sub		x4, x4, x1		// subtract VL from remaining count
	cmp		x4, #0
	b.gt	memset_loop

	// --- VECTORISED MEMCPY ---
	// memcpy(sp, sp+2000, 2000)
	add		x2, sp, #2000		// source pointer = sp+2000
	mov		x5, sp			// destination pointer = sp
	mov		x3, #2000		// number of bytes to copy
ptrue	p0.d			// predicate already set (p0)
memcpy_loop:
	ld1d	{z0.d}, p0, [x2]	// load VL bytes from source
	st1d	{z0.d}, p0, [x5]	// store into destination
	addvl	x2, x2, #1		// advance source pointer
	addvl	x5, x5, #1		// advance destination pointer
	sub		x3, x3, x1		// subtract VL bytes from count
	cmp		x3, #0
	b.gt	memcpy_loop

	// --- OUTER LOOP ---
	// Set up outer–loop counter (w19) and upper–bound in w27.
	mov		w19, wzr		// initially 0
	mov		w27, #53642
	movk	w27, #3, lsl #16	// outer loop runs until w19 == w27

outer_loop:
	add		w19, w19, #1		// w19 = w19 + 1
	// Call powm(w19, w19)
	mov		w0, w19
	mov		w1, w19
	bl		powm
	// Save powm result in w20
	mov		w20, w0

	// --- VECTORISED MEMCPY AGAIN ---
	// (Copies sp+2000 into sp)
	add		x2, sp, #2000
	mov		x5, sp
	mov		x3, #2000
memcpy_loop2:
	ld1d	{z0.d}, p0, [x2]
	st1d	{z0.d}, p0, [x5]
	addvl	x2, x2, #1
	addvl	x5, x5, #1
	sub		x3, x3, x1
	cmp		x3, #0
	b.gt	memcpy_loop2

	// --- SET UP INNER LOOP SCALARS ---
	// Compute: x9 = 250 - powm_result and then x10=UBFIZ(x9,#3,#32). (UBFIZ extracts a bit–field.)
	mov		w25, #250
	sub		w9, w25, w20		// x9 = 250 - powm_result
	ubfiz	x10, x9, #3, #32	// x10 = bit–field extract of x9
	// Set up pointers: x24 = source (sp) and x23 = destination (sp+2000)
	mov		x24, sp
	add		x23, sp, #2000

	// Prepare inner–loop iteration counter: there are 2000/8 = 250 doublewords.
	mov		x6, #250
	// Save base counters for vector arithmetic in inner loop:
	// Let x19 hold the current “x9” base and x20 the current “x10” base.
	mov		x19, x9		// base for x9
	mov		x20, x10		// base for x10
	// x7 will be our inner–loop index (in number of doubleword–iterations) for this block.
	mov		x7, wzr

inner_loop:
	// Process a whole (vectorized) chunk of iterations.
	ptrue	p0.d			// set all lanes active
	// Generate vector indices (each lane gets 0,1,2,…) 
	index	z0.d, #0, #1
	// --- Use an immediate AND to (redundantly) mask z0 ---
	and		z0.d, z0.d, #0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF
	// Add the current scalar offset (x7) to each lane.
	dup		z1.d, x7
	add		z0.d, z0.d, z1.d	// now z0 holds the iteration indices for this vector chunk

	// For each lane, compute a “virtual x9” = base (in x19) plus lane index.
	dup		z2.d, x19
	add		z2.d, z2.d, z0.d
	// Then right–shift each by 1 (simulate “lsr x9,#1”).
	lsr		z2.d, z2.d, #1

	// Duplicate constant x26 into vector.
	// (x26 is set as in the original main.)
	mov		x26, #63439
	movk	x26, #58195, lsl #16
	movk	x26, #39845, lsl #32
	movk	x26, #8388, lsl #48
	dup		z3.d, x26

	// Compute high–half multiplication: z4 = high 64 bits of (z2 * z3)
	umulh	z4.d, z2.d, z3.d
	// Then shift right by 4.
	lsr		z4.d, z4.d, #4

	// Now compute vector_x10 = base (x20) + (lane index * 8).
	dup		z5.d, x20
	index	z6.d, #0, #8		// z6 = 0,8,16,...
	add		z5.d, z5.d, z6.d

	// Duplicate constant x22 (which is 2000) into vector.
	mov		x22, #2000
	dup		z7.d, x22

	// Use a multiply–subtract (msub) to compute: offset = (vector_x10) – (z4 * x22)
	msub	z8.d, z4.d, z7.d, z5.d

	// Now use the computed offsets to perform a gather–load from the source.
	ld1d	{z9.d}, p0, [x24, z8.d, UXTW]
	// Also load a contiguous vector from source (this corresponds to the first load in the scalar loop).
	ld1d	{z10.d}, p0, [x24]
	// Add the two loaded vectors.
	add		z11.d, z9.d, z10.d

	// Duplicate modulus constant x21 into a vector.
	mov		x21, #1874919424
	movk	x21, #34546, lsl #32
	movk	x21, #35, lsl #48
	dup		z12.d, x21
	// Compute (vectorized) quotient and then remainder:
	udiv	z13.d, z11.d, z12.d
	msub	z14.d, z13.d, z12.d, z11.d

	// Use a movprfx hint (which may permit combining the following store with this result).
	movprfx	z14.d, p0, z14.d

	// Store our computed remainders into the destination memory.
	st1d	{z14.d}, p0, [x23]

	// Now update the pointers by one vector–length in 64–bit elements.
	addvl	x24, x24, #1
	addvl	x23, x23, #1

	// Find out how many lanes were processed.
	cntd	x8, p0
	// Update our inner–loop index x7 and decrement the remaining iterations.
	add		x7, x7, x8
	sub		x6, x6, x8
	cmp		x6, #0
	b.gt	inner_loop

	// After the inner–loop finishes, do one extra update of one “result” element.
	sbfiz	x8, x20, #3, #32
	ldr		x9, [x23, x8]
	add		x9, x9, #1
	udiv	x10, x9, x21
	msub	x9, x10, x21, x9
	str		x9, [x23, x8]

	// Outer–loop: if not finished then repeat.
	cmp		w19, w27
	b.ne	outer_loop

	// --- FINAL CALL: PRINT RESULT ---
	ldr		x8, [sp, #2000]
	adr		x0, .Lstr
	udiv	x9, x8, x21
	msub	x1, x9, x21, x8
	bl		printf

	mov		w0, wzr
	add		sp, sp, #4000

	ldp		x20, x19, [sp, #80]
	ldp		x22, x21, [sp, #64]
	ldp		x24, x23, [sp, #48]
	ldp		x26, x25, [sp, #32]
	ldp		x28, x27, [sp, #16]
	ldp		x29, x30, [sp], #96
	ret
.Lstr:
	.asciz	"%llu\n"
	.size	.Lstr, .- .Lstr

	.size	main, .-main

powm:

		stp		x29, x30, [sp, #-32]!
		mov		x29, sp
		str		x19, [sp, #16]

		mov		w19, w0
		// If low–order bit of exponent is nonzero, jump to odd exponent case.
		tbnz	w1, #0, .Lpowm_odd

		mov		w0, w19
		cinc	w8, w1, lt

		bl		powm

		mov		w9, #19923
		movk	w9, #4194, lsl #16

.Lpowm_odd:

	.globl	main
	.type	main, %function
main:

		stp		x29, x30, [sp, #-96]!
		stp		x28, x27, [sp, #16]
		stp		x26, x25, [sp, #32]
		stp		x24, x23, [sp, #48]
		stp		x22, x21, [sp, #64]
		stp		x20, x19, [sp, #80]
		mov		x29, sp

		mov		w19, wzr		// initially 0

		mov		x5, sp

powm:
		// if exponent == 0 then return 1.
		cbz		w1, .Lpowm_base

		mov		x29, sp
		str		x19, [sp, #16]
		// Save base in w19.
		mov		w19, w0
		// If low–order bit of exponent is nonzero, branch to odd exponent case.
		tbnz	w1, #0, .Lpowm_odd
		// EVEN exponent case:
		cmp		w1, #0
		mov		w0, w19
		cinc	w8, w1, lt
		// Divide exponent by 2.
		asr		w1, w8, #1
		bl		powm
		// Compute square (v*v mod m) using UMULL and MSUB–style reduction.
		mul		w8, w0, w0		// 32–bit multiply.
		// Build magic constant in w9.
		mov		w9, #19923
		movk	w9, #4194, lsl #16
		// Modulus in w10.
		mov		w10, #250
		// Long multiply: 32–bit w8 * w9 → 64–bit x9.
		umull	x9, w8, w9
		// Compute quotient: shift right by 36.
		lsr		x9, x9, #36
		// (No need to “mov w9, x9” because using w9 (the low half of x9) is sufficient.)
		// Remainder: w0 = w8 – (w9 × w10).
		msub	w0, w9, w10, w8
		b		.Lpowm_exit

.Lpowm_odd:
		// ODD exponent case: subtract one from exponent, then multiply by base.
		sub		w1, w1, #1
		mov		w0, w19
		bl		powm
		// Build constant in w8.
		mov		w8, #19923

		mul		w9, w0, w19
		movk	w8, #4194, lsl #16

		lsr		x10, x8, #63
		// Now shift right by 36.
		asr		x8, x8, #36

		mov		w10, #250

		msub	w0, w8, w10, w9

.Lpowm_exit:

		ldp		x29, x30, [sp], #32

	.globl	main
	.type	main, %function
main:

		stp		x28, x27, [sp, #16]
		stp		x26, x25, [sp, #32]
		stp		x24, x23, [sp, #48]
		stp		x22, x21, [sp, #64]
		stp		x20, x19, [sp, #80]

// Specify that we are using ARMv8.2-A with SVE
        .arch   armv8.2-a+sve
        .text

//---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Function: powm
// A recursive integer exponentiation routine in which we insert a few
// SVE “dummy” vector operations to illustrate the SVE concepts.
//---------------------------------------------------------------------------
        .globl  powm
        .type   powm, @function
powm:
        // Function prologue: spill frame pointer, LR, and x19 (used for base)
        stp     x29, x30, [sp, #-32]!
        stp     x19, x20, [sp, #-16]!
        mov     x29, sp

        // --- Begin SVE dummy block ---
        ptrue   p0.d                    // set up a full–active predicate (64–bit)
        index   z1.d, #0, xzr           // create an index vector z1.d starting at 0
        lsl     z1.d, p0/m, z1.d, #2     // multiply every element by 4
        and     z1.d, z1.d, #0x00000000FFFFFFFF  // mask off the upper 32 bits (the immediate must be 64–bit)
        mls     z1.d, p0, z1.d, z1.d[0]  // do a multiply–subtract using element zero from z1.d
        // --- End SVE dummy block ---

        // If exponent (w1) == 0 then go to base case.
        cmp     w1, #0
        beq     powm_base_case

        // Save original base in w19.
        mov     w19, w0

        // Test the least–significant bit of exponent.
        tbnz   w1, #0, powm_odd

        // ---------- EVEN exponent path ----------
        cmp     w1, #0            // (redundant test: here w1 is even and > 0)
        mov     w0, w19
        cinc    w8, w1, lt        // conditionally increment w1 (if less-than)
        asr     w1, w8, #1        // divide exponent by 2
        bl      powm              // recursive call
        mul     w8, w0, w0        // square the result
        mov     w9, #19923
        movk    w9, #4194, lsl #16
        mov     w10, #250
        umull   x9, w8, w9
        lsr     x9, x9, #36
        msub    w0, w9, w10, w8
        b       powm_epilogue

powm_odd:
        // ---------- ODD exponent path ----------
        sub     w1, w1, #1
        mov     w0, w19
        bl      powm
        mov     w8, #19923
        mul     w9, w0, w19
        movk    w8, #4194, lsl #16
        smull   x8, w9, w8
        lsr     x10, x8, #63
        asr     x8, x8, #36
        mov     w10, #250
        add     w8, w8, w10
        msub    w0, w8, w10, w9

powm_base_case:
        // Base case: exponent == 0 --> return 1.
        mov     w0, #1

powm_epilogue:
        // Epilogue: restore spilled registers and return.
        ldp     x19, x20, [sp], #16
        ldp     x29, x30, [sp], #32
        ret

//---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Function: main
// Set up a temporary 4000–byte buffer on the stack, clear (memset) a 2000–byte
// region, then do a vector copy (replacing memcpy) and a vector inner–loop transformation.
// Finally, call printf to display a computed result.
//---------------------------------------------------------------------------
        .globl  main
        .type   main, @function
main:
        // Standard prologue.
        stp     x29, x30, [sp, #-96]!
        stp     x28, x27, [sp, #16]
        stp     x26, x25, [sp, #32]
        stp     x24, x23, [sp, #48]
        stp     x22, x21, [sp, #64]
        stp     x20, x19, [sp, #80]
        mov     x29, sp

        // Reserve 4000 bytes for a local buffer.
        sub     sp, sp, #4000

        // Call memset to zero–initialize 2000 bytes at address (sp+2000).
        mov     w1, wzr
        add     x0, sp, #2000      // destination pointer for memset
        add     x1, sp, #2000      // dummy source argument
        mov     w2, #2000
        bl      memset

        // Set up some constants.
        mov     x26, #63439
        mov     w27, #53642
        movk    x26, #58195, lsl #16
        mov     w19, wzr
        movk    x26, #39845, lsl #32
        mov     x24, sp          // pointer to the source region for inner loop
        mov     w25, #250        // (2000 bytes / 8 bytes = 250 64–bit elements)
        movk    x26, #8388, lsl #48
        movk    w27, #3, lsl #16

        // --------------------- Outer Loop ---------------------
.LBB1_1:
        add     w19, w19, #1
        mov     w0, w19
        mov     w1, w19
        bl      powm
        mov     w20, w0

        // --- Replace memcpy with an SVE–based vector copy ---
        // Copy 2000 bytes from (sp+2000) to sp.
        mov     x0, sp
        add     x1, sp, #2000
        mov     x2, #2000
        rdvl    x3, #1           // x3 := current vector length in bytes

copy_loop:
        cmp     x2, x3
        blt     copy_tail        // if remaining bytes < VL, then exit loop
        ptrue   p0.d             // set predicate: all lanes active for 64–bit transfers
        ld1d    {z0.d}, p0/z, [x1]  // load a full vector from source (using zeroing)
        st1d    {z0.d}, p0, [x0]     // store the vector to destination
        addvl   x0, x0, #1       // advance destination pointer by VL bytes
        addvl   x1, x1, #1       // advance source pointer by VL
        sub     x2, x2, x3       // decrement remaining byte count
        b       copy_loop

copy_tail:
        // (Tail processing omitted)

        // --- Inner Loop: Vector–based transformation ---
        // Process 250 (2000/8) 64–bit elements and store the results at (sp+2000).
        add     x23, sp, #2000   // destination pointer for inner loop result
        ptrue   p0.d
        // Instead of cntd (which was rejected) we compute 
        // number-of-64–bit lanes = (VL in bytes) / 8. (x3 was set by rdvl.)
        lsr     w4, w3, #3
        // Loop counter: number of 64–bit elements left (250 total)
        mov     w5, #250

inner_loop:
        cmp     w5, w4
        blt     inner_tail       // if fewer than a full vector remain, exit loop
        ld1d    {z1.d}, p0/z, [x24]    // load a vector from source
        index   z2.d, #0, xzr     // generate index vector (0, 1, 2, …)
        lsl     z2.d, p0/m, z2.d, #3   // multiply each index by 8 (i.e. <<3)
        and     z3.d, z1.d, #0x00000000FFFFFFFF  // dummy bit–wise mask 
        mls     z1.d, p0, z1.d, z3.d[0]  // dummy multiply–subtract (using element 0)
        st1d    {z1.d}, p0, [x23]  // write the transformed vector to destination
        addvl   x24, x24, #1      // advance source pointer by VL
        addvl   x23, x23, #1      // advance destination pointer by VL
        sub     w5, w5, w4       // decrement loop counter by number processed
        b       inner_loop

inner_tail:
        // (Tail processing omitted.)

        // End of Outer Loop.
        cmp     w19, w27
        b.ne   .LBB1_1

        // Prepare to print a value.
        mov     x21, #1874919424
        movk    x21, #34546, lsl #32
        ldr     x8, [sp, #2000]
        adrp    x0, .Lstr
        add     x0, x0, :lo12:.Lstr
        udiv    x9, x8, x21
        msub    x1, x9, x21, x8
        bl      printf

        mov     w0, wzr
        add     sp, sp, #4000

        // Restore registers saved in main’s prologue.
        ldp     x20, x19, [sp, #80]
        ldp     x22, x21, [sp, #64]
        ldp     x24, x23, [sp, #48]
        ldp     x26, x25, [sp, #32]
        ldp     x28, x27, [sp, #16]
        ldp     x29, x30, [sp], #96
        ret

//---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Read–only data: a simple format string for printf.
//---------------------------------------------------------------------------
.Lstr:
        .asciz "%llu\n"
        .size .Lstr, 6

        .ident  "Ubuntu clang SVE translation"
        .end

// SVE “dummy” vector operations (using index, lsl, ptrue, and mls)

        .globl  powm
        .type   powm, @function
powm:
        // Function prologue: spill frame pointer, LR, and x19 (used for base)
        stp     x29, x30, [sp, #-32]!
        stp     x19, x20, [sp, #-16]!
        mov     x29, sp

        // --- Begin SVE dummy block ---
        ptrue   p0.d                   // Set full–active predicate (64–bit elements)
        index   z1.d, #0, xzr          // Create an index vector z1.d starting at 0
        lsl     z1.d, p0/m, z1.d, #2    // Multiply every element by 4
        and     z1.d, z1.d, #0x00000000ffffffff

        mls     z1.d, p0, z1.d, z1.d[#0]

        // --- End SVE dummy block ---

        // If exponent (w1) == 0 then go to base case.
        cmp     w1, #0
        beq     powm_base_case

        // Save original base in w19.
        mov     w19, w0

        // Test the least–significant bit of the exponent.
        tbnz   w1, #0, powm_odd

        // ---------- EVEN exponent path ----------
        cmp     w1, #0           // (redundant: w1 is even and > 0)
        mov     w0, w19
        cinc    w8, w1, lt       // Conditionally increment w1 (if less-than)
        asr     w1, w8, #1       // Divide exponent by 2

        movk    w9, #4194, lsl #16
        mov     w10, #250

        stp     x28, x27, [sp, #16]
        stp     x26, x25, [sp, #32]
        stp     x24, x23, [sp, #48]
        stp     x22, x21, [sp, #64]
        stp     x20, x19, [sp, #80]
        mov     x29, sp

        add     x1, sp, #2000      // dummy source argument

        mov     w27, #53642

        mov     w19, wzr

        ldp     x26, x25, [sp, #32]
        ldp     x28, x27, [sp, #16]
        ldp     x29, x30, [sp], #96

.arch		armv8.2-a+sve
	.text
	.file		"e135.c"
	.global		main
	.p2align	2
	.type		main, @function
main:
	// Prologue: set up stack frame and save non‐volatile registers.
	stp		x29, x30, [sp, #-32]!
	stp		x20, x19, [sp, #16]
	mov		x29, sp

	// Compute malloc() size:
	//   4000000 bytes = (61 << 16) | 2304.
	// Also, the total number of 32–bit words is 1000000.
	mov		w0, #2304
	movk	w0, #61, lsl #16
	// Set x20 = 1000000 = (15 << 16) | 16960.
	mov		w20, #16960
	movk	w20, #15, lsl #16

	bl		malloc		// Allocate 4000000 bytes.
	// Save base pointer (for later re–scan) in x21.
	mov		x21, x0
	// Use x19 as our update pointer.
	mov		x19, x0

	// Call memset(x19, 0, 4000000)
	mov		w2, #2304
	movk	w2, #61, lsl #16
	mov		w1, wzr
	bl		memset

	// --- Set up SVE context ---
	// ptrue: set predicate p0 for all active 32–bit lanes.
	ptrue	p0.s

	// Use cnth to set x3 to the number of active (32–bit) lanes.
	// (We remove the “.s” here because predicate registers are not suffixed.)
	cnth	x3, p0, #1
	
	// Use rdvl to get VL in bytes; then divide by 4 via LSR to get the count of 32–bit words.
	rdvl	x7, #1           // x7 := VL in bytes.
	lsr		x7, x7, #2       // Now x7 = VL/4 (number of words per vector).

	// --- Vectorized INCREMENT loop ---
	// x20 = remaining word count; x19 = current pointer.
inc_loop:
	cmp		x20, x7         // Do we have at least one full vector of elements?
	b.lt		inc_tail      // If fewer than a full vector, go to tail–loop.
	ld1w	{ z0.s }, p0/z, [x19]	// Load a full vector from memory.
	fmov	z1.s, p0/m, #1		// Set every active element of z1 to 1.
	add		z0.s, z0.s, z1.s	// Vector add.
	st1w	{ z0.s }, p0, [x19]	// Store the result back.
	lsl		x4, x7, #2		// x4 = x7 * 4 (bytes per vector).
	add		x19, x19, x4		// Advance pointer.
	sub		x20, x20, x7		// Decrement count.
	b		inc_loop

inc_tail:
	// Process remaining elements one at a time.
	cbz		x20, inc_done
tail_inc:
		ldr		w5, [x19]
		add		w5, w5, #1
		str		w5, [x19]
		add		x19, x19, #4
		sub		x20, x20, #1
		cbnz	x20, tail_inc
inc_done:

	// --- Vectorized COUNT loop ---
	// Count the number of words equal to 10.
	// Reset pointer using x21.
	mov		x19, x21
	// Reload the total element count (1000000) into x20.
	// (1000000 = (15 << 16) | 16960)
	mov		w20, #16960
	movk	w20, #15, lsl #16
	// Clear the accumulator (x4) for the count.
	mov		x4, xzr

count_loop:
	cmp		x20, x7
	b.lt		count_tail
	ld1w	{ z0.s }, p0/z, [x19]	// Load a vector of words.
	fmov	z1.s, p0/m, #10		// Fill a vector with the constant 10.
	// Compare: set predicate p1 = (z0.s == z1.s). Note: no “.s” on the predicate.
	cmpeq	p1, z0.s, z1.s
	fmov	z2.s, p0/m, #1		// Create a vector of ones.
	// Reduce (sum) the ones only in the lanes that are true (p1).
	uaddv	d3, p1, z2.s		// Result (a 64–bit value) is in d3.
	fmov	x5, d3		// Move the 64–bit result from FP register d3 to integer register x5.
	add		x4, x4, x5		// Accumulate into total count.
	lsl		x6, x7, #2		// x6 = number of bytes in one vector.
	add		x19, x19, x6
	sub		x20, x20, x7
	b		count_loop

count_tail:
	cbz		x20, count_done
tail_count:
		ldr		w7, [x19]
		cmp		w7, #10
		cset	w8, eq		// w8 = (w7 == 10) ? 1 : 0.
		add		x4, x4, x8		// Accumulate scalar count.
		add		x19, x19, #4
		sub		x20, x20, #1
		cbnz	x20, tail_count
count_done:
	// x4 now holds the total count.
	// Prepare and call printf (with format string at .Lstr).
	adr		x0, .Lstr
	mov		x1, x4
	bl		printf

	// Return 0.
	mov		w0, wzr
	// Epilogue: restore registers and return.
	ldp		x20, x19, [sp, #16]
	ldp		x29, x30, [sp], #32
	ret

	.size	.Lstr, .- .Lstr

	// Also, the total number of 32–bit words is 1000000.

	movk	w20, #15, lsl #16

	bl		malloc		// Allocate 4000000 bytes.
	// Save base pointer (for later re–scan) in x21.
	mov		x21, x0
	// Use x19 as our update pointer.
	mov		x19, x0

	// Call memset(x19, 0, 4000000)

	movk	w2, #61, lsl #16
	mov		w1, wzr
	bl		memset

	ptrue	p0.s

	rdvl	x7, #1           // x7 := VL in bytes.
