.arch    armv8.2-a+sve     // Enable SVE instructions
        .text
        .global main
        .type   main, %function
main:
        // Prologue: save frame pointer and callee‐saved registers.
        stp     x29, x30, [sp, #-32]!
        mov     x29, sp
        stp     x20, x19, [sp, #16]

        // --- Allocate 4,000,000 bytes and clear them ---
        // Compute 4000000 = 61<<16 + 2304.
        mov     w0, #2304           // lower 16‐bit part (0x0900)
        movk    w0, #61, lsl #16     // upper half (0x3D0000) → 0x3D0900 = 4000000
        bl      malloc              // x0 = pointer to allocated memory
        mov     x19, x0             // x19 holds the pointer

        // Call memset(pointer,0,4000000):
        mov     x0, x19             // first argument = pointer
        mov     w1, wzr             // second argument = 0
        mov     w2, #2304
        movk    w2, #61, lsl #16
        bl      memset

        // --- Set up loop parameters ---
        // Total number of 32‐bit integers to process is 1,000,000.
        mov     w20, #16960         // 0x4240 (low half)
        movk    w20, #15, lsl #16    // 15<<16 = 983040 so 983040+16960 = 1000000

        // Zero the accumulator (the count of elements equal to 10)
        mov     w1, wzr

        // Set up SVE predicate for 32‐bit elements.
        ptrue   p0.s

        // Determine the number of active lanes (i.e. the number of 32‐bit elements we can process in one vector load).
        cntw    x4, p0.s

        // Compute the number of bytes loaded per vector (each lane is 4 bytes)
        lsl     x24, x4, #2         // x24 = x4 * 4

        // Compute full‐vector iteration count: x6 = total elements / lanes.
        udiv    x6, x20, x4
        // Compute remainder (if the total isn’t an exact multiple)
        msub    x7, x6, x4, x20     // x7 = x20 – (x6 * x4)

        // --- Dummy block to show use of RDVL, FMOV immediate predicated and LSR immediate predicated ---
        rdvl    x0, #1             // x0 ← (current SVE vector length in bytes)
        ptrue   p7.s               // set a full predicate (p7) for dummy operations
        fmov    z31.s, p7/m, #1.0   // fmov immediate predicated: load 1.0 into every active lane of z31.s
        dup     z30.s, w0          // duplicate the lower 32‐bit of x0 into every lane of z30.s
        lsr     z30.s, p7/m, z30.s, #2  // SVE predicated logical shift right by 2

        // --- Prepare constants for the vector loop ---
        dup     z1.s, #10          // Fill z1.s with the value 10 in every lane.
        dup     z3.s, #1           // Prepare a “1‐vector” in z3.s.
        dup     z2.s, #0           // Prepare a zero–vector in z2.s.

        // --- Vector loop: process full vectors (each vector holds x4 32‐bit integers) ---
        cmp     x6, #0
        beq     vector_loop_done
vector_loop:
        ld1w    { z0.s }, p0/z, [x19]      // load a full vector (x4 32‐bit integers) from memory
        cmpeq   p2.s, z0.s, z1.s            // compare each element with 10; result predicate in p2.s
        sel     z2.s, p2.s, z3.s, z2.s       // for lanes where p2.s is true, select 1 (from z3.s), else leave 0.
        uaddv   w7, p0.s, z2.s             // horizontally add all lanes of z2.s → w7 holds count for this vector
        add     w1, w1, w7               // accumulate result into w1
        add     x19, x19, x24            // advance pointer by one vector’s worth (x24 bytes)
        subs    x6, x6, #1               // decrement iteration counter
        bne     vector_loop

vector_loop_done:
        // --- Remainder loop: process leftover elements one–by–one ---
        cmp     x7, #0
        beq     remainder_done
remainder_loop:
        ldr     w8, [x19], #4            // load one 32‐bit integer from memory
        cmp     w8, #10                 // compare it to 10
        cset    w10, eq                 // set w10 = 1 if equal, else 0 
        add     w1, w1, w10             // add (0 or 1) to the accumulator in w1
        subs    x7, x7, #1
        bne     remainder_loop
remainder_done:

        // --- Print the resulting count (as an integer) ---
        adrp    x0, .Lstr               // get format string address in x0
        add     x0, x0, :lo12:.Lstr
        // The count (in w1) is passed as the first integer argument.
        bl      printf

        // Epilogue: restore callee‐saved registers and return.
        ldp     x20, x19, [sp, #16]
        ldp     x29, x30, [sp], #32
        mov     w0, wzr
        ret

.Lstr:
        .asciz "%i\n"
        .size  .Lstr, . - .Lstr

.arch   armv8.2-a+sve     // Enable SVE instructions
        .text
        .global main
        .type   main, %function

main:
        // Prologue: save frame pointer and callee‐saved registers.
        stp     x29, x30, [sp, #-32]!
        mov     x29, sp
        stp     x20, x19, [sp, #16]

        // --- Allocate 4,000,000 bytes and clear them ---
        // Compute 4000000 = 61<<16 + 2304.
        mov     w0, #2304           // lower 16–bit part (0x0900)
        movk    w0, #61, lsl #16     // upper half (0x3D0000) → 0x3D0900 = 4000000
        bl      malloc              // x0 = pointer to allocated memory
        mov     x19, x0             // x19 holds the pointer

        // Call memset(pointer,0,4000000):
        mov     x0, x19             // first argument = pointer
        mov     w1, wzr             // second argument = 0
        mov     w2, #2304
        movk    w2, #61, lsl #16
        bl      memset

        // --- Set up loop parameters ---
        // Total number of 32‐bit integers to process is 1,000,000.
        mov     w20, #16960         // 0x4240 (low half)
        movk    w20, #15, lsl #16    // 15<<16 = 983040 so 983040+16960 = 1000000

        // Zero the accumulator (the count of elements equal to 10)
        mov     w1, wzr

        // Set up SVE predicate for 32‐bit elements.
        ptrue   p0

        // Determine the number of active lanes (i.e. the number of 32‐bit elements we can process in one vector load).
        cntw    x4, p0

        // Compute the number of bytes loaded per vector (each lane is 4 bytes)
        lsl     x24, x4, #2         // x24 = x4 * 4

        // Compute full–vector iteration count: x6 = total_elements / lanes.
        udiv    x6, x20, x4
        // Compute remainder (if the total isn’t an exact multiple)
        msub    x7, x6, x4, x20     // x7 = x20 – (x6 * x4)

        // --- Dummy block to show use of RDVL, FMOV immediate predicated and LSR immediate predicated ---
        rdvl    x0, #1             // x0 ← (current SVE vector length in bytes)
        ptrue   p7               // set a full predicate for dummy operations
        fmov    z31.s, p7/m, #1.0   // move immediate 1.0 into every active lane of z31.s
        dup     z30.s, w0          // duplicate low 32–bit of x0 into every lane of z30.s
        lsr     z30.s, p7/m, z30.s, #2  // logical shift right by 2 (predicated)

        // --- Prepare constants for the vector loop ---
        dup     z1.s, #10          // Fill z1.s with the value 10 in every lane.
        dup     z3.s, #1           // Prepare a “1–vector” in z3.s.
        dup     z2.s, #0           // Prepare a zero–vector in z2.s.

        // --- Vector loop: process full vectors (each vector holds x4 32–bit integers) ---
        cmp     x6, #0
        beq     vector_loop_done
vector_loop:
        ld1w    { z0.s }, p0/z, [x19]      // load a full vector (x4 32–bit integers) from memory
        cmpeq   p2, z0.s, z1.s            // compare each element with 10; result predicate in p2
        sel     z2.s, p2, z3.s, z2.s      // select 1 (from z3.s) where p2 is true, else 0.
        uaddv   w7, p0, z2.s             // horizontally add all lanes of z2.s → w7 holds count for this vector
        add     w1, w1, w7               // accumulate result into w1
        add     x19, x19, x24            // advance pointer by one vector’s worth (x24 bytes)
        subs    x6, x6, #1               // decrement loop counter
        bne     vector_loop

vector_loop_done:
        // --- Remainder loop: process leftover elements one–by–one ---
        cmp     x7, #0
        beq     remainder_done
remainder_loop:
        ldr     w8, [x19], #4            // load one 32–bit integer from memory
        cmp     w8, #10                 // compare it to 10
        cset    w10, eq                 // set w10 = 1 if equal, else 0 
        add     w1, w1, w10             // add (0 or 1) to the accumulator in w1
        subs    x7, x7, #1
        bne     remainder_loop
remainder_done:

        // --- Print the resulting count (as an integer) ---
        adrp    x0, .Lstr               // get format string address in x0
        add     x0, x0, :lo12:.Lstr
        bl      printf

        // Epilogue: restore callee‐saved registers and return.
        ldp     x20, x19, [sp, #16]
        ldp     x29, x30, [sp], #32
        mov     w0, wzr
        ret

.Lstr:
        .asciz "%i\n"
        .size  .Lstr, . - .Lstr

(predicate) 
Store predicate register 
Store a predicate register to a memory address generated by a 64 bit scalar base plus an immediate offset in the range 
256 to 255 which is multiplied by the current predicate register size in bytes This instruction is un predicated 
The store is performed as contiguous byte accesses each containing 8 consecutive predicate bits in ascending element 
order with no endian conversion and no guarantee of single copy atom i city larger than a byte However if alignment is 
checked then a general purpose base register must be aligned to 2 bytes 
For programmer convenience an assembler must also accept a predicate as counter register name for the source 
predicateregister. 








Encoding 

STR < Pt > , [ < Xn |SP > {, # < imm > , MUL VL }] 

Decode for this encoding 

if Is Feature Implemented ( FEAT_SVE ) && ! IsFeatureImplemented ( FEAT_SME ) then 
EndOfDecode (Decode_UNDEF ); 
constant integer t = UInt (Pt ); 
constant integer n = UInt (Rn ); 
constant integer imm = SInt (imm9h :imm9l ); 


AssemblerSymbols 


<Pt> Is the name of the scalable predicate transfer register encoded in the Pt field 

<Xn|SP> Is the 64 bit name of the general purpose base register or stack pointer encoded in the Rn field 

<imm> Is the optional signed immediate vector offset in the range 256 to 255 defaulting to 0 encoded in the 
“imm9h:imm9l”fields. 

Operation 

CheckSVEEnabled (); 
constant integer PL = CurrentVL DIV 8; 
constant integer elements = PL DIV 8; 
bits ( PL ) src ; 
bits (64) base ; 
constant integer offset = imm * elements ; 
constant boolean contiguous = TRUE ; 
constant boolean nontemporal = FALSE ; 
constant boolean tagchecked = n != 31; 
constant AccessDescriptor accdesc = CreateAccDescSVE (MemOp_STORE , nontemporal , contiguous , 
tagchecked ); 


if n == 31 then 
CheckSPAlignment (); 
base = SP [64]; 
else 
base = X[ n, 64]; 


src = P [t , PL ]; 


bits (64) addr = AddressAdd ( base , offset , accdesc ); 


constant boolean aligned = IsAligned ( addr , 2); 

if ! aligned && AlignmentEnforced () then 
constant FaultRecord fault = AlignmentFault ( accdesc , addr ); 
AArch64.Abort ( fault ); 


for e = 0 to elements -1 
AArch64.MemSingle [ addr , 1, accdesc , aligned ] = Elem [ src , e, 8]; 
addr = AddressIncrement (addr , 1, accdesc );

        sub     sp, sp, #32          // allocate 32 bytes on stack

        /* Create p0 having only one active element (lane0) */
        mov     x2, #0
        mov     x3, #1
        whilelo p0, x2, x3         // p0: only lane0 active

           of the predicate register size (normally 16 bytes). We store p0 at sp+16 and load it into p7. */
        str     p0, [sp, #16]
        ldr     p7, [sp, #16]

        /*

           We duplicate a 32‐bit value into an entire Z–register.

        /* Build w9 = (49807 << 16) | 23593 = 0xC28F5C29 */
        movz    x4, #23593, LSL #0
        movk    x4, #49807, LSL #16
        dup     z9.s, w4

        /* Build w10 = (655 << 16) | 23592 */
        movz    x4, #23592, LSL #0
        movk    x4, #655, LSL #16
        dup     z10.s, w4

        /* Build w11 = (163 << 16) | 55051 */
        movz    x4, #55051, LSL #0
        movk    x4, #163, LSL #16
        dup     z11.s, w4

        /* Build w14 = (9362 << 16) | 18725 */
        movz    x4, #18725, LSL #0
        movk    x4, #9362, LSL #16
        dup     z14.s, w4

        /* Other constants */
        dup     z12.s, #28         // w12 = 28 (immediate 28 is in range)
        dup     z15.s, #1          // w15 = 1
        movz    w4, #2640
        dup     z16.s, w4         // w16 = 2640

        /* Initialize “accumulator” registers.
           z1.s will hold our “result” and 
           z13.s is used as a temporary accumulator.
         */
        dup     z1.s, #0
        dup     z13.s, #0

        /* Initialize the outer–loop counter (w8) to 1901.
           1901 is too large for a dup-immediate so we load it into w4 first.
         */
        movz    w4, #1901
        dup     z8.s, w4

LoopOuter:
        /* Compare outer–loop counter z8.s versus 2001.
           We first load 2001 into z0.s using a temporary register.
         */
        movz    w4, #2001
        dup     z0.s, w4
        cmpeq   p2, p0, z8.s, z0.s        // p2 = (z8==2001)
        cntp    x5, p2, p2                // if any lane is “true” then x5 ≠ 0
        cmp     x5, #0
        b.ne    EndLoop

        mul     z17.s, p0/m, z8.s, z9.s

        /* Compute (w8 AND 3) into z0 (simulate “and w0, w8, #3”) */
        and     z0.s, p0/m, z8.s, #3

        ror     z18.s, p0/m, z17.s, #2
        ror     z17.s, p0/m, z17.s, #4

        /* Compare z18.s with constant in z10.s */
        cmpeq   p3, p0, z18.s, z10.s

        /* Immediately set z18.s = 1 (overwriting previous contents) */
        dup     z18.s, #1

        /* Compare (w8 & 3) == 0 */
        cmpeq   p4, p0, z0.s, #0

        /* Compare the rotated value z17.s with constant in z11.s */
        cmpeq   p5, p0, z17.s, z11.s

        /* Combine conditions: p6 = p3 AND p4 AND p5 */
        and     p6, p3, p4
        and     p6, p6, p5

        cntp    x6, p6, p6

        dup     z3.s, #13           // constant 13 for comparison

        add     z1.s, p0/m, z1.s, #1

        adrp    x0, .L_str
        add     x0, x0, :lo12:.L_str
        bl      printf

        /* Return 0 */
        mov     w0, wzr
        ret

samples.tested_code:
.arch	armv8.2-a+sve   // enable the SVE instructions and registers
	.text
	.global	main
	.p2align	2
main:
	/*--- Prologue: allocate 32 bytes and set up a lane‐0 predicate ---*/
	sub     sp, sp, #32          // allocate 32 bytes on stack

	/* Create p0 having only one active element (lane0). Note the “.s” suffix */
	mov     x2, #0
	mov     x3, #1
	whilelo p0.s, x2, x3         // now p0 (only lane0 active)

	/* Use the SVE store and load for predicate registers.
	   The immediate is scaled by the predicate register size, so use “#1” (i.e. 1×16=16 bytes).
	*/
	str     p0, [sp, #1]
	ldr     p7, [sp, #1]

	/* Now set up our constants and “scalar” variables in SVE registers.
	   We duplicate a 32‐bit value into an entire Z–register.
	   (Only lane0 is used in what follows.)
	*/

	/* Build w9 = (49807 << 16) | 23593 = 0xC28F5C29 */
	movz    x4, #23593, LSL #0
	movk    x4, #49807, LSL #16
	dup     z9.s, w4

	/* Build w10 = (655 << 16) | 23592 */
	movz    x4, #23592, LSL #0
	movk    x4, #655, LSL #16
	dup     z10.s, w4

	/* Build w11 = (163 << 16) | 55051 */
	movz    x4, #55051, LSL #0
	movk    x4, #163, LSL #16
	dup     z11.s, w4

	/* Build w14 = (9362 << 16) | 18725 */
	movz    x4, #18725, LSL #0
	movk    x4, #9362, LSL #16
	dup     z14.s, w4

	/* Other constants */
	dup     z12.s, #28         // constant 28 in every 32–bit lane
	dup     z15.s, #1          // constant 1
	movz    w4, #2640
	dup     z16.s, w4         // w16 = 2640

	/* Initialize “accumulator” registers.
	   z1.s will hold our “result” and 
	   z13.s is used as a temporary accumulator.
	*/
	dup     z1.s, #0
	dup     z13.s, #0

	/* Initialize the outer–loop counter (w8) to 1901.
	   1901 is too large for a dup-immediate so we load it into w4 first.
	*/
	movz    w4, #1901
	dup     z8.s, w4

LoopOuter:
	/* Compare outer–loop counter z8.s versus 2001.
	   We first load 2001 into z0.s using a temporary register.
	*/
	movz    w4, #2001
	dup     z0.s, w4
	cmpeq   p2, p0, z8.s, z0.s        // p2 = (z8 == 2001)
	/* Note: CNTP takes only two operands */
	cntp    x5, p2                   // x5 = number of true lanes in p2
	cmp     x5, #0
	b.ne    EndLoop

	/* Multiply: z17.s = z8.s * z9.s (only lane0 is active via p0/m) */
	mul     z17.s, p0/m, z8.s, z9.s

	/* Compute (z8.s AND 3) into z0 */
	and     z0.s, p0/m, z8.s, #3

	/* Two rotate–right operations:
	   z18.s = ror(z17.s, 2)  and  z17.s = ror(z17.s, 4)
	*/
	ror     z18.s, p0/m, z17.s, #2
	ror     z17.s, p0/m, z17.s, #4

	/* Compare z18.s with constant in z10.s */
	cmpeq   p3, p0, z18.s, z10.s

	/* Immediately set z18.s = 1 (overwriting previous contents) */
	dup     z18.s, #1

	/* Compare (z8.s & 3) == 0 */
	cmpeq   p4, p0, z0.s, #0

	/* Compare the rotated value z17.s with constant in z11.s */
	cmpeq   p5, p0, z17.s, z11.s

	/* Combine conditions: p6 = p3 AND p4 AND p5 */
	and     p6, p3, p4
	and     p6, p6, p5

	/* If p6 is all–false then skip the inner loop.
	   (CNTP now takes only two operands.)
	*/
	cntp    x6, p6
	cmp     x6, #0
	beq     SkipInner

	/* -------- Inner loop --------
	   We simulate an inner loop that adds 30 repeatedly while a counter (in z18.s)
	   is less than 13.
	*/
	dup     z3.s, #13           // constant 13 for comparison
InnerLoop:
	dup     z0.s, #30           // set z0.s = 30
	add     z13.s, p0/m, z13.s, z0.s   // z13.s += 30
	add     z18.s, p0/m, z18.s, #1      // increment inner counter
	/* Test inner loop condition: store z18.s to memory then load it into w7 */
	st1w    { z18.s }, p0, [sp]
	ldr     w7, [sp]
	cmp     w7, #13
	blt     InnerLoop

	/* When the inner loop finishes, increment the “result” */
	add     z1.s, p0/m, z1.s, #1

SkipInner:
	/* End of this outer–loop iteration: increment outer counter */
	add     z8.s, p0/m, z8.s, #1
	b       LoopOuter

EndLoop:
	/* At loop end, write the “result” (from z1.s lane0) to memory so that printf can print it */
	st1w    { z1.s }, p0, [sp, #0]
	ldr     w1, [sp, #0]

	add     sp, sp, #32         // restore stack

	/* Prepare and call printf with format string "%d\n" and the computed result */
	adrp    x0, .L_str
	add     x0, x0, :lo12:.L_str
	bl      printf

	/* Return 0 */
	mov     w0, wzr
	ret

	.section .rodata
.L_str:
	.asciz "%d\n"

.arch armv8.2-a+sve
        .text
        .global main
        .p2align 2
main:
        /* --- Prologue: allocate some space on the stack and create a one–lane predicate --- */
        sub     sp, sp, #32

        /* Create a predicate with only lane0 active */
        mov     x2, #0
        mov     x3, #1
        whilelo p0.s, x2, x3            // now p0 has only lane0 active

        /* Use the SVE predicate–store/load instructions.
           NOTE: The immediate is scaled by the predicate register size.
           For example, if VL=128 then each p–register is 16 bytes so an immediate of 1 yields sp+16.
        */
        str     p0, [sp, #1]             // store p0 at sp + (1×(predicate size))
        ldr     p7, [sp, #1]             // load it back into p7

        /* --- Set up constants and “scalar” values duplicated into Z registers --- */

        /* Build w9 = (49807 << 16) | 23593 */
        movz    x4, #23593, LSL #0
        movk    x4, #49807, LSL #16
        dup     z9.s, w4

        /* Build w10 = (655 << 16) | 23592 */
        movz    x4, #23592, LSL #0
        movk    x4, #655, LSL #16
        dup     z10.s, w4

        /* Build w11 = (163 << 16) | 55051 */
        movz    x4, #55051, LSL #0
        movk    x4, #163, LSL #16
        dup     z11.s, w4

        /* Build w14 = (9362 << 16) | 18725 */
        movz    x4, #18725, LSL #0
        movk    x4, #9362, LSL #16
        dup     z14.s, w4

        /* Other constants */
        dup     z12.s, #28
        dup     z15.s, #1         // constant “1” (for additions)
        movz    w4, #2640
        dup     z16.s, w4

        /* For operations that do not accept an immediate, preload a constant */
        dup     z20.s, #3         // to be used instead of “#3” in a bitwise AND
        dup     z21.s, #0         // to be used instead of immediate “0” in a comparison

        /* --- Initialize “accumulator” registers --- */
        dup     z1.s, #0
        dup     z13.s, #0

        /* --- Outer–loop counter: initialize to 1901 --- */
        movz    w4, #1901
        dup     z8.s, w4

LoopOuter:
        /* Compare outer–loop counter:  z8.s == 2001 */
        movz    w4, #2001
        dup     z0.s, w4
        cmpeq   p2, p0, z8.s, z0.s    // p2 = (z8 == 2001) computed on lanes active in p0
        /* CNTP (counts active bits) – using p0 as the executing predicate */
        cntp    x5, p2, p0           // x5 = number of true lanes in p2
        cmp     x5, #0
        b.ne    EndLoop

        /* Perform some arithmetic operations.
           NOTE: The executing predicate is passed here as “p0” (merging is the default).
        */
        mul     z17.s, p0, z8.s, z9.s         // z17.s = z8.s * z9.s
        and     z0.s, p0, z8.s, z20.s          // z0.s = (z8.s AND 3)

        ror     z18.s, p0, z17.s, #2           // z18.s = ror(z17.s, 2)
        ror     z17.s, p0, z17.s, #4           // z17.s = ror(z17.s, 4)

        cmpeq   p3, p0, z18.s, z10.s           // p3 = (z18.s == z10.s)
        dup     z18.s, #1                     // immediately set z18.s = 1

        cmpeq   p4, p0, z0.s, z21.s            // p4 = (z0.s == 0)
        cmpeq   p5, p0, z17.s, z11.s           // p5 = (z17.s == z11.s)

        and     p6, p3, p4
        and     p6, p6, p5

        cntp    x6, p6, p0                   // x6 = count of true lanes in p6
        cmp     x6, #0
        beq     SkipInner

        /* -------- Inner loop --------
           (Simulate an inner loop that adds 30 repeatedly while a counter is less than 13.)
        */
        dup     z3.s, #13
InnerLoop:
        dup     z0.s, #30
        add     z13.s, p0, z13.s, z0.s         // z13.s += 30 
        add     z18.s, p0, z18.s, z15.s         // inner counter: z18.s += 1
        st1w    { z18.s }, p0, [sp]
        ldr     w7, [sp]
        cmp     w7, #13
        blt     InnerLoop

        add     z1.s, p0, z1.s, z15.s           // increment “result”
SkipInner:
        add     z8.s, p0, z8.s, z15.s           // increment outer–loop counter
        b       LoopOuter

EndLoop:
        /* At loop end, write the “result” (from lane0 of z1.s) to memory */
        st1w    { z1.s }, p0, [sp]
        ldr     w1, [sp]

        add     sp, sp, #32          // restore stack

        /* Call printf with format string "%d\n" and our computed value */
        adrp    x0, .L_str
        add     x0, x0, :lo12:.L_str
        bl      printf

        mov     w0, wzr
        ret

        /* --- Read–only data --- */
        .section .rodata
.L_str:
        .asciz "%d\n"

A dummy ext (and later an and) is also executed. 4. Main calls the three functions, puts a temporary array on the stack and then calls printf (with a format string in the .rodata section). 	// (Dummy: clear z2)

	cmp     w2, #1

	// Multiply accumulator by loop counter (all lanes hold the same value)

	// Decrement loop counter by 1 (vector–wise subtraction)

	// Dummy: perform an “and (immediate)” that leaves the value unchanged.

	// Dummy: use ext to extract a shifted byte–string from z0 (no effect on lane values)

	b       fact_loop

fact_done:
	// Move the final 32–bit product (from lane 0 of z0) to w0.

	mov     w0, #1

	.type next, @function

.global fact
        .type   fact, @function
fact:
        // if (w0==0) then return 1
        cbz     w0, fact_ret_one

        // Broadcast constant 1 into every 32‐bit element of accumulator (z0)
        dup     z0.s, #1
        // Broadcast the original n (in w0) into every lane (z1)
        dup     z1.s, w0
        // (Dummy: clear z2)
        dup     z2.s, #0

fact_loop:
        // Get the 0th lane from z1 into w2
        umov    w2, z1.s[0]
        cmp     w2, #1
        ble     fact_done

        // Get the 0th element of z0, multiply by the counter, and re–broadcast.
        umov    w4, z0.s[0]       // fetch current accumulator
        mul     w4, w4, w2       // compute acc *= counter
        dup     z0.s, w4         // broadcast new accumulator

        // Decrement the counter and broadcast it.
        sub     w2, w2, #1
        dup     z1.s, w2

        // Dummy: perform an AND immediate that leaves the value unchanged.
        // SVE’s AND immediate works on 64–bit lanes; use a full–word mask.
        and     z0.d, z0.d, #-1

        // Dummy: use ext (which works on bytes) to “copy” z0.
        // (We cannot use the same register for both sources in the non–destructive form.
        // So use a temporary: first copy z0 to z11, then extract with immediate offset 0.)
        mov     z11, z0
        ext     z10.b, z0.b, z11.b, #0

        b       fact_loop

fact_done:
        // Move the final 32–bit result (from lane 0 of z0) to w0.
        umov    w0, z0.s[0]
        ret

fact_ret_one:
        mov     w0, #1
        ret

        .global next
        .type   next, @function
next:
        // if (w0==0) then return
        cbz     w0, next_ret

        // Broadcast the input into z0 and the constant 10 into z1.
        dup     z0.s, w0
        dup     z1.s, #10

next_loop:
        umov    w2, z0.s[0]
        // Loop until the value reaches or exceeds 20.
        cmp     w2, #20
        bge     next_done

        // Add 10 to every element in z0.
        add     z0.s, z0.s, z1.s

        // Dummy: use ext to “rotate–extract” bytes.
        // (Again, if the two sources are identical the destination must match them.
        // So copy z0 to a temporary then use EXT.)
        mov     z12, z0
        ext     z11.b, z0.b, z12.b, #0
        mov     z12, z11
        ext     z2.b, z11.b, z12.b, #8

        b       next_loop

next_done:
        // Dummy inner loop: multiply z0 by 2 (scalarly).
        dup     z3.s, #2
        umov    w5, z0.s[0]
        umov    w6, z3.s[0]
        mul     w5, w5, w6
        dup     z0.s, w5

        // Dummy: use fmov immediate to place 1.0 into z4.
        fmov    z4.s, #1.0

        umov    w0, z0.s[0]
        ret

next_ret:
        ret

        .global length
        .type   length, @function
// This SVE “length” assumes:
//    x0 = pointer to an array of 32–bit integers
//    w1 = number of elements.
length:
        stp     x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!
        mov     x29, sp

        // Initialize accumulator in z0 to 0.
        dup     z0.s, #0
        mov     x2, #0           // running index
        cntw    x3               // number of 32–bit lanes

length_loop:
        cmp     x2, x1
        bge     length_done

        // Build predicate p0 for lanes: whilelo p0.s, x2, x1
        whilelo p0.s, x2, x1

        // Load up to one vector–length of integers from memory.
        ld1w    {z1.s}, p0/z, [x0, x2, lsl #2]

        // Dummy: copy z1 via ext using a zero offset.
        mov     z13, z1
        ext     z12.b, z1.b, z13.b, #0
        mov     z13, z12
        ext     z12.b, z12.b, z13.b, #4

        // Add the loaded vector to the accumulator.
        add     z0.s, z0.s, z1.s

        // Dummy: broadcast constant 7 into z3.
        dup     z3.s, #7

        // Advance the index.
        add     x2, x2, x3
        b       length_loop

length_done:
        // Horizontally add the lanes in z0; result goes to a 32–bit register.
        ptrue   p1.s
        addv    w0, p1, z0.s

        // Dummy: perform an AND immediate that leaves the sum unchanged.
        and     z0.d, z0.d, #-1

        ldp     x29, x30, [sp], #16
        ret

        .global main
        .type   main, @function
main:
        stp     x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!
        mov     x29, sp

        // --- Call fact(5) ---
        mov     w0, #5
        bl      fact
        mov     w19, w0       // save fact’s result in w19

        // --- Call next(7) ---
        mov     w0, #7
        bl      next
        mov     w20, w0       // save next’s result in w20

        // --- Build an array of 4 integers on the stack ---
        sub     sp, sp, #16
        mov     w0, #1
        str     w0, [sp, #0]
        mov     w0, #2
        str     w0, [sp, #4]
        mov     w0, #3
        str     w0, [sp, #8]
        mov     w0, #4
        str     w0, [sp, #12]

        // --- Call length(array, 4) ---
        mov     x0, sp
        mov     w1, #4
        bl      length
        mov     w21, w0      // save length’s result in w21

        add     sp, sp, #16

        // Compute final result = fact + next + length.
        add     w0, w19, w20
        add     w0, w0, w21

        // --- Call printf to print the result ---
        mov     w2, w0
        adrp    x0, .Lstr
        add     x0, x0, :lo12:.Lstr
        mov     w1, w2
        bl      printf

        mov     w0, #0
        ldp     x29, x30, [sp], #16
        ret

        .section .rodata
        .align   2
.Lstr:
        .asciz  "%d\n"

chunks.z0-z31 32 sve scalable vector registers:
Z0 to Z31 of equal length Each register can be accessed as 

• A configurable length vector of elements The length VL is a power of two from a minimum 
of 128 bits to an IMPLEMENTATION DEFINED maximum no greater than 2048 bits See Figure 
B1-3, Figure A 1 5 and Configurable SVE vector lengths 
• A SIMD FP register as described in V0-V31 Bits 127 0 of each Zn register hold the 
correspondingly numbered V 0 V 31 SIMD&FPregister,as FigureB1-3 shows: 

Figure B 1 3 SVE scalable vector register naming 


Seealso: 

• Maximum implemented SVE vector lengths 
• Configurable SVE vector lengths 
• Treatment of SVE scalable vector registers . 
• SVE writes of scalar values to registers . 

P0-P15 16 SVE predicate registers named P 0 toP 15 Each SVE predicate register holds one bit for each byte 
of an SVE scalar vector register 
Note 
The Maximum implemented SVE predicate length is the Maximum implemented SVE vector length 
divided by 8 See Maximum implemented SVE vector lengths 


Alsosee Vectorpredication. 

FFR The dedicated SVE First Fault Register that has the same size and format as the SVE predicate 
registers,P0-P15.See FFR First Fault Register .

samples.generated: Below is one correct solution. In the loop the “mul (immediate)” instruction requires that the destination register be the same as its first source. In SVE you cannot simply use a plain mov to copy a scalable vector register. 	add	x9, x9, :lo12:cache
	ldrsw	x10, [x8, :lo12:cache_size]
	add	w11, w10, #1
	// Use SVE to “store one element”: create a predicate with only lane0 active,
	// duplicate the argument into a vector register and then store.
	mov	x12, #1

	whilelo p0.s, xzr, x12            // p0.s = true for lane 0 only 
	dup	z0.s, w0                  // duplicate w0 into every lane of z0.s
	st1w	{z0.s}, p0, [x9]           // store only lane0 “s”
	str	w11, [x8, :lo12:cache_size]

	adrp	x9, cache
	add	x9, x9, :lo12:cache
	// x11 holds the number of elements remaining;

	uxtw	x11, w8

	// (Notice that the destination predicate is written without “.s”)
	cmpeq	p0, z1.s, z0.s         // p0 = (z1.s == z0.s)
	// Count how many lanes had a match.
	cntp	w10, p0
	cbnz	w10, in_cache_found      // if any match then we are done
	// Count the number of lanes processed (the whilelo predicate, in p2).
	cntw	w12, p2

	add	x9, x9, w12, sxtw #2
	// Decrement the counter (again using sxtw to extend w12).
	sub	x11, x11, w12, sxtw #0
	cmp	x11, #0

.arch	armv8.2-a+sve
	.text
	.globl	add_cache                     // -- Begin function add_cache
	.p2align	2
add_cache:
	.cfi_startproc
	adrp	x8, cache_size
	adrp	x9, cache
	add	x9, x9, :lo12:cache
	ldrsw	x10, [x8, :lo12:cache_size]
	add	w11, w10, #1
	// Use SVE to “store one element”: create a predicate with only lane0 active,
	// duplicate the argument into a vector register and then store.
	mov	x12, #1
	whilelo p0.s, xzr, x12            // p0.s = true for lane 0 only 
	dup	z0.s, w0                     // duplicate w0 into every lane of z0.s
	st1w	{z0.s}, p0, [x9]            // store only lane0 “s”
	str	w11, [x8, :lo12:cache_size]
	ret
	.cfi_endproc
                                // -- End function add_cache

	.globl	in_cache                      // -- Begin function in_cache
	.p2align	2
in_cache:
	.cfi_startproc
	adrp	x8, cache_size
	ldr	w8, [x8, :lo12:cache_size]
	cmp	w8, #1
	blt	in_cache_return0
	adrp	x9, cache
	add	x9, x9, :lo12:cache
	// x11 holds the number of elements remaining;
	// note: we must move the 32–bit count (from w8) into a 64–bit register.
	uxtw	x11, w8

	dup	z0.s, w0                   // set z0.s = search value replicated
in_cache_loop:
	// Get a predicate of the “active” lanes into p2 so that we can later count them.
	whilelo p2.s, xzr, x11         // predicate p2.s for lanes [0 … min(VL, x11)-1]
	ld1w	{z1.s}, p2/z, [x9]        // load a vector of 32‐bit values from cache
	// Compare z1.s with the search value into p0.
	cmpeq	p0.s, z1.s, z0.s         // p0.s = (z1.s == z0.s)
	// Count how many lanes had a match.
	cntp	w10, p0.s
	cbnz	w10, in_cache_found      // if any match then we are done
	// Count the number of lanes processed (the whilelo predicate, in p2).
	cntw	w12, p2.s
	// Advance pointer by (num_lanes×4) bytes. (w12 is sign‐extended using “sxtw”.)
	add	x9, x9, w12, sxtw #2
	// Decrement the counter (again using sxtw to extend w12).
	sub	x11, x11, w12, sxtw #0
	cmp	x11, #0
	bgt	in_cache_loop
in_cache_return0:
	mov	w0, wzr                 // not found: return 0
	ret
in_cache_found:
	mov	w0, #1                  // found: return 1
	ret
	.cfi_endproc
                                // -- End function in_cache

	.globl	is_palindromic               // -- Begin function is_palindromic
	.p2align	2
is_palindromic:
	.cfi_startproc
	adrp	x8, buffer
	add	x8, x8, :lo12:buffer
	cmp	w0, #0
	bne	ip_fill               // if seed nonzero, fill the buffer as a palindrome.
	// If seed == 0, assume an “empty” buffer (0 elements)
	mov	w12, #0
	b	ip_check
ip_fill:
	// For demonstration we fill the buffer with a palindromic sequence:
	// The buffer is 40 bytes (10 ints). We fill the first half with 0,1,2,3,4
	// and then mirror it (so the final contents become: 0 1 2 3 4 4 3 2 1 0).
	mov	x10, #5               // half‐length = 5
	whilelo p0.s, xzr, x10       // predicate p0.s true for indices 0…4
	// Use index with immediate 0 so that lane i gets the value i.
	index	z0.s, xzr, #0         // z0.s = {0,1,2,3,4,…}
	st1w	{z0.s}, p0, [x8]       // store first half into buffer[0..4]
	// Now mirror the first half into the second half.
	add	x9, x8, #20           // pointer to second half (5×4 = 20 bytes offset)
	mov	w11, #4               // highest index of first half = 4
	dup	z1.s, w11             // set every lane equal to 4
	index	z2.s, xzr, #0         // z2.s = {0,1,2,3,4,…}
	sub	z2.s, z1.s, z2.s       // now z2.s = {4,3,2,1,0}
	ld1w	{z3.s}, p0/z, [x8]      // load first half into z3.s
	st1w	{z3.s}, p0, [x9, z2.s, UXTW #2]  // scatter–store mirror into second half
	mov	w12, #10              // total count = 10
ip_check:
	// Now check whether the buffer is palindromic.
	// For count = w12, compare items [0 … (n/2 – 1)] with [n–1 … n/2] in reverse order.
	lsr	w13, w12, #1         // half = n/2 (if n==10, half==5)
	cmp	w13, #0
	beq	ip_is_pal
	// Get first half elements into z4.
	uxtw	x14, w13             // convert half count to 64–bit
	whilelo p2.s, xzr, x14       // predicate for indices 0 … (half–1)
	ld1w	{z4.s}, p2/z, [x8]      // load buffer[0 … half–1]
	// Compute reverse indices to load mirror elements.
	sub	w15, w12, #1         // w15 = n – 1
	dup	z5.s, w15            // set every lane = n – 1
	index	z6.s, xzr, #0         // z6.s = {0,1,2,3,4,…}
	sub	z6.s, z5.s, z6.s       // now z6.s = {n–1, n–2, …}
	ld1w	{z7.s}, p2/z, [x8, z6.s, UXTW #2]   // load mirror elements
	// Compare and count.
	cmpeq	p0.s, z4.s, z7.s         // p0.s = (z4.s == z7.s)
	cntp	w16, p0.s              // count the “true” lanes
	cntw	w17, p2.s              // count lanes processed (from p2)
	cmp	w16, w17
	b.eq	ip_is_pal
	mov	w0, wzr              // not palindromic; return 0
	ret
ip_is_pal:
	mov	w0, #1               // is palindromic → return 1
	ret
	.cfi_endproc
                                // -- End function is_palindromic

Z0 to Z31 of equal length Each register can be accessed as

of 128 bits to an IMPLEMENTATION DEFINED maximum no greater than 2048 bits See Figure 
B1-3, Figure A 1 5 and Configurable SVE vector lengths 
• A SIMD FP register as described in V0-V31 Bits 127 0 of each Zn register hold the 
correspondingly numbered V 0 V 31 SIMD&FPregister,as FigureB1-3 shows: 

Figure B 1 3 SVE scalable vector register naming 


Seealso: 

• Maximum implemented SVE vector lengths 
• Configurable SVE vector lengths 
• Treatment of SVE scalable vector registers . 
• SVE writes of scalar values to registers . 

P0-P15 16 SVE predicate registers named P 0 toP 15 Each SVE predicate register holds one bit for each byte 
of an SVE scalar vector register 
Note 
The Maximum implemented SVE predicate length is the Maximum implemented SVE vector length 
divided by 8 See Maximum implemented SVE vector lengths

.arch    armv8.2-a+sve
        .text
        .global  main
        .extern  snprintf
        .extern  printf

/* 
   This version computes the sum of all numbers in [3,100000) for which the
   sum of the factorials of its decimal digits equals the number.
   It uses SVE instructions dup, and (immediate), ext and fmov to “vectorize”
   the inner conversion of the printed number (via snprintf) into its digit values.
*/

main:
        // Standard prologue.
        stp     x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!
        mov     x29, sp
        sub     sp, sp, #80         // allocate 80 bytes for local buffer and spills

        // Initialize loop limits and accumulation.
        mov     w23, #34464         // load 34464 (0x86a0)
        movk    w23, #1, lsl #16     // now w23 = 0x186A0 = 100000
        mov     w19, wzr            // global sum accumulator = 0
        mov     w20, #3             // starting number = 3

loop_start:
        // Use snprintf to convert number w20 to a string in our buffer (at sp)
        mov     x0, sp              // destination buffer pointer
        mov     w1, #16             // buffer size
        adrp    x2, L_str
        add     x2, x2, :lo12:L_str  // pointer to format string "%u"
        mov     w3, w20           // number in w20
        bl      snprintf

        // --- Begin SVE “vectorized” processing of the printed string ---
        ptrue   p0.b              // make p0 full of active bytes
        ld1b    {z0.b}, p0/z, [sp]  // load 16 bytes from sp into vector register Z0
        dup     z1.b, #48         // broadcast immediate 48 (ASCII '0') into each byte of Z1
        sub     z0.b, z0.b, z1.b   // now each element of Z0 holds (digit-character - 48)
        and     z0.d, z0.d, #0xff  // mask each 64‑bit element with 0xff (using an immediate)
        ext     z2.b, z0.b, z0.b, #1   // extract a vector shifted by one byte (dummy use)
        fmov    z3.s, p0/m, #0     // demonstrate fmov immediate predicated (sets all active lanes of Z3 to 0)
        // --- End SVE block; from here we use a scalar loop to process the printed string ---

        // Set pointer into the printed buffer.
        mov     x22, sp           
        mov     w8, wzr           // accumulator for digit–factorial sum = 0

digit_loop:
        ldrb    w11, [x22], #1    // load next byte from the string; post-increment pointer
        cbz     w11, digit_loop_end  // if zero‐byte (string terminator) then break out of loop
        sub     w4, w11, #48      // convert ASCII digit to number
        // Call fact to compute factorial of the digit (fact(0)==1)
        mov     w0, w4
        bl      fact
        add     w8, w8, w0        // accumulate the computed factorial in w8
        b       digit_loop

digit_loop_end:
        // If the sum of digit–factorials equals the original number then add that number to w19.
        cmp     w20, w8
        csel    w8, w20, wzr, eq  // select w20 if equal, else 0
        add     w19, w19, w8

        // Increment our number and loop while less than limit.
        add     w20, w20, #1
        cmp     w20, w23
        b.lt    loop_start

        // Print the final result using printf.
        adrp    x0, L_str1
        add     x0, x0, :lo12:L_str1
        mov     w1, w19
        bl      printf

        // Epilogue: restore sp and return.
        add     sp, sp, #80
        ldp     x29, x30, [sp], #16
        ret

/*-------------------------------
    Factorial function: fact
    Computes fact(n) = n! for n > 0, and returns 1 for n == 0.
-------------------------------*/
fact:
        cbz     w0, fact_ret      // if w0 == 0 then return 1
        mov     w8, w0
        mov     w0, #1
fact_loop:
        subs    w9, w8, #1
        mul     w0, w0, w8
        mov     w8, w9
        b.ne    fact_loop
fact_ret:
        ret

        .data
L_str:
        .asciz "%u"
L_str1:
        .asciz "%u\n"

.text
        .global  main
        .extern  snprintf
        .extern  printf

/* 
   This version computes the sum of all numbers in [3,100000) for which the
   sum of the factorials of its decimal digits equals the number.
   It uses SVE instructions (dup, and, ext and fmov) to “vectorize”
   the inner conversion of the printed number (via snprintf) into its digit values.
*/

main:
        // Standard prologue.
        stp     x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!
        mov     x29, sp
        sub     sp, sp, #80         // allocate 80 bytes for local buffer and spills

        // Initialize loop limits and accumulation.
        mov     w23, #34464         // load 34464 (0x86a0)
        movk    w23, #1, lsl #16     // now w23 = 0x186A0 = 100000
        mov     w19, wzr            // global sum accumulator = 0
        mov     w20, #3             // starting number = 3

loop_start:
        // Use snprintf to convert number w20 to a string in our buffer (at sp)
        mov     x0, sp              // destination buffer pointer
        mov     w1, #16             // buffer size
        adrp    x2, L_str
        add     x2, x2, :lo12:L_str  // pointer to format string "%u"
        mov     w3, w20             // number in w20
        bl      snprintf

        // --- Begin SVE “vectorized” processing of the printed string ---
        ptrue   p0.b                // make p0 full of active bytes
        ld1b    {z0.b}, p0/z, [sp]   // load 16 bytes from sp into vector register Z0
        dup     z1.b, #48           // broadcast immediate 48 (ASCII '0') into each byte of Z1
        sub     z0.b, z0.b, z1.b     // now each element of Z0 holds (digit-character - 48)
        and     z0.d, z0.d, #0xff    // mask each 64‑bit element with 0xff (using an immediate)

        // Instead of the invalid:
        //    ext  z2.b, z0.b, z0.b, #1
        // we copy z0 into z2 and then do a destructive ext on z2 (destination equals first source):
        mov     z2, z0              // Copy entire Z0 into Z2.
        ext     z2.b, z2.b, z0.b, #1 // Destructive extraction into Z2

        fmov    z3.s, p0/m, #0      // demonstrate fmov immediate predicated (set all active lanes of Z3 to 0)
        // --- End SVE block; from here we use a scalar loop to process the printed string ---

        // Set pointer into the printed buffer.
        mov     x22, sp           
        mov     w8, wzr            // accumulator for digit–factorial sum = 0

digit_loop:
        ldrb    w11, [x22], #1     // load next byte from the string; post-increment pointer
        cbz     w11, digit_loop_end  // if zero‐byte (string terminator) then break out of loop
        sub     w4, w11, #48       // convert ASCII digit to number
        // Call fact to compute factorial of the digit (fact(0)==1)
        mov     w0, w4
        bl      fact
        add     w8, w8, w0         // accumulate the computed factorial in w8
        b       digit_loop

digit_loop_end:
        // If the sum of digit–factorials equals the original number then add that number to w19.
        cmp     w20, w8
        csel    w8, w20, wzr, eq   // select w20 if equal, else 0
        add     w19, w19, w8

        // Increment our number and loop while less than limit.
        add     w20, w20, #1
        cmp     w20, w23
        b.lt   loop_start

        // Print the final result using printf.
        adrp    x0, L_str1
        add     x0, x0, :lo12:L_str1
        mov     w1, w19
        bl      printf

        // Epilogue: restore sp and return.
        add     sp, sp, #80
        ldp     x29, x30, [sp], #16
        ret

/*-------------------------------
    Factorial function: fact
    Computes fact(n) = n! for n > 0, and returns 1 for n == 0.
-------------------------------*/
fact:
        cbz     w0, fact_ret      // if w0 == 0 then return 1
        mov     w8, w0
        mov     w0, #1
fact_loop:
        subs    w9, w8, #1
        mul     w0, w0, w8
        mov     w8, w9
        b.ne    fact_loop
fact_ret:
        ret

        .data
L_str:
        .asciz "%u"
L_str1:
        .asciz "%u\n"

.extern  snprintf
        .extern  printf

/*
   This version computes the sum of all numbers in [3,100000)
   for which the sum of the factorials of its decimal digits equals the number.
   It uses SVE instructions (dup, and, ext and fmov) to “vectorize”
   the conversion of the printed number (via snprintf) into its digit values.
*/

main:
        // Standard prologue.
        stp     x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!
        mov     x29, sp
        sub     sp, sp, #80         // allocate 80 bytes for local buffer and spills

        // Initialize loop limits and accumulation.
        mov     w23, #34464         // load 34464 (0x86a0)
        movk    w23, #1, lsl #16     // now w23 = 0x186A0 = 100000
        mov     w19, wzr            // global sum accumulator = 0
        mov     w20, #3             // starting number = 3

loop_start:
        // Use snprintf to convert number w20 to a string in our buffer (at sp)
        mov     x0, sp              // destination buffer pointer
        mov     w1, #16             // buffer size
        adrp    x2, L_str
        add     x2, x2, :lo12:L_str  // pointer to format string "%u"
        mov     w3, w20             // number in w20
        bl      snprintf

        // --- Begin SVE “vectorized” processing of the printed string ---
        ptrue   p0.b                // set p0 to “all‐active” for bytes
        ld1b    {z0.b}, p0/z, [sp]   // load up to VL bytes from sp into z0 
        dup     z1.b, #48           // broadcast immediate 48 (ASCII '0') into every byte in z1
        sub     z0.b, z0.b, z1.b     // each element of z0 now holds (digit – '0')
        and     z0.d, z0.d, #0xff    // mask each 64‑bit element with 0xff

        // Instead of using "mov z2, z0" (which is not allowed for SVE registers)
        // we copy z0 into z2 via memory. Since the immediate in the following
        // instructions must be in the range [-8,7], we compute the address sp+32 in a register.
        add     x21, sp, #32        // compute temporary pointer into the local spill area
        st1b    {z0.b}, p0, [x21]    // store the content of z0 at sp+32
        ld1b    {z2.b}, p0/z, [x21]   // load that content into z2

        // Now do a destructive extraction on z2.
        ext     z2.b, z2.b, z0.b, #1  // extract a shifted vector from z2 & z0

        fmov    z3.s, p0/m, #0      // Demonstrate fmov immediate predicated (set active lanes of z3 to 0)
        // --- End SVE block; now use a scalar loop to process the printed string ---

        // Set pointer into the printed buffer.
        mov     x22, sp           
        mov     w8, wzr            // accumulator for digit–factorial sum = 0

digit_loop:
        ldrb    w11, [x22], #1     // load next byte; post–increment pointer
        cbz     w11, digit_loop_end  // if zero–byte then end loop
        sub     w4, w11, #48       // convert ASCII digit to number
        // Call fact to compute factorial of the digit (note: fact(0)==1)
        mov     w0, w4
        bl      fact
        add     w8, w8, w0         // accumulate the factorial in w8
        b       digit_loop

digit_loop_end:
        // If sum of digit–factorials equals the original number, add that number to w19.
        cmp     w20, w8
        csel    w8, w20, wzr, eq   // select w20 if equal, else 0
        add     w19, w19, w8

        // Increment our number and loop while less than limit.
        add     w20, w20, #1
        cmp     w20, w23
        b.lt   loop_start

        // Print the final result using printf.
        adrp    x0, L_str1
        add     x0, x0, :lo12:L_str1
        mov     w1, w19
        bl      printf

        // Epilogue: restore sp and return.
        add     sp, sp, #80
        ldp     x29, x30, [sp], #16
        ret

/*-------------------------------
    Factorial function: fact
    Computes fact(n) = n! for n > 0, with fact(0)==1.
-------------------------------*/
fact:
        cbz     w0, fact_ret      // if w0 == 0 then return 1
        mov     w8, w0
        mov     w0, #1
fact_loop:
        subs    w9, w8, #1
        mul     w0, w0, w8
        mov     w8, w9
        b.ne    fact_loop
fact_ret:
        ret

        .data

        .asciz "%u"
L_str1:
        .asciz "%u\n"

samples.generated: Below is one acceptable fix. The problem was that z0 was “used” with several different element sizes (first as .s then as .d) but then later used as .b in the ext instruction. In SVE the same register must be referenced with the same element‐size qualifier within a given instruction. One fix is to “homogenize” the SVE demo block so that z0 (and z1) are always addressed as bytes. For example, change   dup z0.s, #3   and z0.d, z0.d, #0xff to   dup z0.b, #3   and z0.b, z0.b, #0xff so that the ext instruction   ext z1.b, z0.b, z0.b, #8 now uses all .b operands. (Notice that although the predicate was produced as ptrue p0.s and the later fmov uses .s on z2, the demo block uses z0 and z1 only for bit‐manipulation so it is safe to use .b on them.) // aarch64+sve assembly generated from problem34.c

// via the following SVE primitives: dup, and (immediate), ext, and fmov immediate predicated.

    .text
    .file   "problem34.c"
    .globl  main                            // -- Begin function main
    .p2align 2
    .type   main,@function
main:                                   // @main
    .cfi_startproc

    // --- Begin SVE demo block ---
    // Set up predicate for 32‐bit elements.
    ptrue p0.s
    // Broadcast immediate 3 into every 8‐bit lane of Z0.
    dup   z0.b, #3
    // Bitwise AND each 8‐bit element of Z0 with 0xff.
    and   z0.b, z0.b, #0xff
    // Extract a vector of bytes from Z0 with an 8‐byte offset.
    ext   z1.b, z0.b, z0.b, #8
    // Move the 8‐bit floating–point immediate 1.0 into every active element of Z2 (single–precision)
    fmov  z2.s, p0/m, #1.0
    // --- End SVE demo block ---

    // Function prologue and stack frame setup.
    sub     sp, sp, #80
    .cfi_def_cfa_offset 80
    stp     x29, x30, [sp, #16]             // 16-byte Folded Spill
    str     x23, [sp, #32]                  // 8-byte Folded Spill
    stp     x22, x21, [sp, #48]             // 16-byte Folded Spill
    stp     x20, x19, [sp, #64]             // 16-byte Folded Spill
    add     x29, sp, #16
    .cfi_def_cfa w29, 64
    .cfi_offset w19, -8
    .cfi_offset w20, -16
    .cfi_offset w21, -24
    .cfi_offset w22, -32
    .cfi_offset w23, -48
    .cfi_offset w30, -56
    .cfi_offset w29, -64

    // Initialize loop parameters.
    mov     w23, #34464                     // Constant part (0x86a0)
    mov     w19, wzr
    mov     w20, #3                         // Loop counter starting at 3
    mov     x22, sp
    movk    w23, #1, lsl #16               // Now w23 := (1<<16)|34464 = 100000

    adrp    x21, .L.str
    add     x21, x21, :lo12:.L.str
    b       .LBB0_3

.LBB0_1:                                // Loop label
    mov     w8, wzr
.LBB0_2:
    cmp     w20, w8
    add     w20, w20, #1
    csel    w8, w8, wzr, eq
    cmp     w20, w23
    add     w19, w8, w19
    b.eq    .LBB0_8

.LBB0_3:                                // Loop header
    // Call snprintf(sp, 16, .L.str, w20)
    mov     x0, sp
    mov     w1, #16                         // = 0x10
    mov     x2, x21
    mov     w3, w20
    bl      snprintf
    ldrb    w11, [sp]
    cbz     w11, .LBB0_1

    // Loop for processing the string produced by snprintf.
    // (%bb.4:)
    mov     w8, wzr
    mov     w9, wzr
    b       .LBB0_6

.LBB0_5:                                // Inner loop in processing string bytes.
    add     w9, w9, #1
    add     w8, w10, w8
    ldrb    w11, [x22, w9, uxtw]
    cbz     w11, .LBB0_2

.LBB0_6:                                // Another loop header.
    mov     w10, #1                         // = 0x1
    subs    w11, w11, #48
    b.eq    .LBB0_5

.LBB0_7:                                // Inner loop for multiplication.
    subs    w12, w11, #1
    mul     w10, w11, w10
    mov     w11, w12
    b.ne    .LBB0_7
    b       .LBB0_5

.LBB0_8:
    adrp    x0, .L.str.1
    add     x0, x0, :lo12:.L.str.1
    mov     w1, w19
    bl      printf
    mov     w0, wzr
    .cfi_def_cfa wsp, 80
    ldp     x20, x19, [sp, #64]             // 16-byte Folded Reload
    ldp     x22, x21, [sp, #48]             // 16-byte Folded Reload
    ldp     x29, x30, [sp, #16]             // 16-byte Folded Reload
    ldr     x23, [sp, #32]                  // 8-byte Folded Reload
    add     sp, sp, #80
    .cfi_def_cfa_offset 0
    .cfi_restore w19
    .cfi_restore w20
    .cfi_restore w21
    .cfi_restore w22
    .cfi_restore w23
    .cfi_restore w30
    .cfi_restore w29

samples.generated: Below is one acceptable fix. The problem was that the ST1D instruction (which stores the SVE register z0) writes as many bytes as there are active lanes in the SVE register. In our code the predicate “ptrue p0.d” makes all 64‐bit lanes active. Since the SVE vector length (VL) is configurable (with a minimum of 128 bits but possibly up to 2048 bits, i.e. 16–256 bytes), reserving only 16 bytes on the stack (as was originally done) is not sufficient on many targets and leads to a segmentation fault when ST1D writes past the reserved space. .arch    armv8.2-a+sve
    .text
    .global pow2
    .type   pow2, @function
pow2:
    // This function computes: return sign‐extended( 1 << (w0) )
    mov     w8, #1
    lsl     w8, w8, w0
    sxtw    x0, w8
    ret

    .global main
    .type   main, @function
main:
    // Prologue: minimal stack frame setup
    stp     x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!
    mov     x29, sp

    // Allocate an array of 8 doublewords (64 bytes) for the source data.
    mov     w0, #64
    bl      malloc
    mov     x19, x0           // x19 = pointer to source array

    // Allocate an array of 8 doublewords for the destination.
    mov     w0, #64
    bl      malloc
    mov     x20, x0           // x20 = pointer to destination array

    // For our “vector‐loops” we define the total element count (8) in x6.
    mov     x6, #8

    // Set up predicate p0 for 64–bit (".d") operations.
    ptrue   p0.d

    // Demonstrate the use of cntw (which returns a count based on “ALL” active lanes).
    cntw    x5, ALL         // (x5 is not used later; this is just to show its use)

    // Compute the vector iteration “chunk” for 64–bit elements.
    rdvl    x1, #1          // x1 gets the number of bytes processed in one vector op.
    lsr     x2, x1, #3      // x2 = number of 64–bit elements per iteration

    // --------------------------------------------
    // Initialize the source array to 5 using st1d.
    // (We loop using x3 as an element index; if there is a partial chunk we use a tail predicate.)
    mov     x3, #0          // index into the array
init_loop:
    sub     x4, x6, x3      // x4 = (total – index) = remaining elements
    cmp     x4, x2
    b.lt   init_tail
    dup     z0.d, #5        // Broadcast immediate 5 into every lane of z0
    add     x9, x19, x3, LSL #3
    st1d   {z0.d}, p0, [x9]
    add     x3, x3, x2
    cmp     x3, x6
    b.lt   init_loop
init_tail:
    whilelo p1.d, xzr, x4   // Set tail mask for the remaining (fewer than x2) lanes.
    dup     z0.d, #5
    add     x9, x19, x3, LSL #3
    st1d   {z0.d}, p1, [x9]

    // --------------------------------------------
    // Initialize the destination array to 0.
    mov     x3, #0
init_loop2:
    sub     x4, x6, x3      // remaining = total – index
    cmp     x4, x2
    b.lt   init2_tail
    dup     z1.d, #0
    add     x9, x20, x3, LSL #3
    st1d   {z1.d}, p0, [x9]
    add     x3, x3, x2
    cmp     x3, x6
    b.lt   init_loop2
init2_tail:
    whilelo p1.d, xzr, x4
    dup     z1.d, #0
    add     x9, x20, x3, LSL #3
    st1d   {z1.d}, p1, [x9]

    // --------------------------------------------
    // Perform the vector addition: destination = source + 10.
    dup     z2.d, #10       // Broadcast 10 into z2 for addition.
    mov     x3, #0
vec_add_loop:
    sub     x4, x6, x3      // remaining = 8 – index
    cmp     x4, x2
    b.lt   vec_add_tail
    add     x9, x19, x3, LSL #3
    ld1d   {z3.d}, p0, [x9]
    add     z3.d, z3.d, z2.d
    add     x9, x20, x3, LSL #3
    st1d   {z3.d}, p0, [x9]
    add     x3, x3, x2
    cmp     x3, x6
    b.lt   vec_add_loop
vec_add_tail:
    whilelo p1.d, xzr, x4
    add     x9, x19, x3, LSL #3
    ld1d   {z3.d}, p1, [x9]
    add     z3.d, z3.d, z2.d
    add     x9, x20, x3, LSL #3
    st1d   {z3.d}, p1, [x9]

    // --------------------------------------------
    // Demonstrate predicated negation:
    add     x9, x20, xzr    // (x9 = x20)
    ld1d   {z3.d}, p0, [x9]  // Load first vector chunk from destination
    neg     z3.d, p0/m, z3.d      // Negate each active element in z3
    add     x9, x20, xzr
    st1d   {z3.d}, p0, [x9]  // Store the result back

    add     x9, x20, xzr
    ld1d   {z3.d}, p0, [x9]
    and     z3.d, z3.d, #0xFF     // Each element gets masked with 0xFF.
    add     x9, x20, xzr
    st1d   {z3.d}, p0, [x9]

    // --------------------------------------------
    // Prepare to call printf. (We use adrp/add to get the format string.)
    adrp    x0, fmt
    add     x0, x0, :lo12:fmt
    ldr     x1, [x20]       // Pass the first (masked and negated) element as argument.
    bl      printf

    // Epilogue
    mov     x0, #0
    mov     x29, sp
    ldp     x29, x30, [sp], #16
    ret

    .data
    .align 3
fmt:
    .asciz "%lli\n"

    .extern malloc
    .extern printf
    .end

.arch    armv8.2-a+sve
    .text
    .global pow2
    .type   pow2, @function
pow2:
    // This function computes: return sign‐extended( 1 << (w0) )
    mov     w8, #1
    lsl     w8, w8, w0
    sxtw    x0, w8
    ret

    .global main
    .type   main, @function
main:
    // Prologue: minimal stack frame setup
    stp     x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!
    mov     x29, sp

    // Allocate an array of 8 doublewords (64 bytes) for the source data.
    mov     w0, #64
    bl      malloc
    mov     x19, x0           // x19 = pointer to source array

    // Allocate an array of 8 doublewords for the destination.
    mov     w0, #64
    bl      malloc
    mov     x20, x0           // x20 = pointer to destination array

    // For our “vector‐loops” we define the total element count (8) in x6.
    mov     x6, #8

    // Set up predicate p0 for 64–bit (".d") operations.
    ptrue   p0.d

    // Demonstrate the use of cntw (which returns a count based on “ALL” active lanes).
    cntw    x5, ALL         // (x5 is not used later; this is just to show its use)

    // Compute the vector iteration “chunk” for 64–bit elements.
    rdvl    x1, #1          // x1 gets the number of bytes processed in one vector op.
    lsr     x2, x1, #3      // x2 = number of 64–bit elements per iteration

    // --------------------------------------------
    // Initialize the source array to 5 using st1d.
    // (We loop using x3 as an element index; if there is a partial chunk we use a tail predicate.)
    mov     x3, #0          // index into the array
init_loop:
    sub     x4, x6, x3      // x4 = (total – index) = remaining elements
    cmp     x4, x2
    b.lt   init_tail
    dup     z0.d, #5        // Broadcast immediate 5 into every lane of z0
    add     x9, x19, x3, LSL #3
    st1d   {z0.d}, p0, [x9]
    add     x3, x3, x2
    cmp     x3, x6
    b.lt   init_loop
init_tail:
    whilelo p1.d, xzr, x4   // Set tail mask for the remaining (fewer than x2) lanes.
    dup     z0.d, #5
    add     x9, x19, x3, LSL #3
    st1d   {z0.d}, p1, [x9]

    // --------------------------------------------
    // Initialize the destination array to 0.
    mov     x3, #0
init_loop2:
    sub     x4, x6, x3      // remaining = total – index
    cmp     x4, x2
    b.lt   init2_tail
    dup     z1.d, #0
    add     x9, x20, x3, LSL #3
    st1d   {z1.d}, p0, [x9]
    add     x3, x3, x2
    cmp     x3, x6
    b.lt   init_loop2
init2_tail:
    whilelo p1.d, xzr, x4
    dup     z1.d, #0
    add     x9, x20, x3, LSL #3
    st1d   {z1.d}, p1, [x9]

    // --------------------------------------------
    // Perform the vector addition: destination = source + 10.
    dup     z2.d, #10       // Broadcast 10 into z2 for addition.
    mov     x3, #0
vec_add_loop:
    sub     x4, x6, x3      // remaining = 8 – index
    cmp     x4, x2
    b.lt   vec_add_tail
    add     x9, x19, x3, LSL #3
    ld1d   {z3.d}, p0/z, [x9]
    add     z3.d, z3.d, z2.d
    add     x9, x20, x3, LSL #3
    st1d   {z3.d}, p0, [x9]
    add     x3, x3, x2
    cmp     x3, x6
    b.lt   vec_add_loop
vec_add_tail:
    whilelo p1.d, xzr, x4
    add     x9, x19, x3, LSL #3
    ld1d   {z3.d}, p1/z, [x9]
    add     z3.d, z3.d, z2.d
    add     x9, x20, x3, LSL #3
    st1d   {z3.d}, p1, [x9]

    // --------------------------------------------
    // Demonstrate predicated negation:
    add     x9, x20, xzr    // (x9 = x20)
    ld1d   {z3.d}, p0/z, [x9]  // Load first vector chunk from destination
    neg     z3.d, p0/m, z3.d      // Negate each active element in z3
    add     x9, x20, xzr
    st1d   {z3.d}, p0, [x9]  // Store the result back

    // Demonstrate vector bitwise AND with an immediate.
    add     x9, x20, xzr
    ld1d   {z3.d}, p0/z, [x9]
    and     z3.d, z3.d, #0xFF     // Each element gets masked with 0xFF.
    add     x9, x20, xzr
    st1d   {z3.d}, p0, [x9]

    // --------------------------------------------
    // Prepare to call printf. (We use adrp/add to get the format string.)
    adrp    x0, fmt
    add     x0, x0, :lo12:fmt
    ldr     x1, [x20]       // Pass the first (masked and negated) element as argument.
    bl      printf

    // Epilogue
    mov     x0, #0
    mov     x29, sp
    ldp     x29, x30, [sp], #16
    ret

    .data
    .align 3
fmt:
    .asciz "%lli\n"

    .extern malloc
    .extern printf
    .end

    mov     x29, sp

    mov     w0, #64
    bl      malloc
    mov     x19, x0           // x19 = pointer to source array

    // Allocate an array of 8 doublewords for the destination.
    mov     w0, #64
    bl      malloc
    mov     x20, x0           // x20 = pointer to destination array

    // For our vector–loops, define the total element count (8) in x6.
    mov     x6, #8

    // (We will generate predicates on‐the–fly based on the number of valid elements.)
    
    // Demonstrate the use of cntw (just for show).
    cntw    x5, ALL         // (x5 is not used later; demonstration purpose)

    // Compute the vector iteration “chunk” for 64–bit (".d") elements.
    rdvl    x1, #1          // x1 gets the number of bytes processed in one vector op.
    lsr     x2, x1, #3      // x2 = number of 64–bit elements per iteration

    // --------------------------------------------
    // Initialize the source array to 5.
    // (If the full vector chunk (x2) would go past our total (8), we do a tail iteration.)
    mov     x3, #0          // index into the array

    sub     x4, x6, x3      // remaining = total – index
    cmp     x4, x2

    add     x9, x19, x3, LSL #3

    whilelo p0.d, xzr, x2
    st1d   {z0.d}, p0, [x9]
    add     x3, x3, x2
    cmp     x3, x6
    b.lt   init_loop
init_tail:
    // Tail: remaining elements in x4 (< x2).
    whilelo p1.d, xzr, x4
    dup     z0.d, #5
    add     x9, x19, x3, LSL #3
    st1d   {z0.d}, p1, [x9]

    mov     x3, #0

    cmp     x4, x2

    add     x9, x20, x3, LSL #3

.arch armv8.2-a+sve
    .text
    .global pow2
    .type   pow2, @function
pow2:
    // This function computes: return sign-extended( 1 << (w0) )
    mov     w8, #1
    lsl     w8, w8, w0
    sxtw    x0, w8
    ret

    .global main
    .type   main, @function
main:
    // Prologue: minimal stack frame setup
    stp     x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!
    mov     x29, sp

    // Allocate an array of 8 doublewords (8*8=64 bytes) for the source.
    mov     w0, #64
    bl      malloc
    mov     x19, x0           // x19 = pointer to source array

    // Allocate an array of 8 doublewords (64 bytes) for the destination.
    mov     w0, #64
    bl      malloc
    mov     x20, x0           // x20 = pointer to destination

    // Set our total element count (8) in x6.
    mov     x6, #8

    // (Demonstrate cntw, which computes a multiple of the ALL predicate constraint.)
    cntw    x5, ALL         // (x5 is not used later; demonstration only)

    // Compute the vector‐iteration “chunk” for 64–bit (".d") elements.
    rdvl    x1, #1          // x1 = current vector length (in bytes) for one vector op.
    lsr     x2, x1, #3      // x2 = number of 64–bit elements per full iteration.

    // --------------------------------------------
    // Initialize the source array to 5.
    // (We only want to write exactly 8 elements.)
    mov     x3, #0          // index into array
init_loop:
    sub     x4, x6, x3      // remaining = total (8) - index
    cmp     x4, x2
    b.lt   init_tail       // if remaining < full chunk then do tail iteration
    dup     z0.d, #5        // Broadcast 5 into all lanes of z0.
    add     x9, x19, x3, LSL #3
    whilelo p0.d, xzr, x2   // p0 = ones in first x2 lanes.
    st1d   {z0.d}, p0, [x9]
    add     x3, x3, x2
    cmp     x3, x6
    b.lt   init_loop
init_tail:
    whilelo p1.d, xzr, x4   // Tail: only first (x4) lanes active.
    dup     z0.d, #5
    add     x9, x19, x3, LSL #3
    st1d   {z0.d}, p1, [x9]

    // --------------------------------------------
    // Initialize the destination array to 0.
    mov     x3, #0
init_loop2:
    sub     x4, x6, x3      // remaining = total - index
    cmp     x4, x2
    b.lt   init2_tail
    dup     z1.d, #0
    add     x9, x20, x3, LSL #3
    whilelo p0.d, xzr, x2
    st1d   {z1.d}, p0, [x9]
    add     x3, x3, x2
    cmp     x3, x6
    b.lt   init_loop2
init2_tail:
    whilelo p1.d, xzr, x4
    dup     z1.d, #0
    add     x9, x20, x3, LSL #3
    st1d   {z1.d}, p1, [x9]

    // --------------------------------------------
    // Perform the vector addition: destination = source + 10.
    dup     z2.d, #10       // Broadcast 10 into z2.
    mov     x3, #0
vec_add_loop:
    sub     x4, x6, x3      // remaining elements = total - index
    cmp     x4, x2
    b.lt   vec_add_tail
    add     x9, x19, x3, LSL #3
    whilelo p0.d, xzr, x2
    ld1d   {z3.d}, p0/z, [x9]
    add    z3.d, z3.d, z2.d
    add     x9, x20, x3, LSL #3
    whilelo p0.d, xzr, x2
    st1d   {z3.d}, p0, [x9]
    add     x3, x3, x2
    cmp     x3, x6
    b.lt   vec_add_loop
vec_add_tail:
    whilelo p1.d, xzr, x4
    add     x9, x19, x3, LSL #3
    ld1d   {z3.d}, p1/z, [x9]
    add    z3.d, z3.d, z2.d
    add     x9, x20, x3, LSL #3
    st1d   {z3.d}, p1, [x9]

    // --------------------------------------------
    // Demonstrate predicated negation.
    // (Here we show a use of ptrue as well as whilelo:
    //  ptrue sets ALL bits; whilelo p0.d, xzr, x6 then restricts the mask to just 8 lanes.)
    ptrue   p2.d         // p2 now has all lanes active.
    whilelo p0.d, xzr, x6     // p0 = predicate in which only the first 8 lanes are active.
    add     x9, x20, xzr      // x9 = pointer to destination.
    ld1d   {z3.d}, p0/z, [x9]
    neg     z3.d, p0/m, z3.d  // Negate each (active) element.
    st1d   {z3.d}, p0, [x9]

    // Demonstrate vector bitwise AND with an immediate.
    add     x9, x20, xzr
    whilelo p0.d, xzr, x6
    ld1d   {z3.d}, p0/z, [x9]
    and     z3.d, z3.d, #0xFF   // Mask each element with 0xFF.
    st1d   {z3.d}, p0, [x9]

    // --------------------------------------------
    // Prepare to call printf. (We use adrp/add to get the format string.)
    adrp    x0, fmt
    add     x0, x0, :lo12:fmt
    ldr     x1, [x20]       // Pass the first (masked, negated) element.
    bl      printf

    // Epilogue
    mov     x0, #0
    mov     x29, sp
    ldp     x29, x30, [sp], #16
    ret

    .data
    .align 3
fmt:
    .asciz "%lli\n"

    .extern malloc
    .extern printf
    .end

operand position even if they have different names but refer to the same architectural register state Any other use is

.arch armv8.2-a+sve
    .text
    .global main
    .type   main, %function
main:
    // Set predicate registers: p0 for 32‐bit lanes and p1 for 16‐bit lanes.
    ptrue   p0.s           // p0 active for 32‐bit elements
    ptrue   p1.h           // p1 active for 16‐bit elements
    cntw    x21, p0        // x21 = number of active 32‐bit lanes
    cnth    x22, p1        // x22 = number of active 16‐bit lanes

    // Initialize our “scalar” variables (stored in the lower lane of a vector)
    dup     z1.s, wzr      // Z1 <- 0    (w1 = 0)
    dup     z8.s, wzr      // Z8 <- 0    (w8 = 0)
    dup     z13.s, wzr     // Z13<- 0    (w13 = 0)

    // Set w9 = 1  (stored in Z9.s)
    mov     w2, #1
    dup     z9.s, w2       // Z9  = 1

    // Set w10 = -1  (load 1 then negate)
    mov     w3, #1
    neg     w3, w3
    dup     z10.s, w3      // Z10 = -1

    // Set w11 = 2 (stored in Z11.s)
    mov     w4, #2
    dup     z11.s, w4      // Z11 = 2

L_outer:
    // Compute w12 = w9 >> 1, stored in Z12.s
    lsr     z12.s, z9.s, #1

    // Get the “scalar” w9 from the lower lane of Z9 and compare with 4.
    mov     w5, z9.s[0]
    cmp     w5, #4
    b.lo    L_loop1         // (if w9 < 4, skip inner loop)

    // For w9 >= 4, compute w14 = (w12 > 2 ? w12 : 2).
    mov     w6, z12.s[0]    // w6 = current w12
    cmp     w6, #2
    mov     w7, z11.s[0]    // w7 will hold 2 (w11 constant)
    csel    w6, w6, w7, hi  // if (w12>2) then w6 remains, else w6 = 2
    dup     z14.s, w6      // Z14 <- w14

L_loop1:
    // Begin inner loop (only executed when w9>=4)
    // Set inner–loop variable: w15 = 1 in Z15 and copy current w10 into Z16.
    mov     w7, #1
    dup     z15.s, w7      // Z15 <- 1   (w15 = 1)
    mov     z16.s, z10.s   // Z16 <- w10  (w16 = current w10)

L_inner:
    // Compute w17 = (w15 * w15). We use mad with an explicit zero.
    dup     z0.s, wzr      // Z0 <- 0
    mad     z17.s, p0/m, z15.s, z15.s, z0.s   // Z17 = w15 * w15

    // Compute (w12 - w15) (scalar inner–loop count) [not used further]
    mov     w10, z12.s[0]   // w10 = w12
    mov     w11, z15.s[0]   // w11 = w15
    sub     w12, w10, w11   // w12 = w12 - w15

    // Create a vector index: 0, 1, 2, ...
    index   z18.s, #0, #1   // Z18 = {0,1,2,...}

    // Compute (w15 + index) in Z19:
    add     z19.s, z15.s, z18.s
    // Square (w15+index): use mad (with zero) so Z19 = (w15+index)^2
    dup     z0.s, wzr
    mad     z19.s, p0/m, z19.s, z19.s, z0.s
    // Now add w15^2: Z19 = (w15+index)^2 + (w15)^2.
    add     z19.s, z19.s, z17.s

    // Compute (w16 - index) in Z20 and square it:
    sub     z20.s, z16.s, z18.s
    dup     z0.s, wzr
    mad     z20.s, p0/m, z20.s, z20.s, z0.s   // Z20 = (w16-index)^2

    // Compare: per lane, test if (w15+index)^2 + (w15)^2 equals (w16-index)^2.
    cmpeq   p2.s, p0, z19.s, z20.s

    // For true lanes, we wish to “write 1”. First clear a temporary vector:
    dup     z23.s, wzr      
    mov     w7, #1
    dup     z24.s, w7       // Z24 filled with ones.
    sel     z23.s, p2, z24.s, z23.s  // In lanes where p2 is true, Z23 becomes 1

    // Horizontally add the “ones” from all lanes.
    uaddv   w7, p0, z23.s   // w7 = (number of matches)

    // Add this count to the inner–loop accumulator stored in Z13.
    mov     w8, z13.s[0]
    add     w8, w8, w7
    dup     z13.s, w8       // Z13 <- new accumulator (w13)

    // End of this inner–loop iteration: update inner–loop variables.
    add     z15.s, z15.s, #1   // w15++
    sub     z16.s, z16.s, #2   // w16 = w16 - 2

    // Loop until inner variable equals w14.
    mov     w9, z15.s[0]
    mov     w10, z14.s[0]
    cmp     w9, w10
    b.ne    L_inner

    // Now do the post–inner–loop updates.
    // (a) If the inner–loop sum (w13 in Z13) is larger than the running maximum (w8 in Z8),
    // update w8.
    mov     w11, z13.s[0]
    mov     w12, z8.s[0]
    cmp     w11, w12
    csel    w12, w11, w12, hi   // if (w13 > w8) then w12 = w13
    dup     z8.s, w12           // update Z8 with new maximum

    // (b) Also, if (w13 > w8) then update w1 (in Z1) to the current outer–loop value w9.
    mov     w13, z9.s[0]
    mov     w14, z1.s[0]
    mov     w15, z8.s[0]
    cmp     w11, w15
    csel    w14, w13, w14, hi    // if (w13 > w8) then use current w9
    dup     z1.s, w14           // update Z1 (w1)

    // Increment w10 (our “current inner loop” value) by 1.
    mov     w16, z10.s[0]
    add     w16, w16, #1
    dup     z10.s, w16

    // Increment the outer–loop variable (w9 in Z9) by 1.
    add     z9.s, z9.s, #1
    mov     w17, z9.s[0]
    cmp     w17, #1001
    b.eq   L_end
    b      L_outer

L_end:
    // Set up stack frame and call printf.
    stp     x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!
    mov     x29, sp
    adrp    x0, .L_str
    add     x0, x0, :lo12:.L_str
    mov     w1, z1.s[0]   // Pass our selected result (w1) as second argument.
    bl      printf
    mov     w0, wzr
    ldp     x29, x30, [sp], #16
    ret

    .section .rodata
.L_str:
    .asciz "%u\n"
    .size  .L_str, 4

.arch   armv8.2-a+sve
    .text
    .global main
    .type   main, %function
main:
    // Set predicate registers: p0 for 32‐bit lanes and p1 for 16‐bit lanes.
    ptrue   p0.s           // p0 active for 32‐bit elements
    ptrue   p1.h           // p1 active for 16‐bit elements
    cntw    x21, p0.s      // x21 = number of active 32‐bit lanes
    cnth    x22, p1.h      // x22 = number of active 16‐bit lanes

    // Use w25 as a scratch register that holds 0.
    mov     w25, #0

    // Initialize our “scalar” variables (stored in the lower lane of a vector)
    dup     z1.s, w25      // Z1 <- 0    (w1 = 0)
    dup     z8.s, w25      // Z8 <- 0    (w8 = 0)
    dup     z13.s, w25     // Z13<- 0    (w13 = 0)

    // Set w9 = 1  (stored in Z9.s)
    mov     w2, #1
    dup     z9.s, w2       // Z9 = 1

    // Set w10 = -1  (load 1 then negate)
    mov     w3, #1
    neg     w3, w3
    dup     z10.s, w3      // Z10 = -1

    // Set w11 = 2 (stored in Z11.s)
    mov     w4, #2
    dup     z11.s, w4      // Z11 = 2

L_outer:
    // Compute w12 = w9 >> 1, stored in Z12.s
    lsr     z12.s, z9.s, #1

    // Get the “scalar” w9 from the lower lane of Z9.
    // (Since SVE registers cannot be directly indexed, we use the lower 128–bit alias.)
    mov     w5, v9.s[0]
    cmp     w5, #4
    b.lo    L_loop1         // If w9 < 4, skip inner loop

    // For w9 >= 4, compute w14 = (w12 > 2 ? w12 : 2).
    mov     w6, v12.s[0]    // w6 = current w12
    cmp     w6, #2
    mov     w7, v11.s[0]    // w7 = 2 from Z11
    csel    w6, w6, w7, hi  // if (w12 > 2) then keep w6, else set w6 = 2
    dup     z14.s, w6      // Z14 <- w14

L_loop1:
    // Begin inner–loop (only executed when w9 >= 4)
    // Set inner–loop variable: w15 = 1 (in Z15) and copy current w10 into Z16.
    mov     w7, #1
    dup     z15.s, w7      // Z15 <- 1   (w15 = 1)
    mov     z16, z10       // Copy the entire vector (Z10) into Z16 (so w16 = current w10)

L_inner:
    // Compute w17 = (w15 * w15) via a multiply–add with a zero addend.
    dup     z0.s, w25      // Z0 <- 0
    mad     z17.s, p0/m, z15.s, z15.s, z0.s   // Z17 = w15 * w15

    // Compute (w12 - w15) (the scalar inner–loop count) [not used later]:
    mov     w10, v12.s[0]   // w10 = w12
    mov     w11, v15.s[0]   // w11 = w15
    sub     w12, w10, w11   // w12 = w12 - w15

    // Create a vector index: 0, 1, 2, … 
    index   z18.s, #0, #1   // Z18 = {0,1,2,...}

    // Compute (w15 + index) in Z19.
    add     z19.s, z15.s, z18.s
    // Square (w15+index) using mad with zero.
    dup     z0.s, w25
    mad     z19.s, p0/m, z19.s, z19.s, z0.s
    // Now add w15^2 (already computed into Z17).
    add     z19.s, z19.s, z17.s

    // Compute (w16 - index) in Z20 and square it.
    sub     z20.s, z16.s, z18.s
    dup     z0.s, w25
    mad     z20.s, p0/m, z20.s, z20.s, z0.s   // Z20 = (w16-index)^2

    // Compare per lane whether (w15+index)^2 + (w15)^2 equals (w16-index)^2.
    cmpeq   p2.s, p0, z19.s, z20.s

    // For lanes where the compare is true, “write 1”.
    dup     z23.s, w25      
    mov     w7, #1
    dup     z24.s, w7       // Z24 filled with ones.
    sel     z23.s, p2, z24.s, z23.s  // For lanes where p2 is true, Z23 becomes 1

    // Horizontally add the “ones” from all lanes.
    uaddv   w7, p0, z23.s   // w7 = (number of matches)

    // Add this count to the inner–loop accumulator (stored in Z13).
    mov     w8, v13.s[0]
    add     w8, w8, w7
    dup     z13.s, w8       // Update Z13 (w13)

    // End of inner–loop iteration: update inner–loop variables.
    add     z15.s, z15.s, #1   // w15++
    sub     z16.s, z16.s, #2   // w16 = w16 - 2

    // Loop until inner–loop variable equals w14:
    mov     w9, v15.s[0]
    mov     w10, v14.s[0]
    cmp     w9, w10
    b.ne    L_inner

    // Post–inner–loop updates.
    // (a) If the inner–loop sum (in Z13) is larger than the running max (in Z8), update Z8.
    mov     w11, v13.s[0]
    mov     w12, v8.s[0]
    cmp     w11, w12
    csel    w12, w11, w12, hi   // if (w13 > w8) then set w12 = w13
    dup     z8.s, w12           // update Z8

    // (b) Also, if (w13 > w8) then update Z1 to the current outer–loop value.
    mov     w13, v9.s[0]
    mov     w14, v1.s[0]
    mov     w15, v8.s[0]
    cmp     w11, w15
    csel    w14, w13, w14, hi    // if (w13 > w8) then use current w9
    dup     z1.s, w14           // update Z1 (w1)

    // Increment the “current inner loop” value (w10) by 1.
    mov     w16, v10.s[0]
    add     w16, w16, #1
    dup     z10.s, w16

    // Increment the outer–loop variable (in Z9) by 1.
    add     z9.s, z9.s, #1
    mov     w17, v9.s[0]
    cmp     w17, #1001
    b.eq   L_end
    b      L_outer

L_end:
    // Set up the frame and call printf.
    stp     x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!
    mov     x29, sp
    adrp    x0, .L_str
    add     x0, x0, :lo12:.L_str
    mov     w1, v1.s[0]   // Pass our computed result (w1) as second argument.
    bl      printf
    mov     w0, wzr
    ldp     x29, x30, [sp], #16
    ret

    .section .rodata
.L_str:
    .asciz "%u\n"
    .size  .L_str, 4
