.arch   armv8.2-a+sve
    .text
    .global main
    .type   main, %function
main:
    // Set predicate registers: p0 for 32‐bit lanes and p1 for 16‐bit lanes.
    ptrue   p0.s           // p0 active for 32‐bit elements
    ptrue   p1.h           // p1 active for 16‐bit elements
    cntw    x21, p0        // x21 = number of active 32‐bit lanes
    cnth    x22, p1        // x22 = number of active 16‐bit lanes

    // Use w25 as a scratch register that holds 0.
    mov     w25, #0

    // Initialize our “scalar” variables (stored in the lower lane of a vector)
    dup     z1.s, w25      // Z1 <- 0    (w1 = 0)
    dup     z8.s, w25      // Z8 <- 0    (w8 = 0)
    dup     z13.s, w25     // Z13<- 0    (w13 = 0)

    // Set w9 = 1  (stored in Z9.s)
    mov     w2, #1
    dup     z9.s, w2       // Z9 = 1

    // Set w10 = -1  (load 1 then negate)
    mov     w3, #1
    neg     w3, w3
    dup     z10.s, w3      // Z10 = -1

    // Set w11 = 2 (stored in Z11.s)
    mov     w4, #2
    dup     z11.s, w4      // Z11 = 2

L_outer:
    // Compute w12 = w9 >> 1, stored in Z12.s
    lsr     z12.s, p0/m, z9.s, #1

    // Get the “scalar” w9 from the lower lane of Z9.
    mov     w5, v9.s[0]
    cmp     w5, #4
    b.lo    L_loop1         // If w9 < 4, skip inner loop

    // For w9 >= 4, compute w14 = (w12 > 2 ? w12 : 2).
    mov     w6, v12.s[0]    // w6 = current w12
    cmp     w6, #2
    mov     w7, v11.s[0]    // w7 = 2 from Z11
    csel    w6, w6, w7, hi  // if (w12 > 2) then keep w6, else set w6 = 2
    dup     z14.s, w6      // Z14 <- w14

L_loop1:
    // Begin inner–loop (only executed when w9 >= 4)
    // Set inner–loop variable: w15 = 1 (in Z15) and copy current w10 into Z16.
    mov     w7, #1
    dup     z15.s, w7      // Z15 <- 1   (w15 = 1)
    // Copy Z10 into Z16 using movprfx (the proper form is to supply a predicate operand)
    dup     z0.s, w25      // Set up a zero vector in Z0
    movprfx z16.s, p0/m, z10.s
    add     z16.s, p0/m, z16.s, z0.s   // Now Z16 = Z10

L_inner:
    // Compute w17 = (w15 * w15)
    mul     z17.s, p0/m, z15.s, z15.s   // Z17 = w15 * w15

    // (The next three instructions compute a scalar inner–loop count, unused later)
    mov     w10, v12.s[0]   // w10 = w12
    mov     w11, v15.s[0]   // w11 = w15
    sub     w12, w10, w11   // w12 = w12 - w15

    // Create a vector index: 0, 1, 2, … 
    index   z18.s, #0, #1   // Z18 = {0,1,2,...}

    // Compute (w15 + index) in Z19.
    add     z19.s, p0/m, z15.s, z18.s
    // Square (w15+index); note: we use mul (with an implicit zero addend) instead of mad.
    mul     z19.s, p0/m, z19.s, z19.s
    // Now add w15^2 (computed into Z17).
    add     z19.s, p0/m, z19.s, z17.s

    // Compute (w16 - index) in Z20 and square it.
    sub     z20.s, p0/m, z16.s, z18.s
    mul     z20.s, p0/m, z20.s, z20.s   // Z20 = (w16-index)^2

    // Compare per lane whether (w15+index)^2 + (w15)^2 equals (w16-index)^2.
    cmpeq   p2, p0, z19.s, z20.s

    // For lanes where the compare is true, “write 1”.
    dup     z23.s, w25      
    mov     w7, #1
    dup     z24.s, w7       // Z24 filled with ones.
    sel     z23.s, p2, z24.s, z23.s  // For lanes where p2 is true, Z23 becomes 1

    // Horizontally add the “ones” from all lanes.
    uaddv   x7, p0, z23.s   // x7 = (number of matches)

    // Add this count to the inner–loop accumulator (stored in Z13).
    mov     w8, v13.s[0]
    add     w8, w8, w7
    dup     z13.s, w8       // Update Z13 (w13)

    // End of inner–loop iteration: update inner–loop variables.
    add     z15.s, p0/m, z15.s, #1   // w15++
    sub     z16.s, p0/m, z16.s, #2   // w16 = w16 - 2

    // Loop until inner–loop variable equals w14:
    mov     w9, v15.s[0]
    mov     w10, v14.s[0]
    cmp     w9, w10
    b.ne    L_inner

    mov     w11, v13.s[0]
    mov     w12, v8.s[0]
    cmp     w11, w12
    csel    w12, w11, w12, hi   // if (w13 > w8) then set w12 = w13
    dup     z8.s, w12           // update Z8

    mov     w13, v9.s[0]
    mov     w14, v1.s[0]
    mov     w15, v8.s[0]
    cmp     w11, w15
    csel    w14, w13, w14, hi    // if (w13 > w8) then use current w9
    dup     z1.s, w14           // update Z1 (w1)

    mov     w16, v10.s[0]
    add     w16, w16, #1
    dup     z10.s, w16

    // Increment the outer–loop variable (in Z9) by 1.
    add     z9.s, p0/m, z9.s, #1
    mov     w17, v9.s[0]
    cmp     w17, #1001
    b.eq    L_end
    b       L_outer

	// a predicate with “predicate‐as‐counter” encoding is required; here we use p8 and p9.
	ptrue	p0.s           // p0 = all–true (32‐bit lanes for most vector ops)
	ptrue	p8.s           // p8 = all–true for 32–bit counter (for cntw)
	ptrue	p9.h           // p9 = all–true for 16–bit counter (for cnth)

	pfalse	p2             // p2 = all–false (will be overwritten by compare)

	cnth	x22, p9        // x22 = number of active 16‐bit lanes (using counter predicate p9)

	mov	w25, #0

	dup	z1.s, w25      // Z1  <- 0   (will eventually hold our “result”)
	dup	z8.s, w25      // Z8  <- 0   (running max)
	dup	z13.s, w25     // Z13 <- 0   (inner–loop sum)

	mov	w2, #1
	dup	z9.s, w2       // Z9  = 1 (outer–loop variable)

.arch	armv8.2-a+sve
	.text
	.macro EXTRACT_S32 rd, zn
	  st1w { \zn.s }, p1, [sp]     // store only the “lane‐0” (predicate p1 will be true only on lane 0)
	  ldr   \rd, [sp]
	.endm

	.global main
	.type main, %function
main:
	  /* Function prologue: push FP/return address and allocate a scratch slot (4 bytes) */
	  stp	 x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!
	  mov	 x29, sp
	  sub	 sp, sp, #4         // reserve 4 bytes for scalar extraction

	  /* Set up our predicates – note that counter operations require predicates p8/p9,
	     and that ptrue/pfalse must have an element‐type suffix. */
	  ptrue  p0.s             // p0 = all–true (for arithmetic/merging)
	  ptrue  p8.s             // p8 = all–true for 32–bit counter (for CNTW)
	  ptrue  p9.h             // p9 = all–true for 16–bit counter (for CNTH)
	  pfalse p2.s             // p2 = all–false (will be used as destination in compare)

	  /* Set up a predicate (in p1) that is true only on lane 0.
	     (We use this to “extract” the first element from a vector register.) */
	  mov    x10, #1
	  whilelo p1.s, xzr, x10

	  /* Get the number of lanes (for informational purposes) */
	  cntw   x21, p8.s       // x21 = number of active 32–bit lanes
	  cnth   x22, p9.h       // x22 = number of active 16–bit lanes

	  /* Use w25 as a scratch set to 0, and initialize our “scalar” variables
	     (each stored in lane 0 of a vector register) */
	  mov    w25, #0
	  dup    z1.s, w25      // z1  will eventually hold our “result”
	  dup    z8.s, w25      // z8  running max
	  dup    z13.s, w25     // z13 inner–loop accumulation

	  /* Set outer–loop variable to 1 (both in GPR w2 and then duplicated to z9) */
	  mov    w2, #1
	  dup    z9.s, w2
	  dup    z2.s, w2      // z2.s will be used for “+1” increments

	  /* Set up constant –1 in z10 */
	  mov    w3, #1
	  neg    w3, w3
	  dup    z10.s, w3

	  /* Set constant 2 in z11 */
	  mov    w4, #2
	  dup    z11.s, w4

L_outer:
	  /* Compute z12 = z9 >> 1 (logical shift right by 1 on each lane) */
	  lsr    z12.s, p0/m, z9.s, #1

	  /* Using our macro, extract the outer–loop variable (stored in z9) into w5 */
	  EXTRACT_S32 w5, z9

	  /* Now decide the inner–loop count.
	     (If the outer–loop variable is less than 4, we choose 1; otherwise,
	      we choose the greater of (outer >> 1) and 2.) */
	  cmp    w5, #4
	  b.lt   SetInnerCountDefault
	  EXTRACT_S32 w6, z12   // w6 = (outer >> 1)
	  cmp    w6, #2
	  EXTRACT_S32 w7, z11   // w7 = constant 2
	  csel   w6, w6, w7, hi
	  b      SetInnerCountDone
SetInnerCountDefault:
	  mov    w6, #1
SetInnerCountDone:
	  dup    z14.s, w6     // z14 = inner–loop count

L_loop1:
	  /* Begin inner loop: set inner variable (w15) to 1 and duplicate it to z15.
	     Also, copy z10 into z16 (using MOVPRFX). */
	  mov    w7, #1
	  dup    z15.s, w7     // inner–loop variable in z15
	  dup    z0.s, w25     // prepare a zero vector in z0
	  movprfx z16.s, p0/m, z10.s
	  add    z16.s, p0/m, z16.s, z0.s   // now z16 = z10

L_inner:
	  /* Compute (inner variable)^2 in z17  */
	  mul    z17.s, p0/m, z15.s, z15.s

	  /* (We also compute a scalar difference (z12 – z15) even though it is not used later.) */
	  EXTRACT_S32 w10, z12
	  EXTRACT_S32 w11, z15
	  sub    w12, w10, w11

	  /* Build an index vector (0, 1, 2, …) */
	  index  z18.s, #0, #1

	  /* Compute (z15+index)^2 and then add (z15)^2 */
	  add    z19.s, p0/m, z15.s, z18.s
	  mul    z19.s, p0/m, z19.s, z19.s
	  add    z19.s, p0/m, z19.s, z17.s

	  /* Compute (z16-index)^2 */
	  sub    z20.s, p0/m, z16.s, z18.s
	  mul    z20.s, p0/m, z20.s, z20.s

	  /* Compare the two results; note the predicate destination is now p2.s */
	  cmpeq  p2.s, p0, z19.s, z20.s

	  /* For those lanes where the result is true, set a 1; otherwise 0 */
	  dup    z23.s, w25
	  mov    w7, #1
	  dup    z24.s, w7
	  sel    z23.s, p2, z24.s, z23.s

	  /* Horizontally add (reduce) the elements of z23 into x7 */
	  uaddv  x7, p0, z23.s

	  /* Update the inner–loop accumulation (in z13) by extracting it, adding, and duplicating back */
	  EXTRACT_S32 w8, z13
	  add    w8, w8, x7
	  dup    z13.s, w8

	  /* End this inner–loop iteration:
	     (a) increment inner variable (z15 += 1)
	     (b) decrement z16 by 2 (using constant in z11) */
	  add    z15.s, p0/m, z15.s, z2.s
	  sub    z16.s, p0/m, z16.s, z11.s

	  /* Compare the inner variable to the inner–loop count (extracting both) */
	  EXTRACT_S32 w9, z15
	  EXTRACT_S32 w10, z14
	  cmp    w9, w10
	  b.ne   L_inner

	  /* Post inner loop: if inner accumulation (z13) is greater than the current running max (z8),
	     update z8; likewise, update our “result” (in z1) with the outer–loop variable if needed. */
	  EXTRACT_S32 w11, z13
	  EXTRACT_S32 w12, z8
	  cmp    w11, w12
	  csel   w12, w11, w12, hi
	  dup    z8.s, w12

	  EXTRACT_S32 w13, z9   // outer variable
	  EXTRACT_S32 w14, z1   // current result
	  EXTRACT_S32 w15, z8   // current running max
	  cmp    w11, w15
	  csel   w14, w13, w14, hi
	  dup    z1.s, w14

	  /* Increment the “current inner loop” value (in z10) by 1 */
	  EXTRACT_S32 w16, z10
	  add    w16, w16, #1
	  dup    z10.s, w16

	  /* Increment the outer–loop variable. */
	  add    z9.s, p0/m, z9.s, z2.s
	  EXTRACT_S32 w17, z9
	  cmp    w17, #1001
	  b.eq   L_end
	  b      L_outer

L_end:
	  /* Before calling printf we restore our scratch area */
	  add    sp, sp, #4
	  stp    x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!
	  mov    x29, sp
	  adrp   x0, .L_str
	  add    x0, x0, :lo12:.L_str
	  EXTRACT_S32 w1, z1   // result in w1
	  bl     printf
	  mov    w0, wzr
	  ldp    x29, x30, [sp], #16
	  ret

	.section .rodata
.L_str:
	  .asciz "%u\n"
	  .size .L_str, 4

samples.tested_code:
.arch	armv9.2-a+sve2		@ Use an SVE2 target so that “cnth” is accepted
	.text
	.global main
	.extern printf
	.type	main, %function
main:
	/* Prologue */
	stp		x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!
	mov		x29, sp

	/* Set up our scalar “global” registers:
	   w1  => best candidate (initially 0)
	   w8  => max score (initially 0)
	   w9  => candidate n (start at 1)
	   w10 => iteration counter (start at –1)
	   w11 => constant 2
	*/
	mov		w1, wzr		// best candidate = 0
	mov		w8, wzr		// max score = 0
	mov		w9, #1		// candidate n = 1
	mov		w0, #1
	sub		w10, wzr, w0	// w10 = –1
	mov		w11, #2		// constant 2

	/* Set up SVE predicates.
	   p0 is used for uaddv (all‐active for 32‐bit lanes).
	   p8 is used for a counter (we set it for half‐words).
	*/
	ptrue		p0.s
	ptrue		p8.h
		@ The “cnth” instruction (count half‐words) requires that the predicate
		@ operand be marked with “.h”
	cnth		w21, p8.h, #1

outer_loop:
	cmp		w9, #1001
	b.eq		exit_loop

	/* Update candidate counter */
	add		w10, w10, #1

	/* For candidate n < 4, the score remains 0. */
	cmp		w9, #4
	blt		candidate_small

	/* For candidate n ≥ 4:
	   Compute: w12 = n >> 1  (i.e. candidate n/2)
	   Compute: w14 = (w12 > 2 ? w12 : 2)
	*/
	lsr		w12, w9, #1
	cmp		w12, #2
	csel		w14, w12, w11, hi

	/* Initialize candidate’s “score” counter: w13 = 0. */
	mov		w13, wzr

	/* Inner‐outer loop variables:
	     m in w15 (starting at 1)
	     w16 = current candidate counter (w10)
	*/
	mov		w15, #1
	mov		w16, w10

inner_outer_loop:
	cmp		w15, w14
	b.ge		inner_outer_end

	/* Compute m*m (in w17) and save a copy of the current candidate counter (w18) */
	mul		w17, w15, w15
	mov		w18, w16
	/* Set up the inner‐inner loop: start i = m */
	mov		w0, w15
	/* Compute inner‐inner loop count: (w12 – m) in w7. */
	sub		w7, w12, w15
	cbz		w7, inner_outer_continue

	/***** Begin inner‐inner loop (vectorized) *****/
		@ For i = 0 to (w7 – 1) do:
		@   let (m+i) be computed vector‐wise

	whilelt	p1.s, wzr, w7          @ p1.s = lanes 0..(w7–1) active
	index		z2.s, wzr, #1           @ z2.s = [0, 1, 2, …]
	dup		z3.s, w15               @ z3.s = m broadcast
		@ Compute z4.s = (m + i)
	add		z4.s, p1/z, z3.s, z2.s   @ use /z so inactive lanes become 0

	/* Now compute the “left‐side” value:
	   left = (m + i)² + (m*m)
	*/
	mov		w22, #0
	dup		z5.s, w22               @ z5.s = 0
	dup		z6.s, w22               @ clear z6.s
		@ Multiply‐add: z6.s = z4.s * z4.s + z6.s  = (m + i)²
	mad		z6.s, p1/z, z4.s, z4.s
	dup		z7.s, w17               @ z7.s = m*m broadcast
	add		z8.s, p1/z, z6.s, z7.s   @ left = (m + i)² + (m*m)

	/* Now compute the “right‐side” value:
	   right = (w18 – i)²
	*/
	dup		z9.s, w18               @ z9.s = w18 broadcast
	sub		z9.s, p1/z, z9.s, z2.s   @ z9.s = (w18 – i)
	mov		w23, #0
	dup		z11.s, w23              @ clear z11.s
	mla		z11.s, p1/z, z9.s, z9.s   @ right = (w18 – i)²

	/* Compare the two vectors: if (m+i)² + m*m == (w18–i)² then 
	   mark that lane.
	*/
	cmpeq		p2.s, z8.s, z11.s
		@ Instead of writing “mov z13.s, z5.s” (which causes a “too few operands”
		@ error) simply copy the full vector register:
	mov		z13, z5

	dup		z12.s, #1              @ z12.s = 1 in every lane
		@ Using SEL to choose 1 for lanes where the compare was true and 0 otherwise:
	sel		z14.s, p2/z, z12.s, z5.s
		@ Horizontally add (zero‐extending to 64‐bit) the vector elements:
	uaddv	w4, p0, z14.s
		@ Add the result (the count of “hits”) to the candidate’s score.
	add		w13, w13, w4
	/***** End inner‐inner loop *****/

inner_outer_continue:
	/* Update inner‐outer loop variables. */
	add		w15, w15, #1		// m++
	sub		w16, w16, #2		// w16 = w16 – 2
	b		inner_outer_loop

inner_outer_end:
	/* Update best candidate and max score. */
	cmp		w13, w8
	csel		w8, w13, w8, hi
	csel		w1, w9, w1, hi

	/* Increment candidate n and loop. */
	add		w9, w9, #1
	b		outer_loop

candidate_small:
	/* For candidate n < 4 the score remains 0. */
	mov		w13, wzr
	cmp		w13, w8
	csel		w8, w13, w8, hi
	csel		w1, w9, w1, hi
	add		w9, w9, #1
	b		outer_loop

exit_loop:
	/* Prepare arguments for printf. */
	adrp	x0, .Lstr
	add		x0, x0, :lo12:.Lstr
	uxtw	x1, w1
	bl		printf

	/* Return 0; epilogue. */
	mov		w0, wzr
	ldp		x29, x30, [sp], #16
	ret

	.align	3
.Lstr:
	.asciz	"%u\n"
	.size	.Lstr, 4

chunks.cnth:
Set scalar to multiple of predicate constraint element count 
Determines the number of active elements implied by the named predicate constraint multiplies that by an immediate in 
the range 1 to 16 inclusive and then places the result in the scalar destination 
The named predicate constraint limits the number of active elements in a single predicate to 

• A fixed number VL 1 to VL 256 
• The largest power of two POW 2 
• The largest multiple of three or four MUL 3 or MUL 4 
• All available implicitly a multiple of two ALL 

Unspecified or out of range constraint encodings generate an empty predicate or zero element count rather than 
Undefined Instruction exception

samples.tested_code:
.global         main
        .p2align        2
        /* Tell the assembler we want SVE2 features */
        .arch_extension  sve2

main:
        /* Prologue */
        stp             x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!
        mov             x29, sp

        /* Initialize predicates.
           Use p0 (all–true) for most operations and p8 for the counter instructions. */
        ptrue           p0.b
        ptrue           p8.b

        /* Get count (of 32–bit lanes) in p0 – dummy use.
           (For cntw/cnth the predicate operand must be given without any “.b” suffix.) */
        cntw            w2, p8
        rdvl            x3, #1
        cnth            w4, p8

        /* Load the digit string. */
        adrp            x9, .L__const_main_str
        add             x9, x9, :lo12:.L__const_main_str

        /* Loop parameters:
           There are 996 valid 5–digit windows in a 1000–character string.
           x20 = running window index, x21 = 996 */
        mov             x20, xzr
        mov             x21, #996

        /* Compute our “chunk size” = (vector length in bytes minus 4). */
        sub             x23, x3, #4

        /* Initialize the global maximum product to 0. */
        mov             w5, wzr

LoopStart:
        cmp             x20, x21
        b.ge            LoopDone

        /* Compute how many windows remain in this chunk. */
        sub             x24, x21, x20        /* x24 = remaining windows = 996 – current index */
        cmp             x24, x23
        csel            x25, x24, x23, lt    /* x25 = chunk size to process = MIN(remaining, VL–4) */

        /* Compute pointer for the current block (base address + window offset). */
        add             x22, x9, x20

        /* For demonstration, produce an index vector.
           (INDEX requires its step to be an immediate in [–16,15]; so we create a ramp and then add x20.) */
        index           z10.s, #0, #1        /* z10 = {0, 1, 2, …} */
        dup             z11.s, w20           /* duplicate the window offset into every lane */
        add             z10.s, z10.s, z11.s   /* now z10 = {x20, x20+1, x20+2, …} */

        /* We must load (chunk size+4) contiguous bytes from the string.
           Compute x26 = x25 + 4. */
        add             x26, x25, #4

        /* Create a predicate for the load:
           whilels p1.b, xzr, x26 sets p1 true for byte indices less than (x25+4). */
        whilels         p1.b, xzr, x26

        /* Load (chunk size+4) bytes from [x22] into z0.
           (This establishes the “byte‐view” for z0.) */
        ld1b            {z0.b}, p1/z, [x22]

        /* Use ext to form five shifted vectors (each shifted by a different byte offset):
           z2 will hold the “first digit” for each window;
           z3 the second, z4 the third, etc.
           Note: copy z0 via register–to–register move (no “.b” suffix allowed here). */
        mov             z2, z0
        ext             z3.b, z0.b, z0.b, #1
        ext             z4.b, z0.b, z0.b, #2
        ext             z5.b, z0.b, z0.b, #3
        ext             z6.b, z0.b, z0.b, #4

        /* Convert ASCII digits to numeric values.
           Since the ASCII codes for '0'–'9' are 0x30–0x39, the low nybble equals the digit. */
        and             z2.b, z2.b, #0x0F
        and             z3.b, z3.b, #0x0F
        and             z4.b, z4.b, #0x0F
        and             z5.b, z5.b, #0x0F
        and             z6.b, z6.b, #0x0F

        /* Create a predicate for valid window lanes (interpreted as 32–bit elements).
           We form it in the .s view so that later reduction uses matching element sizes. */
        whilels         p2.s, xzr, x25

        /* Initialize a “product” vector in z7.s.
           (We load 1 into w10 then duplicate into every lane.) */
        mov             w10, #1
        dup             z7.s, w10

        /* Multiply each active lane by each digit.
           Here we re–interpret the bytes as 32–bit numbers. */
        mul             z7.s, z7.s, z2.s
        mul             z7.s, z7.s, z3.s
        mul             z7.s, z7.s, z4.s
        mul             z7.s, z7.s, z5.s
        mul             z7.s, z7.s, z6.s

        /* Reduce the current product vector (only in the active lanes given by p2) to find its maximum. */
        umaxv           w7, p2, z7.s

        /* Update the global maximum (in w5) if the current chunk’s max (w7) is higher. */
        cmp             w7, w5
        csel            w5, w7, w5, hi

        /* Extra SVE flavor: use lastb to extract the last active element of z7 (dummy use).
           (Here we use the .s view so that p2 matches the element size.) */
        lastb           w8, p2, z7.s

        /* Reverse the predicate p2 into p3 (dummy use).
           Note: we use the .s view here to match p2. */
        rev             p3.s, p2.s

        /* Splice z0 with itself (dummy use).
           We remove the “.b” suffix so that the destination and source registers use their default type. */
        splice          z0, z0, z0, p0

        /* Increment our window pointer by the number of windows processed in this chunk. */
        add             x20, x20, x25
        b               LoopStart

LoopDone:
        /* When finished, the global maximum is in w5.
           Prepare the printf call so that:
             – x0 = pointer to the format string,
             – w1 = maximum product (as an unsigned integer). */
        adrp            x0, .L_str
        add             x0, x0, :lo12:.L_str
        mov             w1, w5
        bl              printf

        /* Epilogue */
        mov             w0, wzr
        ldp             x29, x30, [sp], #16
        ret
        .size           main, .-main

        .section        .rodata
        .align          3
.L__const_main_str:
        .asciz         ""
        .size           .L__const_main_str, .-.L__const_main_str

        .align          3
.L_str:
        .asciz         "%u\n"
        .size           .L_str, .-.L_str

        .ident          "Ubuntu clang with AArch64+SVE"
        .section        .note.GNU-stack,"",@progbits

.global         main
          .p2align        2
          /* Tell the assembler we want SVE2 features */
          .arch_extension  sve2

  main:
          /* Prologue */
          stp             x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!
          mov             x29, sp

          /* Initialize predicates.
             For most vector operations we want p0 (all‐true) in a “typed” form
             but for the counter instructions (cntw/cnth) the predicate must be passed
             without any element–size suffix.  (Notice that p0 is defined with “.b” because
             it is later used with splice, while p8 is defined with no suffix.) */
          ptrue           p0.b
          ptrue           p8

          /* Get count (of 32–bit lanes) in p0 – dummy use.
             (For cntw/cnth the predicate operand must be given without any “.b” suffix.)
             Note: we add the immediate #1 because the encoding multiplies the count by an immediate
             in the range 1–16. */
          cntw            w2, p8, #1
          rdvl            x3, #1
          cnth            w4, p8, #1

          /* Load the digit string. */
          adrp            x9, .L__const_main_str
          add             x9, x9, :lo12:.L__const_main_str

          /* Loop parameters:
             There are 996 valid 5–digit windows in a 1000–character string.
             x20 = running window index, x21 = 996 */
          mov             x20, xzr
          mov             x21, #996

          /* Compute our “chunk size” = (vector length in bytes minus 4). */
          sub             x23, x3, #4

          /* Initialize the global maximum product to 0. */
          mov             w5, wzr

  LoopStart:
          cmp             x20, x21
          b.ge            LoopDone

          /* Compute how many windows remain in this chunk. */
          sub             x24, x21, x20        /* x24 = remaining windows = 996 – current index */
          cmp             x24, x23
          csel            x25, x24, x23, lt    /* x25 = chunk size to process = MIN(remaining, VL–4) */

          /* Compute pointer for the current block (base address + window offset). */
          add             x22, x9, x20

          /* For demonstration, produce an index vector.
             (INDEX requires its step to be an immediate in [–16,15]; so we create a ramp and then add x20.) */
          index           z10.s, #0, #1        /* z10 = {0, 1, 2, …} */
          dup             z11.s, w20           /* duplicate the window offset into every lane */
          add             z10.s, z10.s, z11.s   /* now z10 = {x20, x20+1, x20+2, …} */

          /* We must load (chunk size+4) contiguous bytes from the string.
             Compute x26 = x25 + 4. */
          add             x26, x25, #4

          /* Create a predicate for the load:
             whilels p1.b, xzr, x26 sets p1 true for byte indices less than (x25+4). */
          whilels         p1.b, xzr, x26

          /* Load (chunk size+4) bytes from [x22] into z0.
             (This establishes the “byte‐view” for z0.) */
          ld1b            {z0.b}, p1/z, [x22]

          /* Use ext to form five shifted vectors (each shifted by a different byte offset):
             – z2 will hold the “first digit” for each window;
             – z3 the second, z4 the third, etc.
             Note: We copy z0 using a register–to–register move.
             (In SVE you cannot simply write “mov z2, z0” so we use movprfx instead.) */
          movprfx         z2, z0
          ext             z3.b, z0.b, z0.b, #1
          ext             z4.b, z0.b, z0.b, #2
          ext             z5.b, z0.b, z0.b, #3
          ext             z6.b, z0.b, z0.b, #4

          /* Convert ASCII digits to numeric values.
             Since the ASCII codes for '0'–'9' are 0x30–0x39, the low nybble equals the digit. */
          and             z2.b, z2.b, #0x0F
          and             z3.b, z3.b, #0x0F
          and             z4.b, z4.b, #0x0F
          and             z5.b, z5.b, #0x0F
          and             z6.b, z6.b, #0x0F

          /* Create a predicate for valid window lanes (interpreted as 32–bit elements).
             We form it in the .s view so that later reduction uses matching element sizes. */
          whilels         p2.s, xzr, x25

          /* Initialize a “product” vector in z7.s.
             (We load 1 into w10 then duplicate it into every lane.) */
          mov             w10, #1
          dup             z7.s, w10

          /* Multiply each active lane by each digit.
             Here we re–interpret the bytes as 32–bit numbers. */
          mul             z7.s, z7.s, z2.s
          mul             z7.s, z7.s, z3.s
          mul             z7.s, z7.s, z4.s
          mul             z7.s, z7.s, z5.s
          mul             z7.s, z7.s, z6.s

          /* Reduce the current product vector (only in the active lanes given by p2)
             to find its maximum. */
          umaxv           w7, p2, z7.s

          /* Update the global maximum (in w5) if the current chunk’s max (w7) is higher. */
          cmp             w7, w5
          csel            w5, w7, w5, hi

          /* Extra SVE flavor: use lastb to extract the last active element of z7 (dummy use).
             (Here we use the .s view so that p2 matches the element size.) */
          lastb           w8, p2, z7.s

          /* Reverse the predicate p2 into p3 (dummy use).
             Note: we use the .s view here to match p2. */
          rev             p3.s, p2.s

          /* Splice z0 with itself (dummy use).
             For splice we now give the vector registers an explicit “.b” suffix so that the default
             type is known. */
          splice          z0.b, z0.b, z0.b, p0.b

          /* Increment our window pointer by the number of windows processed in this chunk. */
          add             x20, x20, x25
          b               LoopStart

  LoopDone:
          /* When finished, the global maximum is in w5.
             Prepare the printf call so that:
               – x0 = pointer to the format string,
               – w1 = maximum product (as an unsigned integer). */
          adrp            x0, .L_str
          add             x0, x0, :lo12:.L_str
          mov             w1, w5
          bl              printf

          /* Epilogue */
          mov             w0, wzr
          ldp             x29, x30, [sp], #16
          ret
          .size           main, .-main

          .section        .rodata
          .align          3
  .L__const_main_str:
          .asciz         ""
          .size           .L__const_main_str, .-.L__const_main_str

          .align          3
  .L_str:
          .asciz         "%u\n"
          .size           .L_str, .-.L_str

          .ident          "Ubuntu clang with AArch64+SVE"
          .section        .note.GNU-stack,"",@progbits

samples.tested_code:
.global main
.p2align 2
.arch_extension sve2

main:
    /* Prologue */
    stp     x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!
    mov     x29, sp

    /* Initialize predicates.
       For most vector operations we want p0 (all‐true) in a “typed” form
       but for the counter instructions (cntw/cnth) the predicate must be passed
       without any element–size suffix. */
    ptrue   p0.b
    ptrue   p8

    /* Get count (of 32–bit lanes) in p0 – dummy use.
       (For cntw/cnth the predicate operand must be given without any “.b” suffix.)
       Note: we add the immediate #1 because the encoding multiplies the count by an immediate in the range 1–16. */
    cntw    w2, p8, #1
    rdvl    x3, #1
    cnth    w4, p8, #1

    /* Load the digit string. */
    adrp    x9, .L__const_main_str
    add     x9, x9, :lo12:.L__const_main_str

    /* Loop parameters:
       There are 996 valid 5–digit windows in a 1000–character string.
       x20 = running window index, x21 = 996 */
    mov     x20, xzr
    mov     x21, #996

    /* Compute our “chunk size” = (vector length in bytes minus 4). */
    sub     x23, x3, #4

    /* Initialize the global maximum product to 0. */
    mov     w5, wzr

LoopStart:
    cmp     x20, x21
    b.ge    LoopDone

    /* Compute how many windows remain in this chunk. */
    sub     x24, x21, x20        /* x24 = remaining windows = 996 – current index */
    cmp     x24, x23
    csel    x25, x24, x23, lt    /* x25 = chunk size to process = MIN(remaining, VL–4) */

    /* Compute pointer for the current block (base address + window offset). */
    add     x22, x9, x20

    /* For demonstration, produce an index vector.
       (INDEX requires its step to be an immediate in [–16,15]; so we create a ramp and then add x20.) */
    index   z10.s, #0, #1        /* z10 = {0, 1, 2, …} */
    dup     z11.s, w20           /* duplicate the window offset into every lane */
    add     z10.s, z10.s, z11.s   /* now z10 = {x20, x20+1, x20+2, …} */

    /* We must load (chunk size+4) contiguous bytes from the string.
       Compute x26 = x25 + 4. */
    add     x26, x25, #4

    /* Create a predicate for the load:
       whilels p1.b, xzr, x26 sets p1 true for byte indices less than (x25+4). */
    whilels p1.b, xzr, x26

    /* Load (chunk size+4) bytes from [x22] into z0.
       (This establishes the “byte–view” for z0.) */
    ld1b    {z0.b}, p1/z, [x22]

    /* Use ext to form five shifted vectors (each shifted by a different byte offset):
       – z2 will hold the “first digit” for each window;
       – z3 the second, z4 the third, etc.
       (In SVE you cannot simply write “mov z2, z0” so we use movprfx instead.) */
    movprfx z2, z0
    ext     z3.b, z0.b, z0.b, #1
    ext     z4.b, z0.b, z0.b, #2
    ext     z5.b, z0.b, z0.b, #3
    ext     z6.b, z0.b, z0.b, #4

    /* Convert ASCII digits to numeric values.
       Since the ASCII codes for '0'–'9' are 0x30–0x39, the low nybble equals the digit. */
    and     z2.b, z2.b, #0x0F
    and     z3.b, z3.b, #0x0F
    and     z4.b, z4.b, #0x0F
    and     z5.b, z5.b, #0x0F
    and     z6.b, z6.b, #0x0F

    /* Create a predicate for valid window lanes (interpreted as 32–bit elements). */
    whilels p2.s, xzr, x25

    /* Initialize a “product” vector in z7.s.
       (We load 1 into w10 then duplicate it into every lane.) */
    mov     w10, #1
    dup     z7.s, w10

    /* Multiply each active lane by each digit. */
    mul     z7.s, z7.s, z2.s
    mul     z7.s, z7.s, z3.s
    mul     z7.s, z7.s, z4.s
    mul     z7.s, z7.s, z5.s
    mul     z7.s, z7.s, z6.s

    /* Reduce the current product vector (only in the active lanes given by p2)
       to find its maximum. */
    umaxv  w7, p2, z7.s

    /* Update the global maximum (in w5) if the current chunk’s max (w7) is higher. */
    cmp     w7, w5
    csel    w5, w7, w5, hi

    /* Extra SVE flavor: use lastb to extract the last active element of z7 (dummy use). */
    lastb   w8, p2, z7.s

    /* Reverse the predicate p2 into p3 (dummy use). */
    rev     p3.s, p2.s

    /* Splice z0 with itself (dummy use). */
    splice  z0.b, z0.b, z0.b, p0.b

    /* Increment our window pointer by the number of windows processed in this chunk. */
    add     x20, x20, x25
    b       LoopStart

LoopDone:
    /* When finished, the global maximum is in w5.
       Prepare the printf call so that:
         – x0 = pointer to the format string,
         – w1 = maximum product (as an unsigned integer). */
    adrp    x0, .L_str
    add     x0, x0, :lo12:.L_str
    mov     w1, w5
    bl      printf

    /* Epilogue */
    mov     w0, wzr
    ldp     x29, x30, [sp], #16
    ret
    .size   main, .-main

    .section .rodata
    .align   3
.L__const_main_str:
    .asciz ""
    .size   .L__const_main_str, .-.L__const_main_str

    .align   3
.L_str:
    .asciz "%u\n"
    .size   .L_str, .-.L_str

    .ident  "Ubuntu clang with AArch64+SVE"
    .section .note.GNU-stack,"",@progbits

samples.tested_code:
.text
.global main
.p2align 2
main:
    // Standard prologue.
    stp x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!
    mov x29, sp

    // Initialize global maximum product (w9) to zero.
    mov w9, wzr

    // Set pointer (x3) to the digits string constant.
    adrp x3, .L__const_main_str
    add x3, x3, :lo12:.L__const_main_str

    // The number of 5–digit windows in the 1000–digit string is 996.
    mov x4, #996

    // Use RDVL to get the current scalable vector “block” size in bytes.
    rdvl x2, #1         // x2 = VL (in bytes); minimum VL is 16.
    // For a window length of 5, a “full block” contains (VL – 4) valid windows.
    sub x5, x2, #4      // x5 = full block window–count (for VL=16, x5=12).

    // Set up a full–predicate for bytes.
    ptrue p0.b

    // Demonstrate CNTW (count 32–bit lanes active) and CNTH (for halfwords).
    cntw x6           // x6 gets the number of 32–bit lanes.
    cnth x7           // x7 gets the number of 16–bit lanes.
    // Dummy use of AND (immediate) to mask x7.
    and x7, x7, #0xff

    // Initialize tail flag (x11) to 0 to indicate no tail exists for the first iteration.
    mov x11, xzr

loop_block:
    // If no more windows remain, exit.
    cmp x4, #0
    beq end_loop

    // Determine the number of windows in this iteration: x8 = min(x5, x4).
    cmp x4, x5
    csel x8, x5, x4, hi

    // (For the first iteration there is no available tail.)
    // If tail flag is already set then do a “spliced load” from memory.
    cmp x11, xzr
    bne load_subseq

    // --- First iteration: load a block of (x8 + 4) bytes.
    add x9, x8, #4      // x9 = block byte–count.
    whilels p1.b, xzr, x9
    ld1b { z0.b }, p1/z, [x3]   // load (x8+4) bytes
    b process_block

load_subseq:
    // --- Subsequent iterations: we already have a tail of 4 bytes.
    // Load only x8 new bytes.
    add x9, x8, #0      // x9 = number of new bytes.
    whilels p1.b, xzr, x9
    ld1b { z8.b }, p1/z, [x3]   // load new bytes
    // Use splice to combine the previous tail (in z7) with new bytes.
    mov x13, #4         // load immediate 4 into x13
    whilels p3.b, xzr, x13
    splice z0.b, z7.b, z8.b, p3   // note: the predicate operand is now just “p3”
    // Now z0 holds the spliced block.
    
process_block:
    // Convert ASCII digits to numerical ones and preserve the block for tail extraction.
    sub z0.b, z0.b, #48
    mov z15.b, z0.b     // save a copy in z15 for tail extraction

    // Use EXT to generate the five “shifted‐by–one” vectors.
    ext z1.b, z0.b, z0.b, #1
    ext z2.b, z0.b, z0.b, #2
    ext z3.b, z0.b, z0.b, #3
    ext z4.b, z0.b, z0.b, #4

    // Widen (zero–extend) each byte to 32–bit.
    uxtl z0.h, z0.b
    uxtl z0.s, z0.h
    uxtl z1.h, z1.b
    uxtl z1.s, z1.h
    uxtl z2.h, z2.b
    uxtl z2.s, z2.h
    uxtl z3.h, z3.b
    uxtl z3.s, z3.h
    uxtl z4.h, z4.b
    uxtl z4.s, z4.h

    // Initialize a “product” vector to ones.
    fmov z10.s, p0/m, #1.0
    fcvtzs z5.s, p0/m, z10.s

    // Compute element–wise product = d[i]*d[i+1]*d[i+2]*d[i+3]*d[i+4].
    mul z5.s, z0.s, z1.s
    mul z5.s, z5.s, z2.s
    mul z5.s, z5.s, z3.s
    mul z5.s, z5.s, z4.s

    // (LSR by immediate 0 is not allowed so we omit that demonstration.)

    // Generate a predicate for the “valid” lanes (only the first x8 lanes are valid).
    whilels p2.s, xzr, x8

    // Demonstrate INDEX: build an (unused) index vector.
    index z8.s, p0, #0, #1

    // Demonstrate REV: reverse the order of p0 (storing in p4).
    rev p4.b, p0.b

    // Reduce the vector product (only on active lanes) to get the maximum.
    umaxv w11, p2, z5.s

    // Demonstrate LASTB: extract the last active element from z5.
    lastb w12, p2, z5.s

    // Demonstrate a scalar maximum (since the immediate form of UMAX isn’t accepted)
    smax w11, w11, wzr
    smax w9, w9, w11

    // Prepare the tail for the next iteration.
    cmp x8, x5
    bne no_tail
    ext z7.b, z15.b, z15.b, #12   // extract the last 4 bytes from the saved copy
no_tail:
    add x3, x3, x8        // advance the pointer (the tail remains in z7)
    sub x4, x4, x8        // decrement the remaining window count

    // Set the tail–flag: if a full block was processed (x8 equals x5) then next iteration uses splice.
    mov x12, #1
    csel x11, xzr, x12, eq

    b loop_block

end_loop:
    // Print the overall maximum product.
    adrp x0, .L_str
    add x0, x0, :lo12:.L_str
    mov w1, w9
    bl printf

    // Return 0.
    mov w0, wzr
    ldp x29, x30, [sp], #16
    ret

samples.tested_code:
.arch armv8.2-a+sve2
    .text
    .global main
    .p2align 2
main:
    // Standard prologue.
    stp     x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!
    mov     x29, sp

    // Initialize global maximum product (w9) to zero.
    mov     w9, wzr

    // Set pointer (x3) to the digits string constant.
    adrp    x3, .L__const_main_str
    add     x3, x3, :lo12:.L__const_main_str

    // The number of 5–digit windows in the 1000–digit string is 996.
    mov     x4, #996

    // Use RDVL to get the current scalable vector “block” size in bytes.
    rdvl    x2, #1         // x2 = VL (in bytes); minimum VL is 16.
    // For a window length of 5, a “full block” contains (VL – 4) valid windows.
    sub     x5, x2, #4      // x5 = full block window–count (for VL=16, x5=12).

    // Set up a full–predicate for bytes.
    ptrue   p0.b

    // Demonstrate CNTW (count 32–bit lanes active) and CNTH (for halfwords).
    cntw    x6              // x6 gets the number of 32–bit lanes.
    cnth    x7              // x7 gets the number of 16–bit lanes.
    and     x7, x7, #0xff

    // Initialize tail flag (x11) to 0 to indicate no tail exists for the first iteration.
    mov     x11, xzr

loop_block:
    // If no more windows remain, exit.
    cmp     x4, #0
    beq     end_loop

    // Determine the number of windows in this iteration: x8 = min(x5, x4).
    cmp     x4, x5
    csel    x8, x5, x4, hi

    // (For the first iteration there is no available tail.)
    // If tail flag is already set then do a “spliced load” from memory.
    cmp     x11, xzr
    bne     load_subseq

    // --- First iteration: load a block of (x8 + 4) bytes.
    add     x9, x8, #4         // x9 = block byte–count.
    whilels p1.b, xzr, x9
    ld1b    { z0.b }, p1/z, [x3]   // load (x8+4) bytes
    b       process_block

load_subseq:
    // --- Subsequent iterations: we already have a tail of 4 bytes.
    mov     x9, x8
    whilels p1.b, xzr, x9
    ld1b    { z8.b }, p1/z, [x3]   // load new bytes
    // Use splice to combine the previous tail (in z7) with new bytes.
    mov     x13, #4         // load immediate 4 into x13
    whilels p3.b, xzr, x13
    splice  z0.b, z7.b, z8.b, p3.b     // splice: combine tail and new bytes
    // Now z0 holds the spliced block.
    
process_block:
    // Convert ASCII digits to numerical ones and preserve the block for tail extraction.
    sub     z0.b, z0.b, #48
    mov     z15, z0             // save a copy in z15 for tail extraction

    // Use EXT to generate the five “shifted‐by–one” vectors.
    ext     z1.b, z0.b, z0.b, #1
    ext     z2.b, z0.b, z0.b, #2
    ext     z3.b, z0.b, z0.b, #3
    ext     z4.b, z0.b, z0.b, #4

    // Widen (zero–extend) each byte to 32–bit.
    // For z0:
    mov     z16, z0
    uxtl    z16.h, z16.b
    uxtl    z0.s,  z16.h
    // For z1:
    mov     z17, z1
    uxtl    z17.h, z17.b
    uxtl    z1.s,  z17.h
    // For z2:
    mov     z18, z2
    uxtl    z18.h, z18.b
    uxtl    z2.s,  z18.h
    // For z3:
    mov     z19, z3
    uxtl    z19.h, z19.b
    uxtl    z3.s,  z19.h
    // For z4:
    mov     z20, z4
    uxtl    z20.h, z20.b
    uxtl    z4.s,  z20.h

    // Initialize a “product” vector to ones.
    fmov    z10.s, p0/m, #1.0
    fcvtzs  z5.s,  p0/m, z10.s

    // Compute element–wise product = d[i]*d[i+1]*d[i+2]*d[i+3]*d[i+4].
    mul     z5.s, z0.s, z1.s
    mul     z5.s, z5.s, z2.s
    mul     z5.s, z5.s, z3.s
    mul     z5.s, z5.s, z4.s

    // (LSR by immediate 0 is not allowed so we omit that demonstration.)

    // Generate a predicate for the “valid” lanes (only the first x8 lanes are valid).
    whilels p2.s, xzr, x8

    // Demonstrate INDEX: build an (unused) index vector.
    index   z8.s, p0, #0, #1

    // Demonstrate REV: reverse the order of p0 (storing in p4).
    rev     p4.b, p0.b

    // Reduce the vector product (only on active lanes) to get the maximum.
    umaxv   w11, p2, z5.s

    // Demonstrate LASTB: extract the last active element from z5.
    lastb   w12, p2, z5.s

    // Demonstrate a scalar maximum (using CMP/CSEL instead of SMAX):
    cmp     w11, wzr
    csel    w11, w11, wzr, ge
    cmp     w9, w11
    csel    w9, w9, w11, ge

    // Prepare the tail for the next iteration.
    cmp     x8, x5
    bne     no_tail
    ext     z7.b, z15.b, z15.b, #12   // extract the last 4 bytes from the saved copy
no_tail:
    add     x3, x3, x8        // advance the pointer (the tail remains in z7)
    sub     x4, x4, x8        // decrement the remaining window count

    // Set the tail–flag: if a full block was processed (x8 == x5) then next iteration uses splice.
    mov     x12, #1
    csel    x11, xzr, x12, eq

    b       loop_block

end_loop:
    // Print the overall maximum product.
    adrp    x0, .L_str
    add     x0, x0, :lo12:.L_str
    mov     w1, w9
    bl      printf

    // Return 0.
    mov     w0, wzr
    ldp     x29, x30, [sp], #16
    ret

    .asciz "%u\n"

    .asciz ""
    .ident "AArch64 SVE translated code"

samples.tested_code:
// Use the SVE2 architecture.
    .arch armv8.2-a+sve2
    .text
    .global main
    .p2align 2
main:
    // Standard prologue.
    stp     x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!
    mov     x29, sp

    // Initialize global maximum product (w9) to zero.
    mov     w9, wzr

    // Set pointer (x3) to the digits string constant.
    adrp    x3, .L__const_main_str
    add     x3, x3, :lo12:.L__const_main_str

    // The number of 5–digit windows in the 1000–digit string is 996.
    mov     x4, #996

    // Use RDVL to get the current scalable vector “block” size in bytes.
    rdvl    x2, #1         // x2 = VL (in bytes); minimum VL is 16.
    // For a window length of 5, a “full block” contains (VL – 4) valid windows.
    sub     x5, x2, #4      // x5 = full block window–count.

    // Set up a full–predicate (all lanes active) for bytes.
    ptrue   p0.b

    // Demonstrate CNTW (count of 32–bit lanes) and CNTH (for halfwords).
    cntw    x6              // Number of 32–bit lanes.
    cnth    x7              // Number of 16–bit lanes.
    and     x7, x7, #0xff

    // Initialize tail flag (x11) to 0 (no tail for the first iteration).
    mov     x11, xzr

loop_block:
    // Exit if no more windows remain.
    cmp     x4, #0
    beq     end_loop

    // Determine the number of windows in this iteration: x8 = min(x5, x4).
    cmp     x4, x5
    csel    x8, x5, x4, hi

    // If a previous tail exists, do a “spliced load”.
    cmp     x11, xzr
    bne     load_subseq

    // --- First iteration: load a block of (x8+4) bytes.
    add     x9, x8, #4           // x9 = block byte–count.
    whilels p1.b, xzr, x9
    ld1b    { z0.b }, p1/z, [x3]  // load (x8+4) bytes
    b       process_block

load_subseq:
    // --- Subsequent iterations: a tail of 4 bytes is already available.
    mov     x9, x8
    whilels p1.b, xzr, x9
    ld1b    { z8.b }, p1/z, [x3]  // load new bytes
    mov     x13, #4              // tail length is 4 bytes.
    whilels p3.b, xzr, x13
    // Note: “splice” takes three vector registers and a predicate. Here we make sure to add the “.b”
    // to the predicate operand and that z0 (the destination) is used destructively.
    splice  z0.b, z7.b, z8.b, p3.b  // splice: combine previous tail and new bytes

process_block:
    // Convert ASCII digits to numbers and save a copy for tail extraction.
    sub     z0.b, z0.b, #48
    movprfx z15, z0          // save a copy of z0 in z15

    // Use EXT to make the “shifted–by–one” vectors.
    // (EXT is destructive so the destination must equal its first source.)
    movprfx z1, z0
    ext     z1.b, z1.b, z0.b, #1
    movprfx z2, z0
    ext     z2.b, z2.b, z0.b, #2
    movprfx z3, z0
    ext     z3.b, z3.b, z0.b, #3
    movprfx z4, z0
    ext     z4.b, z4.b, z0.b, #4

    // Widen (zero–extend) each byte to 32–bit.
    // For z0:
    movprfx z16, z0
    uxtl    z16.h, z16.b
    uxtl    z0.s,  z16.h
    // For z1:
    movprfx z17, z1
    uxtl    z17.h, z1.b
    uxtl    z1.s,  z17.h
    // For z2:
    movprfx z18, z2
    uxtl    z18.h, z2.b
    uxtl    z2.s,  z18.h
    // For z3:
    movprfx z19, z3
    uxtl    z19.h, z3.b
    uxtl    z3.s,  z19.h
    // For z4:
    movprfx z20, z4
    uxtl    z20.h, z4.b
    uxtl    z4.s,  z20.h

    // Initialize a “product” vector to ones.
    fmov    z10.s, p0/m, #1.0
    fcvtzs  z5.s,  p0/m, z10.s

    // Compute element–wise product = d[i]*d[i+1]*d[i+2]*d[i+3]*d[i+4].
    mul     z5.s, z0.s, z1.s
    mul     z5.s, z5.s, z2.s
    mul     z5.s, z5.s, z3.s
    mul     z5.s, z5.s, z4.s

    // Generate a predicate for the first x8 (valid) lanes.
    whilels p2.s, xzr, x8

    // Demonstrate INDEX (build an unused index vector).
    // (Some assemblers want the immediates as bare numbers.)
    index   z8.s, p0, 0, 1

    // Demonstrate REV (reverse the order of the predicate).
    rev     p4.b, p0.b

    // Reduce the vector product (over the active lanes) to get the maximum.
    umaxv   w11, p2, z5.s

    // Demonstrate LASTB: extract the last active element.
    lastb   w12, p2, z5.s

    // Compare and update the scalar maximum.
    cmp     w11, wzr
    csel    w11, w11, wzr, ge
    cmp     w9, w11
    csel    w9, w9, w11, ge

    // Prepare the tail for the next iteration.
    cmp     x8, x5
    bne     no_tail
    // (EXT in SVE is destructive – the destination must equal the first source.)
    movprfx z7, z15
    ext     z7.b, z7.b, z15.b, #12
no_tail:
    add     x3, x3, x8        // advance the pointer (the tail remains in z7)
    sub     x4, x4, x8        // decrement the remaining window count

    // Set the tail–flag: if a full block was processed (x8 == x5), then next iteration uses splice.
    mov     x12, #1
    csel    x11, xzr, x12, eq

    b       loop_block

end_loop:
    // Print the overall maximum product.
    adrp    x0, .L_str
    add     x0, x0, :lo12:.L_str
    mov     w1, w9
    bl      printf

    // Return 0.
    mov     w0, wzr
    ldp     x29, x30, [sp], #16
    ret

    // --- Data sections.
    .section .rodata
.L_str:
    .asciz "%u\n"

    .section .rodata.str1.1,"aMS",@progbits,1
.L__const_main_str:
    .asciz ""
    .ident "AArch64 SVE translated code"

samples.tested_code:
// Use the SVE2 architecture.
    .arch armv8.2-a+sve2
    .text
    .global main
    .p2align 2
main:
    // Standard prologue.
    stp     x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!
    mov     x29, sp

    // Initialize the global maximum product (w9) to zero.
    mov     w9, wzr

    // Set pointer (x3) to the digits string constant.
    adrp    x3, .L__const_main_str
    add     x3, x3, :lo12:.L__const_main_str

    // There are 996 5–digit windows.
    mov     x4, #996

    // Use RDVL to get the VL (in bytes; minimum VL is 16).
    rdvl    x2, #1
    // A full block contains (VL – 4) valid windows.
    sub     x5, x2, #4

    // Set up an all–true predicate for bytes.
    ptrue   p0.b

    // Demonstrate CNTW (count of 32–bit lanes) and CNTH (for halfwords).
    cntw    x6
    cnth    x7
    and     x7, x7, #0xff

    // Initialize the tail flag (x11) to 0 (no tail on first iteration).
    mov     x11, xzr

loop_block:
    // Exit if no more windows remain.
    cmp     x4, #0
    beq     end_loop

    // x8 = min(x5, x4): number of windows this iteration.
    cmp     x4, x5
    csel    x8, x5, x4, hi

    // If a previous tail exists, do a "spliced load".
    cmp     x11, xzr
    bne     load_subseq

    // --- First iteration: load a block of (x8+4) bytes.
    add     x9, x8, #4       // x9 = block byte–count.
    whilels p1.b, xzr, x9
    ld1b    { z0.b }, p1/z, [x3]   // load (x8+4) bytes
    b       process_block

load_subseq:
    // --- Subsequent iterations: a 4–byte tail is available.
    mov     x9, x8
    whilels p1.b, xzr, x9
    ld1b    { z8.b }, p1/z, [x3]   // load new bytes
    mov     x13, #4              // tail length is 4 bytes.
    whilels p3.b, xzr, x13
    // Here we “splice” the previous tail (in z7) with the new z8.
    splice  z0.b, z7.b, z8.b, p3

process_block:
    // Convert ASCII to digit (subtract 48) and save a copy for tail extraction.
    sub     z0.b, z0.b, #48
    mov     z15, z0           // Save copy of z0

    // Create shifted–by–1..4 vectors using EXT.
    mov     z1, z0
    ext     z1.b, z1.b, z0.b, #1
    mov     z2, z0
    ext     z2.b, z2.b, z0.b, #2
    mov     z3, z0
    ext     z3.b, z3.b, z0.b, #3
    mov     z4, z0
    ext     z4.b, z4.b, z0.b, #4

    // Widen (zero–extend) each byte to 32–bit.
    // For z0:
    mov     z16, z0
    uxtlb   z16.h, z16.b      // widen bytes -> halfwords
    uxtlh   z0.s,  z16.h      // widen halfwords -> words
    // For z1:
    mov     z17, z1
    uxtlb   z17.h, z1.b
    uxtlh   z1.s,  z17.h
    // For z2:
    mov     z18, z2
    uxtlb   z18.h, z2.b
    uxtlh   z2.s,  z18.h
    // For z3:
    mov     z19, z3
    uxtlb   z19.h, z3.b
    uxtlh   z3.s,  z19.h
    // For z4:
    mov     z20, z4
    uxtlb   z20.h, z4.b
    uxtlh   z4.s,  z20.h

    // Initialize a “product” vector to 1.
    fmov    z10.s, p0/m, #1.0
    fcvtzs  z5.s, p0/m, z10.s

    // Compute element-wise product = d[i]*d[i+1]*d[i+2]*d[i+3]*d[i+4].
    mul     z5.s, z0.s, z1.s
    mul     z5.s, z5.s, z2.s
    mul     z5.s, z5.s, z3.s
    mul     z5.s, z5.s, z4.s

    // Generate predicate for the first x8 (valid) lanes.
    whilels p2.s, xzr, x8

    // Demonstrate INDEX (note the immediates must be preceded by #).
    index   z8.s, p0, #0, #1

    // Demonstrate REV (reverse the order of p0.b into p4.b).
    rev     p4.b, p0.b

    // Reduce the vector (over the active lanes) to get the maximum.
    umaxv  s11, p2, z5.s
    fmov    w11, s11

    // Demonstrate LASTB: extract the last active element.
    lastb   w12, p2, z5.s

    // Compare and update the maximum.
    cmp     w11, wzr
    csel    w11, w11, wzr, ge
    cmp     w9, w11
    csel    w9, w9, w11, ge

    // Prepare the tail for the next iteration.
    cmp     x8, x5
    bne     no_tail
    // Save the final 4 bytes (tail) in z7.
    mov     z7, z15
    ext     z7.b, z7.b, z15.b, #12
no_tail:
    add     x3, x3, x8    // advance pointer (tail remains in z7)
    sub     x4, x4, x8    // decrement the remaining window count

    // Set the tail flag: if a full block was processed then next iteration does splice.
    mov     x12, #1
    csel    x11, xzr, x12, eq

    b       loop_block

end_loop:
    // Print the overall maximum product.
    adrp    x0, .L_str
    add     x0, x0, :lo12:.L_str
    mov     w1, w9
    bl      printf

    // Return 0.
    mov     w0, wzr
    ldp     x29, x30, [sp], #16
    ret

// --- Data sections.
    .section .rodata
.L_str:
    .asciz "%u\n"

    .section .rodata.str1.1,"aMS",@progbits,1
.L__const_main_str:
    .asciz ""
    .ident "AArch64 SVE translated code"

.text
    .global main
    .type main, %function
main:
    // Standard prologue: save frame pointer and link register.
    stp     x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!
    mov     x29, sp

    // Allocate 8000 bytes on the stack for 1000 8‐byte elements.
    // (8000 is too large for a SP immediate so we load it into x16.)
    mov     x16, #8000
    sub     sp, sp, x16

    // Set up base pointer for our array in x9.
    mov     x9, sp

    // Initialize our loop index (x13) and a scalar accumulator (x14).
    mov     x13, #0         // x13 will index the array in units of 8 bytes.
    mov     x14, #0         // x14 accumulates reduction sums.

    // Set the threshold in x10 to 1,000,000.
    mov     w10, #16960
    movk    w10, #15, lsl #16   // w10 = (15<<16) | 16960 = 1000000

    // --- SVE Setup ---
    ptrue   p0.d            // Create a predicate with all lanes active (doubleword view)
    rdvl    x11, #1         // Get the current vector register length (in bytes)
    cntw    x12, p0         // Count the number of active (double‐word) lanes

    // --- Main SVE Loop: Process array in vector chunks ---
.Loop:
    cmp     x13, #1000      // Have we processed all 1000 elements?
    b.ge    .AfterLoop

    // Load a vector chunk from our array (using the /z form to zero inactive lanes).
    ld1d   {z0.d}, p0/z, [x9, x13, LSL #3]

    // Compute a horizontal sum reduction of the loaded chunk.
    uaddv  d1, p0, z0.d     // d1 = sum of all active 64‐bit elements in z0

    // Move the scalar result from the SIMD FP register d1 to a general register x15.
    fmov   x15, d1         
    
    // Accumulate the per–chunk sum into our overall accumulator (x14).
    add    x14, x14, x15

    // --- Additional SVE operations for demonstration ---
    neg    z0.d, p0/m, z0.d           // Negate the vector elements (merge form)
    and    z0.d, z0.d, #0x00000000000000FF   // Bit–wise AND with immediate 0xFF
    rev    p1.d, p0.d       // Reverse the active predicate lanes
    fmov   z1.d, p0/M, #1.0 // Move the FP immediate 1.0 into each active element of z1

    // Advance the index by the count of elements processed.
    add    x13, x13, x12
    b      .Loop

.AfterLoop:
    // Compare the accumulated sum with the threshold.
    cmp    x14, x10
    b.lt   .Exit

    // If the sum is >= threshold, call printf to print it.
    adrp   x0, .Lstr
    add    x0, x0, :lo12:.Lstr
    mov    x1, x14
    bl     printf

.Exit:
    // Clean up: deallocate the 8000 bytes we allocated.
    mov    x16, #8000
    add    sp, sp, x16

    // Restore saved frame pointer and link register and return.
    ldp    x29, x30, [sp], #16
    mov    w0, wzr
    ret
    .size main, .-main

    .section .rodata
.Lstr:
    .asciz "%i\n"

.type main, %function
main:
    // Standard prologue: save frame pointer and link register.
    stp     x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!
    mov     x29, sp

    // Allocate 8000 bytes on the stack for 1000 8‐byte elements.
    mov     x16, #8000
    sub     sp, sp, x16

    // Set up base pointer for our array in x9.
    mov     x9, sp

    // Initialize our loop index (x13) and scalar accumulator (x14).
    mov     x13, #0         // x13 will index the array in 8‐byte units.
    mov     x14, #0         // x14 accumulates reduction sums.

    // Set the threshold in x10 to 1,000,000.
    mov     w10, #16960
    movk    w10, #15, lsl #16   // w10 = (15<<16)|16960 = 1000000

    // --- SVE Setup ---
    ptrue   p0.d            // Create a predicate with all lanes active (double‐word view)
    rdvl    x11, #1         // Get the current vector register length in bytes
    cntd    x12, p0         // Count the number of active double‐word lanes

.Loop:
    cmp     x13, #1000      // Have we processed all 1000 elements?
    b.ge    .AfterLoop

    // Load a vector chunk from our array (zeros out inactive lanes).
    ld1d   {z0.d}, p0/z, [x9, x13, LSL #3]

    // Compute a horizontal sum reduction of the loaded chunk.
    uaddv  d1, p0, z0.d     // d1 = sum of all active 64‐bit elements in z0

    // Move the scalar result from the SIMD FP register d1 to x15.
    fmov   x15, d1         

    // Accumulate the per–chunk sum into our overall accumulator (x14).
    add    x14, x14, x15

    // --- Additional SVE operations for demonstration ---
    neg    z0.d, p0/m, z0.d           // Negate the vector elements (merge form)
    and    z0.d, z0.d, #0x00000000000000FF   // Bit–wise AND with immediate 0xFF
    rev    p1.d, p0.d       // Reverse the active predicate lanes
    fmov   z1.d, p0/M, #1.0 // Move the FP immediate 1.0 into each active element of z1

    // Advance the index by the number of vector elements processed.
    add    x13, x13, x12
    b      .Loop

.AfterLoop:
    // Compare the accumulated sum with the threshold.
    cmp    x14, x10
    b.lt   .Exit

    // If the sum is >= threshold, call printf to print it.
    adrp   x0, .Lstr
    add    x0, x0, :lo12:.Lstr
    mov    x1, x14
    bl     printf

.Exit:
    // Clean up: deallocate the 8000 bytes we allocated.
    mov    x16, #8000
    add    sp, sp, x16

    // Restore saved frame pointer and link register and return.
    ldp    x29, x30, [sp], #16
    mov    w0, wzr
    ret
    .size main, .-main

.arch armv8.2-a+sve
    .text
    .global main
    .p2align 2
main:
    @ Prologue and set up our all‐active predicate.
    ptrue   p0.s

    @ Build constant C = (52428 << 16)|52429 in z0.s:
    mov     w20, #52429
    movk    w20, #52428, lsl #16
    dup     z0.s, w20           @ z0.s = constant

    @ Set loop counter (w10 = 11) in z1.s:
    mov     w20, #11
    dup     z1.s, w20           @ z1.s = 11

    @ Constant 10 goes into z2.s:
    mov     w20, #10
    dup     z2.s, w20           @ z2.s = 10

    @ Initialize accumulators: w8 in z5.s and w9 in z6.s to 1.
    mov     w20, #1
    dup     z5.s, w20           @ z5.s = 1   (w8)
    mov     w20, #1
    dup     z6.s, w20           @ z6.s = 1   (w9)

    @ Jump into the outer loop.
    b       LBB0_2

LBB0_1:
    @ Outer loop "increment" block:
    add     z1.s, z1.s, #1       @ w10 = w10 + 1 (vector add; all lanes identical)
    umov    w20, z1.s[0]         @ extract lane0 of z1.s into w20
    cmp     w20, #100
    b.eq   LBB0_19              @ if (w10 == 100) jump to LBB0_19
    b       LBB0_2

LBB0_2:
    @ Outer loop header:
    @ Compute umull: (w10 * constant) in 64‐bit then shift right 35 bits.
    umull   z7.d, p0, z1.s, z0.s    @ 64‐bit result in z7.d in every lane
    lsr     z7.d, p0, z7.d, #35      @ logical shift right by 35
    uqxtn   z7.s, z7.d              @ narrow result to 32‐bit (now in z7.s)
    @ Compute msub: w14 = w10 – ((w10 * constant >>35) * 10)
    msub    z4.s, p0, z7.s, z2.s, z1.s   @ z4.s = z1.s – (z7.s * z2.s)
    umov    w20, z4.s[0]           @ extract lane0 from z4.s into w20
    cmp     w20, #0
    @ If w14 ≠ 0 then conditionally compare w10 and 12.
    umov    w21, z1.s[0]          @ extract lane0 from z1.s into w21
    cmp     w21, #12
    b.lo    LBB0_1

    @ Now start the inner "prime‐test" loops.
    @ Set inner loop counter (w15 = 11) in z3.s.
    mov     w20, #11
    dup     z3.s, w20
    b       LBB0_5

LBB0_4:
    @ Inner loop header – increment w15.
    add     z3.s, z3.s, #1        @ w15 = w15 + 1
    umov    w20, z3.s[0]          @ extract lane0 from z3.s
    umov    w21, z1.s[0]          @ extract lane0 from z1.s
    cmp     w20, w21            @ if (w15 == w10)
    b.eq    LBB0_1

LBB0_5:
    @ Begin inner loop checking.
    umull   z8.d, p0, z3.s, z0.s    @ Calculate w15 * constant (64‐bit → z8.d)
    lsr     z8.d, p0, z8.d, #35
    uqxtn   z8.s, z8.d              @ narrow to 32‐bit in z8.s
    @ Compute: w18 = w15 – ((w15 * constant >>35) * 10)
    msub    z9.s, p0, z8.s, z2.s, z3.s
    umov    w20, z9.s[0]            @ extract lane0 from z9.s into w20
    cbz     w20, LBB0_4            @ if (w18 == 0) then branch to LBB0_4

LBB0_6:
    @ Set up values for GCD: let A = w15 (in z11) and B = w10 (in z10).
    mov     z11, z3
    mov     z10, z1
LBB0_7:
    @ Compute remainder = B mod A (using vector udiv and msub).
    mov     z12, z10             @ temp = B in z12
    mov     z10, z11             @ B = A
    udiv    z13.s, p0, z12.s, z11.s   @ quotient = temp / A (each lane)
    msub    z13.s, p0, z13.s, z11.s, z12.s  @ remainder = temp − (quotient * A)
    umov    w20, z13.s[0]         @ extract lane0 from z13.s into w20
    cbnz    w20, LBB0_7           @ while (remainder != 0) keep looping

    @ Now check if the GCD (B in z10.s) equals 1.
    umov    w20, z10.s[0]
    cmp     w20, #1
    b.eq   LBB0_4

    @ Next, compare inner computed values: compare w18 (in z9.s) with w14 (in z4.s).
    umov    w20, z9.s[0]
    umov    w21, z4.s[0]
    cmp     w20, w21
    b.ne   LBB0_11

LBB0_10:
    mov     w20, #1
    @ Set w18 = (result from outer umull, namely in z7.s)
    mov     z9, z7
    cbnz    w20, LBB0_16
    b       LBB0_4

LBB0_11:
    umov    w20, z9.s[0]
    umov    w21, z7.s[0]
    cmp     w20, w21
    b.ne   LBB0_13

LBB0_12:
    mov     w20, #1
    mov     z9, z4            @ set w18 = w14
    cbnz    w20, LBB0_16
    b       LBB0_4

LBB0_13:
    umov    w20, z8.s[0]
    umov    w21, z4.s[0]
    cmp     w20, w21
    b.ne   LBB0_15

LBB0_14:
    mov     w20, #1
    mov     z8, z9             @ w16 = w18
    mov     z9, z7             @ w18 = w13 (the shifted result stored in z7.s)
    cbnz    w20, LBB0_16
    b       LBB0_4

LBB0_15:
    @ Conditional‐select based on (w16 == w13).
    umov    w20, z8.s[0]
    umov    w21, z7.s[0]
    cmp     w20, w21
    cset    w22, eq           @ w22 = 1 if equal, else 0
    cbz     w22, LBB0_4       @ if not equal, branch to LBB0_4
    @ Then set w16 = (w16 == w13 ? w18 : w15) and w18 = (w16 == w13 ? w14 : w10).
    umov    w20, z9.s[0]       @ from w18
    dup     z8.s, w20          @ update w16 with value from w18
    umov    w20, z4.s[0]       @ from w14
    dup     z9.s, w20          @ update w18 with value from w14

LBB0_16:
    @ Next inner‐loop block.
    udiv    z11.s, p0, z3.s, z10.s   @ w0 = w15 / w17 (in z11.s)
    mov     z12, z9                  @ w2 = w18 (in z12)
    mov     z13, z8                  @ w1 = w16 (in z13)
    udiv    z10.s, p0, z1.s, z10.s    @ w17 = w10 / w17 (in z10.s)
LBB0_17:
    mov     z14, z13             @ w3 = w1 (in z14)
    mov     z13, z12             @ w1 = w2
    udiv    z12.s, p0, z14.s, z12.s   @ w2 = w3 / w2
    msub    z12.s, p0, z12.s, z13.s, z14.s  @ w2 = w3 − (w2 * w1)
    umov    w20, z12.s[0]
    cbnz    w20, LBB0_17

LBB0_18:
    udiv    z8.s, p0, z8.s, z13.s   @ w16 = w16 / w1 (in z8.s)
    umov    w20, z11.s[0]         @ extract w0 from z11.s
    umov    w21, z8.s[0]          @ extract w16 from z8.s
    cmp     w20, w21
    cset    w23, eq             @ w23 = 1 if (w0 == w16)
    udiv    z9.s, p0, z9.s, z13.s   @ w18 = w18 / w1 (in z9.s)
    umov    w20, z10.s[0]         @ extract w17 from z10.s
    umov    w21, z9.s[0]          @ extract w18 from z9.s
    cmp     w20, w21
    cset    w24, eq             @ w24 = 1 if (w17 == w18)
    and     w25, w23, w24       @ w25 = w23 & w24
    @ The following two CSINC instructions choose new values conditionally.
    csinc   w23, w10, wzr, ne    @ if nonzero then w23 = w10, else 0
    csinc   w10, w11, wzr, ne    @ if nonzero then w10 = w11, else 0
    @ Multiply accumulators: w9 = w23 * w9, w8 = w10 * w8.
    umov    w20, z6.s[0]
    mul     w20, w23, w20
    dup     z6.s, w20
    umov    w20, z5.s[0]
    mul     w20, w10, w20
    dup     z5.s, w20
    b       LBB0_4

LBB0_19:
    @ When outer loop is done, set w10 = w9.
    umov    w20, z6.s[0]
    dup     z1.s, w20

LBB0_20:
    @ Final GCD loop.
    mov     z12, z5          @ copy w8 into z12 (temporary holding w11)
    mov     z5, z1           @ set w8 = w10
    udiv    z1.s, p0, z12.s, z1.s   @ w10 = w11 / w10 (in z1.s)
    msub    z1.s, p0, z1.s, z5.s, z12.s  @ w10 = w11 − (w10 * w8)
    umov    w20, z1.s[0]
    cbnz    w20, LBB0_20

    @ Prepare to call printf.
    stp     x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!
    mov     x29, sp
    adrp    x0, L_str
    add     x0, x0, :lo12:L_str
    bl      printf
    mov     w0, wzr
    ldp     x29, x30, [sp], #16
    ret

L_str:
    .asciz "%u\n"

    mov     w20, #1

    add     z3.s, p0/m, z3.s, #1     /* w15 = w15 + 1 */

	.arch_extension	sve2
	.text
	.global	main
	.type	main, %function

main:
	@ --- Set up SVE mode ---
	ptrue   p0              @ p0: all 32-bit lanes active

	@ Compute combined constant for "magic" value in z11 = (52428<<16)|52429:
	mov     w1, #52428
	lsl     w1, w1, #16
	mov     w0, #52429
	orr     w0, w1, w0
	dup     z11.s, w0         @ z11.s = constant (magic multiplier)

	@ Initialize loop variables in SVE registers:
	mov     w0, #11
	dup     z10.s, w0         @ z10.s = 11   (first loop counter)
	mov     w0, #1
	dup     z8.s, w0          @ z8.s = 1
	mov     w0, #10
	dup     z12.s, w0         @ z12.s = 10
	mov     w0, #1
	dup     z9.s, w0          @ z9.s = 1

	b       LBB0_2            @ jump into outer loop

LBB0_1:
	@ Outer-loop header (update loop variable z10)
	add     z10.s, p0/m, z10.s, #1   @ z10.s = z10.s + 1
	@ Check: if (z10 == 100) then go to final branch
	mov     w0, #100
	dup     z0.s, w0
	cmpeq   p1, p0, z10.s, z0.s
	cntp    w2, p1            @ w2 = count of true lanes (will be 1 if equal)
	cmp     w2, #1
	beq     LBB0_19
	b       LBB0_2

LBB0_2:
	@ Compute "magic-division" steps on loop-counter z10
	umull   z13.d, p0, z10.s, z11.s  
	lsr     z13.d, z13.d, #35
	rdownn  z13.s, p0, z13.d    @ narrow 64-bit result into 32-bit lanes in z13
	@ Compute: z14 = z10 - (z13 * z12)
	mul     z20.s, p0, z13.s, z12.s
	sub     z14.s, p0, z10.s, z20.s

	@ (Here we compare z10 with 12:)
	mov     w0, #12
	dup     z1.s, w0
	cmplt   p3, p0, z10.s, z1.s   @ p3 true where z10.s < 12
	cntp    w2, p3
	cmp     w2, #1
	blo     LBB0_1             @ if counter < 12, try again

	@ Now start the inner "child" loop:
	mov     w0, #11
	dup     z15.s, w0          @ z15.s = 11
	b       LBB0_5

LBB0_4:
	@ In inner loop, update z15
	add     z15.s, p0/m, z15.s, #1
	cmpeq   p4, p0, z15.s, z10.s   @ compare z15 with z10
	cntp    w2, p4
	cmp     w2, #1
	beq     LBB0_1            @ if equal, jump back to outer loop header

LBB0_5:
	@ Inner-loop work using z15 (and similar to above magic-division)
	umull   z16.d, p0, z15.s, z11.s
	lsr     z16.d, z16.d, #35
	rdownn  z16.s, p0, z16.d
	mul     z20.s, p0, z16.s, z12.s
	sub     z18.s, p0, z15.s, z20.s
	@ If z18 == 0 then branch:
	mov     w0, #0
	dup     z0.s, w0
	cmpeq   p5, p0, z18.s, z0.s
	cntp    w2, p5
	beq     LBB0_4

	@ Prepare for inner inner-loop:
	orr     z0.s, z15.s, z15.s  @ save z15 into z0 (only lane0 is used)
	orr     z17.s, z10.s, z10.s  @ save z10 into z17

LBB0_7:
	@ Inner inner-loop: compute a "remainder-style" loop via division
	orr     z1.s, z17.s, z17.s
	orr     z17.s, z0.s, z0.s
	@ SVE does not have a vector udiv so extract lane0:
	umov    w3, z1.s, #0
	umov    w4, z0.s, #0
	udiv    w5, w3, w4
	dup     z0.s, w5
	umov    w6, z17.s, #0
	msub    w5, w5, w6, w3       @ w5 = w3 - (w5 * w6)
	cbnz    w5, LBB0_7

LBB0_8:
	@ If z17 equals 1 then branch to LBB0_4
	umov    w7, z17.s, #0
	cmp     w7, #1
	beq     LBB0_4

LBB0_9:
	umov    w8, z18.s, #0
	umov    w9, z14.s, #0
	cmp     w8, w9
	bne     LBB0_11
LBB0_10:
	mov     w0, #1
	orr     z18.s, z13.s, z13.s   @ (simulate: mov z18, z13)
	cbnz    w0, LBB0_16
	b       LBB0_4
LBB0_11:

	umov    w9, z13.s, #0

LBB0_12:

	orr     z18.s, z14.s, z14.s
	cbnz    w0, LBB0_16

LBB0_13:
	umov    w8, z16.s, #0
	umov    w9, z14.s, #0

LBB0_14:
	mov     w0, #1
	orr     z16.s, z18.s, z18.s
	orr     z18.s, z13.s, z13.s
	cbnz    w0, LBB0_16
	b       LBB0_4
LBB0_15:
	@ For conditional selects we assume a true condition here.
	mov     w0, #1
	cbz     w0, LBB0_4
LBB0_16:
	@ A division step and further conditional arithmetic.
	umov    w3, z15.s, #0
	umov    w4, z17.s, #0
	udiv    w5, w3, w4
	@ (Simulated further scalar operations:)
	umov    w2, z18.s, #0
	umov    w1, z16.s, #0
	umov    w17, z10.s, #0
	udiv    w17, w9, w17         @ (simulate an inner division)
LBB0_17:
	umov    w3, z16.s, #0
	umov    w1, z18.s, #0
	udiv    w2, w3, w1
	msub    w2, w2, w1, w3
	cbnz    w2, LBB0_17
LBB0_18:
	udiv    w10, w16, w1
	cmp     w5, w10
	cset    w16, eq
	udiv    w18, w18, w1
	cmp     w17, w18
	cset    w18, eq
	tst     w16, w18
	csinc   w16, w17, wzr, ne
	csinc   w17, w5, wzr, ne
	mul     w9, w16, w9
	mul     w8, w17, w8
	b       LBB0_4

LBB0_19:
	@ When the outer loop is done, transfer z9 into z10.
	orr     z10.s, z9.s, z9.s

LBB0_20:
	@ Final inner loop to "reduce" the computed values.
	orr     z11.s, z8.s, z8.s
	orr     z8.s, z10.s, z10.s
	umov    w3, z11.s, #0
	umov    w4, z10.s, #0
	udiv    w5, w3, w4
	dup     z10.s, w5
	umov    w6, z8.s, #0
	msub    w5, w5, w6, w3
	cbnz    w5, LBB0_20

	@ --- Function epilogue ---
	stp     x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!
	mov     x29, sp
	umov    w1, z9.s, #0
	umov    w2, z8.s, #0
	udiv    w1, w1, w2          @ final result in w1
	adrp    x0, L_str
	add     x0, x0, :lo12:L_str
	bl      printf
	mov     w0, wzr
	ldp     x29, x30, [sp], #16
	ret

L_str:
	.asciz "%u\n"
	.size	main, .-main

	ptrue   p0.s                      // predicate p0: all 32‐bit lanes active
	dup     z30.s, #1                 // constant 1 for vector‐immediates

	// Compute combined constant for “magic” value in z11 = (52428<<16)|52429:
	mov     w1, #52428
	lsl     w1, w1, #16
	mov     w0, #52429
	orr     w0, w1, w0
	dup     z11.s, w0                // duplicate the constant into every 32‐bit element

	// Initialize loop variables in SVE registers:
	mov     w0, #11
	dup     z10.s, w0                // z10.s = 11   (first loop counter)
	mov     w0, #1
	dup     z8.s,  w0                // z8.s = 1
	mov     w0, #10
	dup     z12.s, w0                // z12.s = 10
	mov     w0, #1
	dup     z9.s,  w0                // z9.s = 1

	b       LBB0_2                   // jump into outer loop

LBB0_1:
	// Outer‐loop header: update loop variable (z10 = z10 + 1)
	add     z10.s, p0/m, z10.s, z30.s

	// Check: if (z10 == 100) then jump to final branch:
	mov     w0, #100
	dup     z0.s, w0
	cmpeq   p1, p0/m, z10.s, z0.s
	cntp    w2, p1                 // count true lanes (should be 1 if equal)
	cmp     w2, #1
	beq     LBB0_19
	b       LBB0_2

LBB0_2:
	// Compute “magic‐division” steps on the loop–counter z10:
	umull   z13.d, p0/m, z10.s, z11.s  
	lsr     z13.d, z13.d, #35
	rdownn  z13.s, p0/m, z13.d      // round–down and narrow (from .d to .s)
	// Compute: z14 = z10 – (z13 × z12)
	mul     z20.s, p0/m, z13.s, z12.s
	sub     z14.s, p0/m, z10.s, z20.s

	// Compare z10 with 12:
	mov     w0, #12
	dup     z1.s, w0
	cmplt   p3, p0/m, z10.s, z1.s   // p3 true where z10.s < 12
	cntp    w2, p3
	cmp     w2, #1
	b.lo    LBB0_1                 // if counter < 12, try again

	// Now start the inner “child” loop:
	mov     w0, #11
	dup     z15.s, w0               // z15.s = 11
	b       LBB0_5

LBB0_4:
	// Inner loop: update z15:
	add     z15.s, p0/m, z15.s, z30.s
	cmpeq   p4, p0/m, z15.s, z10.s  // compare z15 with z10
	cntp    w2, p4
	cmp     w2, #1
	beq     LBB0_1                 // if equal, jump back to outer loop header

LBB0_5:
	// Inner-loop work (magic–division on z15):
	umull   z16.d, p0/m, z15.s, z11.s
	lsr     z16.d, z16.d, #35
	rdownn  z16.s, p0/m, z16.d      // narrowing round–down
	mul     z20.s, p0/m, z16.s, z12.s
	sub     z18.s, p0/m, z15.s, z20.s
	// If z18 equals 0 then branch:
	mov     w0, #0
	dup     z0.s, w0
	cmpeq   p5, p0/m, z18.s, z0.s
	cntp    w2, p5
	beq     LBB0_4

mult_mod:

    stp     x29, x30, [sp, #-32]!
    stp     x20, x19, [sp, #16]
    mov     x29, sp

    // Save arguments:
    //   x0 holds pointer to first matrix
    //   x1 holds pointer to second matrix.
    mov     x20, x0            // base pointer of first matrix
    // Allocate 2592 bytes for the output
    mov     w0, #2592
    mov     x19, x1            // second matrix pointer
    bl      malloc             // result pointer returned in x0

    // --- Set up constants for the mod–multiply reduction ---
    // (Constants built from several moves to x9 and x10.)
    mov     x9, #23123
    mov     w10, #51712
    movk    x9, #41115, lsl #16
    movk    w10, #15258, lsl #16
    movk    x9, #47151, lsl #32
    movk    x9, #68, lsl #48
    mov     w11, #18         // loop count = 18

    // --- Set up the SVE environment ---
    ptrue   p0.d                   // predicate with all 64–bit lanes active
    dup     z9.d, x9               // broadcast reciprocal constant
    dup     z10.d, x10             // broadcast modulus constant
    dup     z11.d, x11             // broadcast loop–bound (18)

    rdvl    x12, #1               // x12 := current VL (in bytes)
    cntd    x13, p0, #1           // x13 := number of active 64–bit lanes

    // Example use of and (immediate)
    mov     x8, #0
    and     x8, x8, #0xFFFFFFFF

    // --- Outer loop: iterate over 18 rows (x8 = 0 .. 17) ---
mult_mod_outer:
    cmp     x8, #18
    b.ge    mult_mod_done

    // Inner “middle” loop: process 18 dot–products for one row.
    mov     x15, #0               // x15 indexes each dot–product in the row
    mov     x14, x19              // x14 points into second matrix block

mult_mod_middle:
    cmp     x15, #18
    b.ge    mult_mod_next_row

    // --- Inner loop: vectorized dot–product (over 18 elements) ---
    ld1d   {z1.d}, p0/z, [x14]      // load 18 64–bit values from second matrix row
    ld1d   {z2.d}, p0/z, [x20]       // load 18 contiguous 64–bit values from first matrix
    dup    z0.d, #0                // clear the accumulator
    mla    z0.d, z1.d, z2.d, z0.d   // multiply–accumulate: z0 = z0 + (z1*z2)

    // Now perform the mod–reduction:
    //   q = (z0 >> 9), then q = umulh(q, reciprocal), then q >> 11,
    //   and finally subtract q*modulus.
    lsr    z3.d, z0.d, #9
    umulh  z3.d, z3.d, z9.d
    lsr    z3.d, z3.d, #11
    mls    z0.d, z3.d, z10.d, z0.d

    lsl    x16, x15, #3         // x15 * 8 (each result is 8 bytes)
    st1d   {z0.d[0]}, p0, [x0, x16]  // store result in output (only lane 0 is used)

    // Advance the “middle” pointer.
    add    x14, x14, #144       // next block: 144 bytes apart
    add    x15, x15, #1
    b      mult_mod_middle

    add    x8, x8, #1           // next outer row
    add    x20, x20, #8         // advance first matrix pointer by one 8–byte element
    b      mult_mod_outer

    ldp    x20, x19, [sp, #16]
    ldp    x29, x30, [sp], #32
    ret
