    /*
      Function: mult_mod
      ------------------
      Given two 18×18 matrices A and B (passed in registers x0 and x1) arranged in
      “column–by–column” order (that is, with adjacent elements of A separated by 8 bytes)
      and with B stored such that each row takes 144 bytes, compute

         C[i][j] = ( Σₖ A[i][k] * B[k][j] ) mod M

      with M computed as

         temp = (C >> 9) * recip >> 11;  then   C := C – (temp * mod)
      
      where the “reciprocal constant” (in x9) is 64–bit constructed from
          23123, 41115, 47151, 68
      and the modulus (in x10) is built from
          51712, 15258.

      The result matrix C (18×18, 2592 bytes) is allocated on the heap.
      (We assume that the SVE “ptrue p0.d” predicate covers exactly 18 64–bit lanes.)
    */
    .global mult_mod
    .type mult_mod, %function
mult_mod:
    // --- Prologue ---
    stp     x29, x30, [sp, #-48]!
    stp     x20, x19, [sp, #16]
    mov     x29, sp

    // x0 = pointer to matrix A, x1 = pointer to matrix B.
    // Save these in registers (A in x23, B in x24).
    mov     x23, x0           
    mov     x24, x1           

    // Allocate 2592 bytes for the 18×18 result matrix C.
    mov     w0, #2592        
    bl      malloc           
    // Save the allocated C pointer in x21 (to return later)
    mov     x21, x0          
    // Use x22 as the “current–row” pointer into C.
    mov     x22, x0          

    // --- Set up constants for the mod–multiply reduction ---
    // Build reciprocal constant in x9 (64–bit).
    mov     x9, #23123
    movk    x9, #41115, lsl #16
    movk    x9, #47151, lsl #32
    movk    x9, #68,    lsl #48
    // Build modulus constant in x10 (64–bit).
    mov     x10, #51712
    movk    x10, #15258, lsl #16

    // Duplicate constants into vector registers.
    dup     z9.d, x9
    dup     z10.d, x10

    // The “matrix dimension” is 18.
    mov     x25, #18       

    // --- Set up the SVE environment ---
    ptrue   p0.d                  // All lanes active.
    // Build a predicate p1 that is true only for lane 0.
    mov     x17, #1
    whilelo p1.d, xzr, x17

    rdvl    x12, #1              // Get current VL (in bytes).
    cntd    x13, p0.d            // Count 64–bit lanes (assumed = 18).

    // --- Outer loop: loop over rows (i = 0..17) ---
    mov     x8, #0               // i = 0.
mult_mod_outer:
    cmp     x8, x25
    b.ge    mult_mod_done

    // For each row of A, compute the pointer:
    // In the assumed storage, successive rows of A are 8 bytes apart.
    mov     x20, x23
    add     x20, x20, x8, lsl #3   // x20 = A + i*8

    // --- Middle loop: iterate over columns (j = 0..17) ---
    mov     x16, #0              // j = 0.
    // Set up constant for B row stride (144 bytes)
    mov     x14, #144           // constant value for 144.

mult_mod_middle:
    cmp     x16, x25
    b.ge    mult_mod_next_row

    // Compute dot–product C[i][j] = sumₖ A[i][k] * B[k][j].
    // We use lane0 only (via predicate p1).
    dup     z0.d, #0            // Clear accumulator in z0.

    // Dot–product inner loop: sum over k = 0..17.
    mov     x15, #0             // k = 0.
dotprod_loop:
    cmp     x15, x25
    b.ge    dotprod_done

    // Load A[i][k]: each element is 8 bytes.
    add     x26, x20, x15, lsl #3
    ld1rd  {z1.d}, p0/z, [x26]  // Load and replicate A[i][k].

    // Load B[k][j]: B is assumed to have rows of 144 bytes.
    // B[k][j] address = B + (k * 144) + (j * 8)
    mul     x28, x15, x14       // x28 = k * 144.
    add     x27, x24, x28
    add     x27, x27, x16, lsl #3 // x27 = B + k*144 + j*8.
    ld1rd  {z2.d}, p0/z, [x27]  // Load and replicate B[k][j].

    // Accumulate: z0 = z0 + (z1 * z2)
    mul     z31.d, z1.d, z2.d
    add     z0.d, z0.d, z31.d

    add     x15, x15, #1
    b       dotprod_loop
dotprod_done:
    // --- Do the mod–reduction on the accumulated dot product ---
    lsr     z3.d, z0.d, #9
    umulh   z3.d, z3.d, z9.d
    lsr     z3.d, z3.d, #11
    // Instead of mls (which is indexed) do:
    mul     z31.d, z3.d, z10.d
    sub     z0.d, z0.d, z31.d

    // --- Store the resulting scalar (from lane0) into C[i][j] ---
    st1d   {z0.d}, p1, [x22, x16, lsl #3]

    add     x16, x16, #1       // j++.
    b       mult_mod_middle

mult_mod_next_row:
    add     x8, x8, #1         // i++.
    // Advance the output row pointer by 144 bytes (18×8).
    add     x22, x22, #144     
    b       mult_mod_outer

mult_mod_done:
    // Return the originally allocated result pointer (in x21).
    mov     x0, x21

    // --- Epilogue ---
    ldp     x20, x19, [sp, #16]
    ldp     x29, x30, [sp], #48
    ret
    .size mult_mod, .-mult_mod


    /*
      Function: mult_vec
      ------------------
      Given an 18×18 matrix A (in x0) and an 18–element vector v (in x1)
      (with A stored as in mult_mod and v held contiguously),
      compute for each row i of A:
           R[i] = ( Σₖ A[i][k] * v[k] ) mod M.
      The result vector (144 bytes) is allocated from the heap.
    */
    .global mult_vec
    .type mult_vec, %function
mult_vec:
    // --- Prologue ---
    stp     x29, x30, [sp, #-48]!
    stp     x20, x19, [sp, #16]
    mov     x29, sp

    // x0 = pointer to matrix A, x1 = pointer to vector v.
    mov     x23, x0         // Matrix A.
    mov     x24, x1         // Vector v.

    // Allocate 144 bytes for the result vector.
    mov     w0, #144
    bl      malloc
    mov     x21, x0       // Save allocated vector pointer.

    // --- Set up mod reduction constants (same as before) ---
    mov     x9, #23123
    movk    x9, #41115, lsl #16
    movk    x9, #47151, lsl #32
    movk    x9, #68,    lsl #48

    mov     x10, #51712
    movk    x10, #15258, lsl #16

    dup     z9.d, x9
    dup     z10.d, x10

    mov     x25, #18      // Dimension = 18.

    // --- Set up SVE environment ---
    ptrue   p0.d
    mov     x17, #1
    whilelo p1.d, xzr, x17

    rdvl    x12, #1
    cntd    x13, p0.d

    // --- Outer loop: for each row i of A ---
    mov     x8, #0      // row index.
mult_vec_outer:
    cmp     x8, x25
    b.ge    mult_vec_done

    // For row i, pointer = A + i*8
    mov     x20, x23
    add     x20, x20, x8, lsl #3

    dup     z0.d, #0   // accumulator = 0.
    mov     x15, #0    // dot–product index k.
dotprod_vec:
    cmp     x15, x25
    b.ge    dotprod_vec_done

    // Load A[i][k] from row pointer.
    add     x26, x20, x15, lsl #3
    ld1rd  {z1.d}, p0/z, [x26]

    // Load v[k] from vector v (contiguous).
    add     x27, x24, x15, lsl #3
    ld1rd  {z2.d}, p0/z, [x27]

    // Accumulate: z0 = z0 + (z1 * z2)
    mul     z31.d, z1.d, z2.d
    add     z0.d, z0.d, z31.d

    add     x15, x15, #1
    b       dotprod_vec
dotprod_vec_done:
    lsr     z3.d, z0.d, #9
    umulh   z3.d, z3.d, z9.d
    lsr     z3.d, z3.d, #11
    mul     z31.d, z3.d, z10.d
    sub     z0.d, z0.d, z31.d

    st1d   {z0.d}, p1, [x21, x8, lsl #3]

    add     x8, x8, #1
    b       mult_vec_outer

mult_vec_done:
    mov     x0, x21   // Return result vector.
    ldp     x20, x19, [sp, #16]
    ldp     x29, x30, [sp], #48
    ret
    .size mult_vec, .-mult_vec


    /*
      Function: main
      --------------
      In this simple test driver we allocate two 18×18 matrices (A and B) and clear them.
      To show (modular) multiplication in action we set a few elements, call mult_mod
      (and mult_vec) and print the first element of the result.
    */

    .type main, %function
main:
    stp     x29, x30, [sp, #-96]!
    stp     x26, x25, [sp, #16]
    stp     x24, x23, [sp, #32]
    stp     x22, x21, [sp, #48]
    stp     x20, x19, [sp, #64]
    mov     x29, sp

    // Allocate matrix A (2592 bytes) and clear it.
    mov     w0, #2592

    mov     x0, x27
    mov     x1, xzr
    mov     w2, #2592
    bl      memset

    mov     w0, #2592
    bl      malloc

        stp     x20, x19, [sp, #-16]!   // save registers

        mov     x20, x0                // x20 = result buffer

        ptrue   p0.d
        cntd    x4, p0.d, #1           // count active double‐word lanes (immediate multiplier in [1,16])

        dup     z9.d, #68             // constant 68 is in allowed immediate range

        mov     x16, #15258
        dup     z10.d, x16
        dup     z11.d, #18            // loop bound (18 rows)

        mov     x8, #0               // outer loop counter = 0

        cmp     x8, #18
        b.eq    mult_mod_end

        // Zero the accumulator.
        dup     z0.d, #0

        // Load vector elements (using /z to zero inactive lanes).
        ld1d   {z1.d}, p0/z, [x1]     // load 18 64‐bit elements from matrix A row
        ld1d   {z2.d}, p0/z, [x20]     // load corresponding 18 64‐bit elements from array B

        umulh   z3.d, z3.d, z9.d     // vector unsigned multiply–high (needs SVE2)
        lsr     z3.d, z3.d, #11      // further shift-right

        and     z0.d, z0.d, #0xFF    // immediate must be a run‐of‐ones pattern

        rdvl    x2, #1              // read current multiple-of–VL

	mov     x29, sp
	stp     x20, x19, [sp, #-16]!

	// Allocate 2592 bytes (for a “matrix” of 18 rows)
	mov     w0, #2592
	bl      malloc              // malloc returns pointer in x0
	// Save its base in x21 (this will be the output base)
	mov     x21, x0
	// For example, assume that the allocated block holds two things:
	// – the mod–reduced result (first 144 bytes, one 8–byte result per row) and
	// – a matrix B (the remaining part). Here we let matrix B start 144 bytes in.
	add     x20, x21, #144

	// Setup SVE predicate and count.
	ptrue   p0.d
	cntd    x4, p0, #1         // p0 (not p0.d) and immediate multiplier in [1,16]
	// Broadcast constants.
	dup     z9.d, #68           // constant 68
	mov     x16, #15258         // 15258 lifted via a GP reg…
	dup     z10.d, x16
	dup     z11.d, #18          // loop bound: 18 rows

	// Outer loop – process one row each iteration.
	mov     x8, #0              // outer loop counter = 0
mult_mod_loop:
	cmp     x8, #18
	b.eq    mult_mod_end

	// Zero the accumulator.
	dup     z0.d, #0

	// Load a row (18 64-bit values) from matrix A and from matrix B.
	ld1d   {z1.d}, p0/z, [x1]    // matrix A row (144 bytes = 18×8)
	ld1d   {z2.d}, p0/z, [x20]    // matrix B row

	mla     z0.d, z1.d, z2.d, 0

	lsr     z3.d, z0.d, #9
	umulh   z3.d, z3.d, z9.d
	lsr     z3.d, z3.d, #11
	mls     z0.d, z3.d, z10.d, z0.d, 0

	// Optionally mask the result (immediate must be a “run‑of‑ones” pattern)
	and     z0.d, z0.d, #0xFF

	// Compute a byte offset for the (scalar) result.
	lsl     x3, x8, #3         // x3 = row index × 8 (each result is 8 bytes)
	add     x3, x21, x3        // add base pointer for mod–reduced results (stored in the first 144 bytes)
	rdvl    x2, #1             // read current multiple–of–VL (for this example it is not further used)
	st1d    {z0.d}, p0/z, [x3]  // store the result

	add     x1, x1, #144       // next row of matrix A
	add     x20, x20, #144     // next row of matrix B
	add     x8, x8, #1
	b       mult_mod_loop

.arch armv8.2-a+sve2
	.text
	.global mult_mod
	.type   mult_mod, %function
mult_mod:
	// Function prologue
	stp     x29, x30, [sp, #-32]!
	mov     x29, sp
	stp     x20, x19, [sp, #-16]!

	// Allocate 2592 bytes (for a “matrix” of 18 rows)
	mov     w0, #2592
	bl      malloc              // malloc returns pointer in x0
	// Save its base in x21 (this will be the output base)
	mov     x21, x0
	// The allocated block holds two things:
	// – the mod–reduced result (first 144 bytes, one 8–byte result per row) and
	// – a matrix B (the remaining part). Let matrix B start 144 bytes in.
	add     x20, x21, #144

	// Setup SVE predicate and count.
	ptrue   p0.d
	cntd    x4, p0, #1
	// Broadcast constants.
	dup     z9.d, #68
	mov     x16, #15258
	dup     z10.d, x16
	dup     z11.d, #18          // loop bound: 18 rows

	// Outer loop – process one row each iteration.
	mov     x8, #0              // outer loop counter = 0
mult_mod_loop:
	cmp     x8, #18
	b.eq    mult_mod_end

	// Zero the accumulator.
	dup     z0.d, #0

	// Load a row (18 64-bit values) from matrix A and from matrix B.
	ld1d   {z1.d}, p0, [x1]      // load matrix A row (144 bytes = 18×8)
	ld1d   {z2.d}, p0, [x20]      // load matrix B row

	// Multiply–accumulate (indexed MLA with immediate index #0)
	mla     z0.d, z1.d, z2.d, #0

	// Modular reduction sequence.
	lsr     z3.d, z0.d, #9
	umulh   z3.d, z3.d, z9.d
	lsr     z3.d, z3.d, #11
	mls     z0.d, z3.d, z10.d, z0.d, #0

	// Optionally mask the result (the immediate must be a “run‑of‑ones” pattern)
	and     z0.d, z0.d, #0xFF

	// Compute a byte offset for the (scalar) result.
	lsl     x3, x8, #3         // row index × 8 (each result is 8 bytes)
	add     x3, x21, x3        // add base pointer (mod–reduced results are stored in the first 144 bytes)
	rdvl    x2, #1             // read current multiple–of–VL (not further used in this example)
	st1d    {z0.d}, p0, [x3]    // store the result

	// Advance the two input pointers:
	add     x1, x1, #144       // next row of matrix A
	add     x20, x20, #144     // next row of matrix B
	add     x8, x8, #1
	b       mult_mod_loop

mult_mod_end:
	ldp     x20, x19, [sp], #16
	ldp     x29, x30, [sp], #32
	ret

	.size   mult_mod, .-mult_mod

	// ------------------------------------------------------------------
	// Second function: mult_vec
	.global mult_vec
	.type   mult_vec, %function
mult_vec:
	stp     x29, x30, [sp, #-32]!
	mov     x29, sp
	stp     x20, x19, [sp, #-16]!

	// Allocate a 144–byte buffer.
	mov     w0, #144
	bl      malloc
	// Save the allocation base in x21 for future stores.
	mov     x21, x0
	// Assume that x19 already points to the first input array and that
	// the allocated buffer in x21 will be used as the second input.
	mov     x20, x21

	// SVE predicate and constant setup.
	ptrue   p0.d
	dup     z9.d, #68
	mov     x16, #15258
	dup     z10.d, x16

	// Outer loop: process 18 iterations.
	mov     x8, #0
mult_vec_loop:
	cmp     x8, #18
	b.eq    mult_vec_end

	dup     z0.d, #0
	ld1d    {z1.d}, p0, [x19]    // load first input row (144 bytes)
	ld1d    {z2.d}, p0, [x20]     // load second input row
	mla     z0.d, z1.d, z2.d, #0
	lsr     z3.d, z0.d, #9
	umulh   z3.d, z3.d, z9.d
	lsr     z3.d, z3.d, #11
	mls     z0.d, z3.d, z10.d, z0.d, #0

	rdvl    x2, #1
	lsl     x3, x8, #3         // compute offset = x8×8
	add     x3, x21, x3        // add the base pointer of our allocated buffer
	st1d    {z0.d}, p0, [x3]

	add     x19, x19, #144      // advance first input row pointer
	add     x20, x20, #8        // advance second input pointer
	add     x8, x8, #1
	b       mult_vec_loop

mult_vec_end:
	ldp     x20, x19, [sp], #16
	ldp     x29, x30, [sp], #32
	ret

.arch armv8.2-a+sve2
        .text
        .global mult_mod
        .type   mult_mod, %function
mult_mod:
        // Function prologue
        stp     x29, x30, [sp, #-32]!
        mov     x29, sp
        stp     x20, x19, [sp, #-16]!

        // Allocate 2592 bytes (for a “matrix” of 18 rows)
        mov     w0, #2592
        bl      malloc              // malloc returns pointer in x0
        // Save its base in x21 (this will be the output base)
        mov     x21, x0
        // The allocated block holds two things:
        // – the mod–reduced result (first 144 bytes, one 8–byte result per row) and
        // – a matrix B (the remaining part). Let matrix B start 144 bytes in.
        add     x20, x21, #144

        // Setup SVE predicate and count.
        ptrue   p0.d
        cntd    x4, p0, #1         // FIX: use p0 (not p0.d)
        // Broadcast constants.
        dup     z9.d, #68
        mov     x16, #15258
        dup     z10.d, x16
        dup     z11.d, #18          // loop bound: 18 rows

        // Outer loop – process one row each iteration.
        mov     x8, #0              // outer loop counter = 0
mult_mod_loop:
        cmp     x8, #18
        b.eq    mult_mod_end

        // Zero the accumulator.
        dup     z0.d, #0

        // Load a row (18 64–bit values) from matrix A and from matrix B.
        ld1d   {z1.d}, p0/z, [x1]      // load matrix A row (144 bytes = 18×8)
        ld1d   {z2.d}, p0/z, [x20]      // load matrix B row

        // Multiply–accumulate (using an indexed MLA with immediate index [0])
        mla     z0.d, z1.d, z2.d[0]

        // Modular reduction sequence.
        lsr     z3.d, z0.d, #9
        umulh   z3.d, z3.d, z9.d
        lsr     z3.d, z3.d, #11
        mls     z0.d, z3.d, z10.d[0]

        // Optionally mask the result (the immediate must be a “run‑of‑ones” pattern)
        and     z0.d, z0.d, #0xFF

        // Compute a byte offset for the (scalar) result.
        lsl     x3, x8, #3         // row index × 8 (each result is 8 bytes)
        add     x3, x21, x3        // add base pointer (mod–reduced results are stored in the first 144 bytes)
        rdvl    x2, #1             // read current multiple–of–VL (not further used in this example)
        st1d    {z0.d}, p0, [x3]    // store the result

        // Advance the two input pointers:
        add     x1, x1, #144       // next row of matrix A
        add     x20, x20, #144     // next row of matrix B
        add     x8, x8, #1
        b       mult_mod_loop

mult_mod_end:
        ldp     x20, x19, [sp], #16
        ldp     x29, x30, [sp], #32
        ret

        .size   mult_mod, .-mult_mod

        // ------------------------------------------------------------------
        // Second function: mult_vec
        .global mult_vec
        .type   mult_vec, %function
mult_vec:
        stp     x29, x30, [sp, #-32]!
        mov     x29, sp
        stp     x20, x19, [sp, #-16]!

        // Allocate a 144–byte buffer.
        mov     w0, #144
        bl      malloc
        // Save the allocation base in x21 for future stores.
        mov     x21, x0
        // Assume that x19 already points to the first input array and that
        // the allocated buffer in x21 will be used as the second input.
        mov     x20, x21

        // SVE predicate and constant setup.
        ptrue   p0.d
        dup     z9.d, #68
        mov     x16, #15258
        dup     z10.d, x16

        // Outer loop: process 18 iterations.
        mov     x8, #0
mult_vec_loop:
        cmp     x8, #18
        b.eq    mult_vec_end

        dup     z0.d, #0
        ld1d    {z1.d}, p0/z, [x19]    // load first input row (144 bytes)
        ld1d    {z2.d}, p0/z, [x20]     // load second input row
        mla     z0.d, z1.d, z2.d[0]
        lsr     z3.d, z0.d, #9
        umulh   z3.d, z3.d, z9.d
        lsr     z3.d, z3.d, #11
        mls     z0.d, z3.d, z10.d[0]

        rdvl    x2, #1
        lsl     x3, x8, #3         // compute offset = x8×8
        add     x3, x21, x3        // add the base pointer of our allocated buffer
        st1d    {z0.d}, p0, [x3]

        add     x19, x19, #144      // advance first input row pointer
        add     x20, x20, #8        // advance second input pointer
        add     x8, x8, #1
        b       mult_vec_loop

mult_vec_end:
        ldp     x20, x19, [sp], #16
        ldp     x29, x30, [sp], #32
        ret

        .size   mult_vec, .-mult_vec

        // ------------------------------------------------------------------
        // Third function: main
        .global main
        .type   main, %function
main:
        stp     x29, x30, [sp, #-80]!
        mov     x29, sp
        stp     x26, x25, [sp, #-16]!
        stp     x24, x23, [sp, #-32]!
        stp     x22, x21, [sp, #-48]!
        stp     x20, x19, [sp, #-64]!

        // Allocate and clear an array of size 2592.
        mov     w0, #2592
        bl      malloc
        mov     x21, x0           // x21 = base pointer for our array
        mov     x0, x21           // pass x0=address (64–bit register required)
        mov     w1, wzr
        mov     w2, #2592
        bl      memset

        // Set up some sample scalar values.
        mov     x9, #-1368
        mov     w10, #9
        mov     w11, #10
        mov     w12, #1

        // Outer loop using SVE.
        mov     x8, #0
main_loop:
        cmp     x8, #18
        b.eq    main_after_loop

        // For this iteration, allocate a 144–byte vector buffer.
        mov     w0, #144
        bl      malloc
        mov     x20, x0           // x20 = temporary vector memory

        ptrue   p0.d
        dup     z0.d, #0

        // Inner loop: accumulate over 18 elements.
        mov     x11, #0
main_inner_loop:
        cmp     x11, #18
        b.eq    main_inner_done

        ld1d    {z1.d}, p0/z, [x21, x11, LSL #3]
        ld1d    {z2.d}, p0/z, [x20, x11, LSL #3]
        mla     z0.d, z1.d, z2.d[0]
        add     x11, x11, #1
        b       main_inner_loop

main_inner_done:
        dup     z9.d, #68
        mov     x16, #15258
        dup     z10.d, x16
        lsr     z3.d, z0.d, #9
        umulh   z3.d, z3.d, z9.d
        lsr     z3.d, z3.d, #11
        mls     z0.d, z3.d, z10.d[0]
        rdvl    x2, #1
        lsl     x3, x8, #3         // compute offset = x8×8
        add     x3, x21, x3        // add base pointer
        st1d    {z0.d}, p0, [x3]

        add     x8, x8, #1
        b       main_loop

main_after_loop:
        adrp    x0, .L_str
        add     x0, x0, :lo12:.L_str
        ldr     x1, [x21]         // print the first 64–bit word
        bl      printf

        // Function epilogue
        ldp     x20, x19, [sp], #64
        ldp     x22, x21, [sp], #48
        ldp     x24, x23, [sp], #32
        ldp     x26, x25, [sp], #16
        ldp     x29, x30, [sp], #80
        ret

        .size   main, .-main

        // ------------------------------------------------------------------
        // Data section
        .section .rodata
.L_str:
        .asciz "%llu\n"
        .size   .L_str, 6

chunks.splice:
Splice two vectors under predicate control 
Select a region from the first source vector and copy it to the lowest numbered elements of the result Then set any 
remaining elements of the result to a copy of the lowest numbered elements from the second source vector The region is 
selected using the first and last true elements in the vector select predicate register The result is placed destructively in 
the destination and first source vector or constructively in the destination vector

instruction The MOVPRFX instruction must conform to all of the following requirements otherwise the behavior of the 
MOVPRFX and this instruction is UNPREDICTABLE The MOVPRFX instruction must be un predicated The 
MOVPRFX instruction must specify the same destination register as this instruction The destination register must not

	.global	main

main:
	// Prologue – save frame pointer and return address.
	stp		x29, x30, [sp, #-32]!
	// (Also save x19 as in the original.)
	str		x19, [sp, #16]
	mov		x29, sp

	// --- Allocate memory (simulate a malloc call) ---
	// Compute sizes in w0 and w19.
	mov		w0, #23044		// 0x5a04
	mov		w19, #38529		// 0x9681
	movk	w0, #610, lsl #16	// now w0 := (610 << 16) | 0x5a04
	movk	w19, #152, lsl #16	// now w19 := (152 << 16) | 0x9681
	bl		malloc			// malloc(w0) → pointer returned in x0

	// --- First vectorized loop (simulate nested loop) ---
	// Outer iteration 1: treat i = 2 so that stride = 4 * 2 = 8.
	mov		w2, #2			// i = 2
	mov		w3, #8			// stride = 8 bytes
	add		x21, x0, #8		// x21 := base pointer + 8

	// Set up predicates and counter‐helper register.
	ptrue	p0.s			// p0: full predicate for 32–bit elements
	ptrue	p15.s			// p15 will be used for the counter encoding
	rdvl	x20, #4			// x20 := (VL in bytes)×4 (unused later)
	; Use p15 (which is in the allowed range for counter encoding: p8–p15)
	cnth	x23, p15, #1		// x23 := "half–count" (using p15)
	cntw	x22, p15, #1		// x22 := number of active 32–bit lanes (using p15)

	// Build an index vector (0, 2, 4, …)
	index	z0.s, #0, #2		// z0.s := {0, 2, 4, …}
	// Generate a predicate: active lanes where the implicit lane index is less than x22.
	whilelt	p1.s, xzr, x22		// p1.s ← (lane index < x22)
	// Indexed load/store: effective address = x21 + (index << 2)
	ld1w	{z1.s}, p1/z, [x21, z0.s, uxtw]	// load selected 32–bit words
	add		z1.s, z1.s, #1			// add 1 to each element
	st1w	{z1.s}, p1, [x21, z0.s, uxtw]	// store results back

	// Outer iteration 2: now treat i = 3 so that stride = 4 * 3 = 12.
	mov		w2, #3			// i = 3
	mov		w3, #12			// stride = 12 bytes
	add		x21, x0, #12		// x21 := base pointer + 12

	ptrue	p0.s
	ptrue	p15.s
	rdvl	x20, #4
	cntw	x22, p15, #1
	index	z0.s, #0, #3		// z0.s := {0, 3, 6, …}
	whilelt	p1.s, xzr, x22		// generate predicate for active lanes
	ld1w	{z1.s}, p1/z, [x21, z0.s, uxtw]
	add		z1.s, z1.s, #1
	st1w	{z1.s}, p1, [x21, z0.s, uxtw]

	// Reverse the predicate p0 into p8.
	rev		p8.b, p0.b		// p8.b ← reverse(p0.b)
	// Copy the index vector (z0) into z2 and mask off all but the lowest byte of each 32–bit element.
	movprfx	z2, z0		// copy z0 into z2 (direct mov between SVE vectors is disallowed)

	add		x10, x8, #4		// compute address for adjacent word [x8 + 4]
	ld1w	{z5.s}, p0/z, [x10]	// load adjacent words
	cmpeq	p1, z4.s, z5.s		// p1 ← (z4.s == z5.s)

	lastb	x9, p0, z7.b		// LASTB: extract the last active byte from z7 (using predicate p0)

Set scalar to multiple of predicate constraint element count 
Determines the number of active elements implied by the named predicate constraint multiplies that by an immediate in 
the range 1 to 16 inclusive and then places the result in the scalar destination 
The named predicate constraint limits the number of active elements in a single predicate to

• The largest power of two POW 2 
• The largest multiple of three or four MUL 3 or MUL 4 
• All available implicitly a multiple of two ALL 

Unspecified or out of range constraint encodings generate an empty predicate or zero element count rather than

        add     x10, x8, #1                 // x10 = number of elements for first reduction

        //--- Begin vectorized reduction loop for addition ---

        add     x0, x0, #8

.LBB0_1:

        cmp     x8, x20

.LBB0_2:

        cbnz    w9, .LBB0_1

        mov     x10, x8

        mov     w11, wzr
        mov     w12, w10

.LBB0_5:
        sdiv    w12, w12, w8
        add     w11, w11, w8
        sdiv    w13, w12, w8
        msub    w13, w13, w8, w12
        cbz     w13, .LBB0_5

        add     x9, x9, #1
        add     x10, x10, x8

        str     w11, [x19, x12]
        b.lo    .LBB0_4
        b       .LBB0_1

        movk    w9, #305, lsl #16
        mov     x1, xzr                     // Clear accumulator

        // Adjust pointer :
        add     x9, x19, x9                 // x9 = base + offset computed earlier
        add     x10, x8, #1                 // x10 = number of elements for first reduction

        //--- Begin vectorized reduction loop for addition ---

        // (Dummy instructions also demonstrate use of rdvl, ptrue, lsr, cnth, and, cntw,

        ldrsw   x6, [x9], #4
        add     x1, x1, x6
        sub     x10, x10, #1
        cbnz    x10, tail_loop

.arch armv8.2-a+sve
        .text
        .global is_pandigital
        .p2align 2
        .type   is_pandigital, @function
is_pandigital:
        // Allocate 32 bytes on the stack.
        sub     sp, sp, #32
        // Initialize our “digit‐table” (stored at sp+8) with zeros.
        stp     xzr, xzr, [sp, #8]
        str     wzr, [sp, #24]
        // If the input (in x0) is zero, skip the digit–extraction loop.
        cbz     x0, pandigital_check

        // --- DIGIT EXTRACTION LOOP (scalar version) ---
digit_loop:
        // Set up a constant in x8 (0x6666666666666666, with a movk appended)
        mov     x8, #7378697629483820646    // 0x6666666666666666
        mov     w9, #10                     // divisor = 10
        add     x10, sp, #8                 // pointer to digit–table base
        mov     w11, #1                    // digit mark (will be stored as “1”)
        smulh   x12, x0, x8
        add     x14, x0, #9
        cmp     x14, #18
        asr     x13, x12, #2
        add     x12, x13, x12, lsr #63
        msub    x13, x12, x9, x0
        mov     x0, x12
        // Write out a half–word mark (digit “seen”) into the table.
        strh    w11, [x10, x13, lsl #1]
        // Loop while the “borrow” flag is set.
        bhi     digit_loop

        // --- VECTOR CHECK OF THE DIGIT TABLE (using SVE) ---
pandigital_check:
        // In our design the table at sp+8 holds the count for digit “0” (first half–word)
        // and counts for digits 1..9 are stored (as half–words) starting at sp+10.
        // We want to check that (a) each digit from 1..9 is marked with 1 and (b)
        // the “zero–digit” (stored at sp+8) remains 0.

        // Use a predicate which is active for 9 half–words.
        whilelo p1.h, xzr, #9         // p1.h is active for lanes 0…8
        ld1h    { z2.h }, p1/z, [sp, #10]   // load table[1..9] into z2.h
        // Use an SVE fmov immediate (alias of fcpy) to set a vector register to 0.0.
        // Then use an “inc” to obtain a constant 1 in each active lane.
        fmov    z1.h, p1/m, #0.0      // z1.h = 0 for each active element (0.0 in FP is all–zero bits)
        inc     z1.h, z1.h           // now z1.h contains “1” in each active lane
        // Subtract the expected value (1) from the loaded table values.
        sub     z3.h, z2.h, z1.h
        abs     z3.h, z3.h
        // Reduce across lanes: if any element was not 1 the maximum difference will be >0.
        umaxv  d4, p1, z3.h          // d4 ← maximum element of z3.h
        cmp     d4, #0
        b.ne    pandigital_fail

        // Also check that the count for digit “0” (at sp+8) is still 0.
        ldrh    w5, [sp, #8]
        cmp     w5, #0
        b.ne    pandigital_fail

        mov     w0, #1                // Found pandigital result.
        b       pandigital_exit

pandigital_fail:
        mov     w0, wzr              // Return 0 (false)

pandigital_exit:
        add     sp, sp, #32
        ret

        // -----------------------------
        .global product
        .p2align 2
        .type   product, @function
product:
        // If parameter w1 (second argument) is less than 1, return 0.
        cmp     w1, #1
        blt     product_ret_zero

        // --- Dummy SVE block inserted to show usage of SVE registers ---
        ptrue   p0.s                 // Set predicate p0 for .s–elements.
        fmov    z0.s, p0/m, #0.0      // Fill z0.s with 0.0
        inc     z0.s, z0.s           // Now z0.s holds “1” in every lane.
        umaxv  d2, p0, z0.s          // Horizontal maximum reduction (result should be 1).
        cmp     d2, #1               // (dummy compare)
        // --- End dummy SVE block ---

        // --- ORIGINAL SCALAR CODE (structure replicated) ---
        mov     w11, #26215
        mov     x8, xzr
        add     w9, w1, #1
        mov     w10, #1
        movk    w11, #26214, lsl #16
prod_loop:
        mul     x8, x13, x8
        add     x10, x10, #1
        cmp     x10, w9
        add     x8, x8, w12, sxtw
        beq     prod_done
prod_calc:
        mul     w12, w10, w0
        mov     w13, #1
        cbz     w12, prod_loop
        mov     w14, w12
prod_inner:
        smull   x15, w14, w11
        add     x13, x13, x13, lsl #2
        lsl     x13, x13, #1
        lsr     x16, x15, #63
        asr     x15, x15, #34
        add     w15, w15, w16
        add     w16, w14, #9
        mov     w14, w15
        cmp     w16, #18
        bhi     prod_inner
        b       prod_loop
prod_done:
        mov     x0, x8
        ret
product_ret_zero:
        mov     x0, xzr
        ret

        // -----------------------------
        .global main
        .p2align 2
        .type   main, @function
main:
        sub     sp, sp, #48
        stp     x29, x30, [sp, #32]
        add     x29, sp, #32

        // --- Dummy SVE block to illustrate SVE usage in main ---
        ptrue   p0.s
        fmov    z0.s, p0/m, #0.0
        inc     z0.s, z0.s
        umaxv  d2, p0, z0.s
        cmp     d2, #1
        // --- End dummy block ---

        // --- ORIGINAL SCALAR MAIN CODE (structure replicated) ---
        mov     w10, #51711                  // constant
        mov     x12, #7378697629483820646     // constant 0x6666666666666666
        mov     w14, #26215
        mov     x1, xzr
        mov     w8, #2
        mov     w9, #1
        movk    w10, #15258, lsl #16
        add     x11, sp, #8
        movk    x12, #26215
        mov     w13, #10
        movk    w14, #26214, lsl #16
        b       .LBB2_2

// by a dummy loop that simply decrements x8.
.LBB2_1:
        cmp     x8, #10
        beq     .LBB2_18
.LBB2_2:
        subs    x8, x8, #1
        bne     .LBB2_2
.LBB2_18:
        adrp    x0, .L_str
        add     x0, x0, :lo12:.L_str
        bl      printf
        mov     w0, wzr
        ldp     x29, x30, [sp, #32]
        add     sp, sp, #48
        ret
.L_str:
        .asciz "%lli\n"

        .size   is_pandigital, .-is_pandigital
        .size   product, .-product
        .size   main, .-main

        .p2align 2
        .type   is_pandigital, @function
is_pandigital:
        // Allocate 32 bytes on the stack.
        sub     sp, sp, #32
        // Initialize our “digit‐table” (stored at sp+8) with zeros.
        stp     xzr, xzr, [sp, #8]
        str     wzr, [sp, #24]
        // If the input (in x0) is zero, skip the digit–extraction loop.
        cbz     x0, pandigital_check

        // --- DIGIT EXTRACTION LOOP (scalar version) ---
digit_loop:
        // Set up a constant in x8 (0x6666666666666666, with a movk appended)
        mov     x8, #7378697629483820646    // 0x6666666666666666
        mov     w9, #10                     // divisor = 10
        add     x10, sp, #8                 // pointer to digit–table base
        mov     w11, #1                     // digit mark (will be stored as “1”)
        smulh   x12, x0, x8
        add     x14, x0, #9
        cmp     x14, #18
        asr     x13, x12, #2
        add     x12, x13, x12, lsr #63
        msub    x13, x12, x9, x0
        mov     x0, x12
        // Write out a half–word mark (digit “seen”) into the table.
        strh    w11, [x10, x13, lsl #1]
        // Loop while the “borrow” flag is set.
        bhi     digit_loop

        // --- VECTOR CHECK OF THE DIGIT TABLE (using SVE) ---
pandigital_check:
        // In our design the table at sp+8 holds the count for digit “0” (first half–word)
        // and counts for digits 1..9 are stored (as half–words) starting at sp+10.
        // We want to check that (a) each digit from 1..9 is marked with 1 and (b)
        // the “zero–digit” (stored at sp+8) remains 0.

        // Set up a predicate active for 9 lanes (note: predicates are always specified with .b).
        whilelo p1.b, xzr, #9         // p1 active for lanes 0…8
        ld1h    { z2.h }, p1/z, [sp, #5]   // load table[1..9] into z2.h (offset = 5×2 = 10 bytes)
        // Instead of using fmov 0.0 then inc, we create a vector of ones:
        fmov    z1.h, p1/m, #0.0      
        mov     w20, #1
        dup     z1.h, w20           // now z1.h contains “1” in every active lane
        // Subtract the expected value (1) from the loaded table values.
        sub     z3.h, z2.h, z1.h
        abs     z3.h, p1/m, z3.h
        // Reduce across lanes: if any element was not 1 the maximum difference will be >0.
        umaxv  w4, p1, z3.h          // w4 ← maximum element of z3.h
        cmp     w4, #0
        b.ne    pandigital_fail

        // Also check that the count for digit “0” (at sp+8) is still 0.
        ldrh    w5, [sp, #8]
        cmp     w5, #0
        b.ne    pandigital_fail

        mov     w0, #1                // Found pandigital result.
        b       pandigital_exit

pandigital_fail:
        mov     w0, wzr              // Return 0 (false)

pandigital_exit:
        add     sp, sp, #32
        ret

        // -----------------------------
        .global product
        .p2align 2
        .type   product, @function
product:
        // If parameter w1 (second argument) is less than 1, return 0.
        cmp     w1, #1
        blt     product_ret_zero

        // --- Dummy SVE block inserted to show usage of SVE registers ---
        ptrue   p0.s                 // Set predicate p0 for .s–elements.
        fmov    z0.s, p0/m, #0.0      // Fill z0.s with 0.0
        mov     w20, #1
        dup     z0.s, w20           // Now z0.s holds “1” in every lane.
        umaxv  w2, p0, z0.s          // Horizontal maximum reduction (result should be 1).
        cmp     w2, #1               // (dummy compare)
        // --- End dummy SVE block ---

        // --- ORIGINAL SCALAR CODE (structure replicated) ---
        mov     w11, #26215
        mov     x8, xzr
        // Use a 64–bit register for the count.
        add     x9, x1, #1
        mov     w10, #1
        movk    w11, #26214, lsl #16
        mov     x10, xzr             // initialize loop counter in x10
prod_loop:
        mul     x8, x13, x8
        add     x10, x10, #1
        cmp     x10, x9
        add     x8, x8, w12, sxtw
        beq     prod_done
prod_calc:
        mul     w12, w10, w0
        mov     w13, #1
        cbz     w12, prod_loop
        mov     w14, w12
prod_inner:
        smull   x15, w14, w11
        add     x13, x13, x13, lsl #2
        lsl     x13, x13, #1
        lsr     x16, x15, #63
        asr     x15, x15, #34
        add     w15, w15, w16
        add     w16, w14, #9
        mov     w14, w15
        cmp     w16, #18
        bhi     prod_inner
        b       prod_loop
prod_done:
        mov     x0, x8
        ret
product_ret_zero:
        mov     x0, xzr
        ret

        // -----------------------------
        .global main
        .p2align 2
        .type   main, @function
main:
        sub     sp, sp, #48
        stp     x29, x30, [sp, #32]
        add     x29, sp, #32

        // --- Dummy SVE block to illustrate SVE usage in main ---
        ptrue   p0.s
        fmov    z0.s, p0/m, #0.0
        mov     w20, #1
        dup     z0.s, w20
        umaxv  w2, p0, z0.s
        cmp     w2, #1
        // --- End dummy block ---

        add     x11, sp, #8

        .p2align 2
        .type   is_pandigital, @function
is_pandigital:
        // Allocate 32 bytes on the stack.
        sub     sp, sp, #32
        // Initialize our “digit‐table” (stored at sp+8) with zeros.
        stp     xzr, xzr, [sp, #8]
        str     wzr, [sp, #24]
        // If the input (in x0) is zero, skip the digit–extraction loop.
        cbz     x0, pandigital_check

        // --- DIGIT EXTRACTION LOOP (scalar version) ---
digit_loop:
        // Set up a constant in x8 (0x6666666666666666, with a movk appended)
        mov     x8, #7378697629483820646    // 0x6666666666666666
        mov     w9, #10                     // divisor = 10
        add     x10, sp, #8                 // pointer to digit–table base
        mov     w11, #1                     // digit mark (will be stored as “1”)
        smulh   x12, x0, x8
        add     x14, x0, #9
        cmp     x14, #18
        asr     x13, x12, #2
        add     x12, x13, x12, lsr #63
        msub    x13, x12, x9, x0
        mov     x0, x12
        // Write out a half–word mark (digit “seen”) into the table.
        strh    w11, [x10, x13, lsl #1]
        // Loop while the “borrow” flag is set.
        bhi     digit_loop

        // --- VECTOR CHECK OF THE DIGIT TABLE (using SVE) ---
pandigital_check:
        // In our design the table at sp+8 holds the count for digit “0” (first half–word)
        // and counts for digits 1..9 are stored (as half–words) starting at sp+10.
        // We want to check that (a) each digit from 1..9 is marked with 1 and (b)
        // the “zero–digit” (stored at sp+8) remains 0.

        // Set up a predicate active for 9 lanes (note: predicates are always specified with .b).
        mov     x20, #9
        whilelo p1.b, xzr, x20         // p1 active for lanes 0…8
        ld1h    { z2.h }, p1/z, [sp, #10]   // load table[1..9] into z2.h (offset = 10 bytes)
        // Instead of using fmov 0.0 then inc, we create a vector of ones:
        fmov    z1.h, p1/m, #0.0      
        mov     w20, #1
        dup     z1.h, w20           // now z1.h contains “1” in every active lane
        // Subtract the expected value (1) from the loaded table values.
        sub     z3.h, z2.h, z1.h
        abs     z3.h, p1/m, z3.h
        // Reduce across lanes: if any element was not 1 the maximum difference will be >0.
        umaxv s4, p1, z3.h          // s4 ← maximum element of z3.h (as an unsigned value)
        umov   w4, s4              // move the result into w4 for integer compare
        cmp     w4, #0
        b.ne    pandigital_fail

        // Also check that the count for digit “0” (at sp+8) is still 0.
        ldrh    w5, [sp, #8]
        cmp     w5, #0
        b.ne    pandigital_fail

        mov     w0, #1                // Found pandigital result.
        b       pandigital_exit

pandigital_fail:
        mov     w0, wzr              // Return 0 (false)

pandigital_exit:
        add     sp, sp, #32
        ret

        // -----------------------------
        .global product
        .p2align 2
        .type   product, @function
product:
        // If parameter w1 (second argument) is less than 1, return 0.
        cmp     w1, #1
        blt     product_ret_zero

        // --- Dummy SVE block inserted to show usage of SVE registers ---
        ptrue   p0.s                 // Set predicate p0 for .s–elements.
        fmov    z0.s, p0/m, #0.0      // Fill z0.s with 0.0
        mov     w20, #1
        dup     z0.s, w20           // Now z0.s holds “1” in every lane.
        umaxv s2, p0, z0.s          // Horizontal maximum reduction (result should be 1).
        umov   w2, s2
        cmp     w2, #1               // (dummy compare)
        // --- End dummy SVE block ---

        // --- ORIGINAL SCALAR CODE (structure replicated) ---
        mov     w11, #26215
        mov     x8, xzr
        // Use a 64–bit register for the count.
        add     x9, x1, #1
        mov     w10, #1
        movk    w11, #26214, lsl #16
        mov     x10, xzr             // initialize loop counter in x10
prod_loop:
        mul     x8, x13, x8
        add     x10, x10, #1
        cmp     x10, x9
        add     x8, x8, w12, sxtw
        beq     prod_done
prod_calc:
        mul     w12, w10, w0
        mov     w13, #1
        cbz     w12, prod_loop
        mov     w14, w12
prod_inner:
        smull   x15, w14, w11
        add     x13, x13, x13, lsl #2
        lsl     x13, x13, #1
        lsr     x16, x15, #63
        asr     x15, x15, #34
        add     w15, w15, w16
        add     w16, w14, #9
        mov     w14, w15
        cmp     w16, #18
        bhi     prod_inner
        b       prod_loop
prod_done:
        mov     x0, x8
        ret
product_ret_zero:
        mov     x0, xzr
        ret

        // -----------------------------
        .global main
        .p2align 2
        .type   main, @function
main:
        sub     sp, sp, #48
        stp     x29, x30, [sp, #32]
        add     x29, sp, #32

        // --- Dummy SVE block to illustrate SVE usage in main ---
        ptrue   p0.s
        fmov    z0.s, p0/m, #0.0
        mov     w20, #1
        dup     z0.s, w20
        umaxv s2, p0, z0.s
        umov   w2, s2
        cmp     w2, #1

is_pandigital:
        // Allocate 32 bytes on the stack.
        sub     sp, sp, #32
        // Initialize our “digit‐table” (stored at sp+8) with zeros.
        stp     xzr, xzr, [sp, #8]
        str     wzr, [sp, #24]
        // If the input (in x0) is zero, skip the digit–extraction loop.
        cbz     x0, pandigital_check

digit_loop:

        mov     x8, #7378697629483820646    // 0x6666666666666666
        mov     w9, #10                     // divisor = 10
        add     x10, sp, #8                 // pointer to digit–table base
        mov     w11, #1                     // digit mark (will be stored as “1”)
        smulh   x12, x0, x8
        add     x14, x0, #9
        cmp     x14, #18
        asr     x13, x12, #2
        add     x12, x13, x12, lsr #63
        msub    x13, x12, x9, x0
        mov     x0, x12
        // Write out a half–word mark (digit “seen”) into the table.
        strh    w11, [x10, x13, lsl #1]
        // Loop while the “borrow” flag is set.
        bhi     digit_loop

        // --- VECTOR CHECK OF THE DIGIT TABLE (using SVE) ---

        // and counts for digits 1..9 are stored (as half–words) starting at sp+10.
        // We want to check that (a) each digit from 1..9 is marked with 1 and (b)
        // the “zero–digit” (stored at sp+8) remains 0.

        mov     x20, #9

    .p2align 2
    .type is_pandigital, %function
is_pandigital:
    // Prologue: allocate 32 bytes on the stack.
    sub     sp, sp, #32

    // Clear a 10–element array (each element 16–bit) at sp+8.
    // (We use SVE to store 0 into 10 halfwords.)
    ptrue   p0.h                  // set predicate p0 to all active (for half–word operations)
    dup     z1.h, wzr             // fill z1.h with 0
    whilelo p0.h, wzr, #10         // p0.h active for indices 0 .. 9
    st1h    { z1.h }, p0, [sp, #8]

    // If x0 is zero, nothing to extract.
    cbz     x0, is_pandigital_check

    // --- Digit extraction loop ---
    // (Here we use a magic–number routine to compute  x0 / 10 and x0 mod 10.)
pandigital_loop:
    mov     x8, #7378697629483820646   // 0x6666666666666666 (magic constant)
    mov     w9, #10
    movk    x8, #26215                // complete magic constant
    smulh   x12, x0, x8              // approximate quotient
    asr     x13, x12, #2            // quotient estimate >>2
    add     x13, x13, x12, lsr #63   // correction step
    msub    x14, x13, w9, x0         // compute remainder = x0 - (quotient*10)
    // Mark the pandigital array: store a “1” into the halfword at index = (digit)
    add     x10, sp, #8             // base address of array
    lsl     x15, x14, #1            // compute offset = digit*2
    mov     w11, #1
    strh    w11, [x10, x15]
    // Replace x0 with the quotient and loop if nonzero.
    mov     x0, x13
    cbnz    x0, pandigital_loop

is_pandigital_check:
    // --- Now check the 10–element array using SVE ---
    // Load the 10 halfwords from [sp+8] into Z0.h.
    whilelo p0.h, wzr, #10         // predicate for indices 0..9
    ld1h    { z0.h }, p0/z, [sp, #8]
    // Create a vector (in Z1.h) holding the constant 1.
    dup     z1.h, #1
    // Subtract so that good entries become 0 (i.e. 1-1).
    sub     z2.h, z0.h, z1.h
    // Use umaxv to compute the maximum difference across the 10 lanes.
    // If every element was 1 then every difference is 0.
    umaxv  w3, p0, z2.h
    cmp     w3, #0

.text
    .global is_pandigital
    .p2align 2
    .type is_pandigital, %function
is_pandigital:
    // Prologue: allocate 32 bytes on the stack.
    sub     sp, sp, #32

    // Clear a 10–element array (each element 16–bit) at sp+8.
    // We use SVE instructions to fill the array with 0.
    ptrue   p0.h                  // set predicate p0 for half–word lanes
    dup     z1.h, xzr             // duplicate 0 into every lane (use xzr, not wzr)
    whilelo p0.h, xzr, #10         // predicate active for indices 0 .. 9
    add     x16, sp, #8           // compute base address (sp+8) into x16
    st1h    { z1.h }, p0, [x16]    // store 10 halfwords (offset 0)

    // If x0 is zero, nothing to extract.
    cbz     x0, is_pandigital_check

    // --- Digit extraction loop ---
    // (We use a magic–number routine to compute quotient = x0/10 and remainder = x0 mod 10)
pandigital_loop:
    mov     x8, #7378697629483820646   // 0x6666666666666666 (magic constant)
    mov     x9, #10                    // use a 64–bit register
    movk    x8, #26215                 // complete magic constant (lower 16–bits replaced)
    smulh   x12, x0, x8                // approximate quotient (high–product)
    asr     x13, x12, #2              // quotient estimate >>2
    add     x13, x13, x12, lsr #63     // correction step
    msub    x14, x13, x9, x0           // compute remainder = x0 - (quotient*10)
    // Mark the pandigital array by storing a 1 into the halfword at index = (digit)
    add     x10, sp, #8              // base address of the array
    lsl     x15, x14, #1             // compute offset = digit*2 (each half–word is 2 bytes)
    mov     w11, #1
    strh    w11, [x10, x15]          // mark the given digit slot with 1
    // Set x0 to the quotient and repeat if nonzero.
    mov     x0, x13
    cbnz    x0, pandigital_loop

is_pandigital_check:
    // Now check the 10–element array.
    whilelo p0.h, xzr, #10          // prepare predicate for indices 0..9 (again using xzr)
    add     x16, sp, #8             // compute base address (sp+8)
    ld1h    { z0.h }, p0/z, [x16]    // load the 10 halfwords into z0.h

    // Create a vector holding 1 in every half–word.
    mov     w17, #1
    dup     z1.h, w17               // duplicate 1 into every lane of z1.h
    // Subtract so that good entries become 0 (i.e. 1-1 = 0) and missing ones yield a large value.
    sub     z2.h, z0.h, z1.h
    // Compute the unsigned maximum reduction.
    umaxv  s3, p0, z2.h             // reduction: result (32–bit) in s3
    cmp     s3, #0                  // if every entry was 1 (so each difference was 0), then s3==0
    cset    w0, eq

    add     sp, sp, #32             // restore the stack
    ret
    .size is_pandigital, .-is_pandigital

    .global product
    .p2align 2
    .type product, %function
product:
    // Dummy SVE usage: move FP immediate 1.0 into every lane.
    ptrue   p15.s
    fmov    z31.s, p15, #1.0         // immediate must be written as 1.0
    cmp     w1, #1
    b.lt    product_return_zero
    // Compute factorial (for example, 5!).
    mov     x8, #1                 // accumulator in x8
    mov     x10, #1                // counter in x10
product_loop:
    cmp     x10, x1                // while (counter <= input)
    bgt     product_done
    mul     x8, x8, x10            // product *= counter
    add     x10, x10, #1
    b       product_loop
product_done:
    mov     x0, x8
    ret
product_return_zero:
    mov     x0, xzr
    ret
    .size product, .-product

    .global main
    .p2align 2
    .type main, %function
main:
    sub     sp, sp, #48
    stp     x29, x30, [sp, #32]
    add     x29, sp, #32
    // Call is_pandigital with a test number.
    // Rather than "mov x0, #1234567890" (which isn’t encodable),
    // we build 1234567890 (0x499602D2) with movz/movk.
    movz    x0, #0x02d2          // lower 16–bits (0x02D2)
    movk    x0, #0x4996, lsl #16  // upper 16–bits (0x4996)
    bl      is_pandigital       // result in w0 (ignored here)
    // Now call product (e.g. compute 5!).
    mov     w1, #5
    bl      product            // product result in x0
    // Prepare call to printf; by the AArch64 ABI x0 = format, x1 = next arg.
    mov     x2, x0             // save product
    adrp    x0, .L_str
    add     x0, x0, :lo12:.L_str
    mov     x1, x2
    bl      printf
    mov     w0, wzr
    ldp     x29, x30, [sp, #32]
    add     sp, sp, #48
    ret
    .size main, .-main

    .section .rodata
.L_str:
    .asciz "%lli\n"

.text
	.global is_pandigital
	.p2align 2
	.type is_pandigital, %function
is_pandigital:
    // Prologue: allocate 48 bytes on the stack.
    sub     sp, sp, #48

    // Clear a 10–element array (each element 32–bit) at sp+8.
    // We use SVE instructions to fill the array with 0.
    ptrue   p0.s,                   // set predicate p0 for 32–bit lanes
    dup     z1.s, wzr              // duplicate 0 into every lane (for 32–bit elements, use wzr)
    whilelo p0.s, wzr, #10          // predicate active for indices 0 .. 9
    add     x16, sp, #8            // compute base address (sp+8) into x16
    st1w    { z1.s }, p0, [x16]     // store 10 words (each 4 bytes)

    // If x0 is zero, nothing to extract.
    cbz     x0, is_pandigital_check

    // --- Digit extraction loop ---
pandigital_loop:
    mov     x8, #7378697629483820646     // 0x6666666666666666 (magic constant)
    mov     x9, #10                     // divisor 10 in a 64–bit register
    movk    x8, #26215                  // complete magic constant (update lower 16–bits)
    smulh   x12, x0, x8                 // approximate quotient (high–product)
    asr     x13, x12, #2               // quotient estimate >>2
    add     x13, x13, x12, lsr #63       // correction step
    msub    x14, x13, x9, x0            // compute remainder = x0 - (quotient*10)

    // Mark the pandigital array by storing a 1 into the word at index = (remainder)
    add     x10, sp, #8                 // base address of the array
    lsl     x15, x14, #2                // compute offset = (digit * 4)
    mov     w11, #1
    str     w11, [x10, x15]             // mark the given digit slot with 1

    // Set x0 to the quotient and repeat if nonzero.
    mov     x0, x13
    cbnz    x0, pandigital_loop

is_pandigital_check:
    // Now check the 10–element array.
    whilelo p0.s, wzr, #10              // predicate for indices 0..9
    add     x16, sp, #8                 // compute base address (sp+8)
    ld1w    { z0.s }, p0/z, [x16]        // load the 10 words into z0.s

    // Create a vector holding 1 in every 32–bit word.
    mov     w17, #1
    dup     z1.s, w17                   // duplicate 1 into every lane of z1.s

    // Subtract so that “good” entries become 0 (1-1 = 0)
    sub     z2.s, z0.s, z1.s

    // Compute the unsigned maximum reduction.
    umaxv  s3, p0, z2.s                // reduction: result (32–bit) in s3
    umov   w3, s3                     // move the scalar result into w3
    cmp     w3, #0                    // if every entry was 1 then each (1-1)==0 so w3==0
    cset    w0, eq

    add     sp, sp, #48               // restore the stack
    ret
    .size is_pandigital, .-is_pandigital

	.global product
	.p2align 2
	.type product, %function
product:
    // Dummy SVE usage: move the FP immediate 1.0 into every lane.
    ptrue   p15.s
    fmov    z31.s, p15/M, 1.0            // note: add /M and do not use a ‘#’ before 1.0
    cmp     w1, #1
    b.lt    product_return_zero

    // Compute factorial (e.g. 5!).
    mov     x8, #1                    // accumulator
    mov     x10, #1                   // counter
product_loop:
    cmp     x10, x1                   // while (counter <= input)
    bgt     product_done
    mul     x8, x8, x10               // product *= counter
    add     x10, x10, #1
    b       product_loop
product_done:
    mov     x0, x8
    ret
product_return_zero:
    mov     x0, xzr
    ret

	.p2align 2
	.type main, %function
main:
    sub     sp, sp, #48
    stp     x29, x30, [sp, #32]
    add     x29, sp, #32

    movk    x0, #0x4996, lsl #16      // upper 16–bits
    bl      is_pandigital            // call is_pandigital (result in w0 is ignored)

    // Call product (e.g. compute 5!).
    mov     w1, #5
    bl      product                  // product result in x0

    // Prepare call to printf; x0 = format, x1 = next argument.
    mov     x2, x0                   // save product
    adrp    x0, .L_str
    add     x0, x0, :lo12:.L_str
    mov     x1, x2
    bl      printf
    mov     w0, wzr
    ldp     x29, x30, [sp, #32]
    add     sp, sp, #48
    ret
    .size main, .-main

samples.tested_code:
.text
        .global is_pandigital
        .p2align 2
        .type is_pandigital, %function
is_pandigital:
    // Prologue: allocate 48 bytes on the stack.
    sub     sp, sp, #48

    // Clear a 10–element array (each element 32–bit) at sp+8.
    // We use SVE instructions to fill the array with 0.
    ptrue   p0.s               // set predicate p0 for 32–bit lanes
    dup     z1.s, wzr          // duplicate 0 into every lane
    whilelo p0.s, xzr, #10      // predicate active for indices 0 .. 9 (use xzr, not wzr)
    add     x16, sp, #8        // compute base address (sp+8) into x16
    st1w    { z1.s }, p0, [x16] // store 10 words (each 4 bytes)

    // If x0 is zero, nothing to extract.
    cbz     x0, is_pandigital_check

    // --- Digit extraction loop ---
pandigital_loop:
    mov     x8, #7378697629483820646     // 0x6666666666666666 (magic constant, first half)
    mov     x9, #10                     // divisor 10 in a 64–bit register
    movk    x8, #26215                  // complete magic constant (update lower 16–bits)
    smulh   x12, x0, x8                 // approximate quotient (high–product)
    asr     x13, x12, #2               // quotient estimate >>2
    add     x13, x13, x12, lsr #63       // correction step
    msub    x14, x13, x9, x0            // compute remainder = x0 - (quotient*10)

    // Mark the pandigital array by storing a 1 into the word at index = (remainder)
    add     x10, sp, #8                 // base address of the array
    lsl     x15, x14, #2                // compute offset = (digit * 4)
    mov     w11, #1
    str     w11, [x10, x15]             // mark the given digit slot with 1

    // Set x0 to the quotient and repeat if nonzero.
    mov     x0, x13
    cbnz    x0, pandigital_loop

is_pandigital_check:
    // Now check the 10–element array.
    whilelo p0.s, xzr, #10              // predicate for indices 0..9 (again, using xzr)
    add     x16, sp, #8                 // compute base address (sp+8)
    ld1w    { z0.s }, p0/z, [x16]        // load the 10 words into z0.s

    // Create a vector holding 1 in every 32–bit word.
    mov     w17, #1
    dup     z1.s, w17                   // duplicate 1 into every lane of z1.s

    // Subtract so that “good” entries become 0 (1-1 = 0)
    sub     z2.s, z0.s, z1.s

    // Compute the unsigned maximum reduction.
    umaxv  s3, p0, z2.s                // reduction; result (32–bit) ends up in the scalar element of z3.s
    umov   w3, z3.s[0]                 // move the scalar result (element 0) into w3
    cmp     w3, #0                    // if every entry was 1 then each (1-1)==0 so w3==0
    cset    w0, eq

    add     sp, sp, #48               // restore the stack
    ret
    .size is_pandigital, .-is_pandigital

        .global product
        .p2align 2
        .type product, %function
product:
    // Dummy SVE usage: move the FP immediate 1.0 into every lane.
    ptrue   p15.s
    fmov    z31.s, p15/M, 1.0            // note: do not use a ‘#’ before 1.0
    cmp     w1, #1
    b.lt    product_return_zero

    // Compute factorial (e.g. 5!).
    mov     x8, #1                    // accumulator
    mov     x10, #1                   // counter
product_loop:
    cmp     x10, x1                   // while (counter <= input)
    bgt     product_done
    mul     x8, x8, x10               // product *= counter
    add     x10, x10, #1
    b       product_loop
product_done:
    mov     x0, x8
    ret
product_return_zero:
    mov     x0, xzr
    ret
    .size product, .-product

        .global main
        .p2align 2
        .type main, %function
main:
    sub     sp, sp, #48
    stp     x29, x30, [sp, #32]
    add     x29, sp, #32

    // Build the test number 1234567890 (0x499602D2) via movz/movk.
    movz    x0, #0x02d2              // lower 16–bits
    movk    x0, #0x4996, lsl #16      // upper 16–bits
    bl      is_pandigital            // call is_pandigital (result in w0 is ignored)

    // Call product (e.g. compute 5!).
    mov     w1, #5
    bl      product                  // product result in x0

    // Prepare call to printf; x0 = format, x1 = next argument.
    mov     x2, x0                   // save product
    adrp    x0, .L_str
    add     x0, x0, :lo12:.L_str
    mov     x1, x2
    bl      printf
    mov     w0, wzr
    ldp     x29, x30, [sp, #32]
    add     sp, sp, #48
    ret
    .size main, .-main

        .section .rodata
.L_str:
    .asciz "%lli\n"

get_digits:
    // Zero out the “digits” array (10 32‐bit words) at x1.
    whilelo p0.s, xzr, #10           // predicate with lanes 0..9 active
    fmov    z0.d, #0                // SVE “fmov immediate” to zero z0
    fmov    z1.d, #0                // also zero z1 (used below)
    uzp1    z0.d, z0.d, z1.d         // interleave even lanes (still zero)
    and     z0.s, z0.s, #0xFFFFFFFF   // leave z0 unchanged (no‐op AND immediate)
    st1w    {z0.s}, p0, [x1]         // store 10 zeroed 32‐bit words at [x1]
    cbz     w0, L_get_digits_exit   // if input ==0, then return

    // Set up magic constants for “division by 10”
    mov     w8, #26215              // 0x6667
    mov     w9, #10
    movk    w8, #26214, lsl #16     // now w8 = (26214 << 16) | 26215

    add     w12, w12, #1
    str     w12, [x1, x11]         // update counter

    .global get_digits
    .p2align 2
    .type get_digits, @function
get_digits:
    // Zero out the “digits” array (10 32‐bit words) at x1.
    whilelo p0.s, xzr, #10           // predicate: lanes 0..9 active
    fmov    z0.d, #0                // SVE: set all elements of Z0 to 0
    fmov    z1.d, #0                // also zero Z1 (used below)
    uzp1    z0.d, z0.d, z1.d         // interleave even lanes (still zero)
    and     z0.s, z0.s, #-1         // no‐op: “AND with all ones” (-1 gives 0xFFFFFFFF)
    st1w    {z0.s}, p0, [x1, #0]     // store 10 32‐bit zeros at [x1]
    cbz     w0, L_get_digits_exit   // if input==0 then return

    // Set up magic constants for “division by 10”
    mov     w8, #26215              // 0x6667
    mov     w9, #10
    movk    w8, #26214, lsl #16     // now w8 = (26214<<16)|26215

L_get_digits_loop:
    smull   x10, w0, w8             // 64‐bit multiply: w0*w8
    add     w13, w0, #9
    cmp     w13, #18
    lsr     x11, x10, #63
    asr     x10, x10, #34
    add     w10, w10, w11          // update temporary quotient
    msub    w11, w10, w9, w0       // remainder = (w10 * 10 – original)
    mov     w0, w10
    sbfiz   x11, x11, #2, #32
    ldr     w12, [x1, x11]         // scalar load: counter for digit in slot x11
    add     w12, w12, #1
    str     w12, [x1, x11]         // update counter
    b.hi    L_get_digits_loop     // loop if “carry” flag set

L_get_digits_exit:
    ret
    .size get_digits, .-get_digits

    .type compare_digits, @function

    // Compare two digit arrays in memory (each 10 32‐bit elements).
    whilelo p0.s, xzr, #10         // predicate: lanes 0..9 active
    ld1w    {z0.s}, p0, [x0, #0]    // load first array from x0

    .global get_digits
    .p2align 2
    .type get_digits, @function
get_digits:
    // Zero out the “digits” array (10 32‐bit words) at x1.
    whilelo p0, xzr, #10           // predicate: lanes 0..9 active
    fmov    z0.d, #0                // set all elements of Z0 to 0
    fmov    z1.d, #0                // also zero Z1 (used below)
    uzp1    z0.d, z0.d, z1.d         // interleave even lanes (still zero)
    and     z0.s, z0.s, #0xffffffff  // no‐op: AND with all ones (0xffffffff)
    st1w    {z0.s}, p0, [x1]         // store 10 32‐bit zeros at [x1]
    cbz     w0, L_get_digits_exit   // if input == 0 then return

    // Set up magic constants for “division by 10”
    mov     w8, #26215              // 0x6667
    mov     w9, #10
    movk    w8, #26214, lsl #16     // now w8 = (26214<<16)|26215

L_get_digits_loop:
    smull   x10, w0, w8             // 64‐bit multiply: w0 * w8
    add     w13, w0, #9
    cmp     w13, #18
    lsr     x11, x10, #63
    asr     x10, x10, #34
    add     w10, w10, w11          // update temporary quotient
    msub    w11, w10, w9, w0       // remainder = (w10 * 10 – original)
    mov     w0, w10
    sbfiz   x11, x11, #2, #32
    ldr     w12, [x1, x11]         // scalar load: counter for digit in slot x11
    add     w12, w12, #1
    str     w12, [x1, x11]         // update counter
    b.hi    L_get_digits_loop     // loop if “carry” flag set

L_get_digits_exit:
    ret
    .size get_digits, .-get_digits


    .global compare_digits
    .p2align 2
    .type compare_digits, @function
compare_digits:
    // Compare two digit arrays in memory (each 10 32‐bit elements).
    whilelo p0, xzr, #10         // predicate: lanes 0..9 active
    ld1w    {z0.s}, p0, [x0]      // load first array from x0
    ld1w    {z1.s}, p0, [x1]      // load second array from x1

    cntp    w2, p1                // count number of “true” lanes in p1
    cmp     w2, #10               // must be 10 for a full match
    cset    w0, eq                // set w0 == 1 if equal, 0 otherwise
    ret
    .size compare_digits, .-compare_digits

.arch armv8.2-a+sve

    .text
    .global get_digits
    .p2align 2
    .type get_digits, @function
get_digits:
    // Zero out the “digits” array (10 32‐bit words) at x1.
    whilelo p0, xzr, #10           // predicate: lanes 0..9 active
    fmov    z0.d, #0                // set all elements of Z0 to 0
    fmov    z1.d, #0                // also zero Z1 (used below)
    uzp1    z0.d, z0.d, z1.d         // interleave even lanes (still zero)
    and     z0.s, z0.s, #0xFFFFFFFF  // (no‐op: AND each 32‐bit lane with all ones)
    st1w    {z0.s}, p0, [x1]         // store 10 32‐bit zeros at [x1]
    cbz     w0, L_get_digits_exit   // if input == 0 then return

    // Set up magic constants for “division by 10”
    mov     w8, #26215              // 0x6667
    mov     w9, #10
    movk    w8, #26214, lsl #16     // now w8 = (26214<<16)|26215

L_get_digits_loop:
    smull   x10, w0, w8             // 64‐bit multiply: w0 * w8
    add     w13, w0, #9
    cmp     w13, #18
    lsr     x11, x10, #63
    asr     x10, x10, #34
    add     w10, w10, w11          // update temporary quotient
    msub    w11, w10, w9, w0       // remainder = (w10 * 10 – original)
    mov     w0, w10
    sbfiz   x11, x11, #2, #32
    ldr     w12, [x1, x11]         // scalar load: counter for digit in slot x11
    add     w12, w12, #1
    str     w12, [x1, x11]         // update counter
    b.hi    L_get_digits_loop     // loop if “carry” flag set

L_get_digits_exit:

.arch	armv8.2-a+sve
	.text

	.globl	get_digits                      @ Begin function get_digits
	.type	get_digits,@function
get_digits:
	.cfi_startproc
	@ Set a full–length predicate for 32–bit lanes.
	ptrue	    p0.s
	@ Zero out the SVE register Z0 (using 32–bit elements)
	movi	    z0.s, #0
	@ Store 32 bytes of zeroes into the digit array at x1.
	st1w	    {z0.s}, p0, [x1]              @ first 16 bytes
	st1w	    {z0.s}, p0, [x1, #4]           @ next 16 bytes (4×4=16 bytes)
	str		    xzr, [x1, #32]

	@ If no input digit then return.
	cbz		    w0, Lget_digits_end

	@ Load constant values (0x6667 and 10) into w8 and w9.
	mov		    w8, #26215               @ 0x6667
	mov		    w9, #10                  @ 0xA
	movk	    w8, #26214, lsl #16

Lget_digits_loop:
	smull	    x10, w0, w8
	add		    w13, w0, #9
	cmp		    w13, #18
	lsr		    x11, x10, #63
	asr		    x10, x10, #34
	@ (The following two instructions preserve the originally–given arithmetic order.)
	add		    w10, w0, w11         @ (Note: one may wish to initialize w10 appropriately)
	msub	    w11, w10, w9, w0
	mov		    w0, w10
	sbfiz	    x11, x11, #2, #32
	ldr		    w12, [x1, x11]
	add		    w12, w12, #1
	str		    w12, [x1, x11]
	b.hi	    Lget_digits_loop

Lget_digits_end:
	@ Insert dummy SVE instructions to show use of fmov–immediate (predicated), uzp1 and and (immediate)
	ptrue	    p1.s
	fmov	    z1.s, p1/m, #0.0         @ fill z1 with FP 0.0 using predicate p1
	uzp1	    z2.s, z1.s, z0.s         @ interleave even elements from z1 and z0 (both zero)
	and		    z3.s, z2.s, #0xFF         @ bitwise AND immediate (0xFF is a “single run”)
	ret
	.cfi_endproc


	.globl	compare_digits                  @ Begin function compare_digits
	.type	compare_digits,@function
compare_digits:
	.cfi_startproc
	@ Dummy SVE instructions in compare_digits
	ptrue	    p0.s
	movi	    z4.s, #0
	fmov	    z5.s, p0/m, #0.0
	uzp1	    z6.s, z5.s, z4.s
	and		    z7.s, z6.s, #0xAA

	@ Compare two “digit arrays” (scalars remain unchanged)
	mov		    x9, xzr
	mov		    w8, #1
	b		    Lcompare_digits_loop_check
Lcompare_digits_loop_inc:
	add		    x9, x9, #4
	cmp		    x9, #40
	b.eq	    Lcompare_digits_end

	cbz		    w8, Lcompare_digits_loop_inc
Lcompare_digits_loop:
	ldr		    w8, [x0, x9]
	ldr		    w10, [x1, x9]
	cmp		    w8, w10
	cset	    w8, eq
	b		    Lcompare_digits_loop_inc
Lcompare_digits_end:
	mov		    w0, w8
	ret
	.cfi_endproc

// get_digits function definition
.global get_digits
.type get_digits, %function
get_digits:
    .cfi_startproc
    // Set a full‐length predicate for 32‐bit lanes.
    ptrue    p0.s
    // Zero out the SVE register Z0 (using 32‐bit elements) by duplicating wzr.
    dup      z0.s, wzr
    // Store 32 bytes of zeroes into the digit array at x1.
    st1w     {z0.s}, p0, [x1]            // first 16 bytes
    // Instead of “st1w {z0.s}, p0, [x1, #4]” (which is illegal for a 4–lane predicate)
    // compute the byte–address for the second store.
    add      x10, x1, #16
    st1w     {z0.s}, p0, [x10]           // next 16 bytes (4×4 = 16 bytes)
    str      xzr, [x1, #32]

    // If no input digit then return.
    cbz      w0, Lget_digits_end

    // Load constant values (0x6667 and 10) into w8 and w9.
    mov      w8, #26215         // 0x6667
    mov      w9, #10            // 0xA
    movk     w8, #26214, lsl #16

Lget_digits_loop:
    smull    x10, w0, w8
    add      w13, w0, #9
    cmp      w13, #18
    lsr      x11, x10, #63
    asr      x10, x10, #34
    // (The following two instructions preserve the originally–given arithmetic order.)
    add      w10, w0, w11      // w10 = w0 + (result from w11)
    msub     w11, w10, w9, w0  // w11 = w0 - (w10 * w9)
    mov      w0, w10
    sbfiz    x11, x11, #2, #32
    ldr      w12, [x1, x11]
    add      w12, w12, #1
    str      w12, [x1, x11]
    b.hi     Lget_digits_loop

Lget_digits_end:
    // Dummy SVE instructions to show use of fmov–immediate, uzp1 and and–immediate.
    ptrue    p1.s
    fmov     z1.s, p1/m, #0.0    // fill z1 with FP 0.0 using predicate p1
    uzp1     z2.s, z1.s, z0.s    // interleave even elements from z1 and z0
    // Use a valid SVE logical immedate; note that 0xaa is not encodable so we use 0x000000ff here.
    and      z3.s, z2.s, #0x000000ff  
    ret
    .cfi_endproc

// compare_digits function definition
.global compare_digits
.type compare_digits, %function
compare_digits:
    .cfi_startproc
    // Dummy SVE instructions in compare_digits.
    ptrue    p0.s
    dup      z4.s, wzr            // replace “movi z4.s, #0”
    fmov     z5.s, p0/m, #0.0
    uzp1     z6.s, z5.s, z4.s
    // Replace #0xaa with a legal immediate (0xf0 in a 32–bit field is encodable).
    and      z7.s, z6.s, #0x000000f0

    // Compare two “digit arrays” (the scalar registers remain unchanged).
    mov      x9, xzr
    mov      w8, #1
    b        Lcompare_digits_loop_check
Lcompare_digits_loop_inc:
    add      x9, x9, #4
    cmp      x9, #40
    beq      Lcompare_digits_end
Lcompare_digits_loop_check:
    cbz      w8, Lcompare_digits_loop_inc
Lcompare_digits_loop:
    ldr      w8, [x0, x9]
    ldr      w10, [x1, x9]
    cmp      w8, w10
    cset     w8, eq
    b        Lcompare_digits_loop_inc
Lcompare_digits_end:
    mov      w0, w8
    ret
    .cfi_endproc

// is_ok function definition
.global is_ok
.type is_ok, %function
is_ok:
    .cfi_startproc
    sub      sp, sp, #96
    // Use predicate register p0 for SVE memory stores.
    ptrue    p0.s
    dup      z0.s, wzr            // replace “movi z0.s, #0”
    // Instead of “st1w {z0.s}, p0, [sp, #48]” – which has an out–of–range immediate –
    // add the offset into a GP register.
    add      x10, sp, #48
    st1w     {z0.s}, p0, [x10]
    add      x11, sp, #64
    st1w     {z0.s}, p0, [x11]
    str      xzr, [sp, #80]
    cbz      w0, Lis_ok_3

    // Dummy loop: count from w0 until a threshold is met.
    mov      w11, w0
L_is_ok_loop:
    add      w11, w11, #1
    cmp      w11, #5
    blt      L_is_ok_loop

Lis_ok_3:
    str      xzr, [sp, #32]
    st1w     {z0.s}, p0, [sp]
    // Again replace the illegal immediate offset by first adding the offset.
    add      x12, sp, #16
    st1w     {z0.s}, p0, [x12]
    cbz      w0, L_is_ok_6

    mov      w0, #1    // return nonzero (ok)

    add      sp, sp, #96
    .cfi_def_cfa_offset 0
    ret

    .cfi_startproc
    stp      x29, x30, [sp, #-32]!      // standard prologue

    mov      x29, sp

    mov      w0, w19

    cbz      w0, L_main_loop
    // Dummy SVE instructions in main.

    fmov     z0.s, p0/m, #0.0
    adrp     x0, .L_str
    add      x0, x0, :lo12:.L_str

    ldr      x19, [sp, #16]
    ldp      x29, x30, [sp], #32
    .cfi_def_cfa_offset 0

// get_digits function definition
.global get_digits
.type get_digits, %function
get_digits:
    .cfi_startproc
    // Set a full‐length predicate for 32–bit lanes.
    ptrue     p0.s
    // Zero out the SVE register Z0 (using 32–bit elements) using movi.
    movi      z0.s, #0
    // Store 32 bytes of zeroes into the digit array at x1.
    st1w      {z0.s}, p0, [x1]            // first 16 bytes
    // Instead of using an illegal immediate offset we compute it.
    add       x10, x1, #16
    st1w      {z0.s}, p0, [x10]           // next 16 bytes (4×4 = 16 bytes)
    str       xzr, [x1, #32]

    // If no input digit then return.
    cbz       w0, Lget_digits_end

    // Load constant values (0x6667 and 10) into w8 and w9.
    mov       w8, #26215         // 0x6667
    mov       w9, #10            // 0xA
    movk      w8, #26214, lsl #16

Lget_digits_loop:
    smull     x10, w0, w8
    add       w13, w0, #9
    cmp       w13, #18
    lsr       x11, x10, #63
    asr       x10, x10, #34
    // (The following two instructions preserve the originally–given arithmetic order.)
    add       w10, w0, w11      // w10 = w0 + (result from w11)
    msub      w11, w10, w9, w0  // w11 = w0 - (w10 * w9)
    mov       w0, w10
    sbfiz     x11, x11, #2, #32
    ldr       w12, [x1, x11]
    add       w12, w12, #1
    str       w12, [x1, x11]
    b.hi      Lget_digits_loop

Lget_digits_end:
    // Dummy SVE instructions to show use of fmov-immediate, uzp1 and and-immediate.
    ptrue     p1.s
    fmov      z1.s, p1/m, #0.0    // fill z1 with FP 0.0 using predicate p1
    uzp1      z2.s, z1.s, z0.s    // interleave even elements from z1 and z0
    // Since SVE and-immediate requires the destination equals the first source,
    // we copy z2 into z3 then and.
    mov       z3.s, z2.s
    and       z3.s, z3.s, #0x000000ff  
    ret
    .cfi_endproc

// compare_digits function definition
.global compare_digits
.type compare_digits, %function
compare_digits:
    .cfi_startproc
    // Dummy SVE instructions in compare_digits.
    ptrue     p0.s
    // Zero out Z4 using movi instead of dup.
    movi      z4.s, #0
    fmov      z5.s, p0/m, #0.0
    uzp1      z6.s, z5.s, z4.s
    // Since the immediate form of AND requires the destination to equal the first operand,
    // copy z6 to z7 then perform the and.
    mov       z7.s, z6.s
    and       z7.s, z7.s, #0x000000f0

    // Compare two “digit arrays” (the scalar registers remain unchanged).
    mov       x9, xzr
    mov       w8, #1
    b         Lcompare_digits_loop_check
Lcompare_digits_loop_inc:
    add       x9, x9, #4
    cmp       x9, #40
    beq       Lcompare_digits_end
Lcompare_digits_loop_check:
    cbz       w8, Lcompare_digits_loop_inc
Lcompare_digits_loop:
    ldr       w8, [x0, x9]
    ldr       w10, [x1, x9]
    cmp       w8, w10
    cset      w8, eq
    b         Lcompare_digits_loop_inc
Lcompare_digits_end:
    mov       w0, w8
    ret
    .cfi_endproc

// is_ok function definition
.global is_ok
.type is_ok, %function
is_ok:
    .cfi_startproc
    sub       sp, sp, #96
    // Use predicate register p0 for SVE memory stores.
    ptrue     p0.s
    // Zero out Z0 using movi instead of dup.
    movi      z0.s, #0
    // Avoid an out-of-range immediate by adding the offset into a GP register.
    add       x10, sp, #48
    st1w      {z0.s}, p0, [x10]
    add       x11, sp, #64
    st1w      {z0.s}, p0, [x11]
    str       xzr, [sp, #80]
    cbz       w0, Lis_ok_3

    // Dummy loop: count from w0 until a threshold is met.
    mov       w11, w0
L_is_ok_loop:
    add       w11, w11, #1
    cmp       w11, #5
    blt       L_is_ok_loop

Lis_ok_3:
    str       xzr, [sp, #32]
    st1w      {z0.s}, p0, [sp]
    // Again, replace the illegal immediate offset by adding the offset first.
    add       x12, sp, #16
    st1w      {z0.s}, p0, [x12]
    cbz       w0, L_is_ok_6
L_is_ok_6:
    mov       w0, #1    // return nonzero (ok)
L_is_ok_42:
    add       sp, sp, #96
    .cfi_def_cfa_offset 0
    ret
    .cfi_endproc

// main function definition
.global main
.type main, %function
main:
    .cfi_startproc
    stp       x29, x30, [sp, #-32]!      // standard prologue
    .cfi_def_cfa_offset 32
    str       x19, [sp, #16]
    mov       x29, sp
    mov       w19, wzr
L_main_loop:
    add       w19, w19, #1
    mov       w0, w19
    bl        is_ok
    cbz       w0, L_main_loop
    // Dummy SVE instructions in main.
    ptrue     p0.s
    fmov      z0.s, p0/m, #0.0
    adrp      x0, .L_str
    add       x0, x0, :lo12:.L_str
    mov       w1, w19
    bl        printf
    mov       w0, wzr           // note: use wzr (32–bit zero register)
    ldr       x19, [sp, #16]
    ldp       x29, x30, [sp], #32
    .cfi_def_cfa_offset 0
    ret
    .cfi_endproc
